summary: During a LOSA observation, a fuel tanker driver violated right-of-way procedures by driving between an E175 and a parked 737-800 without stopping for a taxiing A319. The reporter classified this as a near miss that could have caused a wing collision, flight cancellation, and fuel spill.

synopsis: Air Carrier ground personnel reported receiving Airways Bill for COMAT with insufficient documentation.
summary: A personal COMAT shipment for [Name] was found to contain prohibited lithium ion batteries in a backup charger, vacuum cleaner, LED lights, a drone, and a PED. The report identifies the specific equipment involved but does not state the outcome or cause of the discovery.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported loss of communications inflight causing a diversion.
summary: The crew diverted to Almaty after a complete data link failure prevented RNP-XX compliance and communication with ATC regarding severe turbulence. The Pilot in Command chose to land without an amended flight release due to the inability to coordinate alternate routing or obtain company clearance.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported EGPWS due to terrain on approach.
summary: During a visual approach to UNV at 6,500 ft MSL, the crew received an EGPWS terrain alert while descending over a south ridge. They executed a maximum power climb to clear the rising terrain and recommended reducing descent rates when crossing the ridge.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot crew reported too many frequency changes, EFB taxi chart confusion and taxiway sign confusion during taxi to runway.
summary: The flight crew taxied to the wrong bridge (RA instead of RB) at IAH due to confirmation bias, distraction by an adjacent aircraft, and confusion over similar taxiway names. This error required a ground stop of another aircraft to prevent a nose-to-nose collision before the crew was notified via telephone.

synopsis: B737-800 pilot reported refusing an aircraft after it was found to be leaking fuel from the refuel manifold. Maintenance discovered rag cloth fragments protruding from the poppet valve which reportedly prevented proper closure of the valve.
summary: A B737 pilot refused the aircraft at ZZZ after maintenance found rag fragments in the refuel manifold valve causing a leak. The pilot criticized the decision to return the aircraft to service the next day without inspecting the fuel tanks or the refuel source for contamination.

synopsis: C-172 pilot reported a fume/smoke event resulting in an immediate landing at the destination airport.
summary: A solo pilot flying to ZZZ1 smelled smoke near the approach course for Runway XX and requested an immediate landing. After landing safely with severe smoke, the pilot requested ground assistance to tow the aircraft to the ramp and squawk it.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported TCAS Alert on approach.
summary: The crew encountered a general aviation aircraft violating Class B airspace on final approach to SEA runway 16R, coming within 300 feet. A TCAS RA prompted a climb to clear the conflict, allowing a stabilized approach and landing without abrupt maneuvering.

synopsis: EMB-175 First officer reported a fumes event during initial climb resulting in a diversion.
summary: The First Officer and Captain diverted a flight at night due to a strange cockpit odor and suspected fuel leak, landing safely with no fire found. Flight attendants reported symptoms, and while a mechanic suspected APU de-ice ingestion, the crew noted no de-icing occurred and the smell dissipated after shutdown.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a fumes event during engine start-up and initial taxi-out. The flight returned to the gate for inspection after a Flight Attendant also reported a burning smell in the cabin.
summary: Flight Attendants reported a burning smell from the aft cabin after engine start but before taxi. Fire and Hazmat teams found no cause, maintenance could not recreate the issue, and the aircraft departed for ZZZ1 uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reporter that during taxi to the gate a baggage cart drove directly in front of them requiring the crew to slam on the brakes to avoid a collision.
summary: During taxi to the gate in Chicago, a baggage cart driver with four carts entered Taxiway A from a service road 15 feet ahead of the aircraft. The flight crew applied emergency brakes to avoid a collision, describing the incident as a major safety hazard and the closest they had ever come to hitting an object on the ground.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a group of passengers did not comply with face mask policy throughout the flight.
summary: Cabin crew reported that a group of passengers refused to comply with mask policy during a two-hour flight despite repeated interventions by flight attendants and adult leaders. Although the crew requested the passengers be denied future transport, airline leadership in ZZZ refused, allowing the group to continue to their next flight.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was non-compliant with face mask policy during flight.
summary: During flight, a flight attendant reported that a passenger repeatedly removed his mask and pretended to sleep while wearing noise-canceling headphones, requiring physical intervention to upright his seat and comply with mask rules. The attendant believes the passenger intentionally ignored instructions despite consuming alcohol and removed his mask again at the jetbridge.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a group of passengers were no compliant with face mask policy during flight.
summary: Flight attendants B and D repeatedly requested passengers in the same party to lift and secure face coverings. Passengers only complied when the flight attendants were walking by.

synopsis: Flight Attendants reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a passenger repeatedly wore his mask below his nose during boarding and in-flight service. Despite multiple requests to comply with airline policy, the passenger was defiant, claimed ignorance, and threatened the crew member with problems.

synopsis: Tailwheel pilot reported that during landing rollout their shoe became stuck on the rudder pedal and eventually slipped off resulting in a partial group loop.
summary: The pilot reported that during the rollout of a tailwheel aircraft, their left sneaker snagged on the rudder pedal, causing loss of directional control. The aircraft veered left, snapping the left landing gear and scraping the left aileron, but resulted in no injuries or other damage.

aircraft: Bombardier Learjet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reported responding to RA while on approach.
summary: A crew inbound to FXE on the FISEL SEVEN ARRIVAL received a TCAS climb resolution advisory while at 3000 ft due to a converging VFR piston single. The controller claimed the target never exceeded 2000 ft, but the crew climbed to 3600 ft to resolve the conflict before returning to their assigned altitude.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported inadvertently entering an MOA.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ1 after touch-and-goes failed to contact ZZZ Approach while following Aircraft Y, having mistakenly identified the surrounding Military Area as an MOA via ForeFlight. The pilot attributed the error to a recent return to general aviation after a COVID-related break from commercial flying.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported difficulty determining the correct pilot-controlled lighting frequency at PDK airport.
summary: A VFR pilot and a commercial instrument-rated passenger attempted a night approach to PDK with the tower closed but could not activate runway lights due to difficulty locating the correct PCL frequency. They landed safely using taxiway and landing lights, later discovering the correct frequency was 120.0, not the CTAF or UNICOM frequencies tried.

synopsis: J3 Cub flight Instructor reported ground loop during tail-wheel instruction.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a J-3 Cub experienced a ground loop during taxi due to a crosswind lifting the left wing. The left main gear struck a sign and the propeller struck the ground, causing damage, prompting the instructor to adopt a stricter intervention rule for future tailwheel instruction.

aircraft: Piper Single Turboprop Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight instructor reported that on-board 'Homesafe' system automatically activated the emergency radio and transponder broadcasts.
summary: During a training flight in a high-performance turbo-prop, the aircraft's "Home Safe" feature automatically triggered a false Mayday and squawk 7700. The crew manually cancelled the automation, reset systems to squawk 1200, and notified ATC that no emergency existed.

synopsis: Pilot reported that while maneuvering in the traffic pattern another aircraft flew in front of them three times, causing several NMACs.
summary: The reporter, descending to join the pattern at ZZZ Airport, experienced three near misses with a Bonanza pilot who ignored traffic and proper entry procedures. The Bonanza crossed 200 feet above the reporter on downwind, cut in front on short final, and forced an avoidance turn when it pulled up into the reporter's path during a go-around.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported that an ADIRU failure caused the crew and aircraft to become lost.
summary: Pilots reported a Fault Tolerant ADIRU navigation failure causing the aircraft to become lost during flight. US engineers determined an undetected ring laser gyro failure caused drift that the system failed to identify.

synopsis: A319 Flight Crew reported a Ground Proximity Warning even though they were established at a safe altitude for terrain avoidance.
summary: Pilots received a brief GPWS "pull up" warning while being radar vectored at 8,200 ft for an ILS approach. They executed an escape maneuver, but the warning ceased immediately, and they completed a normal landing, suspecting a false alarm caused by outdated EGPWS database data.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported forgetting to complete the COVID-19 assessment before the flight due to a distraction.
summary: The pilot failed to submit a required COVID assessment due to flight deck distractions caused by maintenance personnel performing a First Flight of the Day check. The reporter suggests replacing the separate digital form with a barcode scan at each leg to prevent future omissions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ATC re-sequenced them because they slowed to final approach speed at around a 6-mile final inbound to ATL.
summary: The flight crew experienced task saturation due to runway and approach changes, causing them to slow to final approach speed early at 6 miles. ATC cancelled their ILS PRM Runway 9R approach at 1,200 feet AGL due to insufficient spacing with a trailing aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported making a go-around per ATC's instructions due to spacing of aircraft on final into ATL.
summary: The crew executed a go-around on an ILS 9R approach after the Tower controller instructed them to cancel landing clearance due to slowing down six miles from the runway. The controller attributed the incident to task saturation, and the aircraft was subsequently vectored back for a normal landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to divert due to fuel issues related to ATC Zero Center closure and re-routes.
summary: Flight crew diverted from ZZZ1 to ZZZ2 due to ATC sequencing delays caused by a ZZZ1 Center closure. After receiving conflicting headings and uncertain clearance times, they diverted to ZZZ5 at 3,000 pounds fuel, refueled, and arrived at ZZZ2 90 minutes late.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported the hand sanitizer holder is in the way of evacuating passengers on the aircraft.
summary: Cabin crew reported that a hand sanitizer holder obstructed passenger evacuation at an aircraft door. The device was positioned directly in the path, hindering the exit flow during an emergency.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported a deadheading Captain and a passenger were non-compliant with face mask policy.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a Captain and a passenger in seat X4 failed to wear masks while not eating or drinking on Aircraft X. The crew member made an announcement regarding policy, received a complaint letter from the non-compliant passenger, and noted that other passengers also complained about the violation.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy and talking on the phone when not allowed.
summary: Cabin crew reported that a passenger on Aircraft X was non-compliant with mask and cellular device restrictions during pre-departure and after door closure. The passenger's defensive and dismissive behavior, despite repeated instructions and a Captain's announcement, was identified as a potential safety risk.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported the Chart Supplement still shows pre-pandemic hours for SUS Tower. Reporter stated there are no NOTAMs addressing this issue either.
summary: The reporter noted a discrepancy between the actual SUS Tower operating hours (07:00–20:00 local) and the outdated Chart Supplement listing (07:00–23:00 local), with no NOTAMs reflecting the change. They requested that SUS Tower issue a NOTAM or amend the Chart Supplement to display the correct hours.

synopsis: Flight Instructor flying experimental aircraft reported fuel exhaustion inflight.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Super Cub clone experienced an engine power loss during a go-around due to fuel exhaustion caused by unreliable gauges and unexpected fuel transfer between tanks. The aircraft was landed safely in an adjacent field with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action in response to an NMAC with a solo student pilot in the traffic pattern who did not follow ATC instructions to remain on the west side of the freeway.
summary: A pilot transitioning Van Nuys Airport from the north lost separation with a solo student pilot flying opposite direction on the wrong side of the 405 freeway due to an unverified ATC readback. The pilot executed a right turn to avoid a potential midair collision, prompting a recommendation for controllers to verify readbacks for closely separated traffic.

synopsis: Citation 501 pilot reported engine failure during takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna Citation 501 rejected takeoff at 70 knots on Runway XX at ZZZ after hearing a loud bang from the left side. A subsequent inspection revealed a catastrophic left engine failure where the front fan blew out, destroying the blades and cowling, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew observed a UAV within several hundred feet. Flight was in Class B airspace on base turn of approach.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain encountered a drone while descending southbound for a visual approach to RWY 26R at ATL. The drone was spotted at 4,900 ft, approximately 200–300 ft below the aircraft and within two wingspans, but no evasive action was required.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew was on approach to a Class B airport and came within 20 feet of a UAV while on final approach.
summary: During approach to Runway XX at ZZZ at 2,500 ft MSL, a white drone with red markings flew 20 feet below the aircraft's flight path. The pilot reported no time to avoid the drone and notified ZZZ tower of the incident.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to divert due to ATC COVID-19 issues at landing Center facility.
summary: The pilot diverted Aircraft X to ZZZ airport due to a COVID-related closure at ZZZ2 and a diversion ban at ZZZ4. Subsequent delays caused by multiple EDCTs, ground stops, and overwhelmed ZZZ airport operations resulted in a lack of passenger services and a late arrival at ZZZ2.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a fumes event during taxi-in. Aircraft was turned over to Maintenance for inspection.
summary: After landing and taxiing to the gate, the crew detected a "dirty sock" odor in the cabin. The pilot opened doors and windows to ventilate the aircraft, deplaned passengers quickly, and filed a Smoke, Odor and Fumes Report with maintenance.

synopsis: Challenger 300 flight crew reported terrain warning alert while being vectored for landing.
summary: The crew received multiple terrain warnings while vectored for the ILS at ZZZ at 2,500 feet with the autopilot engaged. After climbing to 3,500 feet to silence the alerts, they continued the approach and landed normally despite ATC confirming no terrain existed in the area.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew and Flight Attendant reported a fumes event during initial climb resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced smoke and fumes from cockpit vents during climbout after takeoff, likely caused by oil in the air conditioning packs. They returned to ZZZ airport, landed safely, and were cleared by fire services after exterior and interior inspections found no fire.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a ramp worker providing false assessment of wing icing.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X at ZZZ found frost on the wing after a ramp agent incorrectly reported it clean. The agent refused to re-inspect the wing but eventually deiced the aircraft without incident.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports runway braking action is nil prior to takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced two sideways slides while taxiing onto a snow-covered runway at ZZZ, determining braking action was Nil despite a prior Code 2 report. After requesting and waiting for DOT to re-plow and sand the runway, the aircraft departed safely.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: During boarding on Aircraft X, a cabin crew member at the AFT position repeatedly instructed a passenger in seat X4 to wear his mask properly. The passenger was non-compliant and displayed frustration, requiring two reminders before finally covering his nose and mouth after the doors closed.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported two passengers were not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: A cabin crew member on Aircraft X reported that Passenger X repeatedly wore her mask below her nose during the flight. Despite three reminders, the passenger remained non-compliant with mask policy, ignoring instructions and attempting to hide her behavior from the crew.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that a passenger had to be reminded four times to wear a face mask. Flight Attendant stated that the passenger and his wife were coughing without covering their cough.
summary: Cabin crew on flight ABCD reported that a sick passenger in seat XX1 repeatedly wore his mask incorrectly and coughed uncovered throughout the flight despite four verbal warnings. The passenger refused a replacement mask and continued coughing with his wife, causing concern among other passengers.

synopsis: Maintenance reported wrong lead in lines resulted in confusion and an aircraft was towed into contact with a hangar door resulting in winglet damage.
summary: Maintenance personnel moved Aircraft X from Spot XX at ZZZ hangar line, where the tug driver followed an unlabeled ground line intended for regional jets. The aircraft's right wingtip struck the hangar door due to insufficient clearance caused by the improper and faded line placement.

synopsis: Technician reported engines stored in hangar are not secured or protected from damage or FOD.
summary: The reporter noted that three aircraft engines in Bay X at ZZZ Hangar were left in an uncontrolled environment, making them susceptible to strikes, damage, and undocumented part removal. The narrative recommends creating a secure, locked staging area to prevent tampering and improve control measures.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported an airspace violation after having to divert from original route due to a TRACON facility going ATC Zero.
summary: A pilot flying enroute IFR to ZZZ1 was cleared VFR after a TRACON control issue, but misunderstood ATC's statement that "Class B airspace is down" as the airspace being inactive. The pilot later learned the controller erred due to a COVID cleaning event, prompting a need for explicit Class B clearances in similar situations.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action in response to a NMAC during landing. The other pilot believed the pilot was landing on a different runway.
summary: A pilot executing a touch-and-go on Runway XX at ZZZ Airport encountered another aircraft on left base for the opposite Runway XY. The pilot avoided a midair collision by pitching down then up after the other pilot mistakenly believed the first aircraft was landing on Runway YY.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported the aircraft had a complete electrical failure but the pilot was able to perform a successful diversion and landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a dual alternator failure on a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1, causing total electrical system loss including avionics, flaps, and electric trim. After diverting to ZZZ4 due to fuel concerns, the pilot executed a successful no-flap landing using backup instruments and pilotage, attributing the incident to a mechanical electrical system issue requiring maintenance.

synopsis: Technician reported missing a step to unplug the pressure switch while working on the engine anti-ice valve to be locked open.
summary: A mechanic applying an MEL for the #2 engine anti-ice valve missed the step to unplug the pressure switch because rain and a mask caused their glasses to fog. The reporter suggested removing the mask and finding shelter to improve tablet readability.

synopsis: Center Controller reported that a pilot asked to divert due to an engine problem then said the engine had failed. Due to unclear radio transmissions, Controller was not sure what pilot intentions were for landing location.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X reported losing oil pressure and requested a diversion to ZZZ, but radio issues prevented clear communication. The pilot subsequently declared an engine failure and glided to the airport while the controller provided weather and runway information without confirming the pilot's intentions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to receive a re-route due to a Center going ATC Zero.
summary: Pilots flying at FL220 faced communication delays due to workload and ARINC congestion while navigating a reroute around ZZZ1 Center airspace. After Dispatch ordered a diversion due to lost radar contact, the crew continued as cleared, re-established radar contact with ZZZ5 Center, and completed the flight uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported receiving an amended clearance due to a ATC Center going ATC Zero and questioned if they had violated an FAR by flying in uncontrolled airspace.
summary: The flight crew accepted a shortcut through ZZZ airspace from ZZZ1 Center, believing radar coverage was continuous despite the center's reported closure. Post-flight, Dispatch questioned the legality of the route due to potential lack of radar coverage, though the crew maintained they remained under ATC control in Class A airspace.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported failing to get temperature taken at screening point.
summary: A pilot reported inadvertently missing the temperature screening point at ZZZ after commuting for their first trip since last Spring. The pilot noted they had self-screened at home prior to departure and recorded a temperature of 97.4 degrees.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported concerns with having to wear a face mask in the cockpit especially in a rapid decompression situation.
summary: During cruise at FL370, a flight attendant asked the First Officer to wear a surgical mask, causing the pilot to worry that removing headsets and masks during rapid decompression would exceed the 19-second Time of Useful Consciousness. The incident created a significant distraction for the flight crew regarding emergency procedures and equipment removal.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that an encounter with mountain wave turbulence cause a brief loss of control and resulted in a Flight Attendant injury.
summary: During cruise, flight attendants seated due to chop encountered moderate mountain wave turbulence causing a 20-degree bank and airspeed increase. One flight attendant reported neck pain attributed to the event but remained fit for duty after supervisor review.

synopsis: Ground employee reported that during COVID-19 customer service agents should not use the airplane phones to make announcements.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that customer service agents should not touch aircraft phones for announcements due to COVID risks. The reporter stated agents are unnecessary and obstruct the doorway, as passengers can access gate and baggage information via technology.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported not removing a discontinuity which resulted in the aircraft descending below the MEA during arrival to RNO airport.
summary: During the KENNO2 arrival to ILS Z RWY 16R, the crew descended below 9,000 ft. MEA after failing to remove a waypoint discontinuity, causing VNAV to default to CWS. The Pilot Flying corrected the descent to 8,000 ft. after ATC queried the altitude, and the crew subsequently conducted a visual approach without incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an excursion from assigned altitude occurred during the approach because they set the wrong altitude in the window.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway XX, the flight crew mistakenly set 2,500 ft instead of the cleared 3,500 ft in the altitude window. ATC notified them of the deviation and issued a new clearance to remain at 2,500 ft, allowing the approach to continue without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they encountered severe turbulence associated with mountain wave which caused roll variations and altitude and airspeed deviations.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe clear air turbulence associated with mountain waves at FL360 while flying at .78 MACH. The event caused significant altitude and attitude deviations, but the autopilot recovered the aircraft with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported planning a flight through HF required airspace on a non-HF equipped aircraft.
summary: A dispatcher planned a flight through ZZZ Oceanic airspace on a non-HF equipped aircraft, failing to recall the HF-only communication requirement. The flight continued by relaying position reports via another aircraft on Guard frequency, prompting a recommendation for updated route remarks and overfly permits.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that a high rate of descent during arrival triggered an obstacle caution message nearby an antenna.
summary: The flight crew received an Obstacle Caution message while descending in speed mode from 11,000 ft to 3,000 ft into ZZZ. The crew climbed to 4,000 ft to clear an antenna, attributing the event to an early level-off caused by speed mode and suggesting vertical speed mode or ATC coordination as preventative measures.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported they observed an aircraft pass 500 feet overhead and received a TCAS/RA.
summary: The crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory just before glide slope intercept on the ILS approach while maintaining 3,000 feet. A single-engine aircraft crossed 500 feet above, prompting ATC to identify the traffic, though the crew noted they could have descended earlier.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that after a long flight, they were told one of the crew members had tested positive for COVID-19, yet they were asked to fly the next morning with only 4 hours of rest. Flight Attendant expressed concerns with company's handling of being exposed to COVID-19 and scheduling.
summary: The flight crew, after a 12-hour duty day and a crewmate testing positive for COVID, was ordered to deadhead to base at 04:45 despite being fatigued and potentially illegal. They complied with the directive, resulting in over 20 hours of duty without additional pay, raising concerns about contract and FAR compliance.

synopsis: Two Flight Attendants reported two separate passengers were not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: Cabin crew on Aircraft X from ZZZ to ZZZ1 issued multiple verbal warnings to two passengers who repeatedly wore masks incorrectly or removed them entirely. The passengers ignored policies, mocked crew and gate agents, and refused to comply despite repeated interventions during boarding, cruise, and taxi.

synopsis: DJI Inspire 2 UAS RPIC reported a fly away resulting in the drone flying into the window of a nearby building after liftoff. RPIC was unable to take over manually.
summary: The PIC and crew lost control of a DJI Inspire 2 drone during a test flight at 10 feet, causing it to fly away and crash into a building. The reporter attributed the incident to a manufacturer error that prevented manual override, resulting in total loss of the aircraft with no injuries.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate flight crew reported communication issues with ATC resulting in a minimum fuel situation due to a Center going ATC Zero.
summary: Pilots of a Type X aircraft encountered severe ATC communication failures and confusing reroutes due to an unannounced ATC Zero status at ZZZ2 Center, leading to minimum fuel concerns. After losing contact and receiving conflicting VFR/IFR clearances, the crew diverted to ZZZ6 and later ZZZ4, attributing the dangerous situation to poor ATC methodology during the COVID-19 crisis.

synopsis: C206 pilot reported a tire failure on landing rollout.
summary: The pilot in command of a Cessna 206 landing on Runway XXL at ZZZ experienced a right main tire failure during rollout. The aircraft yawed right, lost directional control, and struck a runway marker light after rolling off the north edge, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an engine failure during cruise.
summary: The pilot reported an engine #1 failure at FL390 caused by vibration and N1 rollback, forcing a descent to FL220. After ATC initially delayed recognition, the crew shut down the damaged engine, landed at ZZZ, and confirmed internal engine damage with oil draining onto the ramp.

synopsis: Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported starter generator failed inflight.
summary: The crew experienced a right generator failure and engine vibration during descent into ZZZ, caused by a cracked gearbox and broken starter. The failure occurred on a starter generator with 300 hours remaining before overhaul, despite a prior service letter recommending replacement due to premature failures.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported missing a readback which resulted in the aircraft being below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a low altitude alert after mishearing a pilot's readback of 060 as 070, causing the aircraft to descend into a 060 MVA near a 064 MVA. The controller attributed the error to expectation bias and potential fatigue from a quick turn and extended work weeks.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller conducting on the job training reported they did not realize the wrong aircraft read back a descent clearance and the aircraft descended below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An instructor and trainee air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to 17,000 feet, but the trainee failed to hear the readback due to frequency congestion. The trainee later issued a low altitude alert when Aircraft X descended below the 15,500-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude, prompting an immediate climb to 16,000 feet.

synopsis: A Departure Controller Instructor and the developmental reported an aircraft turned slower than normal and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller training on combined sectors issued a left turn to Aircraft X at 6,800 feet, causing it to descend below the 11,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude due to a slow turn rate in IFR weather. The instructor intervened to expedite the climb, and the controller attributed the incident to failing to account for weather-induced performance limitations before issuing the turn.

synopsis: Center Controller reported safety concerns with another Center facility going to ATC Zero during peak traffic times and the confusion/stress this causes the controllers.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that management forced the transfer of numerous aircraft into a non-radar environment without communication or approved separation, causing unmanageable sector congestion. The controller cited insufficient training, incorrect briefing materials, and ignored safety warnings as the cause of multiple separation violations and aircraft distress.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported not knowing if they were legal to fly in domestic Class A airspace in an uncontrolled environment after a Center had gone ATC zero.
summary: The flight crew accepted a route shortcut from ZZZ1 Center while cruising, unaware that normal radio coverage would be lost north of ZZZZZ. Although ZZZ3 Center confirmed radar contact, the crew later questioned if they inadvertently entered uncontrolled airspace or violated company policy due to the communication gap.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that the planned route to avoid ATC Zero airspace became unavailable and ATC provided a new route which resulted in the flight being in a non-radar environment. First Officer stated that they were later informed by company that they were not allowed to accept such a route.
summary: The flight crew encountered conflicting routing instructions and a Center closure while en route, leading to a dispatch ACARS message prohibiting the assigned path. Despite considering a diversion, the crew elected to continue to the original destination in a non-radar environment, completing the flight uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported people not wearing a mask while inside the flight operations crew lounge.
summary: A pilot reported that management and support staff in the flight operations crew lounge did not wear masks, leading other line pilots to remove theirs upon entry. The reporter attributed this to a lack of leadership by example, contradicting company expectations for mask usage in all locations.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported entertainment and power systems failed during flight and had to use fight attendants to record data so the affected passengers would receive some type of reimbursement.
summary: During a flight from ZZZZ to ZZZ, Aircraft X experienced the failure of over 50 entertainment and power systems. Dispatch instructed flight attendants to manually enter customer data using handhelds, raising safety concerns regarding increased passenger interaction during the pandemic.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the airspeed indicator failed on the Captain's side during takeoff roll resulting in a rejected takeoff.
summary: During a takeoff roll for a Line Check, the Captain rejected the takeoff after observing a failed airspeed indicator displaying zero speed and an orange flag. The aircraft stopped safely using auto-brakes, was removed from service for inspection and part replacement, and passengers were rebooked with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a nose gear malfunction after takeoff resulting in a return to departure airport.
summary: The crew returned to ZZZ after takeoff due to landing gear retraction failure, autopilot loss, and navigation issues. Upon landing, the nose gear shook and stopped at 90 degrees to the centerline, requiring tire replacement and passenger bus transport, though no fire occurred.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a near midair collision during descent to DEN airport.
summary: The pilot at 10,000 ft received a TCAS climb and level RA after ATC reported traffic at 9,000 ft that was initially not in sight. The crew followed the RA guidance to resolve the conflict, notified ATC, and subsequently received vectors for an uneventful landing at Denver.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported problems associated with the HF equipment on specific oceanic flights.
summary: Pilots on Company Airlines' [aircraft X type] fleet reported HF communication saturation on the X area route due to reduced AIRINC frequency pairs and the airline's failure to install SATCOM. This equipment delay forces reliance on overwhelmed HF radios, causing communication delays and preventing timely access to critical weather and safety information.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported they were not informed of Weight & Balance issue.
summary: The flight crew discovered a weight and balance issue only after flight attendants questioned blocked rows during pushback and departure. Load Planning confirmed the rows must remain empty, revealing that critical blocking instructions were missing from the ACARS weight manifest, potentially risking out-of-balance limits.

synopsis: Pushout Driver reported the tow bar pins broke and the tow bar damaged the aircraft's nose gear.
summary: During the pushback of an Airbus A320, the push driver reported a towbar failure caused by broken bolts and a bent nose gear connection after the tractor jumped. The aircraft broke away but was stopped safely, resulting in damage that grounded the plane for maintenance and required a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: Ground employee reported difficulty moving aircraft off a specific gate due to reduced clearance.
summary: Ramp crew towing Aircraft X and Y types at ZZZ Terminal using a Super Tug X encountered severe space constraints at Gates X, Y, and Z, causing equipment contact with curbs and excessive egress times. The reporter attributes these risks to avoidable gate assignments despite available alternatives, exacerbated by staffing shortages and high operational volume.

synopsis: First Officer reported some confusion regarding their taxi clearance after landing at Mexico City because of poor signage and lighting.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion while taxiing after landing due to missing signage, poor lighting, and Tower interruptions during the runway exit. These factors caused multiple incorrect taxi instructions and delays before the aircraft finally reached the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported an unstable approach and stated they should have executed a go-around.
summary: A crew flying a night approach into ZZZ airport received an unexpected ATC vector to the final approach fix, resulting in a high, unstable descent with excessive speed and sink rate at 1,000 feet. The pilot attributed the event to unfamiliarity with the airport, outdated stable approach criteria, and the vector bypassing planned waypoints, though the landing was completed uneventfully.

synopsis: MD11 Captain reported failure to properly program FMS prior to takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer initiated takeoff without a runway selected in the FMS, causing V-speeds to be lost and the Flight Director to deactivate. The Captain attributed the error to personal complacency and failing to stop the aircraft to resolve the issue before exceeding 100 knots.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported confusion with ATC's clearance resulted in a missed approach.
summary: The Captain and First Officer vectored for an RNAV approach but cancelled after descending below 3,000 feet on a vector to final, which is incompatible with RNP procedures. The missed approach was executed due to the controller's lack of awareness regarding RNP vectoring limitations and the Captain's inexperience.

synopsis: SA-227 Captain reported a nose wheel was lost during takeoff and confirmed post flight.
summary: The pilot reported that the front right wheel was missing after landing at ZZZ2, following earlier signs of increased taxi power and in-flight vibration. The pilot attributed the oversight to misinterpreting these symptoms as a heavy load or known unbalance rather than immediate maintenance issues.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a flight pairing where they had no proper food available and minimal sleep leaving them fatigued and hungry during flights.
summary: A flight crew experienced fatigue and made incorrect SOP callouts during a multi-leg trip due to a lack of onboard meals and delayed hotel transport that severely shortened their layover rest. The pilot attributed these errors to poor sleep quality caused by the pairing's failure to provide food and adequate rest time.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported concerns with being dispatched with an inoperative Slat Flap Control Computer.
summary: The pilot refused dispatch of an electric aircraft due to an inoperative SFCC#2 and its channel. The reporter stated this deferral negatively affected flight safety, as operating with inoperative flight control computers is unsafe.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a passenger was not complaint with face mask policy during flight.
summary: A non-compliant passenger in seat XX6 complained to the Captain after a Flight Attendant woke them to enforce mask policy. The passenger agreed to comply but alleged injury by the crew; the flight landed safely with a Customer Service Supervisor meeting the aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Commercial jet flight crew reported confusing runway over-run markings at Cheddi Jagan International Airport in Guyana.
summary: The First Officer, acting as Pilot Flying, increased vertical speed to 1,498 fpm during a visual approach to Runway 06 at SYCJ by mistaking a long, unmarked displaced threshold for the active runway. This error, caused by degraded markings and poor weather, was corrected after the Captain called out the excessive sink rate, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported MMMX runway centerline markings are faded and suggested that a NOTAM would be appropriate.
summary: A pilot reported that on Runway 5R in Mexico City, centerline markings were missing between 1,000 and 3,000 feet beyond the threshold and faded until Taxiway G. The reporter recommended issuing a NOTAM to warn pilots of this condition.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported an engine failure on takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 90 knots on Runway XXL due to an Engine Fail light and inability to advance Engine #2 above 95%. The aircraft cleared the runway, returned to a different gate for transload and relaunch, and maintenance was debriefed.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Captain reported being ready to push an aircraft that was planned for a reposition, when the cabin door opened, and a cleaning crew came aboard.
summary: During a reposition flight at ZZZ, cleaning crew unexpectedly opened the main cabin door for a security sweep and COVID cleaning while the aircraft was ready for pushback. The reporter attributed this to a lack of coordination regarding ferry flight requirements and suggested restoring the beacon-on checklist step to prevent future safety risks.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a GPWS Alert on initial approach to CHO airport.
summary: Pilots flying a visual approach to Runway 21 at Charlottesville received a GPWS 'terrain pull up' caution while vectored at 3,000 MSL over steep rising terrain. They maintained level flight after visually confirming obstacle clearance and recommended ATC assign 4,000 MSL for this vectoring path.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an overshoot of altitude on departure and made reference to the aircraft being light in weight.
summary: The First Officer hand-flew a light-load aircraft during initial climb and overshot the assigned 5,000 feet to 5,300 feet due to a high climb rate and workload while the Captain managed checklists. The crew corrected the deviation without traffic disruption, attributing the error to manual flight expectations and suggesting increased automation use in busy environments.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna Twin Piston aircraft pilot reported the windshield anti-ice system was inoperative in icing conditions.
summary: The pilot encountered icing during cruise and found the electric windshield switch broke, leaving the system inoperative. The crew returned to ZZZ, descended through ice with limited visibility, and landed safely with only minor ice accumulation.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a long landing possibly outside of the landing zone. Reporter attributed discrepancy to possible company policy of adding speed to straight in landings and the aircraft being light in weight.
summary: The pilot reported a long landing on Runway XXL with a 6-7 knot tailwind, caused by low aircraft weight and company-mandated speed additions. The crew elected to continue the landing using maximum thrust reversers, noting that landing on the opposite runway would have been safer.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported returning to the gate after receiving notification a Flight Attendant onboard had been exposed to COVID-19.
summary: The flight crew pushed back for de-icing in winter conditions before discovering an unacknowledged release amendment removing a flight attendant due to COVID exposure. The aircraft returned to the gate because the crew missed the notification during a quick turn, citing a breakdown in CRM and a lack of mandatory amendment acknowledgement systems.

synopsis: Flight crew reported getting an altitude alert from ATC after descending below the minimum safe altitude during arrival to DEN airport.
summary: The flight crew descending on the CLASH 3 STAR to Denver descended below the 7,500-foot minimum altitude after being cleared for a visual approach to Runway 35L. ATC issued an altitude alert, prompting the crew to climb to 7,500 feet until glideslope interception, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported MHT airport's lack of digital ATIS makes it difficult to properly prepare for the approach.
summary: Pilots reported that at Manchester (MHT), the lack of digital ATIS and VHF range during preflight prevents accurate runway prediction in light winds. This forces high-workload FMC reprogramming en route when complex RNAV arrivals change, creating a risk of errors.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain refused an aircraft due to a deferred Slat Flap Controller Computer, citing concerns that flight control protections would be reduced if other computers were to fail in flight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer refused to operate Aircraft X due to degraded slat/flap functionality from SFCC #2 deferrals and an inoperative rudder travel limiter. They determined the lack of flight control redundancy created unacceptably reduced safety margins for dispatch.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an encounter with turbulence and an updraft resulted in a temporary loss of control and overspeed condition.
summary: During an enroute climb from FL350 to FL390, the crew encountered a severe updraft causing an overspeed and altitude overshoot while the autopilot was engaged. The Pilot Flying disconnected the autopilot to manually recover speed and altitude, reporting the event to ATC and Maintenance with no injuries sustained.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp personnel reported Hazmat Dangerous Goods transported without required Hazmat cargo configuration.
summary: The ramp lead attempted to final a departing flight four times but failed due to unsecured dangerous goods and a missing bag count alert. The lead manually altered the bag count in the load planning software to bypass the error and finalize the flight.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a heading deviation caused by not following SOP's and a change to the crew's normal procedures due to the pandemic.
summary: During cruise, the Pilot Flying misspelled a direct-to waypoint in the FMS while the Pilot Monitoring ate, causing the aircraft to drift off course. Fatigue and typing the fix manually rather than selecting it from the flight plan contributed to the error, which was corrected after ATC queried the deviation.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported being distracted by ATC Zero events, airspace closures due to COVID and forgetting to inform a flight crew that HF radio communication would be necessary.
summary: The pilot missed the HF communication requirement while routing the aircraft through ZZZ oceanic airspace to avoid COVID-related closures and ETOPS areas. The reporter attributed the error to distraction from airspace restrictions and suggested an alert system for HF requirements in specific FIRs.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported smoke in the cockpit and cabin that resulted in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew encountered a false APU leak message followed by cockpit smoke at FL370, prompting an expedited descent to FL310 and diversion to ZZZ. They landed safely after briefly exceeding gear extension speed, with no evacuation required as the smoke dissipated below 10,000 feet.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concerns with many passengers not wearing face masks in the gate area at airport.
summary: A flight attendant reported non-compliance with face covering policies by passengers in the ZZZ terminal concourse during the late afternoon departure bank. The reporter stated that ground personnel, airport police, and management do not enforce the policy, leaving flight attendants as the sole enforcers in an area not owned by the company.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported feeling the company is not doing enough to protect the frontline employees during the pandemic.
summary: A flight attendant reported feeling unsafe due to passengers not wearing masks correctly and criticized the company's ineffective policies, including allowing gaiters and full flights. The reporter cited increased infections among crew, lack of timely exposure notifications, and insufficient protection for frontline workers.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported forgetting to wear a face mask during descent while performing safety duties and collecting passenger trash.
summary: A cabin crew member forgot to wear a face mask while checking seatbelts and collecting trash during initial descent after the seatbelt sign illuminated. The crew member realized the oversight three rows into the aisle, immediately donned the mask clipped to their wings, and continued duties.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a passenger repeatedly removed her mask during boarding, after the safety demonstration, and before landing. The crew member could not issue a final warning as the aircraft was in the landing phase.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was required to remove a mesh face mask, while the Gate Agent did not agree, and use a company supplied mask before departure.
summary: A flight attendant and gate agent were involved during boarding when a passenger wore a non-compliant mesh mask. The flight attendant consulted the manual, confirmed the mask was not approved, and the passenger exchanged it for a solid material mask provided by the crew.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported being assigned to a passenger seat next to a customer that continually removed their face mask.
summary: A flight attendant reported discomfort while seated next to a passenger who repeatedly removed his mask to eat or drink during taxi, takeoff, and landing. The passenger also fell asleep in the crew member's assigned seat, prompting a request for future crew seating arrangements to ensure isolation from such passengers.

synopsis: Flight Attendants reported a passenger was moved to a seat, against company policy, near their jump seat by the Gate Agent.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a Gate Agent assigned a premium passenger to seat X6, a social distance block next to the jumpseat, disregarding crew safety concerns. The passenger later confronted the crew in the galley, causing distraction and discomfort during the flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concern after a passenger stated he and his wife had recently recovered from COVID-19.
summary: A flight attendant documented a passenger requesting water and discussing his recent COVID-19 history while seated near the crew. The reporter expressed concern that the passenger's party might be asymptomatic carriers, posing a potential safety risk to the cabin crew who had contact with them.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was seated in the company social distancing blocked seat.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger with a service animal in seat X6 blocked their assigned seat X4 with luggage during moderate turbulence, forcing the crew member to use a jump seat. The passenger's presence and belongings prevented safe social distancing and distracted the flight attendant from safety duties during the flight and landing.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concerns regarding the assigned jump-seat and its location near passenger seats.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger upgraded to seat X6, located next to the crew jumpseat X4, violating social distancing during a flight with turbulence. The attendant felt unsafe due to the passenger's proximity and requested a system fix to prevent such upgrades until a vaccine is available.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was not complaint with face mask policy.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger in seat YY3 repeatedly removed her face mask on flight XX2. The passenger complied with mask requests from both the reporter and Flight Attendant B after being observed without the mask.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported a curtain restraint missing in cabin area.
summary: A flight attendant discovered a missing curtain tie-back at 10,000 feet and secured the curtain with knots for landing. The incident prompted a fleet-wide inspection and a directive to flight attendants that tie-backs are the only approved restraining means.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was non-compliant with face mask policy and interfered with FA crew duties.
summary: A passenger disrupted Flight Attendant duties by refusing to comply with company, CDC, and FAA face covering policies. This noncompliance reportedly placed the crew and other passengers at risk of contracting COVID-19.

synopsis: Multiple repeat flap failures caused a no flap landing and subsequent errors during maintenance trouble shooting and repair of the affected system.
summary: Aircraft X experienced a flap fault on approach, leading to a go-around and landing with full slats but no flaps due to pilot checklist misinterpretation and fuel concerns. Mechanics faced management pressure to sign the aircraft airworthy despite TSM requirements to replace actuators for a known jam, though the crew attributed the landing error to distraction and fatigue.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp personnel at destination reported missing required Hazmat documents for Hazmat Dangerous Goods shipment.
summary: The reporter noted a missing dry ice checklist for a shipment, stating it was either unchecked or ZZZ forgot to send it with the Airways Bill. No specific aircraft, phase of flight, or further outcome was described in the narrative.

synopsis: M-20 R pilot reported ATC issued an altitude alert during initial approach.
summary: The pilot on final approach in strong quartering headwinds received a Tower altitude alert at 600 feet, 2.5 miles out, while planning to maintain 700 feet until 1 mile. The pilot attributed the alert to descending too early and noted they should have remained 200–300 feet higher.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a track heading deviation after entering incorrect information in the GPS and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot flying IFR at 2,000 feet incorrectly entered RNAV GPS Runway X approach data for ZZZ, causing the aircraft to deviate from the approach plate. The pilot attributed the error to reduced flying experience since the COVID-19 pandemic.

synopsis: C680 Captain reported getting two RAs during climbout, however, they were unable to visually locate the traffic and ATC advised there was no other traffic in the vicinity.
summary: Pilots received two TCAS Resolution Advisories while climbing from FL210 to FL430, instructing emergency climbs despite ATC reporting no traffic. The unseen target appeared directly below on the display, causing the crew to comply with RAs before the conflict cleared and the target disappeared.

synopsis: C150 student pilot conducting a first solo flight and instructor on the ground reported the student experienced an engine failure and landed safely in a field.
summary: A student pilot experienced an unpreventable internal engine failure causing 500 RPM loss and metal-on-metal noise during his first solo cross-country enroute phase. He executed a safe off-field landing with no injuries or visible aircraft damage, and the engine is now undergoing a total overhaul.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported experiencing a NMAC when another small aircraft attempted to make a short approach in front of the reporters aircraft.
summary: The pilot flying an RNAV approach encountered a near miss with Aircraft Y, which was on a short approach and appeared behind and above at 700 feet. The reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot's poor judgment in executing a short approach and their own failure to proactively suggest extending downwind.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported fatigue and confusion resulted in a Rejected Take Off due to misdiagnosing a Bleed Air/ Pack/ Anti Ice Issue.
summary: The crew rejected a takeoff below 50 knots due to a Level 2 Pack 3 Not Closed alert following a Level 1 Pack Flow Disagree. The pilot attributed the event to fatigue and an expectation that the Environmental System Controller would resolve the issue, noting maintenance deferred the malfunctioning pack.

synopsis: Corporate jet pilot reported receiving a low-altitude alert from ATC after takeoff from VNY airport.
summary: ATC advised the Captain that the aircraft was too low during departure from Runway 34L. The Captain requested an expedited climb and confirmed adherence to the SID.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC near LMO airport.
summary: A pilot climbing to 6,300 feet near Boulder Reservoir executed a steep left turn to avoid a head-on near-miss with a lightsport aircraft while distracted by GPS inputs. The pilot attributed the incident to being heads-down for six seconds and noted that ADS-B auditory alerts might have provided earlier warning.

synopsis: Private Pilot reported the cause of the deviation was not flying for 2 months during the pandemic and was rusty and needed practice.
summary: A pilot flying a Garmin-equipped aircraft on a back-course approach descended below the cleared 4,000 feet due to misunderstood ATC instructions, autopilot capture failure, and confusion over chart versus GPS altitudes. The pilot attributed the incident to being out of practice, avionics anomalies, and high workload, though no terrain or traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: Single pilot reported that during takeoff roll the aircraft veered left and departed the runway. During taxi back to parking, pilot did not call ground control for taxi clearance.
summary: The pilot reported that after takeoff clearance, the aircraft veered left off the pavement onto grass, closing the main runway. The aircraft later taxied on the closed turf runway without prior Ground contact, prompting a recommendation for signage requiring taxi instructions for turf operations.

synopsis: Beechjet 400 Captain reported experiencing an engine failure while at cruise altitude resulting in a diversion.
summary: The crew of a three-passenger flight at FL410 experienced a loud bang, high ITT, and vibration in the #2 engine, followed by a fuel smell. They performed a precautionary shutdown, diverted to ZZZ, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Gulfstream IV First Officer reported total loss of elevator and stabilizer trim that resulted in major control issues and a diversion.
summary: During climb after takeoff, the flight crew encountered a frozen pitch trim system and dual flight guidance computer failures that caused uncontrollable pitch-up tendencies and loss of flight director references. The pilots manually controlled the aircraft using split duties and circuit breaker resets to restore instruments, then safely landed under ATC radar vectors.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported that while the student was taxiing a strong gust of wind rotated the aircraft and it went off the taxiway. Flight instructor regained control and taxied back onto the taxiway.
summary: During a training taxi, a strong gust rotated the aircraft 30 degrees off the taxiway because the inexperienced pilot failed to apply brakes. The instructor, distracted by headset issues, took control to return to the taxiway, and the flight was cancelled due to the crosswind.

synopsis: C152 pilot reported that while flying an unfamiliar route they flew over higher terrain that reduced the amount of vertical clearance the pilot would normally have.
summary: A pilot on approach to ZZZ from the northwest flew over an unexpected terrain rise at approximately 500 feet AGL while complying with a clearance to remain below 2,000 feet. The pilot attributed the low altitude to unfamiliarity with the route and plans to fly higher or around the rise in the future to maintain 1,000 feet clearance.

synopsis: SFO Local Controller reported an E175 pilot executed a go-around from short final after encountering wake turbulence from another E175 on final approach to the parallel runway.
summary: An E175 on final for Runway 28 Left encountered wake turbulence from a preceding E175 landing on Runway 28 Right in crosswind conditions. The aircraft yawed right and rolled left, prompting the crew to execute a go-around and successfully land on a subsequent approach.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: The pilot refused to board a passenger on a new aircraft at ZZZ after the previous flight diverted due to an electrical issue and the passenger's unresponsive, non-compliant behavior. The decision was made because flight attendants reported the passenger could not follow instructions, posing a safety risk under FAA Zero Tolerance policies.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they were not allowed into a foreign country due to not having proof of negative COVID-19 test results, nor proof of having been vaccinated.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of Aircraft X were denied entry into Country ZZZZ by a health official who incorrectly demanded a negative COVID-19 test despite crew exemptions. With assistance from airline staff, the crew returned to the gate and departed for ZZZ after declining an offer for an on-site test.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported taxiing into a gate with the use of a Marshall, while the self-parking guidance system was indicating STOP.
summary: The Captain and First Officer ignored a red self-park STOP signal at gate X at ZZZ, following marshaller hand signals instead to park without incident. They identified this as a normalization of deviance caused by organizational complacency, noting it contradicts the safety culture of never accepting red indications.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that an engine compressor stall occurred during takeoff roll, causing the aircraft to swerve and the crew to reject the takeoff.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 60 knots after a loud bang and right swerve caused by an Engine 2 compressor stall. The aircraft was inspected with no damage found, returned to the gate, and the crew continued the scheduled flight.

synopsis: Air Carrier Load Planner reported a communications breakdown between Load Planner and Ramp personnel resulting in aircraft departure with incorrect Hazmat documentation.
summary: Ramp and a Cargo Specialist loaded radioactive Dangerous Goods and ballast on a flight with only 14 bags, violating the 15-bag minimum requirement. The flight departed four minutes after OUT with an invalid load that failed to trigger an ACARS alert.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew taxiing 747-8 aircraft reported taxiway incursion on closed taxiway.
summary: A 747-8 crew missed a NOTAM closing Taxiway Kilo due to expectation bias after switching runways, nearly entering the dimly lit barrier. The International Relief Officer called "Stop," preventing a collision, while ATC issued an invalid clearance before correcting the taxi instructions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing wind shear on final resulting in a go-around. Captain made reference to the First Officer's lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced two go-arounds on Runway XXL due to wind shear and an unstable approach caused by the FO's lack of recency. The Captain declared minimum fuel, landed successfully on the third attempt, and recommended increased recurrent training for pilots returning from extended breaks.

synopsis: Dispatcher forgot to include Non-Tower Operations worksheet with the aircraft paperwork.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X (ZZZ1-ZZZ) arrived at ZZZ after a maintenance block-turn-back while the tower was closed due to staffing and COVID cleaning. The pilot forgot to add the Non-Tower Ops worksheet because of the delay and suggested emailing the worksheet to crews proactively.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported a Hazmat transport procedure violation due to inadequate staffing for the high departure workload.
summary: A dispatcher approved a dry ice request for Aircraft X but forgot to amend the release before the aircraft departed for ZZZ1 due to high workload. The dispatcher attributed the oversight to being overwhelmed with other tasks despite setting a reminder and suggested reducing domestic desk workload.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a child was not wearing a face mask on the flight and questioned how flight attendants could enforce a child to wear a mask.
summary: Cabin crew reported a boarding incident where a family claimed their 3-year-old child was under 2 to avoid wearing a mask despite having a purchased seat. The crew allowed boarding based on the gate agent's inability to verify age, highlighting a lack of policy to check birth dates that creates unfair enforcement of mask compliance.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was not compliant with face mask policy.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger refused to wear a mask while seated in an exit row, citing food consumption as an excuse despite prior crew instructions. The passenger explicitly stated she would not comply, prompting the crew member to suggest a national policy and permanent bans for non-compliant travelers.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 Flight Crew reported the failure of the L/H Generator and a Roll Back on the L/H Engine resulted in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left generator failure followed by a left engine rollback and loud droning noise during cruise and descent. After landing safely at an alternate airport, the left engine spooled down with a smoke plume, revealing starter generator cooling exit streaks but no structural damage.

synopsis: GA pilot reported that during touchdown the aircraft yawed violently, departed the runway, and became stuck in the grass. Subsequent maintenance inspection found that the wheel brake assembly was rusted and had missing parts.
summary: The pilot of a rented aircraft experienced a violent left yaw and runway excursion upon landing at ZZZ1 due to frozen, unlubricated brake caliper slider pins. The aircraft became stuck in the grass and required a tug and 4WD truck for recovery before a mechanic repaired the rusted brake assembly.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported the right brake failed while the student was maneuvering for run-up and aircraft departed the taxiway.
summary: During taxi at ZZZ Airport, a student pilot and instructor experienced a total loss of right brake pressure while maneuvering for a run-up. The instructor shut down the engine to stop the aircraft, but it still departed the taxiway, causing the left main gear to strike a taxiway light.

synopsis: An ATC Supervisor reported instructing a controller to issue an IFR clearance through a Restricted Area due to priority situation.
summary: An Operational Supervisor issued a short-range IFR clearance to an aircraft with an engine malfunction requesting priority landing at a Naval Air Base within a hot Restricted Area. The decision was made for safety of flight to descend through clouds, despite a disagreement regarding its legality, citing an LOA allowing such clearances in IMC.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported they vectored an aircraft under priority handling and requested clearance to return to the departure airport through a TRACON's airspace without a point out.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X, which reported high left engine vibration and requested a return while climbing to 23,000 feet. Due to high workload and a language barrier, the controller transferred the aircraft to Departure without issuing a clearance back to the departure airport, resulting in the aircraft inadvertently leaving adjacent airspace.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported loading the wrong approach in the FMC and received clearance to land on the selected runway because of light traffic due to COVID.
summary: The First Officer on flight XX failed to update the FMC from Runway XXR to the cleared Runway XXL due to distraction during the descent checklist. ATC intercepted the error during vectors, cleared the crew to continue the XXR approach, and the aircraft landed safely without incident.

synopsis: Ground employee reported plastic shields should be added to the tables in a break room.
summary: A CSR reported that two break tables in Zone X room Y should be separated by a wall and window to prevent employee contact, while retaining plastic shields on both tables.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported recurring fume events which have resulted in flight crew experiencing physiological symptoms. Reporter questioned whether maintenance corrective actions are in need of review.
summary: Flight and cabin crew detected petroleum-based fumes during descent below 5,000 ft. on flight ZZZ-ZZZ1, but maintenance overruled their reports and returned the aircraft to service. A subsequent ferry crew refused the aircraft after smelling fumes upon starting engine #1, confirming the issue remained unresolved.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and Dispatcher reported the nose wheel door remained open after gear retraction during climbout. A successful air return was completed.
summary: The crew experienced a nose landing gear door open indication after gear retraction on departure from ZZZ. Following QRH procedures, they determined insufficient fuel for the original destination and returned to ZZZ due to the aircraft system failure.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported landing gear door actuator failed causing doors to remain open, resulting in an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered a gear disagreement message and open gear doors while airborne at 32,000 feet. Recycling the gear failed to resolve the issue, which the crew attributed to a broken actuator.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a block turn back due to failed nose wheel steering actuator.
summary: The crew blocked the aircraft's turn back due to a suspected leak in the steering tube. No further details regarding the specific phase of flight or outcome were provided in the narrative.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Flight Crew reported engine flameout on short final and continued on to land successfully.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine flameout at 15,000 ft MSL while on the ZZZZZ arrival to ZZZ. A successful airborne restart was achieved, and the aircraft landed without incident, with a faulty engine run/stop switch suspected as the cause.

synopsis: GA pilot reported landing on the wrong runway and not being aware of doing so until the Tower Controller instructed the pilot to go-around.
summary: A pilot practicing maneuvers landed on the wrong runway despite ATC clearing them for Runway XX and reporting a holding aircraft. The pilot attributes the error to confirmation bias, noting they touched down just as the tower ordered a go-around before re-clearing the correct runway.

synopsis: Reporter reported possibly flying commercially with a third class physical several years ago.
summary: A pilot realized they may have previously flown commercially on an expired third-class medical certificate four to five years ago due to a lack of tracking. The pilot now uses a database to monitor medical due dates and has corrected the misconception that a second-class medical can lapse into a third-class.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA instructor pilot reported that as they started the takeoff roll a truck began driving toward them from the opposite end of the runway. Pilot elected to continue takeoff and truck drove off the runway, allowing plane to continue.
summary: A pilot conducting a touch-and-go at 33V on Runway 22 encountered a snowplow truck entering the runway head-on at 65 mph. The aircraft failed to lift off due to high density altitude, but the truck exited the runway, allowing the pilot to continue the takeoff.

synopsis: Corporate Captain reported that the flaps failed when they were retracted after takeoff so the crew did an air return and zero flap landing.
summary: The crew experienced a flap system failure at zero degrees during retraction after takeoff, preventing extension, retraction, or reset. They returned to ZZZ and completed a safe zero-flap landing without further interruption.

synopsis: CL604 First Officer reported numerous issues with a new avionics system which caused airborne conflict.
summary: The First Officer and Captain of a corporate flight experienced loss of situational awareness and an unstable approach due to Proline Fusion avionics programming difficulties and Captain errors. The First Officer took control twice to manage speed and traffic, resulting in a normal landing after a debrief on standardization and system limitations.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate Captain reported an incorrect read back for altitude which caused their aircraft to climb an additional 2,000 feet resulting in an airborne conflict with another aircraft.
summary: The Captain and a replacement First Officer misunderstood ATC climb instructions during departure from ZZZ, causing a conflict with an aircraft on downwind. The pilot attributed the error to crew changes and high workload, noting no TCAS alert occurred despite the proximity.

synopsis: During routine engine maintenance, a technician omitted installing O Rings on a scavenge oil transmitter, causing loss of oil quantity and a diversion to a precautionary landing.
summary: A mechanic assisted a colleague with an engine run to test a new scavenge oil transmitter, observing normal parameters. The colleague later forgot to install O-rings, causing oil quantity to drop to zero in flight and forcing a diversion to ZZZ1.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a flight of two military aircraft exited a Military Operating Area and began descending from 25000 feet without communications or a radar handoff from the military controlling agency. The reporter states there is a new military controlling facility and procedures which have been violated many times since the new procedures were implemented.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that two military aircraft exited a new control area without an automated radar hand-off, causing them to fly outside the designated airspace. The controller manually established contact with the aircraft at 25,000 feet, attributing the incident to automation failures and inadequate training on new procedures.

synopsis: Captain reported refusing the aircraft after ELAC2 was placed on MEL.
summary: The pilot refused to depart with a deferred ELAC 2 fault due to concerns over flight control degradation if the remaining computer failed. After notifying maintenance and Dispatch, the crew was swapped to a new aircraft before departure.

synopsis: Ground employee reported co-workers are not complying with face mask policy and supervisors are ignoring the issue.
summary: Crew members reported that two coworkers failed to wear masks properly during a shift at gate X, with one supervisor ignoring their signals from 12 feet away. The incident involved non-compliance with mask protocols while the supervisor observed but took no action.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp Lead reported a communication breakdown between company ramp personnel and other ground personnel [consulting group] regarding Hazmat cargo load.
summary: The Consulting Team failed to verify Dangerous Goods loading on Aircraft X before departure to ZZZ1 due to poor communication and not reviewing the flight card. Their late arrival five to ten minutes prior to departure resulted in unverified cargo, as they did not fulfill their role to locate and check freight.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a track heading deviation during departure. Captain cited distraction dealing with an ECAM alert and lack of flying contributed to the event.
summary: The crew departed ZZZ on the ZZZZZ 4 RNAV SID but faced task saturation due to a simultaneous #1 Pressure Regulator ECAM fault and a last-minute ATC clearance change. This distraction caused a slight delay in turning to the new waypoint, though no conflicts or violations occurred.

synopsis: First Officer reported undocumented transport of Hazmat cargo due to improper DG tracking.
summary: The Captain and First Officer were informed post-block-in that unmanifested flammable gas was loaded in a non-DG labeled container at position 12L on Aircraft X. The reporter attributed this Hazmat violation to improper tracking of dangerous goods materials.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported executing a go-around due to ATC spacing with another aircraft on final. The flight crew overshot their altitude during the go-around and cited the aircraft light weight as a contributing factor.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway XXR at ZZZ, ATC issued a late go-around at 600 AGL due to insufficient spacing with parallel traffic.
