The pilot executed a belly landing on a grass runway as recommended by the POH, resulting in no injuries to the single occupant.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported an engine malfunction in flight resulting in a return to departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported low manifold pressure readings during cruise at 8,500 feet after departing ZZZ. The aircraft returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing, where the pilot confirmed the inability to achieve full power with full throttle.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported they descended below their assigned altitude during descent to DEN and ATC advised them they were below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: The flight crew descended below the RNAV arrival profile and Minimum Vectoring Altitude because the Pilot Flying remained in Vertical Speed mode instead of VNAV while updating speeds. ATC queried the low altitude, and the crew climbed back to 14,000 feet before being vectored to final.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported they had an agreement between themselves regarding face mask policy on the flight deck and may have violated FAR/SOP policy.
summary: During an international departure, the #2 FO remained in the flight crew rest area for takeoff instead of the flight deck due to a dispute over the Captain's refusal to wear a mask. The #2 FO later reported a potential FAR violation regarding his absence, while the Captain and #1 FO believed no regulations were breached.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a change in airport procedures, due to COVID-19, caused the flight crew to miss the required signing of the Flight Release.
summary: The flight crew discovered an unsigned dispatch release at cruise and added 2,000 pounds of fuel en route. Confusion over new terminal procedures caused delays, and the crew failed to notice the unsigned release or the missing fuel entry on the second release until after the fueler added the fuel.

synopsis: Captain reported loss of System B engine driven hydraulic pump and the number 2 engine filter bypass light illuminating resulted in an inflight shutdown of the number two engine and a diversion.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X diverted to ZZZ2 after a #2 engine shutdown caused by a hydraulic B system leak and subsequent flap failure. They successfully landed using electrically extended flaps after troubleshooting the zero hydraulic quantity issue.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a loss of B system hydraulic fluid, followed by the loss of multiple hydraulic pumps resulted in a diversion.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced a rapid loss of Hydraulic System B followed by System A engine pump failure, prompting a diversion to ZZZ1. The pilots managed the emergency using QRH checklists and alternate flap extension, landing safely with only the System A electric pump remaining functional.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that during arrival the Speed Trim Configuration Warning light illuminated and the QRH non-normal checklist was completed prior to landing.
summary: During descent with speed brakes deployed, the pilot experienced speed trim, master caution, and flight control light illuminations. After completing the QRH non-normal checklist, the crew remained on autopilot and successfully executed a CAT 2 auto land on Runway 4L due to low visibility.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an NMAC with traffic from the opposite direction during cruise flight.
summary: The Captain and crew of an aircraft on Y52 at 26,000 ft received a TCAS RA while approaching two head-on aircraft, including Aircraft Y. They executed a descent and left turn, achieving less than 100 ft separation, resulting in a 300–1,000 ft altitude loss with no injuries.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported an inflight engine shut down and loss of hydraulic fluid resulted in a diversion.
summary: During cruise at FL380, the crew shut down Engine 2 following an oil filter bypass indication and diverted to ZZZ3. On approach, System B hydraulic pressure dropped to zero, preventing normal flap extension, but the crew successfully used alternate extension procedures to land safely with manual braking.

synopsis: Deadheading Pilot reported being asked to come to the Flight Deck and act as an ACM (Additional Crew Member) during an inflight event.
summary: A deadheading cabin crew member assisted the flight deck crew after the number two engine was shut down during an urgent situation. The crew member helped with communications and checklists, though the primary crew required minimal assistance.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported after landing at JFK they turned onto a closed taxiway and cited signage issues as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot exited Runway 31R onto closed Taxiway WW instead of planned Taxiway V, misled by illuminated green leadoff lights and insufficient signage. The aircraft safely crossed snow berms to the ramp after Tower approval, though the reporter noted the lights should have been extinguished for the closed taxiway.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they were cleared for a VOR approach which required a procedure turn. There was no procedure turn published on their charts or contained in the FMC.
summary: During a cruise descent to QRO, the crew encountered an FMC database error that auto-sequenced the aircraft into an illegal turn toward mountainous terrain. The pilots manually entered a holding pattern to legally execute the required procedure turn, avoiding a potential CFIT event caused by the mismatch between the FMC and Jeppesen charts.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the missed approach procedure as described in the NOTAM, is in error.
summary: The pilot reported a potential error in NOTAM BHM A0233/21 for the LOC Runway 24 approach at BHM, where the published missed approach heading of 219 does not intercept the required VUZ radial 067. The crew requested and received an amended missed approach procedure from ATC before commencing the approach.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a NMAC with a drone during approach to MOB airport.
summary: A pilot reported a near-miss with a drone quadcopter at 1,800 feet while on final approach to runway 15 at MOB. The drone passed within 15 feet of the left wing, but post-landing inspection revealed no damage, attributed to an illegal drone operation in the airport vicinity.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported smoke in the flight deck and cabin due to the reversers or packs ingesting chemicals that had been used to treat the runway surface.
summary: The crew experienced smoke and false evacuation alarms after landing on a runway treated with Sodium Formate and Potassium Acetate, likely ingested by the reversers and packs. A flight mechanic inadvertently triggered the evacuation warning while attempting to reset detectors, though no fire was found and the aircraft was safely towed to the ramp.

synopsis: BE200 Captain reported experiencing a bleed air failure during climb-out and returned to departure airport and flight landed without incident.
summary: During climb through 10,000 feet, the L Bleed Air Fail light illuminated on the aircraft. The crew executed the emergency checklist, returned to ZZZ, and landed without incident or declared emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot on short final landing at a non-towered airport reported a conflict with an opposite direction arrival which had been transmitting their runway intentions on the wrong frequency.
summary: The pilot, on short final for an RNAV approach after canceling IFR, executed a go-around due to an aircraft rapidly approaching on the opposite runway. The other pilot later apologized, explaining he had keyed the wrong frequency and mistakenly announced intentions to land on the opposite direction.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported taxiing problems by the student which resulted in striking a hanger with a wingtip.
summary: A student pilot under a CFI's supervision applied full power instead of reducing speed while taxiing, causing the right wingtip to strike a hangar door. The impact broke the wingtip lights and damaged the door, resulting in the aircraft being placed into maintenance.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported the aircraft left main landing gear left the taxiway while the aircraft was on the taxiway center line at BTR airport.
summary: The flight crew exited Runway 13 onto Taxiway Foxtrot at BTR per Tower instructions, causing the left main gear to sink into grass due to the taxiway's unsuitability for the aircraft. The crew recovered by adding power, but the incident highlighted a lack of wingspan restrictions and improper ATC routing.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported de-icing crew failure to follow procedure resulted in First Officer injury.
summary: During pre-departure de-icing of an EMB-145 at ZZZ, ground crew sprayed high-pressure Type 1 fluid directly on the First Officer's DV window, causing fluid to enter the unpressurized cockpit and spray the FO's eye. The crew returned to the gate for medical treatment, logged a maintenance discrepancy, and the FO was removed from flying status.

synopsis: A Flight Crew conducting a Visual Approach at night reported the Pilot Flying turned towards the runway prior to the Final Approach Fix and was issued a Low Altitude Alert from the Tower.
summary: The First Officer accepted a visual approach based only on the beacon, turned off flight directors, and flew too close to towers, triggering a low altitude alert. The Captain corrected the course, and the aircraft landed safely, though the crew later debated whether a go-around was necessary due to the First Officer's lack of runway visual contact.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported making a precautionary landing after loss of number three Hydraulic system.
summary: During cruise descent, the crew managed a HYD 3 quantity loss and subsequent failure by executing QRH checklists and landing with manual brakes at ZZZ. The aircraft stopped safely on Runway XX with fire services monitoring, after which maintenance towed it to the gate.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Captain reported diverting after losing cooling to both Inertial Reference Systems, which caused the failure of numerous systems.
summary: The pilot and SIC experienced an IRS 1-2 cool failure shortly after takeoff, causing automatic shutdown of all automation and attitude indicators. The crew hand-flew the aircraft through severe turbulence to divert to ZZZ4, landing safely despite losing autopilot, yaw damper, and navigation systems.

synopsis: Pilot reported on takeoff roll, a ground tug crossed the runway in use, resulted in aborted takeoff with evasive action.
summary: A pilot aborted takeoff from Runway 29R at Stockton after a tug crossed the runway without acknowledging CTAF calls. The incident was caused by the tug's failure to monitor the frequency and night conditions, resulting in a runway incursion.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a repeat failure of the Take Off Warning System and a failure of trailing edge flaps to retract caused an Air Tun Back and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a spurious takeoff configuration warning followed by a trailing edge flap disagreement on departure, prompting a return to the origin airport. They successfully landed with flaps extended to 15 degrees using the alternate system after burning fuel to reduce landing weight.

synopsis: Air Carrier ground personnel reported Hazmat cargo labeled ship on 'Cargo aircraft only' was intercepted prior to being loaded.
summary: A dock agent intercepted a shipment labeled for cargo-only aircraft before acceptance. The shipper incorrectly assumed the product could fly because the flight was a cargo operation.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported having a GPS issue resulting in a track heading deviation.
summary: The pilot experienced an unintended turn and Unable RNP alert near ZZZ VOR while on a direct clearance to ZZZ1, likely due to a GPS issue. After switching to IRS navigation and coordinating a heading with ATC, the crew continued the flight and landed normally.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a track heading deviation. Captain stated when the clearance was sent to the FMC with the new routing the FO was not aware of the LOAD FMC prompt so the new routing was never loaded.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed ZZZ on the ZZZZZ TWO flight plan but failed to load a direct routing clearance into the FMC due to the First Officer missing the LOAD prompt. The Captain admitted distraction prevented resolving the discrepancy despite initial confusion, highlighting a lapse in route check diligence.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a fume/smoke event during arrival taxi to gate.
summary: During taxi to the gate, the 4th Flight Attendant reported cabin smoke, prompting the Captain to stop and request fire services. The odor dissipated quickly, and the crew continued to the gate for evaluation, attributing the incident to poor cabin crew communication and low lighting.

synopsis: Captain reported refusing the aircraft after discovering an empty crew oxygen bottle and after reviewing the AML (Aircraft Maintenance Logbook) that the crew oxygen had been replaced 5 times in the last 30 days.
summary: A flight crew member refused an aircraft after discovering the crew oxygen bottle had emptied within five days of replacement, marking the fifth such failure in a month. The reporter attributed this to a lack of automated historical oversight in the new electronic maintenance log system, which obscured the recurring discrepancy.

synopsis: MD-11 Flight Crew reported encountering severe turbulence which resulted in evasive action for safety of flight.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecasted severe turbulence at FL350, causing autothrottle disconnection and a brief overspeed. They initiated an immediate descent to FL330 for safety, notifying Gander ATC before receiving clearance.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into LAX in trail of a B777.
summary: Pilots on a flight descending from FL320 to FL240 on the HLYWD arrival into LAX experienced an upset with autopilot disconnect due to wake turbulence from a B777 ahead. The crew recovered after ATC approved a course offset, prompting a recommendation for increased spacing and better communication regarding heavy aircraft.

synopsis: DA40 Instructor Pilot reported loss of directional control during landing roll.
summary: During a stage check practicing engine-out approaches, the instructor prevented a runway excursion after the student's left brake failed. While exiting the taxiway, strong wind caused the aircraft to skid into the grass and snow, resulting in no damage or injuries.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported receiving terrain alerts when his aircraft was unable to maintain safe altitude because of ice accumulation.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected moderate rime ice, causing altitude loss below minimum IFR levels and triggering terrain alerts despite ATC-approved altitude changes. The incident was attributed to a lack of positive icing PIREPs and specific local temperature and location conditions.

synopsis: LR-55 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after precautionary shutdown of #1 engine due to a thrust reverser unlock light illuminating in flight.
summary: During initial climb at FL280, Thrust Reverser #1 unlock light and horn activated. The crew performed a precautionary engine shutdown to prevent in-flight deployment and diverted to an alternate airport after advising ATC.

synopsis: A Helicopter pilot reported they received clearance into Class C airspace from the Tower Controller and after handoff to TRACON the TRACON Controller accused them of entering the Class C airspace without authorization.
summary: A pilot departed from an airport near Class C airspace and received a "Cleared to operate in Class Charlie" clearance from Tower, which included an initial 2,500-foot limit later raised to 3,500 feet. Despite this, Approach and TRACON later informed the pilot of a Class C violation, attributing the error to the Tower controller's improper use of clearance phraseology.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet non-flying Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on approach to ASE airport.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring deviated from an LOC E approach clearance to Aspen by descending visually without notifying ATC, triggering altitude alerts when the airport was obscured by clouds. The crew executed a missed approach, climbed, and diverted to ZZZ, attributing the incident to poor communication and unauthorized deviation.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported momentary loss of control following engine start from the right seat.
summary: A CFI trainee alone in the right seat of a training aircraft experienced an unintended forward movement during engine start after slipping off the brake pedals while leaning to crank the ignition. The pilot immediately returned the throttle to idle, re-applied brakes, taxied back to the parking spot, and canceled the flight.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported running off the end of the slick runway after landing.
summary: The pilot reported that a Cessna 210 overran the runway end by 8 feet due to extremely slick conditions not indicated in METARs or NOTAMs. After airport staff pushed the aircraft back, maintenance found no gear anomalies or prop strikes, allowing the flight to depart.

synopsis: CE560 pilot reported shutting down right engine in flight because of fuel contamination.
summary: The pilot performed a precautionary right engine shutdown due to fuel contamination.

synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported a track heading deviation after experiencing GPS jamming near SFO VOR in ZOA ARTCC airspace.
summary: Pilots reported GPS jamming and a GNSS navigation flag while flying from CORKR to SFO at 8,000 feet, causing an unintended turn off course. Controllers eventually vectored the aircraft to the airport, and post-landing inquiries regarding a potential deviation were dismissed by approach control.

synopsis: Air carrier F/O reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on approach to BUF.
summary: The pilot, on a visual approach to Runway 23, received a Low Altitude Alert after aggressively descending below the glideslope intercept altitude to accommodate a short turn. The pilot attributed the event to the clearance geometry and an overly aggressive altitude selection, subsequently climbing to intercept the glideslope.

synopsis: Captain reported a diversion to a precautionary landing following the loss of both Flight Management Computers which caused the loss of Cockpit Display Units and most navigation systems.
summary: The crew experienced recurrent dual FMC, LNAV/VNAV, and autothrottle failures en route to ZZZZ after a pre-flight MAP reset. They diverted to ZZZZ1, held to burn fuel, and landed safely while the First Officer's MAP failure persisted.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a return to gate after Dispatch told them they had an improperly signed maintenance item. The aircraft had several maintenance items that needed to be addressed before the flight due to it just coming out of long term storage.
summary: The crew of a revenue flight departing long-term storage returned to the gate after Dispatch halted taxi due to an unsigned maintenance item X. A clerical data entry error caused a discrepancy between the paper and electronic maintenance logs, requiring the aircraft to be held until the sign-off was corrected.

synopsis: Captain reported refusing the aircraft after discovering that the nose strut was leaking after service due to strut extertion not within limits.
summary: The captain and First Officer found the nose strut fully collapsed and leaking foamy fluid despite a maintenance sign-off, leading to a second inspection that confirmed a solid stream of fluid. Consequently, the aircraft was removed from service due to the unsafe condition, contradicting Maintenance Control's claim that the leak was minor.

synopsis: Captain reported aircraft failed to pressurize correctly on takeoff and after trouble shooting, elected to do an Air Turn Back.
summary: The crew of a 900ER discovered the pressurization outflow valve stuck full open during climb, causing cabin pressure bumps and ice accumulation. Unable to resolve the issue or contact Dispatch via ACARS, they returned to the departure airport for maintenance, landing safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported encountering a loss of control due to severe turbulence and wind shear on descent and approach into SEA.
summary: During approach, the crew encountered unexpected severe turbulence and wind shear that disengaged the autopilot and caused injuries to the Captain, a flight attendant, and passengers. The Pilot Flying manually controlled the aircraft through difficult handling conditions to complete a stabilized landing without exceedances.

synopsis: Captain reported aircraft departed without positive confirmation of Hazmat cargo limitation. Limitation later confirmed cargo within limitations.
summary: The Captain loaded 288kg of dry ice on Aircraft X during pre-flight, mistakenly believing the limit was 320kg instead of 320lbs due to relying on verbal confirmation rather than official documentation. The flight departed as scheduled, but the error was later identified by the Director of Safety, prompting the Captain to commit to verifying weight limits against paperwork in the future.

synopsis: A Flight Crew reported a loss of pressurization then returned to their departure airport and landed safely.
summary: During climb to 27,000 feet, the crew experienced erratic pressurization followed by rapid cabin altitude increase, triggering master warnings and requiring oxygen masks. They descended to 6,000 feet and returned to the departure airport without declaring an emergency, landing safely.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported a Class B airspace violation and cited ATC communication issues and the co-pilot's lack of recent flying as contributing factors.
summary: The Captain and crew of a return flight from ZZZ1 to ZZZ2 possibly penetrated Class B airspace while descending to 1,400 feet MSL due to frequency congestion preventing clearance receipt. Contributing factors included false anticipation of clearance, high ground speed from tailwinds, and the pilot's reduced recent experience.

synopsis: DJI Mavic 2 Zoom drone pilot reported flying a mission without having the proper LAANC authorization.
summary: A drone pilot operating a DJI Mavic Zoom during a mission assumed the Kittyhawk app automatically generated a LAANC authorization. The pilot realized post-flight that no authorization was created due to this incorrect assumption and plans to verify codes before future operations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported after turning onto final at a non towered airport they were temporarily blinded by direct sunlight and had a NMAC with opposite direction traffic.
summary: A pilot entering the traffic pattern turned final into a setting sun, causing temporary blindness and loss of visual contact with the runway. The pilot executed an evasive maneuver to avoid another aircraft 200 feet away, performed a VFR go-around, and landed safely after re-entering the pattern.

synopsis: C208 Captain reported encountering mountain wave action which resulted in momentary loss of control and altitude excursion.
summary: A pilot flying direct ELKES at 14,000 feet encountered a severe mountain wave near Mt Jefferson, causing uncontrolled altitude loss and airspeed decay to 75 KIAS. ATC issued a lower clearance to 13,000 feet and vectors away from terrain, allowing the pilot to stabilize at 12,000 feet after exiting the wave.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilots reported severe turbulence encountered and a Flight Attendant injured.
summary: During cruise at FL390, severe turbulence near a thunderstorm caused a 600-foot altitude loss and activated stick shaker and high-speed warnings twice. The Captain regained control, but Flight Attendant 2 was injured and required hospitalization after the flight continued to the destination.

synopsis: A-321 Captain reported a communications breakdown between flight crew and Dispatch regarding the correct amount of Hazmat cargo on the NOTOC. Hazmat cargo discrepancy corrected after aircraft departure.
summary: The Captain and a ramp loader experienced a Dangerous Goods documentation error regarding Dry Ice location and weight during taxi and takeoff roll. The incident resulted from a communication disconnect between base operations, loaders, and planning, prompting a recommendation to automate Hazardous Goods communication.

synopsis: Medical transport helicopter pilot reported inadvertent IMC caused unforecast mountain obscuration.
summary: A pilot and crew encountered inadvertent IMC while returning to base in a helicopter due to unforecasted haze and lack of moonlight. They recovered by climbing to 9,000 ft and turning left based on crew visibility reports, landing safely without further incident.

synopsis: SA-227 Captain reported a diversion due to smoke in the aft cabin during cruise.
summary: The Captain detected smoke in the aft cabin of Aircraft X during cruise at 13,000 ft, prompting an immediate descent to 10,000 ft and shutdown of the bleeds. The smoke cleared, allowing a safe diversion and landing at ZZZ2, with the Captain suspecting a fault in the bleeds or packs.

synopsis: EMB-XRJ Captain reported running QRH procedure of number 2 ACM failure.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a bleed 1 leak warning while cruising at FL250 with an MEL on pack 2, prompting an immediate descent to 10,000 ft. The crew unnecessarily dumped cabin pressure and later activated the APU to cool the cabin, resulting in a normal landing after the Captain acknowledged these deviations from the checklist were incorrect.

synopsis: C-208 Captain reported a burning odor during initial climb resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a strong burning smell shortly after departure with inoperative bleed air and thermostat controls. The pilot returned to ZZZ for priority handling and fire inspection, but ground crews found no evidence of fire or burning.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an NMAC with a drone during departure from SEA airport.
summary: During departure from SEA on the SUMMA 2 route, the crew spotted a drone near 6,000 feet despite ATC warnings but received no specific avoidance vectors. The pilot reported a near miss with insufficient time to maneuver, noting that a simple vector could have prevented the potential collision hazard.

synopsis: Captain reported an uneventful diversion due to reported fumes of smoke in passenger cabin.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X reported smoke and heat from the left lighting valance and PSUs during climb to 32,000 ft., prompting a return to ZZZ. After executing the smoke procedure and landing with ARFF standby, ground crews found no heat source, and passengers deplaned without incident.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported passengers were boarded before the pilots arrived at the aircraft. No air conditioning was available and passengers began removing their face masks.
summary: A flight attendant reported that during boarding of a nearly full aircraft, a lack of air conditioning caused passenger distress and mask removal for over an hour. Pilots eventually arrived, restored airflow, and departed, though the crew deemed the initial boarding unsafe and recommended deplaning passengers if airflow is not promptly provided.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported enterring Class B airspace during a climb required to resolve an airborne conflict.
summary: A pilot departing Manassas Runway 34R reported a light sport aircraft 100 feet below and traffic above while climbing into the 2,500-foot Class Bravo ring. The pilot attributed the conflict to constrained departure paths and potential Tower unawareness of the traffic under the aircraft.

synopsis: Learjet First Officer reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC after descending early on a cleared instrument approach.
summary: The pilot flying and monitoring pilot on a ZZZ to ASE flight lost visual contact with the airport due to clouds while descending for a LOC DME E approach, triggering ATC altitude alerts. The crew executed a missed approach and diverted to ZZZ1, attributing the incident to communication breakdowns with ATC and CRM issues regarding the visual approach.

synopsis: Twin Engine Jet Pilot reported a NMAC with a helicopter during takeoff.
summary: The pilot flying a fixed-wing aircraft on takeoff from Rwy XL encountered a helicopter crossing the runway at 200 feet AGL after the helicopter failed to acknowledge ATC instructions to remain north. The pilot executed an evasive left maneuver and reduced climb rate to avoid a collision, continuing the takeoff past V1 as an abort was not an option.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Citation First Officer reported a delayed initial turn on the SID which resulted in a ground proximity warning.
summary: During a Part 135 charter departure from EGE on the BEEVR2 SID, the First Officer warned the Captain that the FMS lacked the initial 206-degree turn, but the Captain dismissed the concern. This caused a GPWS "Pull Up" warning, after which the Captain disconnected the autopilot and flew direct to the first fix instead of following the required heading.

synopsis: A student pilot reported losing control of the aircraft, during takeoff roll, which veered off the runway.
summary: A solo pilot exited the runway left during takeoff before rotation, striking two construction berms that damaged the nose and left gear. Emergency procedures were completed, and the pilot evacuated with no injuries reported.

synopsis: C-172 instructor reported aircraft electrical failure during a training flight.
summary: During a VFR training flight, the pilot and student experienced fluctuating then total electrical failure, losing radios, transponder, and instruments. They diverted to ZZZ1 and landed safely without incident, later contacting Approach to report their status.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported flying without proper certification.
summary: A pilot inadvertently conducted two flights after their Biennial Flight Review expired because they mistakenly believed an Instructor Proficiency Check on Date 2 was a valid review. Upon discovering the error, the pilot immediately scheduled a new review and implemented electronic calendar reminders to prevent recurrence.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A single pilot reported a Near Mid-Air Collision (NMAC) with another aircraft entering the landing pattern. Sun position reportedly inhibited early visual contact.
summary: A Mooney pilot and a Cessna flight instructor experienced a near-midair conflict while both maneuvering for a 45-degree entry to Runway XX at ZZZ. The reporter attributed the incident to sun glare and potential simultaneous radio transmissions that caused missed position reports.

synopsis: C-152 pilot reported a nose-wheel problem on landing roll-out.
summary: The pilot landed at ZZZ and experienced nose wheel shaking and loss of control seconds after touchdown. The aircraft was stopped on Runway XXR, towed to the FPO, and found to have no other damage.

synopsis: Aircraft reported that another aircraft entered the traffic pattern incorrectly, creating a conflict.
summary: A student pilot and instructor on a crosswind leg at 33N reported that Aircraft Y entered the left traffic pattern incorrectly and flew dangerously close during a turn to downwind. The reporter stated Aircraft Y's unsafe maneuver created a collision hazard for their aircraft and others in the pattern.

synopsis: A Bonanza 35 Pilot reported engine power loss on initial departure climb and later identified an issue with the fuel pump.
summary: The pilot reported a backfire and power fluctuation shortly after departing Runway XX at ZZZ in an aircraft with a JPI930 engine. The event was attributed to a suspected failed engine-driven fuel pump, which was sent for overhaul after the pilot returned to land safely.

synopsis: Pilot of an amateur-built aircraft reported a windshear-caused ground loop on landing rollout.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway bump and severe wind shear while landing Runway XX in ZZZ, causing a loss of directional control. The aircraft ground looped to the right approximately midfield, but no injuries were sustained.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported performing a go-around on short final due to a business jet landing in the opposite direction following an RNAV approach.
summary: A pilot on short final for Runway 14 executed a go-around after a jet landed straight in on Runway 32 without CTAF calls. The jet likely used an RNAV 32 approach, resulting in a landing with over 10 knots of tailwind despite favorable winds for Runway 14.

synopsis: Tower Controllers reported a flight of two helicopters departed from the ramp without clearance from the tower and had a NMAC with a departing aircraft because Ground Control mistakenly issued them a TRACON frequency which cleared them to depart thinking they were at an adjacent airport.
summary: Two military helicopters (Aircraft X) departed a non-controlled ramp without Local Control clearance after mistakenly contacting TRACON, nearly colliding with a Cessna (Aircraft Y) in the pattern. The near-miss resulted from the helicopters' failure to readback instructions and TRACON's incorrect assumption of their location.

synopsis: ATC approach controller reported issuing a go-around clearance to an aircraft on short final due to a vehicle reported on the runway.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a go-around to Aircraft X on the ILS Runway 31C approach after an airport vehicle entered the runway. The pilot complied with the climb and turn instructions, and the aircraft landed safely on a subsequent approach despite poor visibility from snow.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported re-occurring airborne conflicts between VFR aircraft executing aerobatic maneuvers and IFR arrivals into PSP. Reporter advised they deal with these types of situations every day, which could be easily avoided by having non-voluntary protected airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft Y performed aerobatics between 5,000 and 6,000 feet near V137, climbing directly in front of Aircraft X on an RNAV visual approach. This caused Aircraft X to receive two resolution advisories and prompted the controller to request expanded Class C or B airspace to prevent future conflicts.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ATC Instructor and trainee reported misidentified aircraft in traffic pattern resulted in NMAC.
summary: A VFR pilot on a check ride and another VFR pilot on Local Control training experienced a loss of separation while sequencing for Runway XX. The second pilot misidentified traffic and cut off the first, forcing both to maneuver to avoid a collision before landing safely.

synopsis: AFW Tower Controller reported an unsafe event where a VFR aircraft is transitioning an arrival path for air carriers outside of Class Delta causing an airborne conflict.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic advisories to an arriving aircraft regarding a non-communicating VFR aircraft near WIGZU, resulting in a CA alarm and a sharp turn by the VFR pilot. The controller recommends adding a shelf or key to AFW Class Delta to address frequent altitude conflicts with uncommunicating VFR traffic.

aircraft: Beechcraft / Beech Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: SoCal TRACON Controller reported an unsafe situation with VFR aircraft and IFR aircraft within close proximity to each other just outside the PSP Class Delta/TRSA.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Springs sector observed a high-performance aircraft performing unpredictable aerobatic maneuvers near UDD and PSP, flying close to a regional jet on visual approach. The controller attributed the safety risk to voluntary TRSA participation and the lack of mandatory controlled airspace, which complicates sequencing and separation.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported communication issues with pilots due to having to wear a mask which is exacerbated when new procedural changes are introduced.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X reported unsafe IFR operations at ZZZ due to new altitude restrictions and mask mandates causing communication errors. The reporter attributed these risks to management's rigid rules and poor judgment, warning they could lead to a major incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Controllers reported an aircraft that they were not talking to was on an IFR flight plan, below the MVA and NORDO.
summary: An OJTI trainee accepted a handoff of Aircraft X, which was 500 feet below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude and uncoordinated with ZZZ1, while the OS could not monitor altitude due to scope limitations. The aircraft eventually contacted approach and landed safely, though the incident highlighted MVA discrepancies and communication gaps.

synopsis: Center Controller reported communication issues with pilots while wearing a face mask.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that mandatory mask-wearing caused multiple aircraft to request repeated transmissions due to poor audio clarity. The controller stated this communication barrier creates a safety risk where pilots might misunderstand altitude instructions.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Center Controller reported multiple read back errors while wearing a mandated face mask.
summary: An air traffic controller reported multiple readback errors, including Aircraft X misreading restrictions and frequency, while wearing a mask alone on position. The controller attributed the errors to the mask and recommended that controllers not be required to wear them when no one is in close proximity.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A tower local Controller reported they allowed a military aircraft to land with another aircraft stopped at an intersection on the runway.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X for a LAHSO landing while managing departures and an instrument approach for Aircraft Y. Due to expectation bias and visual difficulty, the controller overlooked Aircraft X holding at an intersection, causing Aircraft Y to stop short to avoid a collision.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A TRACON Controller in training reported vectoring an aircraft in strong winds that delayed its turns, resulting in the aircraft flying below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for an ILS approach in strong winds, issuing a safety alert after the pilot's delayed responses caused the aircraft to descend below the 1500 ft MVA into the 2100 ft MVA. The controller directed a climb to 2100 ft and a heading change, resulting in a safe landing despite the pilot's significant response delays.

synopsis: ZME Controller reported MSAW alert failure contributed to improperly issuing an IFR clearance to aircraft below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to 030 from CGI, inadvertently violating the 035 minimum altitude due to towers. The controller missed the error because the Minimum Safe Altitude Warning system failed to alert, though the aircraft safely passed the obstruction after another controller questioned the altitude.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported having to repeat multiple transmissions due to clarity issues while having to wear a face mask.
summary: An air traffic controller removed their mask to improve transmission clarity after pilots repeatedly requested repeats, but an Operations Manager forced them to re-wear it, causing distraction and a missed transmission. The controller reported that this distraction led to another pilot request for a repeat and recommended allowing controllers discretion to work without masks for safety.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft descended below their assigned altitude and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller issued low altitude alerts when an aircraft descended below its cleared 13,000-foot approach altitude and missed approach crossing altitude. The aircraft continued descending below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude despite instructions to climb, resulting in a reported pilot deviation.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported communication problems with an aircraft while the facility was being cleaned/disinfected.
summary: An air traffic controller, distracted by cleaning staff, issued an RNAV Runway XY clearance while the pilot requested Runway ZA. The pilot's incorrect readback and expectation bias led to a wrong approach path, which the controller detected and corrected via vectors with no safety risk.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A Center Controller reported another Center Controller handed them off an aircraft flying below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller noticed Aircraft X level at 3,000 feet within a 3,500-foot minimum IFR altitude area where the MSAW alarm failed to trigger. The controller alerted the controller ZME, who confirmed the altitude error, and the MSAW alarm activated only after their conversation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an airspace violation and cited not being sure if another sector was open or not open as a contributing factor.
summary: A trainee air traffic controller in ZZZ1 failed to transfer a non-radar SFRA aircraft to ZZZ3 approach because they forgot the airspace was open. The controller reported no conflicting traffic occurred but attributed the error to a lack of memory aids and low currentcy on the position.

synopsis: F11 Controller reported an unsafe scenario with two aircraft that were in a conflict due to a STAR and a VFR practice area being in close proximity.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X on the OMN STAR to SFB received a TCAS RA after an untagged VFR practice aircraft made a hard left turn and rapid descent. The controller attributed the conflict to the dangerous overlap of the STAR with a VFR practice area and radar identification issues caused by the practice aircraft's filed IFR flight plan.

synopsis: Tower Controller in Charge reported they observed a helicopter deviate from its assigned route and did not climb in accordance with SID climb requirements and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft X departing IFR and drifting northwest toward terrain while climbing from 800 to 900 feet. The controller attributed the unsafe proximity to the pilot failing to maintain the required climb gradient and deviating from the instruction to remain north of the runway.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported a taxiway incursion due to the aircraft flight crew not following clearance instructions.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X incorrectly joined Taxiway A instead of the assigned Taxiway B after landing, likely due to expectation bias from preceding aircraft or confusion with taxiway lights. The crew later self-corrected to the proper route without causing operational harm.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported a conflict between an IFR arrival and a high speed highly maneuverable aircraft just clear of the PSP Class Delta/TRSA.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a conflict between Aircraft X on a visual approach to PSP and Aircraft Y, a local VFR jet, due to a lack of tower coordination and the pilot's refusal to communicate. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to the voluntary TRSA airspace design, which allows high-speed, uncoordinated VFR traffic to disrupt IFR arrivals.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot and a Tower Controller reported the pilot flew to the wrong airport. The pilot reported the error was likely due to the pilot's GPS giving false indications or being jammed.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X with a GNS 430W GPS entered the wrong airport airspace due to erroneous GPS data and poor communications, causing erratic maneuvers that required six other aircraft to adjust paths. The pilot eventually landed safely after ATC intervention, attributing the incident to potential GPS jamming and communication difficulties.

synopsis: ATC Controllers reported an airport vehicle did not hold short of the runway for landing traffic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller instructed an Airport Vehicle to hold short of Runway XZC while operating on closed Runway XYR, but the vehicle crossed the runway edge. The Controller issued a go-around for Aircraft X on final approach, and the vehicle reversed and exited the active runway.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported safety related issues with having to wear face masks while on position.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that mandatory mask usage during complex IFR operations caused fogged glasses, breathing difficulties, communication errors, and distractions. These issues led to safety concerns including wrong arrival clearances and altitude deviations, prompting the facility to implement six-foot spacing between positions.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the First Officer (PM) read back the wrong clearance to ATC during departure causing confusion. The First Officer cited lack of flying contributed to the event.
summary: The First Officer, acting as Pilot Flying on the first leg of an OE trip, erroneously reported climbing via the ZZZZZ 3 RNAV SID to Departure Control instead of the assigned heading 100 and 4,000 feet. ATC clarified the error and issued a new clearance to turn left heading 070 and climb to 16,000 feet.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a track deviation due to the First Officer's confusion with the FMC. Reportedly, the First Officer has changed aircraft during the pandemic several times which may have contributed to the event.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported that the First Officer incorrectly executed a secondary flight plan and misinterpreted the FMA during the ZZZZZ arrival, causing a course deviation. The PM reprogrammed the flight computer to rejoin the route, and the flight completed safely after the FO received a post-flight briefing on crew coordination and system interpretation.

synopsis: Air Carrier Lead Ground personnel and load crew reported recurring issue of late planeside arrival of Hazmat cargo which results in departure delays, cargo weight and cargo handling errors.
summary: Ramp cargo personnel missed loading 1,155 pounds of cargo, including human tissue, on Aircraft X departing ZZZ due to late cart delivery. Gate control discovered the error after takeoff, resulting in a 0.82% weight adjustment and a 1.5% shift in the center of gravity.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported Cargo Department accepted a cargo shipment which contained a full oxygen cylinder.
summary: Ground personnel discovered an undeclared, pressurized emergency oxygen cylinder attached to an ejection seat during a physical search of two wheeled crates. The cylinder was not listed on the submitted shipping documents despite being identified as a hazardous item.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported aircraft cargo equipment malfunctioned during preflight loading.
summary: A ground handler reported that a heavy DG create loaded with a wood stand caused the power stow to stop during loading at ZZZ1. While clearance was adequate on the right side, the handler was unaware of the specific issue on the left side that contributed to the equipment failure.

synopsis: Captain reported no positive rate of climb at lift off and elected to set the aircraft back down on the runway and reject the takeoff.
summary: During takeoff rotation, both pilots experienced unresponsive elevators and a loss of lift, preventing a positive climb rate. The crew executed a rejected takeoff, landing safely on the remaining runway with no injuries before maintenance inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the First Officer advanced thrust levers to TOGA without releasing the parking brake.
summary: The First Officer advanced thrust levers to TOGA without releasing the parking brake while lining up, prompting the Pilot Flying to reject the takeoff. The reporter attributed the incident to a communication failure and the First Officer's lack of recent flight experience.

synopsis: B737 MAX pilot reported speed deviations during autopilot-controlled descent.
summary: A 737MAX pilot reported an uncommanded acceleration to Mach .83 during a VNAV descent from FL390, triggering the overspeed warning. The pilot disconnected the autopilot to recover, attributing the event to the aircraft prioritizing glide path over airspeed limits, though the specific cause remains unknown.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported intermittent loss of yellow hydraulic system and yaw damper.
summary: The crew experienced an intermittent Yellow hydraulic pump failure and yaw damper loss on initial climb, causing pressure to fluctuate between zero and 3000 psi. Due to prior system issues and a deferred maintenance item, they elected to return to ZZZ without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Embraer first officer reported altitude and heading deviations caused by unanticipated turbulence.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence in IMC at FL350, causing momentary loss of control with 30-degree course and 500-foot altitude deviations. The pilot attributed the event to entering unseen convective tops and suggested better preflight weather briefings and communication could have helped.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported loss of CPC2 [Cabin Pressure Controller] caused a descent and subsequent maintenance action, resulting in a plane swap at destination airport.
summary: The crew experienced an Auto Press 2 failure at 33,000 ft causing a differential pressure warning, prompting a descent to 24,000 ft where Auto Press 1 took over. Although maintenance deferred the controller, subsequent troubleshooting failed to resolve the issue, resulting in an aircraft swap.

synopsis: C550 First Officer reported a dynamic fuel quantity indication resulting in Maximum Take Off Fuel quantity exceedance.
summary: During a weight-restricted departure from ZZZ, the crew burned fuel to meet limits, but total fuel and center tank quantities increased during acceleration and climb. The Captain hypothesized this was caused by fuel movement or vent system issues, resulting in erroneous quantity indications exceeding the takeoff limit.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported the total loss of left hand hydraulic system fluid quantity, resulting in an air turn back and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: The flight crew continued takeoff after a low left hydraulic quantity warning at 120 KIAS, but suffered total system loss shortly after rotation due to a failed spoiler POV valve. They returned to ZZZ for a safe landing, where maintenance confirmed the valve failure caused fluid leakage over the left wing.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concern for passenger health regarding the face mask policy when the aircraft is on the ground with little or no air circulation and the cabin is hot.
summary: A Flight Attendant reported extreme heat and breathing difficulties during boarding and pre-flight while wearing a mandatory mask. The reporter attributed the safety concern to the combination of stifling cabin temperatures and FAA mask mandates that prevented crew and passengers from removing masks despite heat exhaustion risks.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concern regarding the face mask policy as it covers a passenger's identity and creates a possible way to hide unwanted items under the mask.
summary: A flight attendant reported a passenger in seat X1 continued talking on a phone hidden inside a mask during a cabin sweep. The crew member stated that mandatory mask mandates hinder safety monitoring by obscuring visual cues and preventing the detection of potential threats or hazards.

synopsis: PA--28 Flight Instructor reported an emergency air return immediately after takeoff due to Carbon Monoxide poisoning resulting in a taxiway landing.
summary: A pilot and student in a PA-28 experienced carbon monoxide poisoning during takeoff due to an undetected exhaust crack. The pilot executed an emergency landing on a taxiway after suffering symptoms and receiving a 250 ppm sensor reading, avoiding a runway landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Single Private Pilot reported a NMAC at this location during final approach.
summary: The pilot reported a near-collision on final approach to Runway 29 at AWO with an aircraft landing on Runway 34 without lights or ADS-B. The pilot climbed 100 feet to avoid the collision, attributing the incident to the other pilot's failure to monitor the radio or acknowledge the runway change.

synopsis: GA pilot reported the ATC Controller was busy, rushed and hard to understand possibly due to speaking through a face mask and the facility being short staffed.
summary: The pilot reported a VFR flight following error where they initially told ZZZ1 they were climbing to 4,500 feet instead of the cleared 5,500 feet. Radio congestion and distorted communications prevented the pilot from correcting this mistake before ATC issued traffic avoidance turns for an IFR aircraft at 5,000 feet.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: GA pilot reported thinking the Tower was closed, started to taxi to the runway and was stopped by an airport vehicle who pointed to the radios. The pilot contacted the Tower before takeoff.
summary: Two pilots in a new aircraft at ZZZ failed to contact ATC due to misinterpreting UTC opening times as local closing times on the ATIS and NOTAMs. An airport vehicle intercepted them during taxi, prompting a radio switch that restored communications before takeoff.

synopsis: Private Pilot reported loss of control during a taxi test due to a wind gust.
summary: During a taxi test, a pilot experienced a sudden wind gust exceeding 22 knots that caused a stall and a hard landing on the runway side. The incident resulted in no injuries but triggered the ELT, which the pilot subsequently deactivated after confirming safety with witnesses and ATC.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported an VHF radio dead zone.
summary: The flight crew encountered turbulence at 39,000 feet and requested a descent to 30,000 feet, later asking to stop at 36,000 feet. Due to an 180-mile VHF dead zone, initial requests were not heard, causing a communication delay with ATC before the crew was cleared to 36,000 feet.

synopsis: B-737-800 Captain reported an uneventful 'go around' due to a CFIT event during final approach.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer experienced a glide slope deviation during a visual approach to RWY XX at ZZZ. The First Officer incorrectly set a lower MCP altitude without verbal coordination, causing the aircraft to drop below the final approach fix altitude and necessitating a go-around.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported turning the wrong way on a taxiway at night and when turning around exited the taxiway surface due to poor taxiway lighting and markings at LGA airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain of a jet taxiing at night at LGA turned right instead of left on Taxiway Golf due to poor lighting and disorientation. They likely left the paved surface, resulting in a flat nose tire and dirt on the gear, attributed to inadequate taxiway illumination and crew fatigue.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew reported taxiing the wrong direction which resulted in a runway incursion.
summary: The flight crew experienced a runway incursion on Runway 33 while taxiing to Runway 28 after accepting a late runway change due to high winds. The Captain mistakenly followed the original clearance instead of the new instruction to turn onto Taxiway Mike, compounded by the First Officer's distraction with FMS updates and poor chart monitoring in blowing snow.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported severe turbulence encounter during cruise and ATC communication problem that resulted in altitude excursion, track deviation and conflict with other aircraft.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence while deviating from weather at FL350, causing automation disconnects, a 500-foot altitude deviation, and a TCAS alert. The Captain manually maneuvered to avoid a nearby aircraft and regain control, resulting in no injuries despite high workload and frequency congestion.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported being distracted by a disruptive passenger and forgetting to advise the flight crew the cabin was secure and they were ready to depart.
summary: During pre-flight, the First Officer and Flight Attendant Y failed to verbally confirm cabin secure while managing a disruptive passenger, leading the Captain to open the flight deck door. The crew attributed the error to miscommunication caused by the passenger and confusion over the flight deck door being closed for warmth.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported a Near Mid Air Collision while on approach to landing.
summary: A Cessna 150 instructor and student experienced a near mid-air collision with a Mooney while approaching the traffic pattern. The incident occurred because the instructor relied on right-of-way rules and failed to maneuver despite similar position reports, resulting in less than 200 feet of vertical and lateral separation.

synopsis: Pilot reported a Near Mid Air Collision during departure.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X departed Runway XX at ZZZ Airport while Aircraft Y was on downwind, resulting in Aircraft X crossing beneath Aircraft Y. The reporter attributed the near-miss to misjudging Aircraft Y's position based on its radio call to change to downwind.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported having to repeat transmissions to pilots because they could not understand the instructions, due to reporter wearing a face mask.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a pilot failed to understand instructions due to the controller wearing a mask. The controller stated that the mask mandate is unsafe for air traffic control operations and unnecessary given social distancing measures.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported wearing an FAA mandated face mask is fogging up the Controller's glasses. Reporter cannot remove glasses due to FAA Physical requirements.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that FAA-mandated masks cause their glasses to fog up, rendering vision impaired and effectively voiding their medical certificate while on position. The controller requested permission to remove masks on position to resolve this safety issue.

synopsis: First Officer reported an air turn back after smoke was detected during climb out.
summary: During climb out at 7,000 feet, the pilot encountered cockpit smoke, suspected an electrical issue in the Captain's circuit breakers, and returned to the field. The crew performed an emergency evacuation upon landing, where they were met by rescue staff without incident.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported that the First officer's airspeed and altitude indications became unreliable in cruise, along with both of the Engine Electronic Controls switching to Alternate and elected to have ATC assist with descent and approach.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent IAS and ALT disagrees causing an autopilot disconnect and EECs switching to ALT mode during descent. The First Officer executed the QRH while the Captain flew the aircraft to an uneventful landing after informing ATC of the inability to accept speed restrictions.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a Go Around after the Trailing Edge Flaps did not extend due to flap assymetry.
summary: Pilots on final approach for Runway XXR at 170 knots received a TE Flap Disagree EICAS message with flaps between 20 and 25 degrees. They executed a go-around at 137 knots, completed the QRH, and landed uneventfully on Runway XXC in the abnormal configuration with emergency vehicles present.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported MD-11 Flight Crew performed a precautionary landing after the number 10 main wheel brake showed high temperature.
summary: The crew reported a high temperature on brake #10, which cooled after lowering the gear. They advised ATC to have trucks standing by for potential fire, and the jet landed with no event.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported that B757 Flight Crew executed a missed approach due to a Slat Disagree message.
summary: The flight crew executed a missed approach on Aircraft X due to a mechanical flap issue. They advised ATC of the problem and requested Runway XX, with no ACARS message initially sent.

synopsis: PA-23 Pilot reported a main gear failure and runway excursion on landing.
summary: A private pilot and instructor in a multi-engine aircraft experienced a nose gear collapse during a full-stop landing on a non-active runway after the nose gear indicator light failed. The aircraft veered right due to limited directional control, requiring left brake application, which resulted in the gear collapsing and right propeller damage despite visual confirmation of gear extension.

synopsis: PA23 Flight Instructor reported a nose gear collapse and runway excursion on landing.
summary: During a multi-engine training session, the instructor and student experienced a nose gear collapse and right engine damage after repeated gear cycles and touch-and-go landings. Post-incident inspection revealed the nose wheel was turned past stops, causing excessive side loads that bent the hydraulic actuator and cracked the drag link assembly.

synopsis: J3 Instructor reported that contaminated fuel resulted in a loss of engine power followed by a forced landing.
summary: A student and instructor in a Piper J3 experienced a complete power loss during training due to lead particles clogging the carburetor jet. They executed a successful forced landing with no injuries, later discovering the contamination originated from the fuel system despite prior inspections.

synopsis: Instructor reported executing a go-around from after an airborne conflict with an aircraft that had cleared to land number two.
summary: A student pilot conducting a Private license check on left base executed a go-around after a Yak aircraft on right base climbed above them during the final approach. The Yak pilot, who was cleared to land, reported never seeing the student's aircraft.

synopsis: Pilot reported a Near Mid Air Collision during final approach.
summary: A pilot inbound to ZZZ observed a Navy helicopter on a practice ILS approach and a Cirrus taking off on intersecting runways. The helicopter avoided a collision by hovering before the intersection, likely caused by the Cirrus pilot misinterpreting the helicopter's ILS radio calls as indicating greater distance.

synopsis: An instructor pilot returning to land reported numerous powered parachutes fly in the vicinity of this airport causing conflictions with aircraft arriving and departing the VFR pattern.
summary: A student pilot training at 7F3 encountered approximately 12 radio-equipped powered parachutes interfering with approaches and downwind legs at various altitudes. The pilot aborted a simulated engine-out landing and switched to a non-standard right pattern to avoid the slow, hard-to-see aircraft, deeming the airport unsafe for training.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an aircraft experiencing radio difficulties did not respond to ATC instructions and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller lost radio contact with a pilot climbing at 2,000 feet, causing the aircraft to enter a 3,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude area. The pilot eventually reported a radio equipment failure, received climb instructions via another aircraft, and returned safely to the departure airport.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a passenger's overheated cell phone caused a small carpet area burn. Flight continued uneventfully after extinguishing smoldering carpet and cell phone placed in a thermal containment bag.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew responded to a cabin fire report caused by an overheated cell phone battery burning the carpet. The smoldering carpet was extinguished, the battery was cooled and contained, and the flight continued to ZZZ1 without further incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported loss of Hydraulic system fluid and hydraulic pumps that resulted in a diversion.
summary: During climb from ZZZ, the crew experienced a total loss of Hydraulic System A pressure, prompting a diversion to ZZZ1. Following landing, alternate nosewheel steering failed and System B quantity dropped to 47%, requiring the aircraft to be towed to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not making a crossing restriction during arrival.
summary: During the ZZZZZX arrival, the First Officer prematurely descended to 11,000 feet before reaching ZZZZZ2 while the Captain was distracted by ATC speed deletions and a new ATIS. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to poor situational awareness on their first flight in three months.

synopsis: Heavy aircraft flight crew reported a landing gear malfunction that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: Following a block turn for a hydraulic leak, maintenance replaced a gear valve but failed to bleed the system, leaving air that inhibited gear retraction on the next leg. The crew declared priority handling, landed safely, and maintenance later confirmed the fault was caused by air-entrained fluid from the incomplete bleed procedure.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported that a hydraulic system failure resulted in a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew experienced a left hydraulic system leak and pressure loss while deploying spoilers during descent at 11,000 ft. They executed an extended approach, landed safely on Runway XY, and were towed to the gate after maintenance identified a failed O-ring as the cause.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a high speed rejected take off and returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff on Runway XX after a "R 14TH STAGE DUCT" Master Warning appeared just before V1, resulting in a high-speed abort that exceeded V1. The aircraft returned to the gate after brake cooling and tire inspections, with the reporter citing the unexpected failure and delayed abort initiation as key factors.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Ground Observer reported a possible Near Mid Air Collision the FAA and reporting Pilot provided details of incidents.
summary: The pilot reported two events at uncontrolled airport ZZZ: a spacing 360-degree turn during a 45-degree entry to avoid a Diamond aircraft, and a close encounter with a glider on a parallel runway during final approach. The pilot attributed the risks to high traffic density, lack of glider radio calls, and the airport's complex environment.

synopsis: Student pilot reported a hard landing which severed the left main gear, requiring an emergency landing.
summary: A student pilot performing a solo cross-country return to ZZZ experienced a hard landing on the left main gear due to a crosswind gust, causing the gear to detach. The pilot subsequently executed an emergency belly landing off the runway under CFI guidance, exiting safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported confusion over airport layout and entered an active runway with landing traffic, causing critical ground conflict.
summary: The pilot bounced during a night landing on Runway XX, received conflicting taxi instructions while on the active runway, and inadvertently crossed Runway XX while accelerating to avoid another aircraft. The incident was caused by landing long, loss of situational awareness, and receiving taxi clearances during the landing phase.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC on short final with an aircraft landing on the parallel runway.
summary: A commercial student pilot and instructor on approach to ZZZ experienced a 200-foot vertical separation when another aircraft, mistakenly cleared for the right runway, passed directly underneath them. The other crew corrected to the left runway after the near-miss, and both aircraft landed without incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot on short final at a non towered airport reported they ordered a go around when they observed a truck entering the runway
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a training aircraft executed a timely go-around at 100 feet on short final to avoid a truck entering the active runway. The incident occurred because the hangar tenant crossed without radio communication or monitoring airport traffic.

aircraft: G2 Heritage (Glasair II) / G3 Heritage (Glasair III)
synopsis: A pilot reported while conducting a high speed taxi for a maintenance check they accidentally became airborne and experienced a rough running engine. The pilot landed off the runway in the grass and but able to taxi back onto the runway.
summary: A pilot evaluating an aircraft unintentionally lifted off during a high-speed taxi run-up. The engine ran rough, prompting a teardrop pattern and a grass median landing with no damage to the aircraft or airport property.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine roughness and power loss, causing a diversion and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: During an oil and gas patrol at 4,000 feet, the pilot experienced rough engine running and declared an emergency. The pilot diverted to ZZZ2, following a pipeline and interstate to land safely after gaining 700 feet of altitude.

synopsis: Mechanic reported that a severely frayed control cable was discovered during a routine inspection of a Cessna 400 aircraft.
summary: During a Phase 2/3/D inspection of a Cessna 441, mechanics found the right elevator cable severely frayed with only two strands remaining under a pulley in the aft cabin. The cable was replaced after being identified as a critical fatigue failure, with no other frayed cables detected.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported numerous issues while working traffic and problems associated with the workload and staffing.
summary: An air traffic controller, fatigued by poor staffing and long shifts, accidentally dropped the radar track of an IFR aircraft while managing multiple VFR requests. This error caused a loss of separation with a converging aircraft, requiring the controller to manually re-establish the track and clear the flight for a visual approach.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported new RNAV SID and STAR procedures at their facility do not provide procedural separation between arrivals and departures.
summary: A pilot reported a three-mile separation loss between Aircraft X on the JOHKR SID and Aircraft Y on the RNDRZ STAR due to an unpermitted flyby maneuver. The reporter attributed the issue to flawed Metroplex procedure design and unresponsive oversight personnel.

synopsis: EUG TRACON Controller reported an unidentified VFR aircraft climbed into confliction with an Air Carrier on an RNAV Approach causing the Air carrier to respond to a TCAS/RA. The reporter states this is a recurring traffic situation in their airspace
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X experienced a TCAS RA while on the RNAV 32 Approach due to an unidentified VFR aircraft climbing and turning toward it. The controller vectored the aircraft for a safe ILS 14 landing and attributed the conflict to the approach's path over an uncontrolled airport and mountainous terrain.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: CNO Tower Controller reported a pilot was confused by their taxi instructions and taxied past the hold short lines before the Controller could stop them causing an aircraft on short final to go-around. The reporter states new taxiway markings are routinely confusing the pilots.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued taxi instructions to Aircraft X between parallel runways, but the pilot hesitated and nearly entered Runway 21 due to confusion from a new yellow taxi line. The controller intervened with plain language instructions, stopping the aircraft before the runway edge and diverting an approaching aircraft on final approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runaway stabilizer trim system and elected to air turn back and make a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced an uncommanded high-speed nose-up stabilizer trim runaway at 300 ft AGL during takeoff from ZZZ, which resumed in slow-speed mode at 1,200 ft AGL after flap retraction. The crew stopped the runaway using forward yoke pressure and the electrical trim switch, then returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing after completing the checklist.

synopsis: [Cargo Air Carrier] Ground Personnel reported shipment of undeclared Dangerous Goods during preflight. DG shipment refused.
summary: Ground personnel discovered undeclared UN3481 lithium-ion batteries in a cargo shipment during a manager's inspection prior to tender. The shipment containing 12 boxes of iPhone AirPods was refused and not accepted for transport.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported being instructed to load Hazmat cargo in violation of Hazmat loading secure configuration procedures.
summary: Load planners and crew on a 737-900 freight flight reported an inability to secure 2,022 pounds of dangerous goods per new policy requiring 9 ballast bags or 450 pounds of mail. Despite the conflict, the team loaded the cargo and approved weight balancers following company instructions.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported refusing Illegal Hazmat cargo which was attempted to be loaded on aircraft.
summary: A crew member refused to load UN3077 dangerous goods after reviewing the Emergency Response Guide, which warned of explosion and toxic gas risks. The reporter declined the shipment because no further information on the hazardous material was available locally.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported exceeding the maximum altitude at an intersection during climbout.
summary: The crew momentarily exceeded the 13,000-foot limit at ZZZZZ during a hand-flown departure unfamiliar to both pilots. The Captain, returning after months off, and the First Officer, returning from vacation, attributed the error to high workload and a failure to engage the autopilot sooner.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a 'smoke' in the flight deck event resulting in a return to gate. The aircraft was subsequently taken out of service.
summary: The pilot reported smoke in the flight deck after turning on packs with APU and engine bleed air following de-icing in heavy snow. Suspecting de-icing fluid entered the bleed air system, the crew returned to the gate, and the aircraft went out of service.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a fumes event during pre-flight which eventually resulted in an aircraft swap and an uneventful flight.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew reported an electrical burning and metallic odor at the gate, leading to passenger deplaning and aircraft replacement. Although maintenance found no odor, the crew experienced temporary symptoms, and the pilot suspected a tailwind during engine shutdown as the possible cause.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer and Captain reported four missed approaches due to weather and then a safe landing at an alternate airport.
summary: The First Officer flew Aircraft X from ZZZ2 to ZZZ1, executing multiple go-arounds on RNAV RNP and ILS approaches due to wind gusts, lost visibility, and a 26-knot tailwind exceeding limits. A wind shear warning during the final go-around prompted a diversion to ZZZ3, where the crew landed safely before returning to ZZZ1 after refueling.

synopsis: Pilot reported eye injury after a laser was directed into the cockpit from a ground source.
summary: A pilot experienced a green laser event during landing and continued to fly one leg as pilot monitoring from ZZZ to ZZZ1 the next day. The pilot reported ongoing pressure symptoms in the left eye.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not checking a cargo door that had a MEL on it due to a distraction before departing resulting in a divert.
summary: The crew diverted during departure due to a cargo door caution and pressurization loss, citing rushed QRH execution caused by task saturation, lack of currency, and fatigue. The pilot attributed the error to failing to verify ground checks for the deferred item and rushing the procedure instead of leveling off to reduce workload.

synopsis: First Officer reported a lack of assertiveness caused the flying pilot to descend in rising terrain, triggering EGPWS warnings and an autopilot disconnect to regain altitude.
summary: During descent to ZZZ, the First Officer and Captain received an EGPWS terrain warning at 3,500 ft after descending to a 2,500 ft bug. The Captain disengaged the autopilot and pitched up to clear terrain, with the First Officer later noting they should have been more assertive about rising terrain before descending.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that a drain mast had fatigued and failed during flight and was discovered at the destination airport by maintenance.
summary: The pilot inspected the aircraft after landing and found the forward drain mast fairing had structurally failed during flight, leaving it dangling by the drain tube. Fatigue cracks were observed at the attach points, and the pilot ruled out ground or bird strike as the cause.

synopsis: Captain reported a rejected take off and return to gate because of aircraft controllability issues.
summary: Flight crew rejected takeoff on Runway XXL due to a left rudder malfunction that actuated the left brake and caused right drift. Maintenance failed to detect the issue at the gate, despite the crew's report and a similar prior incident on the same aircraft type.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a loss of engine oil quantity and a loss of oil pressure caused an inflight shut down of the engine and an ATC guided landing.
summary: Pilots on a ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight experienced decreasing oil quantity and pressure, leading to an engine shutdown during descent. Mechanics later found a missing oil plug inside the engine cowl, which caused the leak and required a runway stop for inspection before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported the Right Bleed Trip Off light illuminated during takeoff roll resulting in a rejected takeoff.
