synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an issue on the RNDRZ1 approach and possible confusion with how the chart is written. Crew also noted that ATC advised that over 300 aircraft have had the same situation occur.
summary: Flight crew flying the RNDRZ1 arrival into LAS corrected an FMS-initiated left turn after BERBN while ATC simultaneously vectored them heading 080 for a visual approach. The crew attributed the confusion to the new procedure's ambiguity regarding expected headings and automation behavior, though no deviations occurred.

synopsis: A-321 Captain reported a need for clear definitive Hazmat policy to avoid ambiguities which exist among FOM, company publications and SOP regarding carriage of batteries in the passenger cabin.
summary: During boarding, crew and ground staff incorrectly permitted a passenger to carry mobility device batteries in the cabin based on a misleading FOM hyperlink. The flight departed late, and the Captain later discovered the batteries were actually prohibited, recommending clearer manuals and staff training.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported an uneventful landing after an NMAC event requiring evasive maneuver during approach. No traffic information provided to flight crew.
summary: While flying an RNAV approach, the crew received a climb RA and executed it, avoiding a light civil aircraft vectored by Approach Control that passed 400 feet below. The pilot reported a near miss caused by Approach failing to provide traffic advisories or prevent the conflict.

synopsis: Flight crew on landing flare reported an aircraft took off from an intersecting departure towards their path so they initiated a go-around the same time MMU ATC told them to go-around. The reporters said the other traffic had been instructed to taxi into position and hold.
summary: The flight crew executed a go-around during the landing flare after a single-engine aircraft entered an intersecting runway without clearance. The crew climbed over the intruding aircraft, which was beginning its takeoff roll, and completed an uneventful landing after the incident.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an unstable approach and a hard landing. Both pilots reported lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: A Captain and First Officer with limited recent experience flew a night VOR approach into ZZZZ Airport, resulting in a hard landing due to excessive speed and altitude. Contributing factors included VNAV mode changes, an out-of-service PAPI, high winds, and the crew's failure to execute a go-around despite being unstable.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported slowing below assigned airspeed to avoid wake turbulence from aircraft ahead on approach to ORD, forcing traffic in trail of them to go around.
summary: Pilots flying a Boeing 737-700 on the ILS 27R approach to ORD encountered wake turbulence and misjudged deceleration rates while slowing early. This speed error caused the aircraft behind to execute a go-around after Tower controllers queried the deviation from the assigned 170 kts.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported entering incorrect performance data and cited being rushed for takeoff and FO's lack of flying as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot and First Officer manually entered an incorrect Zero Fuel Weight into the FMS during taxi due to a lack of uplink and schedule pressure. This error caused the VNAV to cap the climb at FL360 instead of the planned FL380, which was corrected after level-off.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported the aircraft returned to the gate to load a shipment of vaccine that was initially forgotten.
summary: A colleague advised that COVID vaccines were missing, causing the aircraft to return to blocks after pushback. The crew then loaded the vaccines before proceeding.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported a Critical Ground conflict during takeoff roll and executing an uneventful rejected takeoff due to a taxiing aircraft crossing the runway.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring aborted takeoff on Runway XX after observing Aircraft Y crossing the hold short line without radio contact. The crew stopped 200–300 feet short of the runway edge using maximum braking and reverse thrust, then returned to the gate after ATC cleared both aircraft on separate frequencies.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported MYR airport diagram indicates taxiway A4 as Z.
summary: The flight crew landed at Myrtle Beach and stopped after discovering charted taxiway A4 did not match the airport layout. Tower confirmed the charts were incorrect, noting the discrepancy almost caused an incorrect turn onto active Runway 36.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported one of the cabin emergency lights was not visible due to the curtain blocking it from view.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a curtain on a Boeing 737 MAX 9 blocked an emergency light, a design issue not present on other 737s. Although the crew notified pilots and maintenance, a mechanic dismissed the concern as factory-standard and cleared the aircraft for departure despite the obstruction.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a loss of communication with the ATC Center resulting in an ADS-B traffic alert. Reporter cited possible COVID-19 related ATC staffing issues may have contributed to the event.
summary: A pilot on an IFR enroute flight lost contact with ZZZ Center after a controller instructed aircraft not to call in. The pilot reestablished communication via ADS-B traffic alerts and subsequent calls, suspecting a potential loss of separation caused by understaffed facilities and overwhelmed controllers.

synopsis: Part 107 pilot was flying in an area they believed to be available for UAS operations. After further review the pilot learned they were in fact in airspace not available to UAS operations which was not noted by any of the UAS apps.
summary: A drone operator with a PPL inadvertently flew a drone below 1,000 feet AGL in a restricted area near San Francisco while filming an unpermitted event. The incursion occurred because four airspace apps failed to alert the pilot, and the operator incorrectly believed the restriction was located farther north.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A flight instructor conducting an instrument approach to MQY airport reported flight school aircraft from an adjacent airport flew into potential conflict with their approach course. The reporter had an NMAC with one of the aircraft requiring them to take evasive action.
summary: The pilot reported that while on an IFR approach, three flight school aircraft from an adjacent airport climbed within 500 feet, with one coming within 100 feet at the same altitude. The pilot veered to avoid a collision and notified ATC, who stated the area was a "beehive" and could not explain the incident.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B767 on descent into MCO.
summary: During a VMC descent on the PIGLT6 arrival past JAFAR at 12,000 feet, the aircraft experienced severe turbulence and uncommanded autopilot rolls up to 40 degrees. The pilot disengaged the autopilot, recovered manually, and attributed the upset to wake turbulence from a preceding 767 caused by tight RNAV arrival spacing.

synopsis: Cessna 210 pilot reported executing an evasive maneuver resulting in an uneventful NMAC event during cruise.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 3,000 feet MSL with autopilot engaged took evasive climbing action to avoid a converging aircraft. The pilot reported a near miss, noting that Approach claimed to have issued traffic advisories that were never received due to silent radios.

synopsis: Vintage aircraft Instructor reported an NMAC event during landing pattern training with Aircraft Z erroneously landing opposite runway in use. Aircraft Z also cause a critical ground conflict with Aircraft Y.
summary: A CFI and student in a non-radio vintage aircraft nearly collided with an Aircraft Z during landing practice at an uncontrolled airport. The Aircraft Z pilot incorrectly entered a left traffic pattern for a right-hand runway while claiming calm winds, causing a runway incursion and a close call with less than 50 feet vertical separation.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 pilot reported an inflight uncommanded engine shut down and subsequent engine relight, and continued to destination airport.
summary: During descent from FL450 to FL240, the First Officer observed Engine 2 N1 and N2 decreasing while Engine 1 remained stable. The crew executed the loss of engine checklist, successfully restarted Engine 2 at FL250, and landed without further incident.

synopsis: PA28A pilot reported an uneventful diversion due to critical engine malfunction.
summary: The pilot experienced rough engine operation during cruise and returned to ZZZ2, landing safely after requesting priority. Post-flight maintenance revealed a loose plastic piece on the left magneto installation caused timing issues, which was confirmed by an 800 RPM drop during a ground magneto check.

synopsis: C172 student pilot on a solo flight and the observing flight instructor reported a loss of aircraft control on takeoff and excursion from the runway.
summary: A student pilot veered left off the runway during a solo takeoff due to loss of control despite right rudder input, stopping on Taxiway XX with no injuries. The instructor attributed the incident to delayed power reduction and plans additional supervised takeoff training before re-solo.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported experiencing a loss of aircraft control caused by a wind gust, resulting in departure from the runway surface and aircraft damage.
summary: During rollout after the 9th landing, a gust lifted the left wing and veered the aircraft left despite full control deflection. The right wingtip dragged, the right gear folded, and the aircraft nosed over off the pavement, damaging the propeller with no injuries.

synopsis: Stationar pilot reported loss of aircraft control and momentary excursion from the runway caused by a wind gust.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway excursion during a turbulent approach at an uncontrolled airport while practicing a wheel landing. A left gust lifted the right wing, causing the aircraft to veer onto the grass before being safely re-entered without damage or injury.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion during landing at BOI due to ambiguous lead-off runway and taxiway edge lighting configuration.
summary: The pilot landed on runway 10R at night and exited onto a blacked-out lead-off line for a relocated Taxiway H due to fatigue and poor visual cues. The aircraft stopped in mud and gravel, requiring a tow after the pilot failed to verify taxiway signage before exiting.

synopsis: Captain reported engine failure on take off roll causing a rejected take off and a return to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang and left yaw during takeoff power application on Runway XX, causing an immediate stop. Inspection revealed bent and broken turbine blades in Engine #1, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the LAS NITZ1 RNAV Engine Out for Runway 8L page diagram depiction of FLAAR and the 12.7 ring is confusing.
summary: A pilot and a Check Airman identified misleading Engine Out diagrams for the NIITZ 1 RNAV departure from Runway 8L, where the chart incorrectly depicted the FLAAR fix distance relative to terrain. They concluded that the lack of a "Not to Scale" warning and conflicting altitude rings could confuse crews during an engine failure.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot Crew reported a critical ground conflict during taxi.
summary: The flight crew experienced two near-mid-air collisions with an unannounced 757 while taxiing to Runway XXL via Taxiways H and G. The Captain stopped the aircraft both times after visually spotting the approaching traffic, as Ground Control had provided no information regarding the 757's presence.

synopsis: First Officer reported engine failure on take off roll, resulting in engine damage and a return to the gate.
summary: During takeoff roll at approximately 15 knots, the crew rejected the takeoff after a loud bang, left yaw, and Engine #1 failure indication. Post-flight inspection revealed damaged fan blades and stators with metal debris in the tailpipe, prompting a request for a runway FOD check.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot Crew reported a NMAC and RA after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew received a takeoff clearance with traffic advisories but encountered an unavoidable Resolution Advisory while climbing between two conflicting aircraft. The crew leveled off at 2,600 feet to comply with the RA, attributing the conflict to ATC failing to inform them of the second traffic or delay the departure.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot Crew reported a critical taxi conflict leaving the gate area.
summary: The flight crew experienced a near collision while taxiing on the inbound line after another aircraft overtook them on the right. The pilots avoided impact by maneuvering right, attributing the event to the other aircraft's decision to pass quickly without communication.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a hazardous situation exist with tall radio towers in the vicinity of GEG airport. Reporters recommends more prominent warnings on approach and airport charts to flight crews .
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to GEG Runway 21 descended toward 3,900 feet but stopped at 5,300 feet after spotting tall radio towers higher than the FAF altitude. The crew leveled off to clear the towers, which were not warned on charts, before completing a safe landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher and a Captain reported the flight departed with hazmat documentation errors and inaccurate data.
summary: Load Planning and Dispatch notified the flight crew that an extra 7 lbs of Hazmat was loaded onto the aircraft, exceeding the 6.0-unit limit. The discrepancy occurred because an additional item was added without the crew's knowledge, causing a mismatch between the manifest and the actual load.

synopsis: First Officer reported receiving a CFIT Warning from ATC.
summary: Pilots descending for a visual approach at ZZZ mistakenly descended below the 3700-foot MSA due to a clearance misunderstanding. They climbed back to the MSA, executed a go-around for being too high on final, and landed safely after the controller attributed the error to potential confusion with another aircraft's altitude.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported possible GPS jamming in this area per aircraft instrument errors, ATIS information and ATC advisory.
summary: During the JCOXX2 departure from ELP, the crew received false terrain warnings and ADS-B failures above 6,450 ft due to military GPS jamming. The First Officer increased climb rate, but the aircraft cleared terrain safely, and the terrain system failure was reported upon arrival at ZZZ.

synopsis: EMB/ERJ-145 flight crew reported continuing to an uneventful landing in spite of CFIT indications of multiple GPWS alerts during a visual final approach. Flight crew maintained visual clearance of the rising terrain.
summary: The crew flew a visual approach to Runway XX near rising terrain after ATC denied a requested ILS to Runway YY. Despite false GPWS and glideslope cautions caused by using an ILS frequency for visual reference, the First Officer landed safely using raw data.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported aircraft generated CFIT Warning while on approach.
summary: Two pilots unfamiliar with ZZZ airport accepted a visual approach for XXL despite a tailwind, failing to comply with prescribed speeds. This resulted in an unstable approach, EGPWS terrain warnings, and a go-around before a safe landing.

synopsis: A Flight Crew reported while flying a new RNAV arrival the Controller told them they should have turned to a heading at a fix but the procedure specifies 'expect' vectors at the fix.
summary: Pilots flying Aircraft X on the RNDRZ1 arrival to ILS 26L at LAS turned to heading 020 after HOGOG because ATC failed to issue the expected 080 vector at BERBN. The reporter attributed the deviation to unclear chart inset data and the aircraft's flight management system linking the arrival directly to the approach.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported confusion regarding medical certification expiration date in reference to the COVID-19 extension.
summary: A pilot discovered their company listed their medical certificate as expired two months early due to confusion over FAA COVID extension verbiage. The conflicting expiration dates on the FAA letter and certificate caused misunderstandings for the pilot, AME, and company, highlighting a need for clearer guidance.

synopsis: Eyewitness Pilot reported observing a critical ground conflict during taxi when an aircraft taxiied onto a runway while another aircraft was on takeoff roll at ORD airport.
summary: Pilots reported a runway incursion where Aircraft Y entered RWY 9C while Aircraft Z was on takeoff roll due to ATC failing to issue a hold short clearance. The reporter attributed the event to poor visibility, inadequate signage, and the unsafe use of RWY 22R as a taxiway.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported after the aircraft had been sanitized a strong odor remained for a lengthy period of time resulting in throat and eye irritation.
summary: Cabin crew reported strong chemical irritation to their eyes and throats after cleaners sprayed the aircraft before boarding. Relief was only felt after takeoff when the air circulation system began operating.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A flight instructor providing instruction on base leg at a LMO non-towered airport reported a near miss with another aircraft in the pattern.
summary: A pilot and student on final approach detected a conflicting aircraft on a right base via personal ADS-B In equipment. The pilot reduced power and turned right to avoid a collision, prompting the other aircraft to break off, while the pilot attributed the safe outcome to the ADS-B In display.

synopsis: Pilot reported after discovering a serious engine oil leak, he was directed to fly to another airport so it could be fixed, instead of getting a ferry permit.
summary: The pilot reported reduced power and a 20-knot airspeed loss during straight-and-level flight in a helicopter, suspecting a cracked cylinder or bad valve. After discovering oil spray and a 1.5-quart oil loss, the pilot flew the aircraft back to the base for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: Bonanza pilot reported miscommunication with ATC due to the noise from the cabin door opening inflight.
summary: The pilot of a Bonanza VFR flight reported that a cabin door opening in flight caused wind noise and distraction, leading to a missed clearance into Class Bravo airspace. The pilot attributed the incident to poor judgment in attempting to close the door instead of immediately unplugging the passenger's microphone to restore communication.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported two aircraft were not complying with assigned headings and altitudes for final approach sequencing resulting in a NMAC. While attempting to resolve the situation the reporter shipped another aircraft to the Tower without issuing an approach clearance causing that aircraft to go around.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored three aircraft, causing a head-to-head near miss between Aircraft 1 and 3 due to radio communication failures and a missed approach clearance for Aircraft 3. The controller's distraction led to Aircraft 2 executing a go-around, with the incident attributed to pilot non-response and the controller forgetting to issue a clearance.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported GPS jamming in their airspace during busy periods created an unsafe sector operation.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that GPS jamming, combined with high traffic and frequency congestion, severely affected aircraft operations. Management refused to lower sector traffic numbers or stop the jamming, instructing controllers to simply assign headings instead.

synopsis: ATC TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict and cited short staffing levels due to COVID-19 scheduling as a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a conflict between Aircraft X on a visual approach and Aircraft Y on the localizer at 3,000 feet by turning Aircraft Y to heading 090. The controller attributed the incident to combined sectors, high traffic volume, and reduced staffing due to an open Special Flight Rules Area and COVID-19.

synopsis: ATC Ground Controller reported giving incorrect taxi instructions to a crew resulting in a ground conflict. Controller reported the crews had not flown into their airport in a while due the COVID-19 pandemic, which may have contributed to the event.
summary: A North Tower Ground controller inadvertently issued an incorrect taxiway name to Aircraft Y while holding it short of Runway XC due to a departing Aircraft X. Aircraft Y taxied past the runway hold bars before stopping, though the controller asserts no runway crossing clearance was given.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a father with two children were non-compliant with face mask policy during the flight.
summary: The flight crew encountered a male passenger and his two children who refused to wear masks and disrupted the cabin during cruise. The pilot notified Dispatch and arranged for a response team, noting the passenger was allowed to board despite pre-flight non-compliance.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported airport diagram [page 10-9] missing displaced threshold distance which is needed for landing zone calculation.
summary: A pilot reported that the 10-9 diagram displayed a displaced threshold, but the 10-9a page lacked the required distance under the threshold box. This missing data prevented the calculation of the Landing Zone.

synopsis: B737 NG flight crew reported a jammed horizontal stabilizer trim system and elected to make an Air turn Back and precautionary landing.
summary: The Student Captain and First Officer experienced inoperative electric stabilizer trim shortly after takeoff, leading to a "STAB OUT OF TRIM" light and excessive manual trim forces. They completed Jammed Flight Control checklists, diverted to the nearest airport, and landed safely with Flaps 15 after confirming the stabilizer was jammed.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported a baggage cart drove in front of the aircraft as it was taxiing to parking in the ramp and they had to brake to avoid.
summary: During taxi, an airline baggage truck and trolley drove rapidly across the aircraft's path from left to right, crossing a stop line despite eye contact. The Captain braked to avoid a close ground conflict, though no impact occurred.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported they had to stop suddenly while taxiing to avoid a vehicle on the taxiway which they eventually followed to parking.
summary: After landing and turning onto a high-speed taxiway, the crew stopped when a reserve pilot spotted a Follow Me car approaching at 30–40 mph from the left. The car slowed, allowing the aircraft to follow it safely to the pad with no further incident.

synopsis: An airline pilot flying as a passenger reported while the aircraft appeared to be flying a Visual Approach it flew too close to towers located near the airport.
summary: Two airline pilots, seated as passengers on a flight descending for a visual approach to Spokane (GEG) Runway 21, reported the aircraft flew dangerously close to two 950-foot towers southeast of the airport. The crew observed an abnormally low vertical proximity to the towers, which they attributed to a lack of adherence to standard arrival procedures and insufficient visual confirmation.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a EGPWS terrain warning on approach into Reno airport.
summary: The Captain and a new First Officer executed a go-around during a visual approach to Runway 16L at Reno due to an unstabilized descent caused by gusty quartering tailwinds and speed brake extension. After an EGPWS terrain warning, they performed an escape maneuver and landed uneventfully on a subsequent approach.

synopsis: ERJ First Officer reported the DEN Jeppesen 10-9 airfield diagrams do not correlate with the magnetic variation change.
summary: A pilot reported discrepancies in Jeppesen's DEN 10-9 charts where airfield diagrams showed incorrect magnetic runway headings compared to the info page due to unupdated magnetic variation. The reporter attributed this to a lack of attention to detail and recommended Jeppesen develop a system to identify variation shifts beyond runway renumbering requirements.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported a runway incursion due to insufficient runway and taxiway signage and markings.
summary: A pilot reported a jet runway incursion at Runway 22R and 9C caused by non-standard signage and ATC failure to advise holding short. The reporter attributed the event to missing holding position markings and signs that failed to designate the runway intersection.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported they landed safely with a brake malfunction but neglected to notify Dispatch of the malfunction.
summary: The Pilot Flying executed a go-around on final approach into ZZZ after receiving a right brake fault advisory. Following the QRH checklist, the crew landed with an extended rollout, using asymmetric braking to maintain centerline, and taxied to the gate with the right outboard brake confirmed inoperative.

synopsis: Ramp employee reported that passenger counts and baggage are increasing, but there are not enough piers open to safely accommodate baggage handling.
summary: Pier workers reported a serious tripping hazard caused by placing bags on the ground due to limited floor space in consolidated piers as passenger and baggage volumes increased. Despite identifying this risk to operations leadership, no corrective actions have been taken to reopen closed piers or space out the work.

synopsis: A Medevac pilot reported they set too low an altitude for the approach procedure and received a terrain warning alert.
summary: The pilot descended below the required 11,800 feet between waypoints ZZZZZ and ZZZZZ1 during an RNAV (GPS) approach, triggering a TAWS terrain warning. The pilot attributed the error to complacency and mentally anticipating the next altitude restriction without verifying the chart.

synopsis: Gulfstream V flight crew reported impacting another aircraft's wingtip at the start of taxi.
summary: The flight crew operating a Challenger on the ramp at FBO ZZZ contacted a parked Challenger on a tug while taxiing after the pilot not flying incorrectly confirmed winglet clearance. Although the reporting aircraft sustained no damage, the parked Challenger was damaged, and the incident occurred after ground personnel left without informing the crew.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported having to ask Controller several times if they were cleared to land during approach. Reporter stated the Controller was probably overwhelmed working three positions/frequencies at the same time.
summary: A pilot conducting night currency landings reported that a single controller managing Delivery, Ground, and Tower frequencies failed to issue landing clearances, likely due to being overwhelmed. The situation was exacerbated by a 40-knot tailwind causing high ground speeds, leading to controller annoyance when the pilot requested clarification.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: GA pilot reported a conflict after being told to cross a runway, and while crossing observed an aircraft on short final. Pilot cited distraction and ATC staffing as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing to Runway XX, looked down at a checklist and nearly missed a regional jet on final approach for Runway YX. The pilot attributed the near miss to distraction and noted that a single controller was likely handling both Ground and Tower duties.

synopsis: Cessna 350 pilot reported taking evasive action after takeoff due to a helicopter executing a simultaneous takeoff from the opposite end of the runway.
summary: A fixed-wing pilot departing Runway XX encountered a helicopter departing left of the runway while climbing out. The helicopter was observed 100–150 feet off the pilot's left wing, prompting a hard climb to clear the other aircraft.

synopsis: ZSE Center Controller working the Assist position reported an aircraft cleared for an approach descended below the published Minimum Enroute Altitude but was not issued a low altitude alert by the Radar Controller. The reporter stated it is a common occurrence for aircraft flying this procedure to descend below the published minima.
summary: An air traffic controller observed an aircraft descend below the 12,100-foot MEA during an RNAV approach after crossing the Initial Approach Fix. The controller verbally alerted the pilot, who requested and received a visual approach clearance, though the reporter noted a low altitude safety alert was not issued.

synopsis: Controller reported similar calls signs may have contributed to an aircraft taking another aircraft's assigned altitude. Controller also cited staffing issues as a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X and Y near ZZZ, but Aircraft X descended to 60 instead of the assigned 80, likely due to a misheard clearance or radio interference. The controller attributed the missed deviation to fatigue, staffing shortages, and a failure of the Low Altitude alert system.

synopsis: ZLC Center Controller conducting training reported he and the trainee did not realize an aircraft was on a route that placed it below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and trainee issued a climb to 13,000 feet after a delayed MSAW alert caused Aircraft X to enter a higher Minimum IFR Altitude. The incident resulted from a route line obscuring the altitude text on the display and a 40-second pilot delay in complying with the clearance.

synopsis: Center Operations person reported procedural confusion when they took over the operations of a TRACON facility that went ATC Zero due to COVID-19 cleaning.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at ZZZ ARTCC assumed control of ZZZ TRACON airspace during an ATC Zero event caused by a COVID-19 facility shutdown, deviating from the published contingency plan to clear and hold aircraft. The controller reported that while operations were orderly, the decision to assume airspace was made without following established procedures, highlighting a need for updated baseline guidance.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a CFIT event during a visual approach due to an ATC communications breakdown between flight crew and Approach Control who was working multiple frequencies with similar callsigns.
summary: Company A pilots received a descent clearance to 6,000 feet MSL while being vectored for a visual approach at ZZZ, which was intended for another carrier with a similar call sign. The error occurred due to simultaneous transmissions on different frequencies, taking the aircraft below the Minimum Vector Altitude without triggering GPWS or ATC warnings.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a ramp incursion resulting in a conflict and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The crew experienced confusion while taxiing at night at ZZZ after landing, mistakenly believing no ramp frequency existed. This error, caused by unfamiliarity with the new terminal and a new First Officer, led to entering the ramp area before contacting Ramp Control.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported low engine oil pressure on final approach and continued the approach to a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew received an E2 OIL LOW PRESS warning on engine two during a visual approach to Runway XXL at 10,000 feet. They continued the approach with engine two at idle, landed safely, and shut down the engine on the taxiway after confirming no fire or smoke.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported being notified by company that during a previous flight they had flown off course while conducting an approach and below the minimum terrain altitude for the procedure. The reporter stated they never received a terrain alert in the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a close terrain encounter during an RNAV approach in IMC caused by communication misunderstandings, FMS discontinuities, and distraction. No GPWS or ATC warnings were received, but the crew eventually received a missed approach clearance and landed safely on a second attempt.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not filing correct paperwork for a tow bar that broke during pushback. The Captain stated lack of flying contributed to the oversight.
summary: During pushback, the tow bar broke at the tug connection, prompting the crew to set brakes and replace the bar before continuing. The Captain later admitted that limited recent experience and searching the wrong manual caused a failure to log the event in the Aircraft Maintenance Log as required.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported a communication breakdown between Dispatch and Ramp personnel regarding Hazmat loading configuration resulting in removal of Hazmat cargo.
summary: A flight dispatcher failed to instruct the ramp agent to exclude live animals from the main deck due to distraction regarding dry ice restrictions. Consequently, crickets were loaded into the aft bulkhead compartment, requiring the dispatcher to order their removal after the ramp agent disputed their classification.

synopsis: Pilot reported issues with the CTAF pilot controlled runway lights at SGU. Reporter stated the CTAF frequency is utilized by several airports nearby which allegedly is causing the runway light problems.
summary: A pilot at St. George Municipal (SGU) reported that an aircraft at Mesquite Municipal cycled the shared CTAF frequency, causing SGU's runway lights to flash through all settings and turn off three times during the final approach to Runway 19. The pilot attributed this nuisance to multiple airports sharing one frequency and landed safely with lights on low.

synopsis: B737 MAX 9 Captain reported the shear pin broke during pushback and they failed to have maintenance inspect the aircraft as required.
summary: During pushback of a 737 MAX, a tow bar shear pin failed. The pilot initially planned an information-only logbook entry based on 737 NG procedures, but a fleet Captain later clarified that the MAX manual requires a mandatory inspection for this event.

synopsis: Air carrier light crew reported a Cabin Press Warning EICAS message while crossing a mountain range on a one pack deferred flight. Flight crew completed an uneventful landing after developing a successful workaround.
summary: Pilots operating an aircraft with Bleed 1 on MEL experienced inadequate pressurization during climb to FL XX0, triggering a Cabin Press warning at 12,000 feet. After descending to 10,000 feet and consulting Dispatch, they continued to ZZZ1 due to insufficient drift-down performance over mountains, noting the MEL lacked clear guidance for single-bleed operations.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the auto pilot was not programmed correctly for the approach and the aircraft descended below the Minimum Safe Altitude.
summary: During the LIBER 3 arrival, the crew descended below the 4,200 ft minimum safe altitude after prematurely arming the approach and setting the altitude alert to 1,700 ft. This triggered a terrain warning and ATC low altitude alert, requiring a manual climb to 4,200 ft before the crew re-engaged the autopilot and landed safely.

synopsis: EMB-175 pilot reported while taxiing off the runway they had to apply maximum braking to avoid a vehicle driving on the taxiway.
summary: During landing rollout, the pilot took controls at 60 knots and applied maximum brakes to avoid an airport operations vehicle on the high-speed taxiway. The vehicle swerved into the grass, and ATC admitted unawareness of its presence, resulting in no damage or injuries.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a student flew a cross country flight without having the correct solo endorsement.
summary: A flight instructor at a Part 141 school sent a student on a solo flight without a current endorsement after missing a syllabus reminder due to not reviewing the CFI guide. The instructor discovered the error during the next flight preparation and immediately issued the required endorsement.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported the engine failed soon after switching the fuel tank selector from 'both' to 'left' position due to uneven fuel burn. The pilot immediately pitched the aircraft for best glide speed, followed procedures, and was able to regain engine power when the fuel tank selector was placed back to 'both' position.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 3,000 feet while on flight following with ZZZ Approach after selecting the left fuel tank. Power was restored at 2,300 feet by returning the selector to both, and the flight resumed to ZZZ1 after confirming the failure was caused by the fuel tank selection.

synopsis: BE400 pilot reported that while descending on a Visual Approach they received a Terrain Alert.
summary: During a VFR visual approach to Runway XXL, the Second in Command received a terrain advisory at 4,500 feet while northeast of a mountain peak. The crew arrested the descent and returned to 4,500 feet, maintaining an estimated 1,500 feet above ground level with no further warnings.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: First Officer and Captain reported a taxiway excursion while turning onto the parallel taxiway at UDD. Reporters were told, this is a common issue at the airport.
summary: The PIC and SIC of a charter aircraft departed the prepared surface into soft sand while turning onto a parallel taxiway at Bermuda Dunes after landing. The aircraft was recovered by airport personnel and towed to the FBO, where maintenance inspection returned it to airworthiness status.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC during initial approach to JYO airport.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a pattern aircraft experienced a near collision at Leesburg while on left downwind for Runway 17. The incident involved an unexpected departure to the north that violated standard right-hand procedures, with no prior Tower warning or clearance issued.

synopsis: GA pilot on arrival to OPF Airport reported another aircraft appeared from behind a small cloud resulting in an NMAC.
summary: A pilot arriving on the WAVUN5 arrival at 6,000 feet reported a Cessna 182 or 206 emerging from a cloud in the opposite direction, passing within 100 to 150 feet. The crew subsequently reported the near-midair collision to Miami Center and Miami Approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported the PAPI's at HPN Runway 16 being reversed.
summary: A pilot reported reversed PAPI light indications during arrival at HPN, where outboard lights appeared red instead of white. The pilot contacted the tower the next morning, and a controller agreed to dispatch operations to inspect and resolve the system error.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported finding out a FAA facility was going to close via personal sources rather than through the flight release information.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X increased ramp fuel from 6,600 to 10,000 pounds after learning via personal sources that destination ZZZ1 was closed for cleaning. The crew held for 20 minutes before landing safely, avoiding a potential fuel emergency that would have occurred without the extra fuel.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported that while flying at low altitudes between 500-1,000 feet AGL came within 200 feet of a small UAS.
summary: A pilot flying a routine route at 600–700 feet AGL encountered a small white drone at close proximity. The pilot deviated to avoid the slower drone, which moved from the 1 o'clock to the 10 o'clock position within seconds.

synopsis: GA pilot reported they were on a runway holding short of an intersecting runway when they observed an aircraft about to land on their runway at ISP. They taxied off and advised Tower.
summary: The pilot landed and was instructed to taxi onto an intersecting runway where another aircraft was landing. The pilot took evasive action, causing the other aircraft to go around, attributing the near collision to the controller forgetting the landing aircraft due to traffic volume.

synopsis: Pilot reported two waypoints near Truckee, CA, with identical identifiers: VERDI. One is a visual reporting point while the other is an Intersection.
summary: Pilots navigating near Truckee, CA, face a hazard due to two waypoints sharing the identifier VERDI: one over the town and another on a mountain ridge. Entering the town's location into a GPS may route aircraft over the ridge, creating a collision risk in mountainous terrain.

synopsis: Corporate pilot reported a track heading deviation after misprogramming the FMS resulting in two fixes being dropped from the route. Pilot cited time pressure and lack of recent flying as contributing factors.
summary: The PNF on a ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight inadvertently omitted waypoints ZZZZZ2 and ZZZZZ3 from the FMS by linking the SID directly to the STAR. This error, caused by rushing and failing to review the flight plan per SOPs, resulted in the aircraft flying several nautical miles east of the cleared route at FL300.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported undocumented Hazmat cargo transported due to erroneous Hazmat documents were provided to flight crew at departure.
summary: The pilot discovered a missing HAZMAT remark on the Air Waybill and Dispatch Release while en route, despite the Ops Agent failing to notify Dispatch of fire extinguishers and oxygen cylinders. Dispatch confirmed the agent is responsible for this notification, as these items are classified as HAZMAT.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported executing an uneventful landing after a mechanical diversion due to a pressurization pack failure during climb.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X experienced a No.2 pack bleed trip off and subsequent cabin altitude warning while climbing to FL390, forcing an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and oxygen mask deployment. Due to communication limitations, the crew diverted to ZZZ3 and landed safely, noting that ACARS capability would have aided decision-making.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported problems with the localizer inbound to LCH.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced localizer deviations on an ILS approach to Runway 15 at LCH, causing the autopilot to be disengaged at 1,300 feet MSL. The crew completed a visual landing after sighting the runway at 1,100 feet MSL and reported the issue to the tower, requesting an antenna inspection.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the taxiway diagram at MYR airport does not match the ground signage.
summary: The pilot reported a discrepancy between updated taxiway diagrams and ground signage while taxiing to Runway 18. Ground confirmed the diagram changed to Taxiway Z, but signs still read A4, prompting a recommendation to update signs or issue a NOTAM.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported an altitude deviation during arrival. Captain cited the First Officer's lack of flying and being distracted by a PA as contributing factors.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed a 12,000-foot crossing altitude by 800 feet during a re-routed arrival with a 45-knot tailwind. The Captain attributed the error to poor monitoring caused by distractions, the First Officer's mode change to VS, and underestimating the First Officer's skills after a year-long leave.

synopsis: B-737 Captain reported executing a challenging mechanical diversion due to pressurization failure during climb. The diversion was concluded with an uneventful overweight landing.
summary: Flight ZZZ1 experienced a cabin altitude warning at 11,000 ft due to door 1L failing to seat properly, causing a loss of pressurization. The crew diverted to ZZZZ2, landing overweight after managing oxygen levels and avoiding terrain and thunderstorms.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a track deviation and cited lack of flying by both pilots contributed to the event.
summary: Reserve pilots on a delayed arrival at ZZZ airport flew through the localizer while distracted by speed card verification, failing to notice the APPR mode was not armed. The crew corrected the flight path after ATC query and landed safely, attributing the deviation to poor attention management during the visual approach.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported not following company communication procedures and cited lack of flight time between training and actual OE flight as a contributing factor.
summary: A Captain and Check Airman flew two legs in an aircraft with an inoperative First Officer audio panel, which also disabled ACARS. They failed to monitor required company communication frequencies per the FOM due to inexperience and oversight, despite the Check Airman signing the aircraft.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported engine vibrations along with smoke and odor in the cabin. They shut down the number two engine, diverted, and landed safely.
summary: During climb through 34,000 feet, the flight crew encountered severe vibration, smoke, and erratic indications on engine 2, causing a precautionary shutdown and diversion. Post-landing inspection revealed damage to the engine's fan blades, spinner, and cowling, though the specific cause of the in-flight failure remains unknown.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported AutoFlight Systems malfunction after takeoff.
summary: Pilots lost auto throttles, electric trim, and autopilot shortly after takeoff due to a stabilizer trim failure. They diverted to ZZZZ to avoid marginal weather and RVSM airspace restrictions, landing uneventfully after manual flight and early fuel burn.

synopsis: First Officer reported the SKBO/BOG 10-3H OSOSU 1R RNAV SID at or below altitude depictions can be deceiving. Because the blue crossing altitude depictions are so prominent compared to the smaller MEA numbers, a crew could easily cross OSOSU too low for terrain clearance.
summary: A pilot reported that the SKBO/BOG 10-3H RNAV SID crossing altitude depiction at OSOSU is deceptive because the "at or below 17,000 feet" instruction conflicts with the 17,000 feet MEA for the next segment. This discrepancy could cause crews to cross too low for terrain clearance, unlike the safer 10-3G SID.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported both GPS units failed.
summary: The pilot experienced complete failure of both GPS units enroute 1.5 hours into the flight. After coordinating with Dispatch, the aircraft diverted to ZZZ uneventfully, with no reported GPS jamming from other aircraft or ATC.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew and a dispatcher reported the aircraft's number 3 engine had a compressor stall on departure.
summary: The First Officer flying a three-engine aircraft experienced compressor stalls on engine 3 at 1,000 feet, marked by loud bangs, shuddering, and smoke observed by ATC. The crew reduced thrust, returned to the airport, dumped fuel at 12,000 feet, and landed safely without determining the specific cause.

synopsis: Technician reported signing off on a work order but not being qualified to do so.
summary: A mechanic admitted to signing off on a window modification for a MAX aircraft despite lacking the required MAX difference training. The error occurred because the mechanic had only attended RII class and was not qualified to approve those specific items.

synopsis: Light Transport aircraft Captain reported ATC issued a low altitude warning during visual approach to EKO airport. Captain replied that airport and terrain in sight. Flight executed an uneventful landing.
summary: While descending at 14,000 feet on a radar vector to EKO, the crew received a visual approach clearance and a subsequent low altitude alert from ATC. The crew confirmed visual conditions with terrain in sight and continued the approach despite the warning.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported the aircraft would not climb during takeoff after out of the ground effect despite full power being applied and settled back on the ground resulting in a departure from the runway, and a nose gear collapse.
summary: The pilot attempted a short-field takeoff in calm weather with flaps at 12 degrees. The aircraft failed to climb after leaving ground effect, settled back onto the runway, veered left, and the nose gear collapsed in soft dirt 100 feet from the runway.

synopsis: PA-28 flight instructor reported an NMAC event during traffic pattern training. Reporter stated ATC's response was inadequate.
summary: A pilot monitoring an aircraft on downwind reported a near miss with a departing aircraft that passed 50–100 feet below and ahead. The instructor called Tower, which issued an ineffective right 360-degree clearance, so no avoidance maneuver was executed.

synopsis: Cessna 180 Pilot reported a runway excursion during landing caused by loss of directional control. No aircraft or environmental damage.
summary: The pilot experienced a non-violent ground loop during landing in a tailwheel aircraft following avionics upgrades. The event was caused by excessive power, a flat touchdown, and unobserved crosswinds, but resulted in no damage due to the pilot's calm energy management and ample grassy terrain.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported observing a UAS pass by their aircraft. After this distraction they forgot to descend as planned and entered controlled airspace.
summary: A VFR pilot flying a cross-country to TPF inadvertently flew 3 miles above the Tampa Bravo floor at 1,900 feet due to an altimeter misread and distraction from a suspected drone. The pilot corrected the altitude after realizing the error, attributing the incident to the visual distraction.

synopsis: Cessna 182 pilot reported a total electrical failure occurred, resulting in loss of communication and navigation equipment. The pilot then navigated using their tablet and entered Class B airspace without operating ADS-B equipment.
summary: The pilot experienced VHF transmission failure shortly after takeoff, followed by total electrical power loss 1.5 hours later. Navigating via iPad, the pilot entered ZZZ2 Class B airspace without ADS-B, considering the situation an emergency despite acknowledging an option to land short of the destination.

synopsis: GA pilot reported they misidentified the traffic in the RNT airport pattern after being instructed to follow and turned onto final too soon resulting in a NMAC with preceding traffic.
summary: The pilot, flying as number 3 on short final, mistook number 1 traffic for number 2 and failed to cross-check the GTN 750 ADS-B display. This led to a near-miss with a high-wing aircraft, prompting an immediate go-around, while a non-functional GTX-345 audio alert was identified as a contributing factor.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: GA pilot reported not being able to activate an IFR Flight plan due to ATC not having it on file. An adjacent ATC facility could not provide help either. Pilot also reported entering Class Bravo airspace unintentionally after misreading the aircraft's new GPS system.
summary: The pilot of a newly acquired aircraft inadvertently entered Class B airspace after ATC could not activate the flight plan due to staffing shortages. The incursion resulted from misreading unfamiliar GPS equipment and expecting a clearance, though the pilot was subsequently vectored out by ZZZ1 Approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported that due to the inoperative radio they made an approach and landing without communicating and had an NMAC with another aircraft. During taxi to parking, the pilot of the other aircraft followed them closely and took photographs of the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a VFR aircraft with an inoperative radio experienced a close call with Aircraft Y during pattern entry and taxiing at ZZZ. The reporter attributed the unsafe spacing and Aircraft Y's distracted taxiing to the other pilot using a cell phone to take pictures while operating the aircraft.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported an NMAC on short final was not detected by the Local Control trainee, the Instructor, or the Controller in Charge until the Ground Controller brought it to their attention.
summary: During local training, a trainee controller failed to notice Aircraft X flying dangerously close behind Aircraft Y on short final due to distraction and lack of visual monitoring. The trainee only issued a go-around after the instructor intervened, while the Controller in Charge minimized the risk despite the near-collision.

synopsis: Center Controller reported that the ZZZ Center Contingency Plan was not followed for COVID -19 ATC cleaning of an underlying Approach facility.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that ZZZ Approach closed for COVID cleaning, but the agreed contingency plan was not followed. The reporter stated the plan should have been adhered to, with any adjustments made after the occurrence rather than ignoring the established procedures.

synopsis: Center Controller reported that due to COVID-19 cleaning, four separate data input keyboards were not functioning properly.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZZZ Center reported that Level 3 cleaning caused four data input keyboard failures, including a stuck code button that prevented viewing handoffs and delayed sector openings. The controller attributed the equipment damage to the cleaning process and requested its cessation, noting SOC acknowledgment of the issue but inability to act.

synopsis: ZAN Controller reported developmental issued IFR clearance below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic control trainee issued a direct clearance to Aircraft X at 3,800 feet while the aircraft was below the 4,000-foot Minimum IFR Altitude. The incident occurred because the trainee felt rushed to finish the briefing, though the aircraft continued without incident.

synopsis: GEG TRACON Controller reported they issued a clearance that placed an aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude. The Controller's radar map was inaccurate and the Low Altitude Alert did not function.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a safety alert to Aircraft X for descending below the 6,500-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude during an RNAV approach due to a missing fix on the radar display. The controller attributed the delay in reaction to the lack of an automated Low Altitude Alert and discrepancies between the approach plate and radar map.

synopsis: Center Controller reported safety concerns with having to wear face masks while on position. Controller referenced the face mask is distracting and make instructions difficult for pilots to understand.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZZZ Center reported that a mandatory mask order caused read-back errors and headset interference, hindering effective communication with pilots. The controller stated this mandate compromised the ability to safely separate aircraft and issue instructions, creating an unsafe environment.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 flight crew reported overlooking an open maintenance entry in the aircraft logbook and operating the aircraft.
summary: The crew and maintenance personnel missed an open logbook entry for a No.1 engine starter cutout issue due to a skipped blank page and folded separator. This oversight caused a late departure to ZZZ1, where the defect was discovered, MEL'd, and the blank page voided.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported confusion with the LGA airport La Guardia 7 SID engine out procedures.
summary: The flight crew at LGA paused taxi after ATC changed their clearance from the LA GUARDIA 7 WHITESTONE to the GLDMN 7 departure. Confusion arose from Jeppesen chart titles listing separate GLDMN and NTHNS departures without a comma, requiring a radio call and briefing to clarify the correct procedure before departing safely.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported an indicated airspeed disagree issue during arrival.
summary: The crew experienced multiple airspeed and altitude disagreement warnings during descent into ZZZ at FL 220, likely caused by pitot line issues on a long-parked aircraft. They managed the unreliable airspeed using QRH procedures and split airspeed indicators to land safely, recommending pitot static checks and cover usage for parked aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported flying VOR Runway 25 approach to MRLB airport and being 5 degrees or more off centerline and offset to the runway.
summary: A pilot flying a VOR approach to Runway 25 in LNAV/VNAV noted a significant offset between the FMC profile and raw data, requiring a maneuver to land safely. The pilot questioned the VOR's accuracy after another airline executed a missed approach on Runway 7 due to a 2,500-foot lateral offset.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the First Officer inadvertently turned off the number one engine rather than engine number 2 during taxi-in resulting in a momentary EGT spike. Both crew members cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: During taxi at ZZZZ, the First Officer mistakenly selected Engine 1 instead of Engine 2 for shutdown, causing a transient EGT exceedance when the Captain's correction led to the switch being returned to ON. The incident was attributed to reduced flight time and habit transfer, but required only minimal inspection with no operational delays.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported an 'electrical burning smell' during initial climb resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: Flight attendants reported an electrical burning smell in the forward galley just prior to leveling off at FL340. The crew returned to ZZZ, performed the smoke/fumes checklist, and executed an overweight landing with no fire or deviations found.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported safety and health concerns with personnel having to wear face masks.
summary: The pilot reported that mandatory mask policies for flight attendants and ground personnel may cause fatigue, communication degradation, and safety risks during heavy exertion or noisy operations. The reporter argues that insufficient research and cost-benefit analysis were conducted regarding these potential harms to aviation safety.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a CFTT event during approach to ABQ airport.
summary: During a visual approach to El Paso Runway 22, the crew descended to 5,100 feet and received a "too low" alert from Tower, prompting a climb to 5,500 feet. The crew landed safely, and ATC later confirmed the approach was legal despite the alert, attributing the issue to a steep angle and proximity.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that a foreign airport under COVID-19 closure scheduling does not allow for proper pre-flight procedures.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X faced an unrealistic 10-minute departure window at ZZZZ airport due to a scheduled shutdown at XA:00 local. Despite delays from deplaning and a last-minute departure change, the crew safely took off at XX:03Z, attributing the unsafe pressure to poor scheduling rather than operational failure.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported safety related concerns with flying into and out of a challenging foreign airport. Reporter cited lack of flying, training and fatigue inducing scheduling all increase the risk of flying into this location.
summary: A four-pilot crew operating an [aircraft type] on a training sequence into and out of ZZZZ reported that night training, reduced proficiency, and a fatiguing schedule created a safety risk. The reporter concluded that while no incident occurred, the combination of night operations, terrain challenges, and inadequate rest opportunities threatened crew performance.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported an Oceanic flight experiencing maintenance issues was not able to establish voice communications with the Dispatcher and the flight crew did not send ACARs messages through the correct channels so they were unable to connect with maintenance control.
summary: The flight crew diverted due to left flap disagree and autopilot aileron alerts, unable to troubleshoot via SATCOM or VHF phone patch. The reporter attributed the issue to maintenance communication failures, noting that reliance on ACARS excluded Maintenance from the loop and delayed resolution.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported one of their aircraft was found to have wiring issues causing the ADS-B to malfunction. The aircraft had been in storage for an extended time period.
summary: The airline received two FAA notifications that Aircraft X was not broadcasting ADS-B Out parameters. After deferring the issue for a year, maintenance in ZZZ1 found an uncapped wire not specified in Certificate of Approval X.

synopsis: GA pilot reported that while on short final to JZP, a non-towered airport, another aircraft taxied onto the runway and was not communicating on CTAF.
summary: A pilot on short final aborted a landing and executed a sidestep after another aircraft entered the runway without checking final or responding to CTAF calls. The intruding aircraft failed to make radio contact despite the pilot's warnings and visible landing lights.

synopsis: GA pilot descending into IWS non-towered airport reported they took evasive action to avoid traffic and climbed into Class B airspace without a clearance.
summary: The pilot, flying a low-wing aircraft prior to descent at a non-towered airport, initiated a rapid climb to avoid unseen traffic shown on ADS-B. This evasive maneuver caused an unintentional entry into Class B airspace without clearance, though the pilot subsequently descended and landed safely.

synopsis: GA Flight Instructor reported an NMAC during climbout while practicing touch and goes at SLN airport. Reporter stated the conflicting aircraft was never pointed out by ATC requiring a level-off evasive maneuver from the student.
summary: During a student touch-and-go on Runway 36 at SLN, a helicopter crossed the runway head-on 200 feet above the aircraft during climbout. The pilot attributed the near-miss to SLN Tower failing to issue traffic advisories despite acknowledging the helicopter's presence.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC with a UAV near LZU airport.
summary: Pilots receiving flight following from Approach spotted a suspected fixed-wing UAS at 5,300 feet and executed a climbing right turn to avoid it. Approach confirmed no other traffic was in the area after the crew reported the tailless, five-foot wingspan object.

synopsis: PA-32 pilot reported experiencing electrical failure in flight and nose wheel collapse on landing after emergency deployment of the landing gear.
summary: During approach to ZZZ, the pilot experienced total electrical failure, preventing gear indication confirmation. After emergency gear deployment and a nose gear collapse on rollout causing a propeller strike, the aircraft stopped with no reportable damage.

synopsis: GA pilot reported taking evasive action after ATC-assigned heading resulted in close conflict with another aircraft.
summary: The pilot, while on an IFR approach to STS, executed an emergency descent of 300–400 feet after a GTN 70 warning to avoid a converging aircraft vectored nearby by ATC. The pilot attributed the conflict to an unsafe vector and radar latency, noting that immediate action was required without time to notify the controller.

synopsis: Private pilot reported a taxiway incursion and cited lack of flying and being distracted dealing with a flooded engine as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot missed a right turn onto Taxiway 1 while taxiing for departure at a known HotSpot, inadvertently entering the X/XX intersection. Contributing factors included a lack of recent cross-country operations, distraction from a flooded engine, and expectation of a different active runway due to frequent runway changes.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controller reported an unsafe shift due to weather and lack of staffing resulting in handoff and separations issues.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector Y faced severe congestion and separation conflicts due to uncoordinated handoffs from Sector X and continued departures from ZZZ1 Airport during bad weather. The controller took evasive action, including a 35-degree turn, and requested a D-side assistant who was unavailable due to staffing shortages, leading to potential military airspace violations and safety concerns regarding mask usage.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer on a Visual Approach in DAL airspace reported a NMAC and TCAS/RA alert for a VFR small aircraft.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to DAL received a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to a small aircraft in Class B airspace. The crew executed the maneuver to avoid the conflict, landed safely, and questioned why the intruder was in the airspace without specific ATC avoidance instructions.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported receiving a Ground Proximity Warning due to an incorrect flap setting but continued to land due to a medical emergency on the aircraft.
summary: During a medical diversion with priority handling, the crew missed the flaps 30 call due to a simultaneous Tower radio transmission, triggering a "too low, flaps" EGPWS warning between 600 and 700 feet. The crew extended flaps to 30 by 500 feet and elected to continue the landing due to the medical situation and runway length, resulting in a normal landing.

synopsis: Ramp workers reported they used the wrong tow bar for a B737 MAX 9 aircraft and when they removed it the aircraft rolled because the brakes were not set.
summary: Ground crew attached an incorrect tow bar to a 737-900MAX due to equipment shortage and confusion, causing the aircraft to roll back a few feet after brakes were assumed set. No injuries or damage occurred, and the correct tow bar was subsequently used to reposition the aircraft.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Regional Jet First Officer reported distractions from wake turbulence on arrival in trail of a B757 led to an unstabilized approach.
summary: The pilot reported that being placed 5nm behind a 757 caused intermittent wake turbulence, leading to a loss of situational awareness and a high, fast approach. Although the aircraft was configured by 1,000 feet AGL while still stabilizing, it landed without incident.

synopsis: Flight Crew and Dispatcher reported a bad routing due to weather that would have taken the crew over the 50 NM range for aircraft not certified to fly over water.
summary: The Captain and Dispatcher of a non-EOW aircraft exceeded the 50-mile overwater limit while deviating for thunderstorms due to congested ATC frequencies preventing timely rerouting. Although Dispatch later authorized the deviation for weather, the crew returned to the boundary safely, noting that excessive Dispatch notifications distracted from flight operations.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Push Back crew member reported the tug driver was pushing the aircraft when they observed a conflicting aircraft taxiing and immediately towed the aircraft back to parking to avoid collision. The reporter stated he crew had little experience at this gate, the ramp markings are confusing and they receive insufficient training..
summary: During a B787 pushback, an inexperienced driver followed confusing ground markings and encroached on a live taxiway, nearly colliding with an approaching B737. The driver stopped and reversed the aircraft after realizing the error, attributing the incident to unclear gate markings and insufficient specific pushback training.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported the student lost control of the aircraft landing in a crosswind and the aircraft's wing clipped a taxiway sign.
summary: A student and instructor practicing landings in a crosswind overcorrected with rudder after drifting left, clipping the right wing on a runway sign. The instructor subsequently regained control and returned the aircraft to the runway.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported communication problems with push crew after wireless headset failed and a traditional cord and head set were not available.
summary: Ground crew struggled with untrained use of new wireless headsets, causing pushback and takeoff delays. The reporter refused hand signals, and the lack of available wired headsets resulted in increased fuel burn and weight calculation delays.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the course, as depicted on this approach, gets too close to terrain.
summary: Pilots flying the VOR DME 25 approach to LIR found the FMC displayed course extended 10 miles beyond the D 10.0 teardrop turn depicted on the approach plate. They manually used Heading Select to intercept the inbound leg, noting the FMC error posed a threat of flying too close to rising terrain.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a high speed rejected takeoff due to an engine failure.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff due to a right engine failure at approximately 91 knots, stopping the aircraft on the runway. Fire services found no fire, and the crew successfully followed ECAM procedures and training protocols.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported over-speeding the aircraft and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot hand-flew the aircraft and exceeded VMO, reaching approximately 335 knots. The reporter attributed this overspeed to a lack of flying experience over the past year.

synopsis: Medium Large Transport Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival to SEA in trail of a B767.
summary: The flight crew encountered substantial wake turbulence from a preceding Boeing 767 while landing at Seattle, despite maintaining a higher and wider glide path. The aircraft experienced significant roll and pitch at 4,000–5,000 feet, which the pilots countered without injury or passenger complaints.

synopsis: E-170 Captain reported undocumented Hazmat transport by ACARS Dispatch notification stating departure Ground Personnel inadvertently left Hazmat case on board.
summary: The flight crew discovered an electrostatic fogger case left on board by ground crew at ZZZ, which was later identified as containing hazardous materials. The pilot reported that without prior notification of the Hazmat contents, the crew could not have diverted or returned to offload the item.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported on pre-flight that both O2 walk around bottles in the aft section had their masks attached to the low flow port instead of the Hi flow port as required.
summary: During preflight, a pilot discovered two aft oxygen bottles with masks incorrectly set to Low instead of High, likely due to Line Maintenance provisioning errors following a merger. The pilot corrected the settings, noting the risk of inadequate oxygen flow for passengers or crew during decompression or medical distress.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that life vest installed on an in-service aircraft were from a retired aircraft type and not approved for installation on this aircraft.
summary: A flight attendant discovered an unserviceable infant life vest kit during preflight checks and instructed a Line Maintenance Technician to manually swap incorrect adult vests with infant vests from other non-serviceable kits. The reporter attributes this systemic issue to a lack of flight attendant training on cabin safety equipment and inadequate company mitigation despite years of prior reporting.

synopsis: Technician reported that during scheduled maintenance, he replaced numerous fasteners on the right-hand wing leading edge access panels and was asked about compliance issues.
summary: A mechanic inspected Aircraft X's leading edge panels, replacing loose fasteners on the right wing per the task card. Maintenance Control later claimed a missing bonding check and incorrect sign-off, but the mechanic determined the task card did not require a bonding check and the error originated from Maintenance Control's write-up.

synopsis: Rans S6 Coyote Light Sport Aircraft pilot reported while completing a high-speed taxi to test out new brakes the aircraft veered left and struck a pole on the side of the runway.
summary: The owner/pilot lost directional control during a high-speed taxi test on the main runway after modified co-pilot brakes locked the left side. The aircraft struck a runway post, causing minor fuselage damage attributed to a sticking left master cylinder.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported communication issues with ATC left them too high near their destination and stated the Controller was overworked and understaffed.
summary: Pilots reported a late handoff between frequencies XYZ.A and XZB.A, leaving them at 22,000 feet 30 miles from the airport. They descended only due to visual conditions, attributing the delay to an ATC controller who was saturated with work due to inappropriate staffing.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported observing his student during first solo flight lose control of the aircraft during landing resulting a landing gear collapse.
summary: A student pilot flying a training aircraft experienced a hard landing and bounce on final approach to Runway XX. The aircraft porpoised, departed the runway left, and collapsed the nose gear because the student lowered the nose instead of maintaining pitch or initiating a go-around.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported they left an aircraft on a heading longer than they planned and the aircraft flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored an aircraft on downwind but failed to notice it was in a 6,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude while approaching the controller's 9,900-foot limit. The controller immediately turned the aircraft toward the final approach course and lower terrain upon realizing the proximity during the pilot's clearance readback.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 First Officer reported miscommunication when an RPDC failed and impacted systems unexpectedly.
summary: A Remote Power Distribution Unit failure caused multiple system issues, including an APU fuel valve failure, during a flight that continued to destination. Upon landing, the First Officer encountered an engine fuel valve failure while shutting down the left engine, which resolved after following the checklist.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a critical ground conflict during the start of taxi with an aircraft that had partially pushed back from nearby gate.
summary: The flight crew taxied after pushback and clearance, striking the wingtip of an adjacent aircraft that was pushing back simultaneously. The collision occurred within 10 feet of departure, causing the crew to stop and hold position upon realizing the contact.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported returning to departure airport following a malfunction of the engine bleed air valve.
summary: The flight crew experienced Bleed Valve 1 closure and anti-ice system failures shortly after takeoff while climbing through 13,000 feet in IMC. Unable to reset the valve via QRH, they returned to ZZZ to avoid icing conditions and landed safely.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported the ATC Tower at POU airport closed mid-afternoon during the COVID-19 pandemic, but unbeknownst to the reporter, the Tower had returned to normal hours of operation during this flight. Reportedly, there was no notice or NOTAM advising of the change.
summary: The pilot flying southbound at 1,800 feet near POU airport self-announced on CTAF, unaware the tower had resumed normal hours without a NOTAM. ATC advised a potential violation occurred due to this lack of notice, though the flight landed safely.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and a Flight Attendant reported a minimum crew issue prior to boarding of deadheading flight attendants and pilots.
summary: A flight attendant reported that deadheading crew members remained on board during pre-flight, causing a minimum crew violation before customer boarding. The reporter attributed this to low situational awareness regarding crew status and recommended clarifying procedures for deadheading personnel to deplane until minimum working crew is present.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported final configuration was not accomplished until 700 feet which is not in accordance with the manual.
summary: The Captain, flying a B737 MAX after a two-year absence, failed to stabilize by 1,000 feet AGL on a Visual Approach due to automation issues and a TRACON restriction to maintain 2,600 feet. He incorrectly believed final configuration was required by 500 feet, resulting in an unstable landing that should have been a go-around.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported an altitude deviation during approach caused by possible fatigue, a late runway change and lack of recent flying experience during the pandemic.
summary: The Captain, acting as Pilot Flying during descent into ZZZ, descended below the 3,000-foot clearance while distracted by FMS corrections after a last-minute runway change. The pilot leveled off at 2,600 feet to intercept the glide path, attributing the error to fatigue, lack of recency, and reduced situational awareness.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported concerns over Weather Radar powering ON when switching electrical power or releasing parking brake, possibly endangering ground crew.
summary: During post-flight duties on a B767, the crew cycled BUS TIE switches per a new Company Bulletin, causing a significant electrical shift that triggered a known weather radar power-on anomaly on both NAV Displays. The reporter states this procedure likely caused the anomaly, which poses a safety risk to ground personnel and recommends halting the procedure until the issue is resolved.

synopsis: An air carrier pilot reported GPS jamming.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent GPS jamming while approaching the Crimean area in Ukrainian airspace, indicated by ADS-B alerts and inertial mode. They suspect intentional interference from Russian military activity and recommend routing flights further east to avoid the area.

synopsis: CRJ900 First Officer reported receiving a GPWS alert while on a downwind vector for an ILS approach.
summary: During an ILS approach in ZZZ, the First Officer reported an autopilot malfunction causing an unprompted right turn and GPWS cautions. The Captain took manual control to climb away from terrain, attributing the incident to the autopilot failure and the First Officer's delayed disengagement of automation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: GA pilot reported observing a UAS passing near their aircraft as they approached an airport.
summary: Pilots on an ILS approach to Runway 27R at OPF observed a small, shiny metallic object crossing their flight path and passing under the right wing. The crew identified it as likely a drone, reported it to the tower, and landed safely without taking evasive action.
