synopsis: Inspector reported performing RII on cockpit windows and EFB installation on a B737 MAX aircraft without proper authority to perform the inspection.
summary: A mechanic signed off Required Inspection Item EFB window modification task cards on a B737 MAX aircraft while unaware they lacked specific MAX qualification. The work was subsequently re-inspected by a Quality Control inspector after the manager identified the mechanic was not authorized to sign off on MAX aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Inspector reported undocumented hazmat cargo was transported due to a breakdown of hazmat handling procedures.
summary: A Lead Avionics Technician reported that a Part Power Stops package loaded on Aircraft X lacked a required Dangerous Goods Form, despite containing UN3373 Class 9 material. The vendor failed to identify the requirement, prompting a recommendation for duplicate documentation and oral confirmation of package contents.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA student pilot reported a propeller strike during landing resulting in a runway excursion and nose gear collapse.
summary: A student pilot soloing a light aircraft bounced on touchdown during the final landing, pitched down instead of executing a go-around, and struck the propeller. The aircraft veered off the runway, collapsing the nose gear and damaging the tail before stopping, with the pilot attributing the accident to improper recovery from the bounce.

synopsis: Wide body air carrier F/O reported receiving a low altitude alert from ANC Tower on a visual approach to Runway 33.
summary: Pilots on a heavy aircraft executing a visual approach to Runway 33 at PANC drifted right of course in strong left gusty crosswinds, prompting a Tower altitude alert. The crew corrected the flight path and landed normally, noting that cold temperatures and wind required higher altitude maintenance and an earlier turn to final.

synopsis: Beech F90 pilot reported an NMAC during final approach.
summary: The pilot arrived at uncontrolled ZZZ, lost position awareness while avoiding clouds and traffic, and inadvertently aligned for Runway XY instead of the announced Runway XX. The error resulted from G1000 display settings and distraction, but the pilot descended to avoid a Cessna and completed a safe landing.

synopsis: Cessna 150 Student Pilot reported loss of engine power in climb led to an off airport landing.
summary: The pilot reported a loss of engine power during the initial climb phase of flight. No specific cause or outcome was described in the narrative.

synopsis: Reporter stated extensive burn damage was discovered when performing overhaul inspection on an A321 Escape Slide.
summary: Mechanics discovered severe burn damage on an inflatable slide unit during inspection, where the material was burned through the air holding tube. The reporter noted the unit lacks an independent battery, relying on aircraft power for lighting, and was last maintained by [Company] with an FAA 8130-3 release.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft descended much quicker than anticipated and flew below their Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X during a difficult descent in poor weather, resulting in the aircraft descending below the 3,600-foot minimum vectoring altitude before exiting the sector. The controller attributed the incident to late handoffs at high altitudes and faster-than-normal aircraft speeds caused by winds aloft.

synopsis: Ground Controller reported safety concerns with working combined positions, being overworked and under staffed especially in weather conditions.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that staffing four positions simultaneously during IFR conditions with thunderstorms and heavy traffic was unsafe and overwhelming. The controller attributed compromised safety and depleted efficiency to mandatory six-day workweeks and insufficient staffing levels.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controller working combined position reported communication issues with an aircraft after being distracted by a nearby manager having a loud conversation.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a busy arrival push into the ZZZ Metroplex reported that understaffing and conflicting in-trail requirements created an unsafe workload. The situation was worsened by an Operations Manager's loud conversation, which distracted the controller and compromised the ability to safely manage aircraft clearances.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported departure gate push back without required hazmat documents.
summary: The flight crew stopped pushback and held the aircraft during start and taxi after realizing they lacked the final dangerous goods report. They resumed operations only after receiving the required documentation from the ground team.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude overshoot during departure and cited the aircraft being light and lack of flying as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot hand-flew a light aircraft on the ZZZZZ RNAV departure from ZZZ and overshot the ZZZZZ1 restriction by 500 feet while retrieving a sunshade. The crew corrected the altitude after ATC verification, attributing the deviation to high climb rate and pilot proficiency deficits.

synopsis: Ground reporter reported ground conflict when towing aircraft.
summary: During a 777-300 tow from Gate XX to XY, the crew stopped short of an intersection to avoid a collision with an aircraft pushed in the wrong direction by a ramp agent onto the service road. The tow resumed only after the agent corrected the push and the other aircraft cleared the taxiway.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a ground conflict with a vehicle that had crossed the runway hold short lines during their landing roll requiring the Captain to immediately apply full brakes and thrust reversers.
summary: The crew landed at an untowered airport after tower closure and saw a truck crossing the hold short line near the planned exit. The pilot applied full brakes and maximum reverse, stopping within a few hundred feet of the truck, which halted before reaching the runway centerline.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported icing and engine vibration after takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that during climb out through 4,500 feet, the right engine ran rough with black smoke and vibration, causing performance deterioration in icing conditions. The crew returned to ZZZ and landed; maintenance attributed the issue to an over-rich engine mixture.

synopsis: MD10 Captain reported a loud thump on takeoff and landing. Post flight inspection revealed Hazmat pallet was not secured for air transport.
summary: A loud thump occurred during takeoff, descent, and landing of an aircraft carrying an unsecured Hazmat pallet. The incident resulted from loading personnel failing to lock the pallet due to being short-handed and hurried, while the new First Officer did not inspect the locks.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported TCAS Alert on descent.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported a TCAS alert with less than 400 feet miss distance while descending to FL330 on the HOBRKK3 arrival into LIT. The crew attributed the conflict to a Memphis Center controller vectoring them into traffic below, suspecting a lack of coordination regarding the descent clearance.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported SEA Tower Controllers were requesting gate information during a critical phase of flight. The reporter stated SEA Tower routinely transmits instructions during critical phases of flight.
summary: The pilot reported that SEA Tower distracted the crew during landing on Runway 34L by asking for gate assignments and issuing taxi instructions while the aircraft was slowing through 100 knots. The reporter stated these actions occurred during critical flight phases, causing unnecessary distraction and compromising monitoring duties.

synopsis: A departing Helicopter pilot reported they were initially assigned 2,000 feet then could not establish communications with ATC in a timely manner and ATC advised them they flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: A pilot experienced one-way communication failure with Departure while climbing to 2,000 ft. on radar vectors, despite verifying correct frequency and equipment. The controller later stated the aircraft was 400 ft. below Minimum Vectoring Altitude during the outage, though the pilot could not determine the cause.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported Lightning strike during climb.
summary: Pilots departing DFW encountered lightning strikes at 12,000 feet, causing temporary engine shutdowns and radar failure. They returned to DFW after ATC vectors, attributing the incident to premature departure resumption while severe weather remained near the airport.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a track heading deviation during approach to SJU airport. Captain stated they were confused over similar sounding intersections DONQU and DONKE.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a clearance to fix DONQU as DONKE while approaching SJU airspace due to similar names. The controller corrected the error, and the aircraft proceeded to the correct fix without further issues.

synopsis: 737-80 flight crew reported loss of engine oil inflight.
summary: The flight crew experienced a low oil quantity indication on the #2 engine of a Boeing 737 during cruise, which later progressed to low oil pressure. They executed an inflight engine shutdown and diverted to ZZZ, attributing the initial quantity warning to an indication issue while the pressure drop necessitated the shutdown.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported selecting the incorrect flap setting during a go-around maneuver. The Captain stated lack of flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer executed a go-around below 1,000 feet AGL due to a runway incursion, but the First Officer incorrectly selected flaps 2 instead of the required flaps 3. The Pilot Flying noticed the low airspeed, manually increased speed, and compensated for the error, attributing the mistake to a lack of recent experience.

synopsis: A Pilot flying in foreign airspace reported GPS jamming.
summary: Pilots reported GPS jamming while flying airway T561 between INBAL and UBONA in Russian airspace. The interference occurred within the UUWV sector, disrupting navigation signals.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported STALL FAIL message during climb.
summary: The flight crew received a STALL FAIL caution below 1000 feet after rotation. They returned to ZZZ, landed normally on the longest runway, and taxied to the gate without assistance.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported health concerns for the crew and passengers having to wear face masks after the APU was inoperative and the cabin temperature was hot.
summary: A flight attendant reported becoming lightheaded and requiring ice to cool down while wearing a mask on a fully loaded aircraft with a deferred APU returning to ZZZ1. The crew member attributed the heat stress and hypoxia risk to the combination of high cabin temperatures and mandatory mask usage, calling for a policy review.

synopsis: Technician reported disconnecting the wrong connector when complying with MEL procedures, causing a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: A mechanic inadvertently disconnected the wrong connector while complying with an MEL procedure for an inoperative engine anti-ice valve during a quick turn. The error caused an over-pressure light to illuminate after departure, resulting in the aircraft being diverted.

synopsis: Technician reported being advised of signing off for work that was not completed. Technician cited COVID-19 pandemic related worry and distraction as contributing factors.
summary: A mechanic reported signing for a bolt and bushing that was not installed due to confusing job cards and a lack of a qualified technician to verify the work. The reporter admitted installing the component despite the paperwork error, attributing the incident to pandemic-related staffing issues and new personnel working alone.

synopsis: C150 pilot flying in the middle of the night had an Electrical Power failure and could not activate airport lighting. When the pilot flew to the nearest commercial airport which was open with lighting and approached to land they had to sidestep to a parallel runway due to an opposite direction departure.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna experienced electrical failure and radio loss during descent to ZZZ1, forcing a diversion to ZZZ with 30 minutes of fuel remaining. The pilot landed on Runway XXL at ZZZ to avoid departing traffic, then secured the aircraft and acquired a backup handheld radio.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a having a near miss, possibly attributable to a malfunctioning ADSB.
summary: The pilot reported a near miss with another aircraft while flying north in a Bravo veil, noting the other plane passed 100 feet above. The pilot attributed the incident to high-wing visibility limitations and suspected non-functioning ADS-B equipment, subsequently taking evasive action.

synopsis: Private pilot flying C-150 aircraft reported NMAC with another aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced a near miss with an aircraft 100 feet above while distracted by radio operations, attributed to a high-wing blind spot and suspected ADS-B equipment failure. Post-flight checks confirmed the ADS-B Out was not transmitting, prompting the pilot to take the aircraft to an avionics shop for inspection.

synopsis: C172 Student Pilot doing solo touch and goes reported hitting a runway light.
summary: A student pilot veered right while adding power during a touch-and-go solo lap, striking a runway light. The incident occurred on the runway during the takeoff roll phase of the flight.

synopsis: GA pilot reported loss of directional control on landing roll that resulted in a runway excursion and aircraft damage.
summary: The pilot attempted a crosswind landing in gusty winds from the left seat of an aircraft with asymmetric controls, resulting in a runway excursion, ground loop, and gear collapse. The pilot attributed the accident to poor decision-making and insufficient skill for the conditions, causing aircraft damage but no injuries.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported runway incursion during taxi.
summary: A pilot with an inoperative radio crossed Runway XX at an uncontrolled airport while another aircraft began its takeoff roll. The pilot accelerated to clear the runway just as the other aircraft became airborne 200 feet away, resulting in no conflict but highlighting the risks of NORDO operations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Light aircraft Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC with another aircraft in the traffic pattern at FDK airport.
summary: A pilot in a left traffic pattern at FDK nearly collided with a departing aircraft that entered the pattern without scanning. The pilot avoided the conflict by pitching down 45 degrees to 400 feet AGL, attributing the incident to the other pilot's reckless disregard for traffic.

synopsis: Pilot reported a rejected take off after communication problems with ATC resulted in Ground Conflict.
summary: The pilot and copilot initiated a takeoff on Runway XXR after mishearing a clearance, but the Tower cancelled it at 50 AGL as a Cessna Caravan crossed the departure end. The pilot attributed the incident to the Tower's rapid instruction pace, which may have prevented the controller from verifying the readback.

synopsis: A person reported an aircraft conducted low level aerobatics over a populated area and buildings in the vicinity of the runway.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X performed reckless low-altitude maneuvers and a high-speed approach with landing gear retracted near a restaurant at GA2. The reporter describes these unauthorized airshow-style stunts as clear FAR violations that create a significant crash risk to the restaurant and nearby homes.

synopsis: Flight Attendant in Charge, along with two other flight attendants, reported a fume event resulting in physiological symptoms. Three flight attendants were evaluated as unfit to fly.
summary: Flight attendants on Aircraft X experienced a toxic fume event during descent, causing severe symptoms attributed to carbon monoxide poisoning. The Captain confirmed the bleed air issue, but the company cited FAM deviations regarding medical calls while the aircraft continued operating with an inoperative APU.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported taking a wrong turn during taxi in that required repositioning by a tug.
summary: The Captain and First Officer entered a closed portion of Taxiway X after landing due to distraction, a frozen chart, and miscommunication regarding taxiway status. The aircraft was repositioned by a tug after an unsuccessful 180-degree turn attempt, with no damage reported.

synopsis: B737 MAX Captain reported that the CAT III Placard was not visible to the flight crew due to the cockpit displays not configured properly by Maintenance.
summary: A Captain operating a Boeing MAX aircraft could not locate the digital CAT III placard during HGS operations due to Maintenance inadvertently de-selecting the display setting. The Chief Pilot confirmed the error and arranged repairs, while noting a lack of manual guidance regarding the Captain-side placard location.

synopsis: B737 MAX series flight crew reported landing without Tower clearance. The FO cited MAX series differences as contributing.
summary: The crew landed a Boeing MAX without Tower clearance after failing to switch frequencies due to distraction from gusty winds and unfamiliarity with the aircraft following a short-notice change from a -800. The First Officer did not contact Tower as instructed, and the Captain realized the error only after clearing the runway.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew came within 100 feet of a drone while on final approach at LAS airport.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to Runway 1 Right at LAS observed a drone approximately 100 feet overhead while descending through 4,100 feet MSL. They reported the encounter to the Tower and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a max effort stop was required on the landing roll to avoid a collision with a truck crossing the runway.
summary: During landing roll-out on Runway XX, the Captain applied full brakes and reversers to stop 100 feet from a fuel truck crossing the runway. The reporter attributes the incident to the truck driver failing to monitor CTAF or other airport frequencies while operating on the airfield.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported decreasing oil quantity followed by total loss of oil pressure caused an inflight shut down and a precautionary landing at destination airport.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain experienced an Engine 2 oil leak during cruise, causing low quantity and pressure indications. They declared a mayday, shut down the engine, and landed safely at ZZZ, attributing the failure to an undetected leak missed during prior maintenance checks.

synopsis: A321 flight and cabin crews reported a flight attendant was injured during taxi out when the First Officer abruptly applied brakes to avoid a collision with a vehicle.
summary: During taxi out, a white van failed to yield, causing the First Officer to brake heavily and injure a flight attendant. The aircraft returned to the gate for medical attention after the pilot reported the near-collision to Ground Control.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain and a Flight Attendant reported a passenger's child was resisting wearing a face mask. After this problem started the parent then stated the child was under 2 and did not need to wear the face mask.
summary: During pushback, the Captain and Flight Attendant disputed a passenger count due to a child's mask compliance, leading the Captain to initially count the child as a passenger rather than an infant. The Captain later admitted to mistakenly counting the infant as a child due to high workload and fatigue, though the flight continued without incident.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE-525 flight crew reported communications failure caused a runway incursion and another aircraft to execute a go around.
summary: A departing crew crossed the hold short line at ZZZ after a "line up and wait" clearance before receiving a conflicting "hold short" instruction due to a suspected radio dead spot. The situation caused an arriving aircraft to go around, and the crew resolved the communication issue by switching to a second radio with a topside antenna.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported a fume event during arrival deplaning due to ground crew spraying the cargo bins without previously notifying the fight crew. Flight crew experienced temporary physiological symptoms.
summary: Flight crew on Aircraft X experienced pesticide odor and minor symptoms during deplaning at ZZZZ when ground spraying began before recirculation fans were fully secured. The incident resolved quickly, prompting recommendations for improved coordination and fan deselection prior to cargo bin spraying.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported loss of engine power and elected to execute an Air Turn Back to a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot reported a loss of power and vibration in a single-engine aircraft at 1,800 feet after departing ZZZ, caused by a loss of compression in cylinder 4. The pilot maintained altitude, landed safely, and the aircraft was grounded for repairs with no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported an NMAC event with 5-6 hang gliders while descending toward destination with VFR Flight Following.
summary: A pilot flying VFR with flight following while descending south of Orlando encountered 5-6 hang gliders within 100-200 feet. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the hang gliders being undetectable on radar and operating without notifying ATC.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC during approach and landing roll at LVJ airport. The pilot stated the aircraft's radio was disabled which contributed to the event.
summary: A pilot flying a position flight into Houston with a failed radio was escorted by a friend who made CTAF calls. During the landing roll, another aircraft overflew at 150 feet, forcing that pilot to execute a go-around due to the close proximity.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported a student pilot flew through the final approach course and below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller vectored a student pilot in Aircraft X onto an approach but the aircraft flew through final into a 6000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude. The controller issued a low altitude alert, and the crew subsequently cancelled IFR to continue training under VFR conditions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported procedure disagreements between the FMC and the chart exist on the PVR OBRUG 1B Arrival.
summary: A pilot descending into MMPR on the OBRUG 1B reported a conflict between the FMC constraint to cross OBRUB at or above FL230 and the chart requirement to cross at FL230. After being cleared to FL200 then "descend via" at FL260, the pilot deleted the FMC constraint and crossed above FL230, questioning which source was correct.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an altitude deviation during approach to LAS resulting in a CFTT. The crew mistakenly believed they had been cleared for a visual approach which contributed to the event.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring mistakenly dialed the altitude window to zero while high on the RNAV (GPS) 1R approach at LAS, causing an unauthorized descent to 6,000 feet instead of the cleared 6,600 feet. After ATC confirmed the clearance and visual conditions, the crew completed the visual approach and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported their FMC Database contained a different crossing restriction than what was published on their Jeppesen chart.
summary: The flight crew identified a discrepancy between the Jeppesen OBRUG 1B arrival chart and the FMC database regarding the OBRUG crossing restriction at FL 230. The chart specified "at FL 230" while the FMC defaulted to "at or above FL 230," prompting a recommendation to check other arrivals for similar errors.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported the surface area before the landing threshold appears to look like a usable runway surface and could cause confusion while back taxiing for departure which is a common procedure at this airport.
summary: The pilot and First Officer observed a potential hazard while back taxiing to Runway 10, where the unprepared surface matched the bleached white runway, obscuring the threshold. The reporter noted this lack of contrast, combined with controller instructions for quick back taxiing, could create a safety risk, especially at night.

synopsis: Captain reported a fumes event during cruise resulting in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew at FL390 diverted to ZZZ after detecting an acrid electrical odor from the flight deck ventilation system. Executing the unannunciated fumes checklist by turning off IFE and recirculating fans eliminated the odor, leading to a normal landing despite initial communication difficulties with the destination.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a GPWS event during approach to AVL airport requiring a pull up maneuver.
summary: During an RNAV 35 approach to AVL, the crew received a GPWS terrain alert while descending from 6,000 to 5,100 feet due to a high descent rate of 1,500 FPM. The pilot attributed the false alert to wind drift near a tall antenna and noted that future approaches should involve earlier altitude requests and slower descent rates.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported miscommunication lead to a departure with a fuel leak that required a diversion and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine fuel leak undetected during preflight, despite ATC reports of vapor and a runway inspection confirming fuel on the ground. The aircraft diverted to ZZZ2 after an ECAM fuel imbalance warning, landing safely with ARFF support to inspect the engine.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported receiving a Ground Proximity Warning during initial approach into HLN airport.
summary: Pilots descending into HLN for a visual approach received a clearance to 10,000 feet but lost radar vectors. A GPWS terrain alarm occurred because the aircraft descended prematurely to the Final Approach Fix altitude instead of following segment-by-segment approach altitudes, requiring an immediate climb.

synopsis: Citation flight crew reported experiencing pressurization malfunction after takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported an EMERG PRESS ON light illuminating while climbing out of ZZZ. After running the checklist failed to resolve the issue, the pilot advised ATC and landed back at ZZZ.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported a loss of nose wheel steering caused the aircraft to be towed to the gate after landing.
summary: During approach, a 'Steer Fail' message triggered a go-around and QRH troubleshooting, leading ATC to declare an emergency despite the crew's assessment. The aircraft landed safely using rudder and differential braking but required a high-speed tug tow to the gate due to failed tiller steering and an unsuccessful ground reset.

synopsis: Technician reported that an out of calibration borrowed tool with altered calibration date was used to conduct maintenance on an aircraft.
summary: The Crew Chief at ZZZ used a tool with expired calibration and an altered date to complete a Nose Landing Gear Shock Strut Fluid Check because assigned mechanics lacked valid tooling. He reportedly borrows tools from other airlines with part numbers differing from the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: Technicians reported that an aircraft anti skid module was improperly placed on MEL and dispatched for service.
summary: ZZZ Maintenance discovered a hydraulic leak in Aircraft X's Normal Anti-Skid Module and deferred the system by capping lines after Engineering Authorization. The aircraft flew multiple legs without incident, as the left gear remained pressurized via secondary hydraulic redundancies.

synopsis: GA student pilot reported landing while another aircraft was still on the runway at GTU airport.
summary: A student pilot landed on Runway 18 while another aircraft remained on the runway, misinterpreting a go-around instruction as intended for a following aircraft. The pilot attributed the error to distraction during the round-out and failure to recall the rule against landing behind an aircraft still on the runway.

synopsis: Instructor reported an NMAC event during a training flight with an aircraft that was dropping skydivers.
summary: A flight instructor and student in Aircraft X encountered a jump aircraft (Aircraft Y) within 300 feet vertically while performing low-level maneuvers near an uncharted "Area 51" dropzone. The near-miss resulted from maneuver fixation, poor traffic awareness, and ambiguous location references, prompting the crew to descend and exit the area.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Solo pilot reported encountering windshear during landing flare which caused the aircraft to departed the runway surface.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing at ZZZ, sudden wind gusts caused the aircraft to bounce and drift off the runway into soft sand and tumbleweeds. The pilot applied rudder and brakes to stop the aircraft in the sand after the wheels were pulled left by the terrain.

synopsis: Pilot reported differences in MEL procedures listed for a TKS deicing system that was not installed on the aircraft.
summary: The pilot discovered low TKS fluid and a conflicting MEL deferral listing the system as "not installed" during preflight. After operating the flight based on clear weather forecasts, the pilot parked the aircraft while Operations coordinated with the FAA to resolve the MEL discrepancy.

synopsis: Center Controller reported a military aircraft reported a NMAC with another military aircraft as they were exiting their refueling track.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and Y under MARSA, resulting in a near collision with 0.12 miles and 400 feet separation when Aircraft Y climbed through FL265 while Aircraft X was at FL270. The controller attributed the event to relying on MARSA without applying IFR separation rules and identified a need to radar identify and separate aircraft before terminating MARSA.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a vector to final for a visual approach to BHM from ATC that created a conflict with a published ground obstacle.
summary: Pilots vectored for a visual approach to BHM Runway 6 reported that an ATC clearance direct to MCDEN at 3,000 feet would have flown over a 2,049-foot tower. The crew requested and received a revised clearance direct to CEMPO to avoid the obstacle, recommending ATC change policy to prevent future hazards.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence departing DFW in trail of a B747.
summary: The crew departed Runway 18L behind a B747 and encountered wake turbulence during a right turn to BLECO, causing an uncommanded roll and bank angle warning. The Pilot Flying corrected the bank, and the reporter attributed the incident to insufficient spacing between the Heavy aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a CFIT event during approach under Approach Control which was followed by an uneventful visual landing.
summary: The flight crew received a GPWS terrain caution while descending from 6,000 to 5,100 feet on a left base leg to Runway 35 at AVL at night. The crew climbed back to 6,000 feet and switched to a visual approach, noting the descent violated the 6,200-foot minimum sector altitude.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude and track heading deviation during approach to an international airport. The crew stated this sequence of flights, since the COVID-19 pandemic started, are very long and fatiguing which may have been a factor in the event.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway XXL, the autopilot executed an aggressive right turn to intercept an unstable Localizer, prompting the Captain to disconnect automation and manually recover. The crew attributed the event to potential software or signal issues, while noting that fatigue and differing situational awareness contributed to the aggressive response and temporary altitude deviation.

synopsis: A Citation pilot reported experiencing their aircraft unexpectedly pitched up on two different occasions and was informed by another pilot they had experienced the same issue.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced excessive immediate pitch-up forces immediately after liftoff, requiring manual nose-down trim to control the aircraft. The reporter suspects the cause was incorrect trim rigging, noting a similar but less severe event on the previous flight.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a ground conflict after they began their takeoff roll with an aircraft crossing their runway 1,500 feet ahead.
summary: A pilot training a pre-solo student initiated a takeoff roll without clearance, stopping 1,000 feet from a Piper Cherokee crossing the runway. The incident was caused by expectation bias and inattentiveness, resulting in a stop after tower intervention.

synopsis: GA pilot reported not realizing the field was Tower controlled and almost entered a taxiway without clearance.
summary: The pilot, unfamiliar with a small airport, attempted to taxi to Runway 36 using the CTAF frequency but was stopped by a Tower controller who clarified the field was tower-controlled. The pilot realized the chart indicated part-time tower operations, avoided entering the taxiway near another aircraft, and attributed the error to high operational tempo and insufficient chart review.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported not performing the Before Taxi Checklist and subsequently had not set the flaps to the takeoff setting prior to moving the aircraft. Reporter cited distraction from dealing with face mask issues in the cabin area may have contributed to the event.
summary: The Captain and First Officer moved the aircraft to burn fuel after a runway change but failed to set takeoff flaps or complete the Before Taxi Checklist before taxiing. The Captain attributed this error to distraction from pre-pushback passenger issues and interrupting the First Officer's flow, though the flight departed uneventfully after correcting the configuration.

synopsis: B737 MAX flight crew reported the aircraft abruptly pitched down during flap extension while on a visual approach with automation engaged. Pilot flying disconnected automation and executed an uneventful landing.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway XXR, the aircraft abruptly pitched down 8 to 10 degrees as the Captain selected Flaps 30, triggering a GPWS 'Caution Obstacle' alert. The First Officer disengaged the autopilot and autothrottle to correct the flight path and land uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a track heading deviation during cruise after instituting a 2 mile right offset as a SLOP while still under radar contact. Captain cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew instituted a 2-mile right offset for SLOP while still under radar service, prompting an ATC query about their track. The pilots attributed this error to low recent flight time and a failure to recall the standard operating procedure requiring SLOP only after losing radar contact.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported receiving a low oil ECAM warning for the Number 2 engine during cruise. The crew followed QRH procedures and decided to shut the engine down and divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew at FL360 diverted to ZZZ after an ECAM low oil quantity advisory on Engine 2 escalated to low oil pressure, requiring an engine shutdown. Following priority handling and a gradual descent, the aircraft made an overweight landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a fume event during pre-flight resulting in flight cancellation for maintenance action.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance identified a foul odor at the gate caused by the number 1 air conditioning pack on an A320. The aircraft departed the next day with Pack 1 deferred under the MEL, prompting the captain to recommend a safety campaign on odor events.

synopsis: Captain reported an altitude deviation during departure.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying and Pilot Flying briefed the ZZZZZX departure from ZZZ, incorrectly stating all altitudes were at or above 2,000 feet at ZZZZZ1. The reporter attributed this error to assuming post-COVID restriction changes rather than verifying the required crossing altitude.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot conducting a practice VOR Approach to a non towered airport reported a tower near the final approach course two miles from the runway is not depicted on any charts.
summary: A pilot conducting a VFR practice approach on the BFR VOR 13 procedure observed an uncharted tower approximately 17.4 DME from the OOM VOR on Radial 159. The obstruction, located about two miles right of the runway, caused the pilot to avoid using this approach in IMC due to insufficient separation.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC during cruise in ZOA Class E airspace.
summary: The pilot and copilot in a private aircraft experienced a near mid-air collision at 6,500 feet while en route from Oakland to ZZZ1. The incident occurred because the pilot was distracted by radio communications and failed to scan for traffic or monitor ADS-B, allowing another aircraft to pass immediately beneath them.

synopsis: Lake LA4-200EP pilot reported a forced landing on a dirt road due to engine loss of power.
summary: The pilot of a Lake Amphibian experienced an engine power loss and executed a forced landing on a dirt road. The narrative does not specify the phase of flight, the cause of the power loss, or the outcome of the landing.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported they were going to ferry an aircraft for a friend but while on the ramp a FSDO official approached them and told them the aircraft was not allowed to fly due to improper maintenance.
summary: A pilot and a passenger attempted to relocate a tagged Cessna 172, but an FSDO official stopped them on the ramp. The aircraft was grounded because exterior brackets were improperly removed with bolts instead of rivets, rendering it unairworthy until Cessna or a recognized authority addressed the violation.

synopsis: A departing General Aviation pilot reported they altered their course to avoid parachutists near the airport.
summary: The departing pilot encountered skydivers under canopy south of the runway while climbing to 400 feet after takeoff on Runway 10. The pilot attributed the conflict to a lack of notification from the jump aircraft or AWOS regarding active skydiving operations.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Helicopter Single Pilot reported a near miss with a drone at 1,200 ft.
summary: A helicopter pilot encountered a suspected four-rotor drone while circling a landmark at 1,200 ft. The pilot descended to avoid the object but could not locate the operator after making a wide circle.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported soon after assuming control of the sector they observed an aircraft which had already been cleared for an approach descend below the Minimum IFR Altitude due to the previous controller not issuing the appropriate crossing restriction.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a third aircraft descending below the 5,600-foot Minimum IFR Altitude while managing inbound traffic. The controller attributed the situation to expectation bias and noted the previous controller failed to issue proper crossing restrictions or vectors to maintain safe altitudes.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: MRI Tower Controller reported an aircraft was lined up for a taxiway instead of the runway resulting in a conflict and go-around. Reporter stated this is a common occurrence and cited worn runway and taxiway markings may be contributing to the events.
summary: Aircraft X initiated a go-around while final for Runway 25 after reporting a phantom aircraft, which controllers could not see. The pilot later attributed the error to worn markings causing confusion with Taxiway N, recommending fresh paint and diagram updates.

synopsis: Eugene TRACON Controller reported an unsafe operation with numerous VFR aircraft at the CVO uncontrolled airport.
summary: An ATC controller reported that Aircraft X, an IFR arrival at CVO, deviated from its missed approach and flew below MVA to avoid uncontrolled VFR traffic. The controller attributed the incident to disorderly VFR operations at CVO and recommended establishing a tower and upgrading EUG to Class C airspace.

synopsis: EUG TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict between an air carrier aircraft and a VFR helicopter. Controller suggested EUG should be a Class C airport requiring VFR aircraft to be in contact with ATC while crossing air carrier approach/departure paths.
summary: An ATC controller reported a potential conflict between an RNAV approach Aircraft X and a VFR Aircraft Y crossing the approach path 500 feet below. The controller noted that Aircraft Y was not in contact with ATC while crossing conflicting altitudes, suggesting Class C airspace is needed to prevent future dangerous situations.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported an aircraft descended below its assigned altitude and into a Restricted Area. The reporter has witnessed this occurring at other times and suggested a fix with an altitude restriction above the Restricted Airspace as is done on other routes.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a pilot descend below the 29,000-foot restriction into active Restricted Airspace R2501, reaching 25,200 feet. The controller issued an immediate climb to 29,000 feet to exit the airspace, attributing the deviation to unclear arrival restrictions.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported the PFD installed in the MAX aircraft is too small and hard to read, posing a safety issue.
summary: A pilot reported that the Boeing 737 MAX Primary Flight Display is too small to read clearly during non-normal situations like engine failure or MCAS issues. The pilot suggested redesigning the display to match the 737 NG format to ensure pilots can maintain aircraft control effectively.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the lack of recent experience caused the improper use of SOP's during a takeoff configuration irregularity.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain took off from Runway X in ZZZ with a red-lined TO indication on the FMA due to a Flight Director problem. The Captain proceeded despite the fault, and the PM's lack of recent experience delayed recognizing the error, resulting in an unsafe departure that should have been aborted.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported executing a go-around after encountering wake turbulence from previous arrival on an intersecting runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding arrival on Runway 27R while flaring for a visual approach to Runway 35 at PHL. The resulting wing dip and enhanced ground effect caused the aircraft to float, prompting a successful go-around and subsequent landing on Runway 27R.

synopsis: Regional Jet Captain reported similar sounding fixes EMMLY instead of EMILY, resulted in a turn off course.
summary: During climb, the crew incorrectly entered waypoint EMILY instead of EMMLY into the FMS due to a spelling cross-check error. ATC identified the heading deviation, provided the correct heading, and the crew corrected the waypoint to continue safely.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported executing a go-around on approach to HKG after receiving a low altitude alert from ATC.
summary: The flight crew descended below the required altitude on the ILS 25L approach to Hong Kong, triggering an ATC low altitude alert and a missed approach. The crew believed they were at 4,500 feet with altimeter setting 1006, but ATC reported they were 200 feet low, possibly due to an altimeter error.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate airport after shutting down #2 engine following loss of oil quantity.
summary: The flight crew diverted en route after an ECAM low oil quantity advisory on engine two escalated to low oil pressure, requiring an engine shutdown. Following QRH procedures, they executed an overweight landing at the alternate airport, attributing the event to a mechanical issue.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude deviation caused by lack of recent flight experience, fatigue and three clearance changes before departure.
summary: Pilots missed the 3,000-foot SID altitude constraint after a runway and departure change to ZZZZZ2, climbing to 3,700 feet before correcting. The error was attributed to distraction, fatigue, and lack of recent experience following a six-month furlough.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an abrupt stop was required to avoid a collision during low visibility taxi at DEN involving another air carrier on a different Ground Control frequency.
summary: During taxi out in 400 RVR, DEN Ground issued conflicting clearances on separate frequencies, causing a near miss between our aircraft and another carrier on Taxiway WA. We stopped just before collision after ATC admitted the error of issuing simultaneous clearances to both aircraft.

synopsis: Flight crew reported having a stick shaker activation during a go around, which was attributed to a hydraulic system failure.
summary: The First Officer (PF) and Captain (PM) experienced a complete Center hydraulic system failure during an RNAV approach to ZZZ, causing a stick shaker activation due to poor airspeed monitoring. After executing a go-around and completing the QRH, the crew switched roles and successfully landed with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported receiving a Low Altitude Alert from the tower controller.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 25L at HKG, the crew received a low altitude alert and executed a go-around after ATC reported the aircraft was 200 feet below the required altitude at the LOTUS waypoint. The incident occurred while the Pilot Monitoring checked speed restrictions on the EFB, allowing the aircraft to descend below the glideslope in FLCH mode without immediate detection.

synopsis: Captain reported a diversion and fuel dumping due to trailing edge flap drive and position sensing/control failure.
summary: The crew experienced flap drive system failures and a flap overspeed event during departure from ZZZZ. They diverted to ZZZZ1, dumped fuel, and burned weight to land safely at maximum landing weight due to tire speed limitations.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported icing conditions resulted in unreliable airspeed indications, followed by a descent and diversion to a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered unreliable airspeed and altimeter indications on a Boeing 737 while descending through light rime icing to FL300. They diverted to ZZZ, suspecting the pitot-static heating system was overwhelmed, and landed safely after instruments normalized below 15,000 feet.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a flight attendant notified them the ovens were turned off due to odor in forward galley.
summary: During cruise, a flight attendant reported a "dirty socks" odor from forward galley oven #2, which dissipated after being turned off. The pilot pulled both oven circuit breakers, suspecting the cause was lack of use for one year, and notified maintenance.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a speed deviation occurred during the SID procedure and stated that a prolonged period of time off for both pilots was the main cause.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, both returning from extended leave, accelerated to 280 knots during climb above 10,000 feet on the ZZZZZX departure because the 250-knot restriction was not programmed in the FMS. The Captain attributed the error to distraction from re-qualification and a failure to communicate his speed management technique to the crew.

synopsis: Regional Jet Captain reported confusion with the amount of ORD NOTAMS, poor signage and charting, which resulted in taxiway and runway incursion.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed a hold-short line for closed Runway 27L while taxiing at ORD due to missing signage and inaccurate Jeppesen charts. The reporter attributed the incident to poor airport layout and charting, noting the controller failed to issue a specific crossing clearance.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a flap half speed and spoiler/stab fault status message resulted in a diversion and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: During takeoff from ZZZ, the crew encountered Flap Half Speed and SPLR/STAB faults followed by an overspeed clacker activation at 250 knots. They diverted to ZZZ1 for a high-speed landing with flaps extended, where maintenance grounded the aircraft after failing to determine the cause.

synopsis: Regional Jet Captain reported issued LIINN published holding on the LIINN3 STAR is not depicted on Jeppesen plates.
summary: Pilots flying the LIINN3 Arrival into CLT found the published hold at LIINN missing from their Jepps chart but present on the NOAA chart. After advising ATC, they were reassigned to hold on current heading instead of the published northwest hold.

synopsis: EMB XRJ-145 Captain reported auto flight system malfunctioned during departure and arrival phase by uncommanded reversion to Roll-Go Around mode.
summary: Pilots experienced uncommanded FMS switches to ROLL-GA mode during departure and approach, causing an autopilot-initiated climb from 7,400 to 7,600 feet. The Pilot Flying disengaged the autopilot, arrested the climb, and hand-flew a visual landing after the FMS repeatedly reverted to Go Around mode despite re-sequencing attempts.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Medium Transport Crew reported conflicting departure instructions issued by ATC verses the MDW3 SID narrative, resulted in a deviation.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted the Midway 5 SID text and depiction during departure from Runway 04R, initially turning right to 100 degrees instead of the tower-assigned left turn to 250 degrees. The crew corrected the heading immediately after tower intervention, attributing the error to the confusing chart narrative and a failure to clarify instructions with ATC.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine failure during taxi and elected to evacuate the aircraft because of fuel streaming out of the engine drains.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine failure while taxiing to Runway X, causing a fuel leak from the cowl drain tube. The pilot evacuated two passengers to the grass due to distraction while coordinating transport, forgetting to turn off the fuel pump, which likely caused the leak.

synopsis: A pilot reported after temporarily losing control of the aircraft entering a downdraft the Captain side attitude indicator began malfunctioning.
summary: The pilot experienced a Captain-side attitude indicator failure during IMC turbulence on the first leg, causing a temporary loss of control with altitude and heading deviations. The pilot stabilized the aircraft using the co-pilot's instruments, climbed to VMC conditions, and continued to the destination where the faulty unit was replaced.

synopsis: An Air Taxi pilot reported their brakes froze causing all four main tires to blow out during landing.
summary: The crew departed from a slush-covered runway, and cold weather caused the brakes to freeze. Upon landing, all four main tires blew out, prompting ATC to close the runway.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: X Cub Instructor reported student's loss of directional control during crosswind landing training resulting in a ground loop.
summary: A pilot training a student on crosswind landings in a taildragger experienced a ground loop when the wind picked up. The narrative does not specify the aircraft type, altitude, or further outcome.

synopsis: Instructor reported student failed to maintain directional during landing training resulting in a ground contact with the wing tip.
summary: An instructor and a learner pilot ground looped an aircraft during landing at ZZZ Airport after a bounce and left gust caused a rightward drift. The learner failed to correct the crosswind, and the instructor failed to call for a go-around, resulting in minor right wing tip damage and termination of the lesson.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot departing a non towered airport reported a NMAC with an arriving aircraft.
summary: A helicopter crew departing an uncontrolled airport experienced a near-midair conflict with a Piper Twin landing on an intersecting runway due to blocked visibility, garbled radio calls, and confusion over the active runway. No evasive action was taken, and both aircraft continued operations after acknowledging the miscommunication.

synopsis: A GA pilot on a VFR flight receiving flight following reported a NMAC with VFR traffic they had been issued and had in sight.
summary: A VFR pilot flying a non-ADS-B equipped rental aircraft at 6,500 feet in Class E airspace took evasive action after Approach failed to provide updated advisories on a converging Bonanza. The pilot climbed 200 to 300 feet, resulting in a separation of less than 200 feet as the Bonanza passed below and behind.

synopsis: C172 flight Instructor reported an NMAC during approach to landing as a result of turning down the radio volume and not hearing an inbound aircraft's radio transmissions.
summary: A flight instructor and student conducting training at ZZZ had a near miss on final approach to Runway 21 with another aircraft. The instructor failed to hear the other pilot's radio calls because the COM 1 volume was turned down too low during steep turn practice.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC in aerobatic practice area with an aircraft from a flight school. Pilot stated they would now use the school's frequency to maintain situational awareness.
summary: A solo pilot conducting aerobatics in a Cessna near [Location] experienced a near-midair collision with a ZZZ flight school aircraft while diving from 3,500 to 2,500 feet. The pilot avoided the conflict by executing a hard right climbing turn, attributing the event to the other aircraft being hidden by ground clutter and below radar coverage.

synopsis: Solo student pilot reported departing the runway surface on landing resulting in damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that after an unremarkable landing, the aircraft drifted right upon braking and exited the runway at low speed. While turning back to the runway, the horizontal stabilizer struck an embankment, followed by a normal shutdown.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General Aviation Fixed Wing pilot report his parked aircraft was severely buffeted by rotor wash from landing helicopters.
summary: A pilot on the ramp at UOX experienced severe propwash from two helicopters making a formation landing on Runway 9. The pilot's immediate control inputs prevented aircraft damage, though the incident highlighted hazardous training operations near tiedown areas.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported refusing an aircraft after a fume/smoke event during pre-flight. Captain stated that Maintenance did not determine the cause of the smoke event.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X experienced cockpit smoke and an electrical fire shortly after disconnecting the GPU, which maintenance attributed to a faulty Number 2 CDU. The Captain refused to fly the aircraft because the smoke's root cause was not investigated, despite maintenance deferring the CDU and company pressure to proceed.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine failure on landing and was forced to make an off field landing due to fuel starvation.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 experienced an abrupt engine stop on downwind due to fuel exhaustion, despite the JPI 450 fuel computer indicating 13 gallons remaining. The pilot executed a successful off-airport landing with no injuries and minor aircraft damage.

synopsis: Single-piloted Chancellor pilot reported impacting a parked aircraft while taxiing.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft contacted an unoccupied parked aircraft while taxiing. There were no injuries and, to the pilot's knowledge, no substantial damage occurred.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported descending below published minimums during a practice VOR approach.
summary: During a simulated instrument approach in a training aircraft, the student pilot descended to 540 feet while wearing foggles near the AYCEE intersection. The instructor ordered an immediate climb due to the inability to see terrain height, after which the student removed the foggles to continue the circling approach.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported that during landing rollout another aircraft began takeoff roll from the opposite end of the runway without making any radio calls. Reporter exited the runway and stated that the other aircraft stopped on the runway.
summary: An instructor and student in a VOR approach circle-to-land conducted a touch-and-go when another aircraft initiated an opposite-direction takeoff roll without checking for traffic. The instructor diverted to an intersecting runway, and the other pilot stopped, though the reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot's failure to verify runway clearance.

synopsis: Hobbyist drone pilot was unaware they were flying in controlled airspace until approached by a public official.
summary: A recreational pilot flying a DJI drone near ZZZ Harbor received a ticket for operating within 2.5 miles of an airport without tower permission or proper FAA registration. The pilot reported the incident after realizing they lacked the required Part 107 license and failed to display registration markings on the aircraft.

synopsis: First Officer reported conflicting procedures between B737 NG and B737 MAX flight operating manuals.
summary: A pilot reported a safety concern regarding conflicting engine run-up requirements for icing conditions between the cold temperature reference page and the AOM for NG and MAX aircraft. The pilot noted the AOM is more restrictive and warned that high task loading during rapidly changing weather could cause crews to forget these critical procedures.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported compressor stalls during climb and elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced two loud bangs and vibrations from the #2 engine while climbing through 8,500 ft. MSL out of ZZZ, suspecting a compressor stall. After leveling at 9,000 ft. and completing checklists, they returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing on Runway 28R.

synopsis: Ramp employee reported that while towing an aircraft to the gate, a nearby aircraft began to push back, almost clipping the wings of the aircraft being towed.
summary: A ground handler towing Aircraft X to gate XX stopped the tug to retrieve an observer when Aircraft Y began pushing from gate XY, nearly clipping wings. The reporter attributed the near-miss to Aircraft Y pushing off while the handler was still parking Aircraft X.

synopsis: Air Carrier ground personnel reported ground handling issues with new procedure/equipment. Reporter recommends reverting to previous procedure.
summary: Ramp staff reported that the TC175 scanner failed to distinguish between freight and human remains, complicating aircraft servicing. The reporter attributed this issue to new training that eliminated the printed Departure Staging Guide, recommending its reinstatement.

synopsis: Air Carrier ground personnel reported Dangerous Goods mistakenly not loaded on departed flight. DG rescheduled on subsequent flight.
summary: Ground staff ZZZZ and ZZZ investigated a Human Remains shipment for Aircraft X. They located the intact cart at the gate, confirmed it was loaded, and successfully re-staged it for a later flight where it was verified onboard.

synopsis: Tug driver towing an aircraft reported a near miss with a taxiing aircraft when it did not hold short on taxiway as instructed by ATC to give way to the aircraft being towed.
summary: Ground crew towing an aircraft to the Super-bay reported a near miss when Aircraft Y pilots failed to hold short of Quebec and yield on Bravo 1 as instructed by Ground Tower. The crew slowed and held position to avoid a collision while turning, but the other aircraft continued without stopping.

synopsis: First Officer reported that the loss of a generator and the failure of the electrical system to reroute power caused the failure of many cockpit display units and a diversion to a closer airport with maintenance support.
summary: The First Officer reported that during a night arrival into ZZZ2, multiple flight instruments and displays failed due to suspected Generator 2 or GCU faults. The crew hand-flew a visual approach after autopilot failure and landed safely, with displays restoring shortly before and after touchdown.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a taxiway incursion in LAX due to lack of signage indicating where the assigned taxiway starts.
summary: The crew encroached onto Taxiway B-7 while taxiing to Gate XX at LAX due to missing eastbound signage for the runway exit. Ground Control instructed a hold short, but no conflict occurred as the aircraft followed another plane into the ramp.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported landing in a field after engine trouble precluded returning to departure airport.
summary: The PIC and instructor experienced partial power loss shortly after takeoff, limiting the aircraft to 300 feet AGL. They executed a planned emergency landing in a nearby field with no damage, though the cause of the power loss remains undetermined.

synopsis: BE-35 pilot reported an airspace incursion resulted after being distracted by a wake turbulence encounter departing CFO.
summary: The pilot departed CFO Runway 26 behind Aircraft Y, encountering wake turbulence at 60 knots that caused a left veer. While addressing a startled passenger, the pilot inadvertently climbed to 7,200 feet into the 7,000-foot Class B shelf before descending after Tower intervention.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runaway autopilot caused the ailerons to bind , making the aircraft difficult to control for landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a runaway autopilot that bound the ailerons during a right turn at 12,000 ft in IMC, causing altitude fluctuations between 11,700 and 12,350 ft. After receiving priority from ATC, the pilot manually flew the RNAV approach and landed at ZZZ without incident.

synopsis: Single Pilot reported flying into icing conditions and the control surfaces freezing.
summary: A PC-12 pilot encountered mixed icing during a night climb to 17,000 ft, freezing the elevators and causing a loss of pitch control. The pilot descended into warmer rain to melt the ice, recovered control, and landed safely, attributing the incident to inadvertent icing, fatigue, and delayed avoidance.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported violating a Class C airspace while dealing with a flap malfunction.
summary: A pilot conducting a personal practice flight experienced a flap system failure while returning to ZZZ1. While managing the malfunction, the pilot inadvertently entered Class C airspace by selecting a direct route without monitoring altitude, later admitting the error to Approach Control.

synopsis: PA-28 Single Pilot reported encountering inflight icing resulting in altitude loss as well as loss of Comm 1 and Nav 1. Reporter requested ATC routing assistance and completed effective trouble shooting to execute an uneventful landing at destination.
summary: A pilot flying IFR encountered severe icing at 5,000 feet, causing loss of altitude and failure of primary flight instruments, communications, and navigation. After descending to 3,000 feet where ice melted and instruments recovered, the pilot used backup equipment to complete an ILS approach into ZZZ1 in rain.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA Single Pilot reported an NMAC event in landing pattern of F70 airport with aircraft that had a longer than normal downwind leg.
summary: The pilot and Aircraft Y experienced a close call at a busy small airport while both were on final approach. The conflict occurred because Aircraft Y flew an excessively wide downwind and long final without announcing position, prompting the pilot to execute a second go-around to avoid collision.

synopsis: Lead Ramp Serviceman reported lack of equipment sanitation due to on-time departure pressure and working with different personnel throughout the airport.
summary: A Lead Ramp Serviceman reported that time pressure and supervisor scrutiny during gate operations prevented proper disinfection of wireless headsets before crew use. This created a health exposure risk for staff, who expressed distrust in the provided wipes and occasionally refused to wear the equipment.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a GPWS terrain alert on a visual approach to ROA.
summary: The flight crew operating a visual approach to Runway 24 at Roanoke received a GPWS "pull up - terrain" alert at 3,000 feet due to terrain right of the flight path. They complied by climbing to avoid the terrain, which was in sight, and maintained a higher altitude until past the obstacle.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Light twin engine pilot in training reported an engine failure during landing.
summary: During a twin-engine training flight, a student pilot and instructor executed a simulated engine failure followed by a missed approach. The aircraft failed to climb and veered off the runway because the student left the left fuel pump on high, flooding the engine and preventing power recovery.

synopsis: Captain reported that during a maintenance action to MEL an Anti Ice problem, and emergency exit light battery pack exploded, causing the aircraft to be evacuated and CFR to be called.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an emergency exit light battery explosion while at the gate with the jet bridge connected. The crew initiated an evacuation, cut power to the APU and batteries, and noted that a megaphone would have aided communication during the event.

synopsis: Technicians reported leaving the accessory gearbox drive pad cover uninstalled and released the A319 aircraft for service.
summary: Two AMTs and a crew chief installed an IDG on Aircraft X, performing engine runs and leak checks with no issues noted before taxiing to the gate. The aircraft later experienced in-flight engine oil loss because the gearbox pad cover was missing, though the crew reported never seeing it removed or being informed of its absence.

synopsis: Technician reported troubleshooting an IDG problem led to the decision to replace the Generator Control Unit, which led to confusion as to whether it corrected the problem, or not.
summary: A mechanic addressed a low IDG oil pressure ECAM advisory by replacing the GCU, though the specific reasoning for this conclusion was unclear. Subsequent checks of the IDG oil service and DPI found no faults, leading the reporter to call for better troubleshooting documentation.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor Pilot reported landing on a highway after experiencing engine failure shortly after takeoff.
summary: A student pilot in a Piper PA-28-140 experienced an engine sputter at 30–50 feet AGL during a practice takeoff, followed by a brief power surge. The pilot executed an emergency landing on a divided highway between moving vehicles, avoiding power lines and traffic, before emergency services arrived to tow the aircraft.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported that the loss of all electrical power resulted in a diversion, and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: An instructor and student pilot experienced a total electrical failure in cruise IMC while flying a newly purchased aircraft. They managed the emergency using partial panel procedures, diverted to an alternate airport, and landed safely after a second power loss, with maintenance later finding no visible damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported the student pilot lost control of aircraft during landing practice.
summary: During a student training flight at ZZZ, the student locked brakes on both main gear during rollout, causing a left tire blowout and wheel pant damage. The instructor took control to stop the aircraft off-center, resulting in a one-hour runway closure for removal.

synopsis: BE33 pilot reported the engine quit when the fuel tank selector lever stuck in the OFF position. The engine was successfully restarted when the selector was able to be moved to a proper position at about 700 feet altitude.
summary: During cruise at 2,500 feet MSL, the fuel selector lever stuck in OFF, causing engine failure and a descent. The pilot restarted the engine at 700 feet MSL after selecting a tank and diverted for maintenance to clear debris and lubricate the mechanism.

synopsis: A pilot taxiing for departure reported observing an aircraft taxi onto the active runway without a clearance as another aircraft was on landing roll.
summary: A pilot reported a near-miss runway incursion where Aircraft Y crossed hold-short markings within 100 feet of landing Aircraft Z due to a blocked taxiway and terse Tower instructions. The reporter attributed the incident to the pilot's failure to seek clarification during non-standard procedures and the Tower's lack of awareness of the incursion.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported operating the aircraft with the stall warning inoperative contrary to the required equipment list.
summary: Pilots discovered a non-functional stall warning during preflight and initially deemed it non-essential under FAR 91.205, proceeding with the flight. A club member later clarified the system was required equipment per the POH weight and balance section, revealing the crew had misinterpreted the regulatory requirements.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of engine control, resulting in an In Flight Shut Down and a precautionary emergency landing.
summary: During final approach to RWY XXL, the pilot experienced a throttle control disconnection causing full engine power, necessitating a go-around and landing with limited power control. Post-landing inspection revealed the threaded throttle control had fully unscrewed from the fuel controller rod, requiring the aircraft to be towed to the ramp.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an NMAC with a light aircraft on approach to LAX.
summary: A crew descending on the ILS to LAX 25R experienced a near miss with an untracked Piper Cherokee crossing LYCOM at 10,500', passing less than 300' above. The small aircraft lacked ADS-B and radio contact, prompting a side-step to 24R for a successful landing.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a taxiway incursion and cited communication problems with ATC as a contributing factor. Reportedly, the Controller's instructions sounded muffled due to wearing a face mask.
summary: The Captain and First Officer misheard a Tower clearance to exit Runway XXL via Taxiway 2X "not" Taxiway 1 as "or" due to the controller's mask and speech speed. They exited onto Taxiway 1 instead, but Ground Control corrected the error before any conflict occurred.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported communication errors between departments over a MEL that restricted cargo form being loaded within 5 feet of a damaged sidewall panel and which subsequently was loaded and flew in service.
summary: Aircraft X arrived at ZZZZ with cargo loaded in prohibited forward bay positions despite a 50-DIP repair restriction. The reporter attributes this to a system failure where Maintenance was notified of the restriction, but Station Operations and Central Cargo Loading were not.

synopsis: Mechanics reported missing portable fire extinguisher after aircraft had undergone an interior modification, requiring an Engineering Authorization to account for the missing required safety equipment.
summary: The pilot reported a missing second fire extinguisher in the first-class overhead bin following a new interior modification. The reporter suspects the Engineering Change Order was incomplete because no separate authorization was issued for the extinguisher installation.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported an alternator failure caused a diversion and a precautionary landing.
summary: During an instrument training flight, the pilot experienced an alternator failure leading to total electrical loss and intermittent communications. The aircraft landed safely at a closer airport after contacting the tower with a handheld radio, and maintenance later repaired a wiring issue.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported student pilot lost directional control after landing and experienced a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot on their second solo flight veered off the runway after landing. The pilot returned to the runway without assistance, and no damage or emergency services were required.

synopsis: An Air Ambulance Helicopter pilot reported that their helicopters have been flying without current revisions to the Rotorcraft Flight Manual which had not been received by the company. The reporter stated revisions used to be available through software tools which are no longer available to pilots or maintenance technicians.
summary: Mechanics discovered three missing Rotorcraft Flight Manual revisions in an aircraft flown for seven months after its 2020 base transfer. The reporter attributes the error to pilots failing to verify documents, lack of software access, and an unupdated address that prevented mailed revisions from reaching the base.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported an aircraft landed behind them on the runway before they had exited the runway.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion after landing during a busy pattern when a Seminole landed approximately 600 feet behind them before they could exit. The pilot attributed the near-miss to tight spacing and believed a collision would have occurred without a go-around, clearance cancellation, or slower exit.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported clearing an aircraft for a new approach and issued a crossing restriction below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller instructed Aircraft X to cross a fix at 3,000 ft during an RNAV GPS Runway 32 approach into MIC but climbed it to 3,500 ft due to discomfort with the clearance. The controller later determined the correct crossing altitude for WAKUD was 3,400 ft to maintain the required 3,500 ft minimum vectoring altitude.

synopsis: First Officer reported confusion interpreting a clearance transitioning from a STAR to the ILS Approach.
summary: The crew identified a potential altitude discrepancy while descending via the RNDRZ 1 Arrival into Las Vegas for the ILS 1L approach. Closing the discontinuity at ROAMN caused the FMS to drop the 8,000 ft hard altitude, prompting the Pilot Flying to manually reprogram the constraint to avoid being high.

synopsis: First Officer reported that during a lavatory break, both pilots were out of the cockpit at the same time and the flight attendant was swapping seats in the cockpit, leaving the aircraft uncontrolled.
summary: During cruise, the Captain left the flight deck unattended while a flight attendant switched seats, leaving no pilot at the controls. The First Officer immediately returned to the flight deck to secure the aircraft and later corrected the Captain on the unsafe lavatory exchange procedure.

synopsis: Instructor and student reported descending below Minimum Descent Altitude, which they attributed to an incorrect altimeter setting, and turbulence.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 172S descended below the 2,020-foot Minimum Descent Altitude during a VOR-A approach in IMC due to high workload, turbulence, and an altimeter setting error. ATC issued a low altitude alert, prompting a climb back to minimums instead of an immediate missed approach, violating 14 CFR 91.175.

synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving an RA caused by a VFR light twin, while they were on final approach .
summary: Pilots on an RNAV approach encountered uncontrolled VFR traffic at 2,500 feet while at 2,000 feet, resulting in a TCAS RA and a descent to 1,850 feet. Radar playback confirmed a 300-foot vertical separation as the VFR aircraft legally threaded between Class D and Class B airspace.

synopsis: An Instructor pilot flying into a non towered airport reported a NMAC with another aircraft in the VFR traffic pattern.
summary: An experimental aircraft overflew and descended in front of a C172 in the traffic pattern, cutting it off. The C172 was forced to descend below pattern altitude to avoid a collision.

synopsis: A Flight Instructor reported a vehicle entered the active runway at a non towered airport without communicating while their aircraft was stopped on the runway. Another aircraft had to go around due to the vehicle on the runway.
summary: During a night training flight involving touch-and-goes, a maintenance vehicle entered the active runway while an aircraft was stopped and forced another student to go around. The reporter attributed the unsafe situation to the vehicle's unauthorized entry and the airport manager's failure to respond to contact attempts.

synopsis: Controller reported military aircraft flew below the Minimum IFR altitude after permission for special activity was denied.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and Y in IR302 after both pilots requested unauthorized entry into MHRC Special Activity Airspace. The controller denied entry, lost radio contact with Aircraft X, and eventually cleared both aircraft to ZZZ after realizing they lacked radar identification.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported a military aircraft conducting practice approaches did not comply with the Missed Approach assigned altitude and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An Approach controller vectored Aircraft X below the 3,800-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude during a missed approach due to expectation bias and distraction. The controller corrected the error by instructing a climb to 4,000 feet, and the aircraft safely exited the restricted area.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported they failed to complete the landing checklist because of distractions and loss of situational awareness.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a loss of situational awareness during a visual approach to 34L, resulting in an unannounced landing checklist and a high sink rate. The crew attributed the incident to their shared failure to maintain awareness amidst speed changes and wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft.
