synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported a runway excursion on landing rollout.
summary: The pilot reported veering off Runway XX onto grass during landing due to inadvertent asymmetric toe brake application caused by feet slipping on the pedals. The aircraft stopped on the grass with no damage or injuries, was inspected, and returned to service.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported neglecting to remove tail tiedown weight prior to taxi.
summary: The pilot rushed the preflight due to time pressure and lack of recent experience with tiedowns, missing the tail tiedown. This caused the pilot to drag the tiedown weight approximately 50 feet before realizing it was still attached to the aircraft.

synopsis: BE-200 Captain reported miscalculating fuel used causing fuel starvation and engine failure on final.
summary: The PIC experienced a right engine failure on ILS final to Runway XL while returning from ZZZ1 with X passengers. The cause was fuel starvation due to the pilot misreading the fuel gauge and failing to account for fuel burned during startup procedures.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Captain reported concerns when ATC directed him to taxi on a taxiway that was NOTAMed closed to aircraft over 30,000 pounds at APC airport.
summary: The pilot reported a poorly written NOTAM at Napa (APC) that closed Taxiway C to aircraft over 30,000 lbs, conflicting with a Tower clearance to exit there after landing on Runway 6. The crew complied with the ATC instruction to avoid traffic delays but noted the NOTAM required clarification to prevent future operational dilemmas.

synopsis: Helicopter Instructor reported a runway incursion occurred when the student air taxiied across the runway while traffic was waiting to take off. Instructor stated they did not realize the student's requests to ATC for crossing were blocked both times.
summary: A helicopter instructor and student attempted to air taxi across Runway XY/XZ without receiving ATC clearance due to blocked transmissions. They mistakenly interpreted a coincidental traffic advisory as acknowledgment, nearly conflicting with an aircraft cleared for takeoff that held short until the helicopter passed.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft reported a near miss with a large UAS while flying on an IFR flight plan. The pilot was able to see and avoid it in time.
summary: During an IFR training flight at 10,000 ft, a drone and chase plane turned directly into the aircraft's path, triggering a G1000 NXi Traffic Alert. The pilot disconnected the autopilot and executed a left turn and dive to avoid a mid-air collision, while ATC attempted to redirect the drone.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Single Private Pilot reported, after a year away from flying due to COVID-19, not following proper IFR communication procedures after departure.
summary: A pilot with limited recent IFR experience departed ZZZ for ZZZ1 and switched to ZZZ2 Center at 500 feet AGL before being instructed to do so by the tower. The pilot attributed this improper ATC communication procedure to inexperience with departures from towered fields.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC in cruise near SLE airport.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a private aircraft encountered a target on ADS-B while northbound at 3,100 feet. The student executed a climbing right turn to avoid the converging aircraft, which was later visually confirmed 700 feet below, prompting a temporary climb to 3,800 feet before contacting Portland Approach.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a gear-up landing occurred during a training flight. Instructor stated they had flown a fixed gear aircraft earlier and had not focused on the differences with flying a retractable gear aircraft.
summary: During a training flight in a retractable-gear Cessna 172, the instructor landed with the gear retracted while demonstrating a simulated engine failure. The error occurred because the instructor, who had flown a fixed-gear aircraft earlier that day, neglected to extend the gear while focusing on airspeed and maneuvering.

synopsis: Beech F90 Captain reported diverting due to deteriorating engine parameters which caused an in-flight shut down of the right engine.
summary: During cruise, the pilot diverted from ZZZ to ZZZ2 due to worsening engine trends, eventually shutting down the right engine. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 13 at ZZZ2 with no injuries, and the Center Controller verified the crew's safety on the ground.

synopsis: There was an eyewitness of a UAS operating at a University. The eyewitness believed the UAS was flying at an unsafe altitude due to the proximity of a nearby airport.
summary: A licensed Remote Pilot observed a two-person UAS crew operating a small drone near a 275-foot building within the ZZZ airport traffic pattern. The reporter believes the crew violated altitude limits by flying well above the 100-foot campus ceiling and 300-foot tower authorization.

synopsis: Commercial UAS operator reported flying a UAS near a Class B airport without authorization.
summary: A drone pilot conducting a video mission at 150 ft. over a gas station inadvertently entered Class B airspace. The incident occurred because the pilot failed to consult the B4ufly app, relying instead on other applications that did not identify the no-fly zone.

synopsis: Commercial UAS crew operating a UAS exceeded authorized altitude during climb while in close proximity to Class C airspace.
summary: The Remote Pilot in Command breached a 400 ft ceiling while climbing a UAS, caused by distraction from a crew member and delayed monitoring of the Ground Control Station screen. The pilot immediately stopped the climb and descended, noting that a crew member should have read altitude during the fast ascent.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported missing an ATC speed assignment on arrival into LAX when they were distracted by a wake turbulence encounter in trail of a heavy B777.
summary: The flight crew missed a speed reduction to 210 knots due to simultaneous cabin medical calls and wake turbulence while on the ILS 25L arrival. Consequently, ATC canceled their approach clearance for being too fast, vectored them for spacing, and re-cleared them for the approach.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported runway incursion after landing.
summary: The flight crew stopped on a high-speed exit after a wildlife alert but failed to fully clear the Runway 26R hold short line. The Tower Controller subsequently instructed them to hold, then cleared them to cross the runway and contact Ground.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence departing ATL in trail of an Airbus.
summary: The flight crew experienced heavy rolling motion requiring full aileron input while accelerating for takeoff after being diverted to the north side due to south runway congestion. The pilot attributed the turbulence to wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus and later informed passengers via PA above 10,000 feet.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp employee reported another ramp employee had to take evasive action to avoid an aircraft whose Captain had released brakes before being cleared to do so.
summary: The pilot released brakes without authorization while the ground lead waited at the nose gear and the pushback tractor driver was not ready. The lead had to jump back to avoid being run over by the moving aircraft.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a dirty sock" odor was detected in the cabin during cruise resulting in a diversion."
summary: Flight crew diverted an Airbus to ZZZ1 during climb to FL280 after flight attendants reported a "dirty sock" odor and passenger illness. The crew executed smoke and overweight landing procedures, resulting in an uneventful landing where paramedics treated several ill occupants.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an unstabilized approach due to lack of recent flying experience, weather, and ATC instructions.
summary: The pilot reported that a tailwind, ATC speed restrictions, and recent inexperience caused delayed aircraft configuration, resulting in flaps 30 being selected below 1,000 feet. The pilot attributed the error to distraction from airspeed management and insufficient altitude monitoring during the final approach.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported a communication breakdown between Flight Attendant and Maintenance personnel regarding proper disposal of Hazmat waste.
summary: Cabin crew reported that an Aircraft Maintenance Supervisor instructed them to dispose of two containers of medical sharps in a red bag left in a wheelchair within the jetbridge. The crew complied despite expressing safety concerns about the risk of needle exposure to others handling the waste.

synopsis: Technician reported ambiguity in AMM references for task cards resulted in not using the required tooling to return B737 MAX aircraft to service after storage.
summary: During a 737-MAX return-to-service audit, mechanics discovered that maintenance tasks on Aircraft Z were stamped complete without required tooling due to vague job cards and missing tooling lists. The aircraft was grounded, paperwork was pulled, and tooling was ordered to ensure correct task accomplishment before release.

synopsis: Private Pilot reported runway incursion occurred during taxi and cited being new to the airport as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed the runway hold line at C3 while taxiing from D3 to perform a run-up, noting the hold lines had been moved back. Upon realizing the error, the pilot executed a 180-degree turn, returned to taxiway C, and contacted ground control for instructions to return to the hangar.

synopsis: Air taxi flight crew was on a descent when they noticed a small UAS within 50-100 feet of their flight path. Crew notified ATC.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X on the ZZZZZ3 arrival at 8,000 feet reported a small drone with four green lights passing below the left wing. The drone was estimated 50 to 100 feet below the aircraft and was reported to ZZZ Center before the handoff to Approach.

synopsis: Flight Instructor and trainee reported that during a training flight the left main gear collapsed on landing, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway. Both pilots exited the aircraft safely.
summary: A private pilot and CFI in a Cessna 172RG experienced a left main landing gear collapse during rollout at ZZZ2 after a crosswind landing. The gear failed to lock despite a green indicator, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway with minor damage but no injuries.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC occurred during takeoff climb and also expressed concern about Tower operations at the airport.
summary: The pilot of a departing aircraft at Merrill Field encountered a head-on conflict with a low-altitude Cessna 172 on the Chester Creek Departure route. The pilot attributed the near miss to the tower controller's failure to warn of the traffic conflict or the Cessna's deviation from pattern altitude.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet pilot reported an NMAC with a small aircraft on approach to APA airport.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X reported a near-mid-air collision with Aircraft Y during a visual approach to APA at Centennial Airport. The conflict occurred when Aircraft Y turned final on a collision course, which the pilot attributed to student pilots overshooting and a lack of staggered spacing by the tower controller.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a ground gate return due to a fume event during taxi.
summary: Flight attendants on flight ZZZ-ZZZ1 reported moderate fumes and extreme heat from forward air supply vents during taxi after engine start, causing crew illness. The flight deck shut down engines, maintenance deferred the forward PACK, and the aircraft departed after re-boarding.

synopsis: Commercial UAS pilot realized after several flights they had been flying with an expired Part 107 license.
summary: A pilot flew multiple flights on an expired license, unaware of the expiration until checking their FAA account. The incident occurred because the physical license lacked an expiration date and the certificate was inaccessible due to office closure.

synopsis: Pilot reported getting a terrain alert after not noticing the aircraft was not on glideslope. Reporter stated they were focused on the poor weather conditions and did not monitor the approach progress.
summary: The pilot flying a coupled RNAV XX LPV approach to ZZZ overshot the turn to final and descended without glideslope guidance due to diverted attention from heavy rain and complacency. After a terrain alert, the pilot climbed, broke out of the rain, and landed visually, admitting to misinterpreting weather and failing to execute a missed approach.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: POU Tower Controllers reported not being able to see the aircraft of a student pilot after a rejected takeoff due to construction of a new hangar. The student pilot also reported describing the rejected takeoff.
summary: A pilot aborted a takeoff on Runway 24 due to an engine sputter and taxied off, but a new hangar blocked the tower's view of the aircraft. This blind spot prevented controllers from verifying the aircraft's position, creating safety concerns for following traffic and prompting recommendations to raise the tower or lower the hangar.

synopsis: First Officer reported that the Captain's side window experienced a short in the window heat system, requiring an emergency descent and a diversion to a precautionary landing.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a left side window heat short and subsequent failure at FL360, causing an emergency descent and diversion to ZZZ3. The crew attributed the failure to repeated heat cycling, donned oxygen masks, and landed safely with emergency vehicles standing by.

synopsis: First Officer reported compressor stalls forced an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain experienced rapid engine bursts and transient ECAM messages on the right engine during the ZZZZZ3 departure at 1,050 feet AGL. They returned for an immediate landing after the engine parameters normalized, with post-flight inspections revealing no significant damage.

synopsis: B737 MAX First Officer reported numerous performance and weight issues caused a delay and required off-loading passengers and baggage multiple times and multiple clearance requests before departing.
summary: The flight crew of a 737 MAX at ZZZZ faced a four-hour departure delay due to overweight conditions caused by rising temperatures and a procedural breakdown between Dispatch and ATC regarding flight plan clearances. After offloading passengers and bags to resolve weight limits and securing a valid clearance, the aircraft departed safely.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported auto throttle anomalies on take off and again on landing required a go around.
summary: Pilots reported autothrottle anomalies on a Boeing 737 Max during takeoff from ZZZ and below 50 feet on a visual approach to Runway 31, causing unexpected thrust surges and a go-around. Maintenance removed the aircraft from service after the crew manually managed thrust and landed safely, suspecting an autothrottle or coding fault.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported the Captain notified Dispatch that a flight delay was required to correct a Weight & Balance discrepancy. During the correction process the Hazmat cargo had to be moved to complete the Weight & Balance adjustment.
summary: The Captain reported a delay on flight XXX due to unaccounted freight loaded onto the aircraft by the ramp team. The delay was required to correct the weight and balance calculations before departure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew was flying a published SID and climbing above 10,000 feet when an object, possibly a UAS, passed by the aircraft.
summary: During climb through 13,500 feet on the ZZZZZ2 SID, the First Officer observed an unidentified black and white object pass extremely close to the aircraft's left side. The Pilot Monitoring was occupied with FMS programming and did not see the object, which the First Officer could not identify as a balloon or drone.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine failure occurred and performed a forced landing at an airport.
summary: The pilot reported a total engine failure at 12,000 feet MSL and requested a forced landing from ATC. The aircraft subsequently landed on Runway XX at ZZZ.

synopsis: Cirrus pilot reported a prop strike occurred during a landing attempt after encountering jet blast from a preceding heavy aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft encountered jet blast from a departing heavy cargo plane on short final, causing a destabilized landing, prop strike, and go-around. The pilot attributed the incident to the heavy jet's delayed departure and a lack of Tower warnings regarding the hazard.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a NMAC on approach stating they did not hearing hear other aircraft but upon landing realized their volume was turned down.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss during the traffic pattern at an uncontrolled airport caused by inadvertently lowering the radio volume due to passenger distraction. This prevented hearing another aircraft's calls, though the pilot landed safely after the other aircraft extended its downwind leg.

synopsis: Technician reported not installing a cotter pin in the nut for a bolt on the aft bearing hangar for the Thrust Reverser gearbox fairing.
summary: A lead mechanic performing a 300-hour inspection on Aircraft X at Base XXX admitted to likely failing to cotter pin a hangar bearing bolt nut due to staffing disruptions. The unsecured nut later fell into the thrust reverser gearbox drain hole, where it was discovered by a pilot after a flight.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Houston Center Controller reported problems with unsafe practices involving a weather-related situation.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Eagle Lake sector diverted 15 inbound aircraft to a safer route due to weather, but the Supervisor and Traffic Management Unit ordered them to continue through the weather. The controller reported this management decision ignored safety concerns and reflected an unsafe mentality of pushing aircraft to their limits.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Houston Center Controller reported unsafe practices regarding Management and weather.
summary: An air traffic controller at Houston Center reported that TMU opened arrival fixes despite moderate turbulence and heavy precipitation. The controller attributed this unsafe decision to a management mindset prioritizing flow over safety, fearing future incidents.

synopsis: Captain reported notifying Dispatch at destination that the revised Departure Flight Release was missing required Hazmat cargo information.
summary: The pilot reported that on a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1, the HAZMAT NOTOC was not annotated on the dispatch release after a weather reroute. Upon landing, the pilot contacted Dispatch to disclose the discrepancy.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported confusion and communications problems during push back and taxi.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, on the First Officer's second leg of an OE, began taxiing without setting flaps due to distraction during a Single Engine Taxi. The crew stopped the aircraft, set flaps 1, completed the Before Taxi Checklist, and continued the flight to ZZZ1 without further incident.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported malfunctioning pressurization system on descent.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a cabin pressurization failure during descent on the ZZZZZ 2 RNAV arrival due to closed inlet and extract valves with an open safety valve. They expedited descent to 10,000 feet, manually controlled the outflow valve, and completed an uneventful landing after ATC granted shallow descent vectors.

aircraft: Heavy Transport; Low Wing; 4 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported a Rejected Take Off after receiving a #2 generator drive fault light which was a repeat write up.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at approximately 30 knots due to a Level 2 Gen Drive 1 Fault alert. The aircraft returned to the maintenance area for repair, and this incident is a repeat write-up.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported stabilizer trim failure at takeoff resulted in fuel jettison with failure of the jettison system that led to holding for fuel burn to below max landing weight and a return to the departure airport.
summary: Pilots experienced a stabilizer trim failure after takeoff, causing a pitch mismatch and 'STAB out of trim' alert. They returned to land safely after fuel dumping was interrupted by crossfeed relay failure, attributing the incident to a failed trim gear fuse pin.

synopsis: First Officer reported during landing roll out, he shut off the left engine fuel lever instead of deploying the left thrust reverser and used wheel brakes only to slow the aircraft to a safe stop.
summary: The Pilot Flying inadvertently shut down the left engine during landing rollout by confusing the thrust reverser unlock lever with the shutoff lock. This error, attributed to muscle memory triggered by operating only the left thrust lever due to a disabled right reverser, resulted in a single-engine stop using brakes only.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported executing a go-around at SAN when it became clear another air carrier aircraft was in position for takeoff on their landing runway.
summary: Pilots on an RNAV Z Runway 27 approach to San Diego executed a go-around after discovering a stationary heavy jet on the active runway. The reporter attributes the incident to the tower placing the aircraft on the runway for a maintenance irregularity without ensuring it was ready to depart, combined with crew distraction from checklists.

synopsis: Captain reported an air turn back due to aircraft shudder.
summary: The crew experienced an increasing shudder after lift-off, prompting an immediate return to ZZZ. Post-flight inspection revealed a detached elevator balance tab, which was missed because the initial check focused only on flaps and landing gear doors.

synopsis: First Officer reported an air turn back after cabin would not pressurize.
summary: Flight XXXX crew experienced a pressurization failure during climb from ZZZ, where outflow valves failed to close and cabin altitude rose to 4,000 feet at 11,000 feet. The crew returned to ZZZ under emergency priority, landing safely with no injuries attributed to a suspected pressurization system part failure.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that during preflight, a portable fire extinguisher and its mounting bracket were discovered missing, resulting in an aircraft swap.
summary: The pilot discovered a missing halon and bracket during preflight on a Boeing 737, leading to an out-of-service declaration due to lack of parts. Passengers were deplaned, and the crew departed 90 minutes later on a replacement aircraft after the reporter attributed the oversight to previous crew negligence.

synopsis: King Air pilot reported loss of directional control after landing resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that upon touchdown in gusty, variable winds, the aircraft veered right despite brake and beta application, exiting the runway into dirt. No damage or injuries occurred, but the cause remains unknown, with a possible tailwind suspected and an inspection initiated.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot Monitoring reported Pilot in Command lost control while landing in a crosswind.
summary: The Pilot in Command and right-seat monitor landed Aircraft X at ZZZ Airport when a sudden wind shift caused loss of directional control during the flare. Despite attempting a go-around, the aircraft veered right and stopped nose-down.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of directional control after landing in gusty winds resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A solo pilot flying a Garmin-equipped aircraft exited the runway on the second landing attempt due to an exceptional wind gust that caused a sharp left veer. Despite applying full right rudder and braking, the aircraft left the runway surface and came to rest with a flat left tire.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported an NMAC with a PA-44 in the landing pattern.
summary: A Cessna Skyhawk pilot and student on downwind reported a near-midair collision with a Piper Seminole that appeared to be on a direct course despite Tower instructions to follow. The Seminole passed within an estimated 400 feet horizontally while banking right, prompting the pilot to request a short approach to increase separation.

aircraft: Bellanca Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Pilot reported engine power loss and elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot of a Bellanca Crusiair experienced repeated, unprovoked power losses during cruise climb and cruise phases due to suspected fuel system anomalies. After notifying ATC and returning to the departure airport, the pilot executed a safe power-to-idle landing and taxied to the hangar under own power.

synopsis: A Pilot reported GPS jamming.
summary: During initial climb at 1,000 ft, the pilot's Garmin GTN635 lost terrain awareness due to GPS jamming in White Sands restricted area 5107B. Albuquerque Center placed the pilot on an IFR flight plan after the pilot reported an inability to maintain terrain clearance, noting a potential controlled flight into terrain risk.

synopsis: UAS crew failed to obtain LAANC authorization prior to UAS flight.
summary: The pilot admitted to human error by neglecting to file the UAV flight with AIRMAP despite having prior experience and ground permission. The flight proceeded with three visual observers and clear line-of-sight, but the pilot plans to implement a checklist to ensure proper authorization in the future.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Center Controller reported a radar site outage caused confusion leading to the Radar Controller vectoring an aircraft below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: A Radar Controller vectored Aircraft X below the Minimum IFR Altitude during a missed approach despite a known ZZZ1 radar outage, an error missed by both the Controller and Radar Assist. The reporter identified the conflict when requesting a climb to 4000 ft, attributing the oversight to suppressed outage alerts and inadequate memory aids.

synopsis: Captain reported that the Flight Attendant could not open the main entry door and had written the door up four times with no corrective action.
summary: A pilot reported that the main cabin door required immense force to open after pressurization to a 7.5 PSID differential, despite four previous write-ups. The pilot identified this as a safety hazard and recommended ferrying the aircraft for flight testing to determine the cause of the jamming.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported flight control vibration in flight and did an air turn back.
summary: Pilots reported a consistent vibration during flap extension on two flights, which led to a return to ZZZ. Maintenance found the left elevator trim control rod disconnected, likely due to prior tail damage sustained in ZZZ3.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported terrain alert during climb.
summary: During a VFR climb on a SUMMA departure, the First Officer flew a heading that drifted the aircraft toward Mt. Rainier due to a 50-knot southwest wind. A terrain warning triggered before the Pilot Monitoring could intervene, prompting an immediate turn that resolved the alert.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported strong odors, a PACK 1 FAIL issue and vibrations during initial descent. The flight crew decided to divert to nearest suitable airport for an expedited descent and successful landing.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ3 during descent due to loud noises, chemical odors, and violent shaking following a recent lavatory leak repair. Although maintenance attributed the event to a simple air system failure, the pilots insisted on a full inspection after landing, citing the severity of the symptoms and potential unseen damage.

synopsis: Technician reported confusion in signing off items when returning an aircraft to service after storage.
summary: A mechanic requested the reporter to witness the removal and storage of over-wing slide bottle pins, which was signed off as a Required Inspection Item. The reporter noted no arming occurred and questioned why disarming was recorded on a non-routine, suggesting a specific Task Card is needed for storage procedures.

synopsis: Technician reported misunderstanding reference for placing a main tire on MEL and dispatching the aircraft.
summary: The pilot discovered exposed cord on the #4 tire during the pre-flight walkaround but departed after the Aircraft Maintenance Manual lacked a specific replacement requirement. The flight proceeded without delay, though the reporter suggested the manual needs clearer language prohibiting tires with exposed cord.

synopsis: Pilot reported autopilot system failure caused difficulties on approach and landing.
summary: A pilot flying a TBM turboprop into ZZZ experienced autopilot mode selector flickering and excessive workload from multiple weather systems, leading to altitude deviations and navigation errors. The flight remained safe with a visual landing, but the pilot attributed the issues to low experience, equipment confusion, and decision-making errors, prompting a post-flight debrief and avionics repair.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC during go-around on a training flight.
summary: A student pilot and instructor flying Aircraft X on a pattern for Runway 3 executed a go-around after realizing Aircraft Y, landing on parallel Runway 30L, would not clear the runway in time. The conflict occurred because the tower's "left downwind" instruction did not account for the parallel traffic, causing Aircraft X to overfly Aircraft Y as it crossed Runway 3.

synopsis: Corporate flight crew reported NMAC on approach to land.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot, while on a visual approach to Burlington Airport Runway 24, spotted traffic 200 feet below their 3,000-foot altitude. To avoid a conflict, the pilot climbed to 4,000 feet before descending back to 3,000 feet to complete the final approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported NMAC during sightseeing flight.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X encountered Aircraft Y twice while sightseeing over downtown Pittsburgh at 2,000 feet MSL. The reporter attributed the hazardous convergences to the other pilot's failure to scan for traffic, forcing evasive maneuvers in complex airspace with limited obstacle clearance.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a NMAC near a Class C airspace.
summary: A helicopter pilot near ZZZ Class C airspace descended and turned southeast after Tower advised of Aircraft Y approaching from the west at 500 feet above. The pilot reported that Tower failed to issue avoidance vectors to Aircraft Y, which subsequently passed below the helicopter and later entered a TFR area.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a ground conflict occurred during landing rollout when another aircraft took off from the opposite end of the runway.
summary: The pilot landing on Runway 34 at RNT encountered Aircraft Y taking off from Runway 16 while the tower was closed. The pilot attributed the near collision to not hearing Aircraft Y's departure calls despite having a functional radio.

synopsis: Recreational Drone Pilot reported inadvertently flying within Class B airspace from the parking lot of a stadium complex. The Pilot was unaware of the incursion until advised by security personnel.
summary: A recreational pilot flew a DJI Mini 2 drone for 11 minutes in Class B airspace near ZZZ airport and a stadium without authorization. Security staff intercepted the pilot, instructed an immediate landing, issued a warning, and recorded identification details to prevent future violations.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported they approved a direct route for an aircraft which placed the aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude. The reporter had to relay climb instructions through another aircraft due to poor radio reception.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a 9,000-foot clearance to a pilot en route from ZZZ to ZZZ1, overlooking a 10,000-foot terrain box. A Minimum Safe Altitude Warning triggered, and poor radio reception delayed a relayed climb clearance until the aircraft transited the terrain at 9,000 feet before climbing to 10,000 feet.

synopsis: DCA Tower Controller reported a runway incursion between two air carriers.
summary: Local Control cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Ground Control inadvertently allowed Aircraft Y to enter Runway 1. The controller canceled the takeoff but Aircraft X had passed V1 and departed safely; the reporter attributed the incursion to the pilot's lack of attention.

synopsis: BUR Tower CIC reported an unsafe situation when the Local Controller mistakenly cleared an aircraft for takeoff with an aircraft on final to a crossing runway.
summary: A CIC controller monitoring Local Control missed a takeoff clearance given to Aircraft X on Runway 15 while distracted by a phone call. Aircraft X began its roll as Aircraft Y flared for Runway 8, forcing an abort after 1,000 to 1,500 feet due to the controller's failure to monitor the frequency.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported they assumed adjacent sectors were combined but they were not, which resulted in an airspace violation and two aircraft on conflicting routes entering the next facility sector.
summary: An air traffic controller working a first day shift after a schedule change failed to hand off Aircraft X climbing from 20,000 feet to the low altitude sector. This oversight caused a loss of separation with an eastbound aircraft at 23,000 feet, forcing ZZZ1 Center to execute last-minute turns to avoid a collision.

synopsis: Light Transport aircraft Captain reported deviation from clearance during climbout.
summary: The pilot of an IFR flight departing PHX mistakenly turned to join the PXR 350 radial instead of maintaining the assigned 270 heading for traffic spacing. This error resulted from misinterpreting "intercept" as "join" and failing to question the 80-degree intercept angle, though the flight continued without incident.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus Captain reported the STAR chart for the LAS RNDRZ 1 RNAV arrival is confusing and does not match the aircraft PFD.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to Runway 25L reported confusion caused by the RNDRZ 1 RNAV arrival chart, which depicted a small box at intersection BERBN that was easily missed. The crew and ATC agreed the chart design is confusing and requires examination to prevent navigational errors.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a near miss with a UAS while on approach.
summary: A pilot flying a Korry 4 arrival at 4,000 feet over the Hudson River reported a shiny black, flat oval object resembling a drone passing 100 feet below the aircraft. The crew took no evasive action due to the brief encounter and immediately notified Air Traffic Control and law enforcement.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported unreliable airspeed and indications in flight that required a missed approach and ATC assistance to land safely.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced unreliable airspeed and a PFD failure during a descent in IMC while approaching ZZZZ, likely due to a suspected lightning strike. The crew climbed to VMC, verified instrument reliability, and landed safely, later logging AFCS and ADS Probe 1 fault messages.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported fuel quantity instruments malfunctioning inflight resulting in a diversion.
summary: During descent into ZZZ at 28,000 feet, the crew received false zero fuel indications for both tanks, causing a diversion to ZZZ1. The quantities returned to the expected 3,600 pounds one minute later, attributed to improper fuel quantity indication.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported Ground Personnel forgot headset attached to nose gear.
summary: Pushback crew left a headset attached to the nose gear, causing sparks upon arrival at ZZZ. Both flight and ground crews missed the oversight, but no aircraft damage occurred despite the potential risk of engine failure.

synopsis: B737 MAX First Officer reports missing an entry in the Takeoff Performance System.
summary: A MAX pilot, fatigued after a long duty period, initially selected the wrong runway in the Takeoff Performance System due to task saturation and ground congestion. The error was caught during the before takeoff checklist, but changing the runway caused V speeds to disappear, requiring a manual takeoff initiation.

synopsis: A319 Captain Check Airman re-qualifying another Captain reported the Captain failed to comply with a crossing restriction issued by ATC during approach.
summary: A First Officer intervened during a Captain's requalification when the Captain selected open descent instead of managed descent, causing the aircraft to descend below the cleared 8,000 feet. The Captain was re-cleared to cross at 7,000 feet, and the incident was attributed to a lack of recent flight experience and failure to verify inputs.

synopsis: CE-680 Captain reported diverting after landing gear indicating system malfunctioned. A normal approach and landing were made.
summary: The pilot and First Officer experienced a right main gear miscompare indication during a visual approach to ZZZZ, causing a diversion to ZZZ1. Maintenance later determined a stuck uplock switch falsely signaled the gear was up, though visual confirmation and a successful landing proved the gear was down and locked.

synopsis: B737 MAX Captain reported realizing after departure that they had not changed the takeoff flaps setting as discussed before takeoff. Pilot reported as contributing factors several interruptions and a different gauge scan because the flap indicator on the B737 MAX aircraft is in a different position than on an NG.
summary: The Captain of a 737 MAX departing ZZZ failed to complete the before takeoff checklist due to distractions, resulting in a departure with flaps 1 instead of the intended flaps 5. The error was discovered at acceleration altitude, but the use of VR max speeds prevented a tail strike despite the configuration mismatch.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew had a near miss with a UAS while on approach.
summary: Pilots flying a visual approach to runway 36R at CLT encountered a black quadcopter drone at 2,700 feet on the localizer intercept. The drone passed co-altitude near the right wing, prompting the crew to file a PIREP to the tower regarding the illegal operation in Class B airspace.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew was on final approach descending past 3,000 feet when they noticed a UAS above them and notified ATC.
summary: During landing, approximately 1-2 miles from the FAF at 2,900 ft, the crew observed a drone about 50 ft above the aircraft. The pilot reported the incident to ZZZ tower, passed below the drone, and completed the landing safely.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported BFM airport has temporary taxiway lines that do not match the Jeppesen Chart or NOTAMs.
summary: The Captain and First Officer mistakenly followed an uncharted taxi line at Mobile Downtown due to construction barriers and confusing NOTAMs, deviating from the charted left turn. They stopped the aircraft, shut down, and were chocked by ground personnel after contractors confirmed the error, noting this confusion has occurred previously.

synopsis: Citation I flight crew reported an inverter failure caused the autopilot to fail resulting in a temporary loss of control.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X experienced an autopilot upset during an RNAV arrival to ZZZ at 20,000 feet caused by a number 2 inverter failure. The crew manually regained control after losing 1,800 feet and deviating 90 degrees, then switched to the number 1 inverter to continue the flight.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported confusion about whether or not they had clearance into a Class Charlie airspace while under flight following, and a quick termination within 1 mile of the Class Charlie airspace.
summary: Pilots conducting a training flight from BAF to ZZZ entered the BDL Class C surface area after ATC terminated radar services without explicit clearance. The crew assumed entry was authorized due to their direct trajectory, though they later acknowledged this potential incursion resulted from failing to confirm clearance or alter course.

synopsis: Texan T6/Harvard pilot reported taking evasive action during a training flight in response to a NMAC with a aircraft that entered their MOA block.
summary: During a VFR training flight in an MOA between 12,000 and 17,999 feet, the pilot and student executed a nose-low recovery maneuver and narrowly avoided a civilian multi-engine aircraft. The near-miss occurred because the pilot dismissed an initial TCAS contact as company traffic, while the controller failed to issue a traffic advisory due to the dynamic nature of the training.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot providing training at a non-towered airport reported an NMAC.
summary: A pilot practicing landings at untowered ZZZ reported a Cessna crossing left to right at 1,100 feet on the right downwind. The Cessna queried radio capability despite the pilot's confirmed functional radio and prior traffic sequencing.

synopsis: Pilot reported an FMS error caused them to deviate off course. The pilot reported prior to the deviation they were issued a reroute to avoid military airspace that is uncharted.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 40,000 ft. deviated from an ATC-issued clearance due to an FMS sequencing error, coming within one mile of uncharted military airspace. The controller later admitted that government enroute charts intentionally omit these hazards, which ATC manages to keep public flights clear.

synopsis: Pilot reported right main brake malfunctioned, causing a runway excursion and aircraft damage.
summary: After landing at ZZZ, the right brake failed and rudder authority was lost, causing the aircraft to depart the runway's left side. The nose gear collapsed in soft dirt and engines stopped, but there were no injuries and the crew exited safely.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported having to strike a student to release the flight controls during takeoff after the student attempted to stop the aircraft from rotating and did not respond to verbal commands from the instructor to release the controls.
summary: During a Cessna 152 takeoff, an instructor struck a student to regain control after the student grabbed the yoke and prevented rotation. The instructor aborted the flight, returned to the airport, and deemed the student unfit for future flights due to this dangerous interference.

synopsis: PA-34-200T instructor pilot and student reported brake failure during landing roll so the instructor turned onto an intersecting runway to stop safely.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in Aircraft X experienced brake failure during landing at ZZZ, causing an unauthorized entry onto an intersecting runway. The incident resulted from the instructor's prior knowledge of unaddressed brake defects, requiring differential power to stop the aircraft safely.

synopsis: An eyewitness saw two UAS flying within a Special Air Traffic Rule (SFAR) area close to numerous operating fixed wing and rotor wing aircraft.
summary: A surface observer reported two unauthorized quadcopter UAS operating over persons near Destin Airport within the SFAR 93 area. The reporter attributed the incident to unlicensed operators violating airspace rules and recommended issuing a NOTAM to warn of this common occurrence.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: POU Tower Ground Controller reported a hanger blocks the view of the runway and issues related to the blockage.
summary: Two tower controllers managed Aircraft X's delayed exit and high-speed taxi to Taxiway A while Aircraft Y was on final and Aircraft Z was rotating. A hangar obstructing the view of Taxiway A caused a delayed takeoff cancellation for Aircraft Y, which was stepped on, though Aircraft X was eventually observed clear of the runway.

synopsis: JAX TRACON Controller reported airspace issues related to GA traffic crossing air carrier final approach paths without communication. Controller suggested the JAX Class C needs to be extended to avoid these issues.
summary: An air traffic controller reported unsafe conditions at Jacksonville (JAX) Runway 26 where VFR aircraft on 1200 codes between 1,500 and 3,500 feet MSL blocked low-altitude approaches for arriving jets. The controller attributed the hazard to erratic traffic from a new flight school at FHB and recommended extending the Class C airspace.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a 2 hour delay due to the new automated maintenance reporting system having software issues.
summary: The First Officer reported a suspected bird strike on the #2 engine during the walk-around, but initial maintenance found no damage and cleared the aircraft for departure. The aircraft was later taken out of service at the destination because maintenance software could not accept the inspection write-up.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crews reported that during taxi from the gate the aircraft's right winglet struck the horizontal stabilizer of another aircraft at an adjacent gate. The flight crew of the other aircraft reported they were waiting for the marshallers to get into position at the gate and felt the aircraft move when it was struck.
summary: The flight crew taxiing a single-engine aircraft on Taxiway 4 struck the horizontal stabilizer of an aircraft at Gate 2 due to misjudged wingtip clearance and expectation bias. The incident resulted from poor risk management and task loading in a congested area, leading to a return to the gate with no injuries.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported crew scheduling tried to fly the First Officer beyond Far 117 limits.
summary: A First Officer and Captain faced potential FAR Part 117 violations during a deadhead and ferry turn due to maintenance delays and scheduling errors. The First Officer exceeded the unpublished Last Block In time after Crew Scheduling failed to provide clear guidance or rest accommodations despite repeated warnings.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported confusion and distractions when flying into Denver.
summary: The flight crew reported excessive workload and multiple reprogramming events during descent into Denver due to non-specific ATIS and conflicting runway transitions assigned by Center and Approach. These frequent, weather-unrelated changes caused VNAV discontinuities and required constant briefing updates while managing turbulence and high terrain.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported excessive frequency congestion at EWR airport due to VFR transitioning aircraft using the same Tower frequency as arrival and departure traffic. The reporter stated these operations used to have separate frequencies to alleviate the congestion.
summary: Newark Tower controllers reported that returning airliner traffic volumes have caused excessive workload and frequency congestion on the primary tower frequency. The reporter states the tower must revert to a dedicated station and frequency for VFR and helicopter traffic to manage the rush hour demands.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported a communication breakdown with Maintenance regarding Thermal Containment Bag replacement.
summary: A cabin crew member reported using a Thermal Containment Bag on Aircraft X for an overheating passenger device and noted separate issues with mask compliance and a medical emergency. The reporter failed to inform the supervisor about the bag usage despite successfully relaying maintenance instructions to the flight crew.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an unreliable glideslope signal at SJU Airport.
summary: The crew of a long-duty flight at SJU experienced an abrupt pitch-up and autopilot disengagement while intercepting the ILS Runway 08 glide slope at 3,000 ft. The pilots manually stabilized the aircraft and completed a hand-flown approach, suspecting a false glide slope signal noted in company safety alerts.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Light Transport aircraft pilot reported a LH Engine Fire CASS message which resulted in an engine shutdown and a return flight to departure airport.
summary: The crew received a left engine fire CASS message at 8,000 feet during cruise and secured the engine. They returned to ZZZ where fire responders met the aircraft, confirmed no fire, and deplaned passengers without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported seeing an aircraft taxiing too fast towards them and were readying to take evasive action before the other aircraft finally stopped.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X, cleared for takeoff on Runway 01 at DCA, observed Aircraft Y rapidly approaching the runway intersection. Aircraft Y stopped short after hard braking, allowing the crew to continue the takeoff, though the controller initially attempted to issue a rejected takeoff command before confirming the stop.

synopsis: B737 MAX Flight Attendant reported confusion over seat pocket safety cards being the correct type or not for the aircraft.
summary: The Captain and Flight Attendants discovered mismatched safety cards in seat pockets and overhead bins on a 737 MAX. Maintenance confirmed the seat and demo cards were correct for the specific tail number, though the origin of the overhead bin cards remained unverified.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported deviating from standard practices to seat a service member and his military working dog for the flight.
summary: A flight attendant relocated a large military service dog and handler from an aisle seat to the 1L door area during taxi after the dog blocked the aisle, as the agent had incorrectly assigned them a non-bulkhead seat. The crew completed the flight with the dog secured at the door, and the attendant reported the incident, acknowledging she should have denied boarding or returned to the gate rather than relying on the agent's placement.

synopsis: Instructor reported taking evasive action when two ultralights maneuvered too close in ZJX Class E airspace.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with two ultralight aircraft while flying at 1,500 feet in Class E airspace. Upon exiting a turn, the crew observed the ultralights approximately 500 feet horizontally away and slightly higher, prompting immediate evasive action.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported left brake malfunctioned on landing roll out causing a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 172 experienced left brake failure during the landing roll at ZZZ, causing the aircraft to overshoot the second exit. To stop, the pilot turned the aircraft 180 degrees onto a dirt road, resulting in right-wing damage to a fence and a subsequent hydraulic fluid leak from the left brake assembly.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Private pilot reported while on short final another aircraft entered the runway and began to takeoff.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X landed on Runway 21 at a non-controlled airport while Aircraft Y entered the runway, stopped, and then took off without communicating. The reporter attributed the near-miss to Aircraft Y's failure to monitor the correct frequency and stop on the active runway, compounded by heavy crosswinds affecting the approach.

synopsis: Center Controller reported reneging on a handoff for a helicopter that was off the filed airway, below the MEA, and the minimum IFR altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller coordinating a helicopter on Victor route XY to ZZZ1 initially approved a direct clearance without verifying the /A equipment suffix or Minimum Enroute Altitude (MEA). The controller later realized the helicopter was below the 4500-foot MEA, climbed it to 5000 feet, and attributed the error to infrequent route usage and poor coordination.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Center D-Side Controller reported a near midair, which reporter advised was due to a Radar Controller's control technique and reported inadequate control instructions.""
summary: A D-side observer reported that an overwhelmed controller in Sector X nearly caused a midair collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y near 10,000 feet due to poor judgment, inadequate instructions, and failure to maintain positive separation. The controller issued conflicting clearances and delayed urgent traffic avoidance instructions, leaving the aircraft in conflict until the observer intervened.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported having to divert after losing yellow system hydraulic quantity during cruise.
summary: The flight crew diverted from ZZZ to ZZZ2 after a left hydraulic quantity drop caused pressure loss and flight control degradation. Following a safe landing with inoperative nose wheel steering, the aircraft was towed to the gate after fire/rescue reported significant fluid leakage from the right wheel well.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Ramp worker reported a near collision between two aircraft being pushed to their assigned spots.
summary: The pushback operator of Aircraft Y halted its pushback from Gate XXY on Taxiline XY Dashed to avoid a potential collision with Aircraft X, which was simultaneously pushing back on Taxiline XY. The operator waited until Aircraft X completed its pushback and taxied out before resuming the movement.

synopsis: Air Carrier cargo ground personnel reported undocumented transport of Hazmat cargo due to ground handling errors.
summary: A Manifest Agent's date error caused an unmanifested Class 9 dangerous goods shipment to be loaded onto the flight despite missing from the Departure Staging Guide. The shipment arrived at the destination, requiring a re-manifest and re-shipment the following day to correct the documentation.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported the taxiway signage is misleading at DEN airport.
summary: The flight crew missed a turn to Taxiway WA at Denver while taxiing to Runway 34L due to a misleading direction sign indicating straight ahead instead of right. Ground Control corrected the error by instructing them to turn inside the deice pad and follow the preceding aircraft.

synopsis: Flight crew reported unauthorized transport of a personal portable oxygen container with passenger in passenger cabin.
summary: A Ramp Agent informed the Pilot-in-Command that a passenger was "with air," but the crew failed to clarify that this meant portable oxygen. The incident resulted from poor communication and lack of Hazmat training, allowing the passenger to board with the prohibited item.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported deviations from standard practices due to distractions in the cabin, causing check list omissions.
summary: The flight crew missed the before start checklist below the line before pushback due to distractions from a passenger mask issue and a faulty ramp headset while rushing to recover from a weather delay. They realized the omission only after pushback had commenced.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported descending in accordance with a TCAS/RA alert for VFR traffic above them.
summary: During departure from Atlanta, our aircraft received a TCAS RA due to a twin-engine piston aircraft at 14,500 ft that was not communicating with Atlanta Center. We descended to 13,500 ft to comply with the resolution advisory while the target fluctuated between 14,400 and 14,500 ft.

synopsis: Air carrier Maintenance Technician reported cargo spill cleanup procedures were not correctly followed.
summary: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported an unidentified alkali spill on an A300 at ZZZ, noting the source was unknown due to empty cargo containers. The reporter expressed concern that the aircraft was returned to service without a required deferral or completed spill form, contrary to General Maintenance Manual procedures.

synopsis: Pilot reported losing both MFD and PFD, resulting in a probable airspace violation.
summary: The pilot departed VFR with an inoperative PFD and COM 1, relying on COM 2 until the MFD screen blanked, causing a total loss of navigation and communication. After 20 minutes, systems recovered, but the pilot noted a possible Class B airspace entry due to the inability to display boundaries during the outage.

synopsis: Pilot reported a near collision during departure after they announced their intentions on the wrong frequency. The Tower was closed at the time of the event.
summary: A fatigued pilot departing ZZZ for ZZZ1 after a Customs delay failed to enter the correct Tower frequency due to stress. The pilot initiated takeoff unaware of a helicopter on the runway, aborted the rotation to avoid a collision, and attributed the near-miss to fatigue-induced errors in frequency selection.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported losing lift during takeoff and ran off the runway onto the grass.
summary: A solo student pilot conducting a commercial cross-country flight in a ZZZ1-ZZZ-ZZZ1 diverted left onto the grass during takeoff after rotating at 55 knots in 12-knot winds. The pilot attributed the loss of lift to incorrect control inputs, resulting in no visible aircraft damage.

synopsis: A flight instructor reported an NMAC on final approach with an aircraft that had reported them in sight to the Tower.
summary: A commercial single-engine training flight on final approach at ZZZ avoided a collision with a pipeline patrol aircraft that crossed the approach path at 1,400 feet. The pilot leveled off to let the other aircraft pass 75 feet below, attributing the near miss to ATC allowing the crossing and the pilot's failure to correct course despite claiming visual contact.

synopsis: TRACON Controller in training reported they vectored a departing aircraft while the aircraft was still below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller training on position assigned Aircraft X, conducting IFR practice approaches, a climb to 3,000 feet. The controller failed to notice the previous controller had issued an inappropriate altitude clearance that violated the 2,500-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a rejected take off due to aircraft shuddering.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at approximately 100 knots due to a jolt and shaking caused by two blown left main tires. Fire Rescue confirmed no fire or injuries, and passengers were deplaned via air stairs after the crew shut down the engines and coordinated with operations.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported issues with Electronic NOTOC information format.
summary: The crew on Aircraft X identified a missing UN HAZMAT number on the ENOTOC but proceeded after Load Control confirmed compliance. The reporter attributes the error to the confusing ENOTOC layout and incorrect verification by Load Control, leaving the actual HAZMAT cargo unknown.

synopsis: B747-400 First Officer reported the autoland system was malfunctioning during approach/landing.
summary: The crew performed a recertification autoland at ZZZZ1 on an aircraft with a deferred autoland system. The landing was deemed unsatisfactory due to intermittent loss of raw data glideslope indications on both pilot sides, suggesting the system deferral was improper.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an airborne conflict resulting in a TCAS RA.
summary: While cruising at FL370 near CAMJO, the crew received a TCAS Climb RA and executed the maneuver while Jacksonville Center issued a conflicting turn instruction to another aircraft. The conflict cleared at 37,700 feet, and the crew reported the event, noting that ATC staffing shortages may have contributed to the situation.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported dispatch and maintenance mishandling of the flight Operations including the aircraft, destination issues and a viable backup plan.
summary: The crew experienced a late departure after maintenance grounded the aircraft due to open write-ups, followed by a risky plan to fly to a mountainous airport with potential runway light outages. GPS and terrain warnings were temporarily lost due to jamming, though signals returned before descent, prompting the reporter to criticize reactive operations management.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported MEL procedures were not followed correctly and they had to divert due to insufficient fuel loaded for the flight.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ2 after a fuel system MEL for the inoperative right inner fuel quantity indicator led to a false fuel reading and significant imbalance. Manual verification confirmed the right inner tank was empty despite system indications, causing the crew to suspect insufficient fuel and execute a precautionary landing.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported a loss of the green hydraulic system inflight resulting in an expedited descent and landing.
summary: The crew received a green hydraulic system low quantity ECAM warning while descending through FL330 enroute to ZZZ. After holding at FL220 to complete checklists, they landed uneventfully on Runway XXC and were towed in due to the green hydraulic system failure.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported the First Officer discovered a fuel upload discrepancy and a subsequent check by Maintenance revealed that there was 6,500 pounds less fuel onboard than requested.
summary: The First Officer discovered a 6,500-lb fuel discrepancy during preflight checks, prompting Maintenance to verify quantities via magnetic level indicators and tank sticking. The Right Inner Tank contained only 4,000 lb instead of the indicated 10,500 lb, requiring fuel uplift and reinstatement of the Inner Tank Fuel MEL.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence departing ATL in trail of an A321.
summary: The crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A321 at 1,100–1,300 feet AGL after being cleared for takeoff while the lead aircraft was still rolling. The reporter attributes this to Air Traffic Control issuing early clearances, causing significant rolling that required manual control and raised safety concerns.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported missing a turn at Taxiway A5 in DLH airport. Captain stated ATC mentioned it was a common occurrence at the location in the airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, a new crew at an unfamiliar airport, inadvertently passed the runway entrance while distracted by a hydraulic procedure discussion during a rushed taxi. The pilot attributed the error to reduced situational awareness caused by the new crew, morning rush, and unclear chart markings, noting ATC confirmed the area is a frequent hotspot.

synopsis: Flight Attendant crew reported a fume event which resulted in physiological symptoms and medical treatment.
summary: Four flight attendants on Aircraft X reported an oily, dirty sock smell from gaspers during boarding and later suffered headaches, nausea, and tingling during the flight to ZZZZ1. The crew attributed these symptoms to a fume event, resulting in delayed ground medical transport, hospitalization, and a final diagnosis of lung injury.

synopsis: Sundowner Instructor reported an NMAC event during landing training.
summary: A flight instructor with a nervous student pilot mistakenly entered left base for Runway XY instead of the assigned Runway XX at ZZZ. The error caused another aircraft on right downwind to descend below them, resulting from the instructor's distraction and habit of landing on the usual runway.

synopsis: Robinson R-44 pilot reported an NMAC event with a non-ADS-B-equipped helicopter.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X nearly collided midair with an inbound Canadian helicopter while flying southwest of ZZZ. The near miss occurred because the other pilot's aircraft lacked ADS-B Out equipment, preventing electronic detection until a visual sighting prompted an evasive maneuver.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported an NMAC event during training flight with a Cessna P210 Centurion who was not on correct radio frequency.
summary: A Centurion aircraft passed directly below the reporting aircraft at a faster speed from the 8 o'clock position while not on the practice frequency. The crew initiated a climb and left bank to increase separation between the two aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a critical ground conflict during takeoff with a non-reporting aircraft on runway at CPT non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot departing Cleburne Regional Airport encountered a student aircraft that failed to announce a back-taxi after a go-around. The pilot rotated and veered right to avoid the traffic, which was obscured by the runway's elevation, maintaining separation despite the lack of radio communication.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC at non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot flying a fast corporate aircraft to ZZZ Airport encountered two instances where slower training aircraft turned final directly ahead, causing rapid closure. While the pilot executed safe go-arounds and a landing, a subsequent gear-up landing by another aircraft closed the runway.

synopsis: BE-76 flight instructor reported an engine temperature problem during takeoff resulting in a return to departure airport.
summary: During a Part 141 MEI training flight, an instructor and student experienced rapid engine temperature rises after takeoff due to engine plugs left in by the student. The aircraft landed safely, but the incident was caused by the student's incomplete preflight and the instructor's failure to verify it.

synopsis: Part 107 crew had a lost link with the UAS. After attempting a return to home (RTH) function the Crew was unable to regain control of the UAS which crashed shortly after.
summary: The pilot reported a drone lost signal, initiated a return-to-home, drifted away, and crashed onto a building roof after regaining control. The incident resulted in no injuries or property damage.

synopsis: FAI TRACON Controller reported ZAN Center was not complying with established procedures to route aircraft away from military special use airspace. Reporter stated this is a routine occurrence.
summary: Anchorage Center failed to remove Aircraft X from the HRDNG STAR before transferring it to FAI Approach while Lightning Group airspace was active. Consequently, the Approach Controller had to vector the aircraft away from the restricted Viper B MOA/ATCAA to ensure safety.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported while following ZDV center clearance, TRACON reported the descent was through holding pattern traffic.
summary: The flight crew received conflicting holding and descent clearances from Denver Center and Approach while transitioning from the CLASH 3 to NIIXX 2 arrival into Denver. Center inadvertently descended the aircraft through a holding stack before Approach vectored them around weather to intercept final for runway 35R.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported crossing restrictions and speed issues while flying into RIC airport on the RNAV (RNP) Y Runway 16 Approach.
summary: The flight crew flying an RNAV (RNP) Y approach to Runway 16 at RIC encountered FMC alerts and a high deviation after the HEMME waypoint. They corrected the path by deploying speedbrakes and landing gear 30 miles out, successfully completing the landing despite the steep descent profile.

synopsis: Flight crew and Dispatcher reported receiving email from Duty Officer regarding unmanifested inaccessible Dangerous Goods on board on a previous flight.
summary: Ramp personnel loaded unmanifested inaccessible dangerous goods and dry ice into the aircraft belly and cabin at ZZZ due to improper manifesting and handling. The discrepancy was discovered during offloading at ZZZ1, prompting a recommendation for additional training for cargo loaders and dangerous goods staff.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported incorrect loading location of Radioactive Hazmat cargo after aircraft departure.
summary: Ramp agents incorrectly loaded radioactive materials in position X instead of Y, missing software warnings. The flight continued safely after ground approval based on low exposure rates, with the cause attributed to the agent's failure to heed special handling alerts.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain and a Flight Attendant reported an unsuitable work environment due communication issues between the Captain and a Flight Attendant.
summary: Cabin crew reported that a Flight Attendant previously removed for verbally attacking pilots was secretly reassigned to an international flight without their knowledge. This created an unsafe and uncomfortable work environment, causing the crew significant distress during the flight.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported a fume event during climb reoccurred during descent resulting in health issues.
summary: Cabin crew detected odors during climb and descent, resulting in a slight headache. They briefed the crew, reported the incident to the company, completed a fumes report, and deplaned after passengers.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a gate checked bag with Lithium Ion powered laptop was erroneously put in the cargo.
summary: A flight attendant reported a passenger's potential lithium battery in a pink tag bag, prompting consultation with the captain and gate agents. The captain retrieved the bag and returned the laptop to the passenger, resolving the safety concern.

synopsis: CL604 First Officer reported missing a crossing restriction during descent.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced two Undesired Aircraft States during a ZZZ arrival in a CL604 due to VNAV capturing floor altitudes from the approach procedure instead of the STAR. The reporter attributed these events to inadequate training on the Pro Line Fusion avionics suite and confusing FMS programming logic.

synopsis: C152 reported an NMAC event during landing training.
summary: A pilot practicing traffic patterns at ZZZ experienced a close call with another aircraft while turning to right downwind for Runway XXR. The other pilot, reportedly distracted and having lost sight of the reporter, executed a climbing left turn to avoid a collision in controlled airspace.

synopsis: Cessna 185 pilot reported a track heading deviation due to improperly operating the vacuum driven directional gyro.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 185 in Bravo airspace deviated from an ATC-assigned heading after failing to manually set the vacuum-driven directional gyro. The pilot corrected the heading and aligned the gyro with the magnetic compass, attributing the error to recent experience primarily in glass cockpit aircraft.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GA pilot reported a runway excursion due to loss of directional control on landing.
summary: The pilot landed long on Runway XX with a crosswind, lost directional control on touchdown, and slid sideways into a marshy ditch. The aircraft stopped abruptly, causing minor right wingtip damage, but there were no injuries.

synopsis: Instructor and student pilots reported the student experienced a runway excursion on landing rollout during a solo flight.
summary: A student pilot executing solo touch-and-goes at ZZZ veered off the runway onto adjacent grass after the nose veered right during flap retraction. The pilot chose to exit the runway to avoid a potential spin or nose drop, resulting in no damage or injuries, though training was subsequently suspended.

synopsis: Technician reported multiple magneto failures of factory rebuilt magnetos on the same PA-32 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic replaced a failed left magneto with a factory rebuilt unit, but the right magneto failed during takeoff, forcing a return landing. The reporter attributes the issue to premature failure of factory rebuilt magnetos, noting only 100 hours between failures and warning of potential catastrophic loss of life.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ZJX Center Controller reported an aircraft started a climb due to incorrect readback/hearback which resulted in a loss of standard separation.
summary: A controller failed to verify Aircraft X's incorrect readback of a climb to FL200 while managing high traffic near CEW. This misunderstanding caused a loss of vertical separation with descending Aircraft Y, forcing a turn for lateral separation and highlighting sector congestion issues.

synopsis: EWR Tower Controller reported solar glare approximately 1.4 miles S/SE of EWR Tower.
summary: Solar panel reflection caused visibility issues for arrivals and departures on the Northeast flow 1.5 miles south/southeast of Newark. The reporter recommends removing or reorienting the panel to eliminate the glare from the tower's line of sight.

synopsis: B737 MAX Captain reported not activating the auto brake system for RTO when completing the before takeoff checklist.
summary: The Captain failed to set the autobrakes to RTO during preflight on a MAX aircraft due to the selector's relocated position and obstruction by paperwork. The error was discovered after takeoff during clean-up, though the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported numerous interruptions caused distractions during pre-departure checks and caused concern over following published procedures.
summary: The flight crew faced significant time pressure during pre-departure checks due to a tight hotel pickup schedule and mandatory COVID health screenings. These constraints caused repeated interruptions from other ground teams, increasing workload and creating a threat of missing required International/Oceanic checks before departure.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into MIA.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a Boeing 777 during descent and departure at MIA due to ATC minimizing separation and placing them behind a heavy aircraft in strong quartering tailwinds. The pilot attributed the rapid rolls and safety risks to these operational practices and requested changes to descent sequencing and takeoff spacing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported individuals walking in front of the aircraft as it began taxiing on the ramp.
summary: During taxi clearance at PHX, the First Officer stopped Aircraft X after three individuals walked in front of the right engine. The crew notified the Ramp Controller and waited for the pedestrians to clear the area, attributing the incident to the individuals' lack of common sense and failure to recognize the danger.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported NOTAMS were not updating through the company's system.
summary: A dispatcher relieving two others failed to access updated NOTAMS due to system failure, task saturation, and server overload while managing storm re-routes. The flight landed safely, but the reporter attributed the issue to the FAA NAIMS system not updating and poor shift turnover communication.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported NOTAMs were not available due to equipment outage so they could not release flights. The reporter stated the dispatchers were told by Supervisors to contact airports operations to get NOTAMs but this was not sufficient and in violation of company procedures.
summary: A dispatcher delayed releasing 13 flights due to FAA server damage from a roof leak that disabled NOTAMs, compounded by thunderstorms near ZZZ. The reporter cited management's inadequate mitigation plan and the inability to legally verify all NOTAMs via phone calls as the cause for the late releases.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported the stick shaker activated on approach. The crew reconfigured the aircraft and continued on a stabilized approach.
summary: The flight crew experienced a stick shaker activation at 1,500 feet on left base for Runway XX due to flight spoilers remaining deployed while extending flaps to 45 degrees. The spoilers were immediately retracted, restoring airspeed, and the aircraft completed a stabilized approach and landed without incident.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported the engine shut down by itself while they were holding short for takeoff.
summary: During a local training flight at ZZZ, the aircraft experienced an uncommanded engine shutdown while holding short of Runway XX. Restart attempts failed, requiring a tow to the ramp, and a post-flight inspection resulted in the aircraft being squawked.

synopsis: During taxi into the gate, airline pilot reported receiving conflicting directions from the marshaller and the automated docking system.
summary: During taxiing to the gate, the pilot encountered conflicting signals between a visual docking system reading "STOP" and marshallers waving the aircraft in. The crew resolved the issue by having a marshaller reset the system, then completed the taxi using marshallers only due to good daylight visibility.

synopsis: Captain reported a fume event during initial climb resulted in an air return.
summary: During climb at 7,000 feet, flight attendants reported cabin fumes, prompting the crew to return to ZZZ and execute the QRH fumes procedure. After landing despite a bird strike ahead, ground inspection found no heat source, but rising cabin temperatures due to no airflow required deplaning.

synopsis: Flight crew reported a GA aircraft flew through their approach path necessitating a go-around and re-vectoring for the approach.
summary: The crew executed a go-around during a visual approach to ZZZ after a non-communicating VFR aircraft made an unexpected turn, forcing a deviation from the final approach course. Contributing factors included a last-minute runway change, insufficient briefing of conflicting traffic, and crew fatigue.

synopsis: Pilot reported landing with the nose landing gear not locked and hydraulic flow indicators illuminated.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft at ZZZ with an unlocked nose gear after hydraulic and emergency extension attempts failed to provide indication or extension. The crew executed a soft landing holding the nose off, followed by a ground evacuation and shutdown.

synopsis: B737-800 Pilot reported failing to make proper AML entries for hydraulic system maintenance event.
summary: The pilot failed to log a low Hydraulic System B quantity before maintenance serviced it, allowing the aircraft to depart without an entry. A subsequent leak was discovered in a wing during post-flight troubleshooting at ZZZ1.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot back taxiing at an international non-towered airport reported traffic not in CTAF communications was on approach to the same runway and initiated a go-around on short final.
