summary: The flight crew descended below 15,000 feet at TAKBE without ATC clearance for a visual approach, confusing a direct routing instruction with descent authorization. This occurred during a challenging arrival at COD involving turbulence and windshear, though the crew subsequently received clearance and landed safely on the second attempt.

synopsis: Dash 8-400 Captain reported jammed pitch trim system severe enough to cause a diversion.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Dash 8-400 experienced a jammed pitch trim during climb at 10,000 feet, causing a loss of autopilot and requiring substantial nose-down control force. They diverted to ZZZ1 due to high workload and airspeed restrictions, landing safely without incident.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after inflight shutdown of the right engine following a compressor stall and EGT overtemp event.
summary: During a reduced power departure, the right engine suffered a compressor stall and over-temperature at 400 feet AGL while turning right. The crew secured the engine, returned to the departure airport, and executed a single-engine ILS landing with no injuries or further damage.

synopsis: Challenger CL600 First Officer reported unable to pressurize cabin and diverted to a precautionary landing.
summary: During departure, the aircraft failed to pressurize and leveled off. After running the QRH checklist and finding manual pressurization control impossible, the crew returned to the field.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported a trim malfunction on descent and followed QRH procedures to land successfully.
summary: During the approach phase, the crew experienced an uncommanded stabilizer trim malfunction while configuring for landing. The Captain executed immediate action items to disconnect the trim systems, elected to continue the approach, and landed safely before reporting the discrepancy to maintenance.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a ground gate return to unload Hazmat cargo due to no Hazmat documentation provided to flight crew.
summary: The flight crew discovered unsecured hazardous materials during taxi after receiving conflicting ACARS messages from operations. The captain refused the shipment, returned to the gate to have two red bags and two boxes removed, and cited a lack of cargo information and improper securing as safety concerns.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that the MSLP ATUMA3B SID depiction differs from the narrative.
summary: The pilot reported a discrepancy between the ATUMA3B departure chart and its narrative text regarding the climb to 8,000 ft and subsequent turn to heading 315. The chart and FMC indicate turning at the CAT fix, while the narrative instructs turning only after reaching 8,000 ft without specifying the fix.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported hydroplaning and poor braking action while performing a slow turn during taxi but were able to safely regain aircraft control.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Boeing 737 hydroplaned on wet Taxiway XX while turning at 15 knots after landing, losing nose wheel steering and braking. The aircraft skidded 15 feet near the edge before regaining traction, which the crew attributed to poor drainage or unusually slick pavement conditions.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a fumes event during cruise resulting in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew diverted Flight ZZZ1 from FL370 after a rapid cabin altitude rise triggered oxygen mask deployment and subsequent smoke reports. The pilot attributed the incident to an open MEL for the #1 engine HP bleed valve combined with oxygen generator heat in warm ambient conditions.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported being notified of undocumented Hazmat on an airborne flight.
summary: Dispatch received notification from Ramp regarding 60 kg of undeclared dry ice on Aircraft X. Since the quantity was within limits, no further action was required, though the crew was advised to submit a report.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported numerous diversions and deviations while navigating through severe weather, exacerbated by an MELed speed bug resulting in hail damage when finally reaching destination airport.
summary: The flight crew penetrated a storm cell while climbing from 17,000 feet to FL210, encountering turbulence, rain, and ice despite ATC radar guidance. Subsequent inspection revealed extensive radome damage and an exposed antenna, leading to flight cancellation and maintenance evaluation.

synopsis: Technician reported that they inadvertently deployed a door slide while repairing a cabin conditioned air gasper that had fallen out.
summary: A mechanic performing a service check on Aircraft X deployed an R2 escape slide inflation reservoir bottle while reaching through its cover to access an air outlet distribution valve. The deployment occurred because the AMM instructions were insufficient, leading the mechanic to use an unintended access point.

synopsis: Technician reported not receiving email notifications for engine inspections because the station was left off an email list.
summary: A mechanic reported loose EGT thermocouple leads on all four probes causing erratic readings, while a separate IT issue with a screen saver function caused desktop performance problems. The engine error was corrected, and the computer issue was resolved by disabling the screen saver.

synopsis: Ramp Agent reported a precautionary landing due a water bottle hindering the nose landing gear from retracting.
summary: A ramp agent placed a vitamin water bottle on the main landing gear, preventing the nose gear tires from retracting and causing an emergency landing. The reporter admitted that stress from a tight schedule led to skipping the arrival walk-around, which would have detected the obstruction.

aircraft: Lake Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Lake aircraft pilot reported numerous electrical systems failures during flight and elected to divert.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical failures during cruise caused by a broken battery terminal connector, initially misdiagnosed as a hydraulic pump short. The connector failure resulted from vibration due to a nose wheel shimmy on the previous landing, which widened a pre-existing crack.

synopsis: A pilot departing SZT non-towered airport reported they taxied on to the runway to depart when they noticed another aircraft on short final. The pilot taxied off the runway onto the grass.
summary: A pilot forgot to check for landing traffic and entered the runway while a small aircraft was on short final, causing the other pilot to execute a go-around. The pilot attributed the near-miss to distraction and subsequently exited the runway onto the grass.

synopsis: A pilot departing O61 non-towered airport reported they observed an arriving aircraft head on to them as they were taking off and had to turn to avoid them. The reporter thought they heard the aircraft report inbound to the opposite direction runway they departed from.
summary: The pilot holding short of Runway 31 took off after hearing a small aircraft on final, believing it was for Runway 31, but discovered the aircraft was actually landing on Runway 13. The pilot immediately turned right to avoid a collision and attributed the error to confirmation bias regarding the runway clearance.

synopsis: A Private Pilot reported a conflict with another aircraft on an opposing base leg and took evasive action.
summary: A private pilot and instructor flying a complex aircraft into ZZZ experienced a near collision with another aircraft on a non-standard wide base leg. The pilot attributed the incident to the non-radar tower's inability to accurately sequence traffic and the other pilot's deviation from standard pattern entry.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reported an engine coolant leak and fearing an immediate engine failure, elected to land on a taxiway.
summary: The pilot departed runway XY and detected a significant coolant leak at 400–500 ft on the crosswind leg. Declaring an emergency due to potential engine loss, the pilot turned 180 degrees and landed on Taxiway C to avoid further maneuvers.

synopsis: General aviation pilot was in cruise flight at approximately 6,500 feet. An undescribed UAV passed in the opposite direction approximately 1,000 feet below.
summary: Pilots reported spotting a drone flying south approximately 1,000 feet horizontally and 500–1,000 feet below their aircraft while at 6,500 ft MSL, 2 miles north of CCR. The drone was traveling in the opposite direction of the plane.

synopsis: Pilot reported ATC issued complex and confusing taxi instructions during the landing rollout which led to confusion about being cleared to cross a runway.
summary: The pilot received complex taxi instructions with two runway crossings while still rolling after landing, causing confusion. Miscommunication regarding the route led to the pilot taxiing on an active runway before exiting to the ramp, though no collision occurred.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An aerobatic pilot who has a FAA waiver for a designated Aerobatic Practice Area reported traffic routinely flies through the airspace when it is advertised in use.
summary: A pilot practicing aerobatics in a waived Aerobatic Practice Area north of HGR reported concerns about VFR traffic entering the airspace. The pilot attributed the risk to limited frequency monitoring capabilities and requested that "Hot" APAs be displayed more prominently on digital navigation systems like TFRs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported they did not receive the obstacle clearance departure procedure or a SID from ATC or the Foreflight App. The reporter suggested obstacle departure procedures [ODP] automatically populate on the Foreflight software.
summary: A pilot departing San Diego (SEE) in VFR conditions followed a complex electronic route instead of the required Mission Bay Two obstacle departure due to avionics limitations and confirmation bias. This resulted in a terrain alert and a possible pilot deviation when the pilot failed to turn right as expected by the Approach Controller.

synopsis: C172 instructor and student pilots reported that student pilot lost directional control during takeoff roll while on a solo flight, resulting in a Rejected Take Off and a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control during takeoff on Runway XX at ZZZ, veering left into the grass after applying right rudder and inadvertently tapping the left toe brake. The takeoff was rejected with no damage to the aircraft or airport property.

synopsis: A Tower controller and flight crew reported the flight crew departed an airport with a closed tower without approval for release from the ARTCC. The Tower Controller reported they failed to advise the flight crew to hold for release after issuing their clearance prior to Tower closing.
summary: Ground Control and an IFR pilot were involved during a facility evacuation for COVID-19 cleaning. The pilot departed without a hold-for-release instruction after the tower closed, contacted Center at 1,500 feet, and was later notified of a possible pilot deviation.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported a CFIT event during approach resulting in a go-around. A communications breakdown between flight crew and ATC was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway XXR at ZZZ, the flight crew descended below the cleared 3,000 feet due to autopilot mode confusion and delayed speedbrake retraction. This triggered a low altitude alert, prompting a missed approach and safe re-vectoring for another attempt.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an inadvertent release of the parking brake, allowing the aircraft to roll forward.
summary: The pilot reported that while adjusting rudder pedals, they likely released the parking brake, causing the aircraft to roll back 12 feet during pre-departure. A safety walkaround confirmed no damage to the aircraft or injuries, and no ATC contact was required.

synopsis: A flight crew reported they flew into military Restricted Airspace when were assigned a vector off course and issued a frequency change. They could not establish communications on the new frequency in a timely manner due to frequency congestion and saturation on the new frequency.
summary: Pilots lost communication with en route ATC while being vectored, causing an inadvertent entry into Special Use Airspace. The incident resulted from ATC task saturation and frequency management issues, requiring a Guard frequency transmission to re-establish contact and exit the restricted area.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported misgivings when the aircraft assigned for the flight had a faulty pressurization system and he would be operating in to and out of a high altitude airport.
summary: The pilot reported that an aircraft with a faulty pressurization system was dispatched from high-altitude ZZZZ. A potential Alternate channel failure during takeoff would force an oxygen mask deployment and a divert to an unserved airport, as returning would exceed passenger oxygen time limits.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp vehicle driver reported a near-collision with an aircraft that was taxiing into the gate area.
summary: A ground vehicle driver nearly collided with an aircraft turning onto a taxi lane without clearance or wing walkers present. The driver accelerated to avoid the wing tip after hearing a faint horn, noting the plane entered the path without warning before being stopped by ground crew.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported bright lights from a sports field complex near the approach end of the runway were mistaken for the PAPIs.
summary: Pilots approaching Runway 2 at BMI mistook four bright lights from a nearby sports complex for PAPI lights in IMC conditions, causing momentary spatial disorientation. After cross-checking instruments and descending to 800 feet to locate the actual runway environment, they completed a stabilized landing without incident.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after experiencing smoke from the First Officer yoke and a battery discharge annunciation.
summary: The crew detected smoke from the First Officer's yoke and battery discharge lights during climb, prompting a return to the departure airport. They followed QRH procedures, received ILS vectors, and executed an uneventful landing at maximum weight without requiring assistance.

synopsis: A Flight Crew reported a taxiway incursion due to poor signage.
summary: The flight crew erroneously turned onto Delta taxiway instead of Bravo at LFPG due to poor signage, language barriers, and misprioritized tasks. Ground ATC detected the error and issued corrected taxi instructions to reach the stand without traffic conflict.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 Flight Attendant reported a DOT violation due to no operative lavatories with passengers on board.
summary: The reporter stated that a full aircraft with all lavatories inoperative was held below 16,000 feet. This situation violated DOT requirements mandating operable lavatories whenever an airplane is on the tarmac.

synopsis: PA-28 student pilot reported loss of directional control resulted in a runway excursion. Flight instructor reported accompanying the student on the return flight to home airport.
summary: The pilot and student landed an aircraft that veered left into grass, and the student later went off the runway during a solo. Although maintenance verbally cleared the aircraft for return flight, the pilot realized no written confirmation existed, prompting an investigation to obtain a written statement from the inspecting mechanic.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported a nose gear collapse on landing and suspects metal fatigue caused the strut failure.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft on Runway XX after a stabilized RNAV approach when the fixed nose gear collapsed, causing the plane to skid to a halt. The reporter attributes the failure to metal fatigue in the strut weld near the engine frame.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp personnel reported undocumented 'Hazmat labeled cargo' during unloading.
summary: Ground staff discovered a leaking oily substance from a military mail parcel while unloading airmail from Aircraft X, contaminating three other parcels. The reporter attributes the cause to improper shipping by the shipper and recommends holding the parcel while informing shippers not to send such items on passenger aircraft.

synopsis: Gulfstream G280 flight crew reported that the First Officer's windshield shattered at top of climb, causing a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a shattered right forward windscreen at 40,000 feet while in IMC during cruise. They donned oxygen masks, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely after following the emergency checklist.

synopsis: Cessna 414A single pilot reported a CFIT event during a high workload approach. Pilot overcame workload and executed a safe landing.
summary: During a busy arrival, the pilot's trim actuator failed while descending, causing a warning horn that led to a frequency programming error and a misread altitude clearance. The pilot descended to 2,100 feet instead of 2,600 feet, triggered a low altitude alert, and subsequently climbed to the correct altitude before joining the localizer.

synopsis: R-22 Instructor reported an NMAC event during landing pattern training. R-22 executed an evasive maneuver to prevent a collision with a solo student on parallel runway.
summary: A helicopter instructor and student flying left traffic at 300 AGL descended to 150 AGL and turned right to avoid a solo student pilot in a fixed-wing aircraft who turned early left at 300 AGL. The reporter attributed the near collision to the student's lack of situational awareness and tight pattern flying.

synopsis: Super King Air 200 flight crew reported autopilot failure including an uncommanded pitch trim event caused them to overshoot the assigned altitude prior to autopilot disconnect.
summary: The copilot flying on autopilot during takeoff experienced a mode failure where the aircraft overshot 3,000 feet to 3,300 feet despite altitude capture indications. The captain took control to correct the climb and trim issues, avoiding a conflict with traffic at 4,000 feet, and the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a fume event that started one hour prior to landing resulting in physiological symptoms.
summary: Cabin crew detected a strong, irritating odor during descent into Country I, which entered the cockpit and forced the reporter to use oxygen. Mechanics later found burned catering paper behind coffee makers, but the reporter stated this was not the source of the odor experienced in flight.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported a Too Low Flaps warning occurred on final approach and conducted a go-around to a successful landing. Reporter stated that differences in viewing the flap position indicator in the MAX and the NG type aircraft contributed to an incorrect flap setting.
summary: The flight crew received a 'Too Low Flaps' warning on short final and executed a go-around, followed by an uneventful landing. The pilot attributed the event to the MAX flap gauge's lack of depth perception compared to the NG, prompting a new habit of pointing to the gauge for verification.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported the jetway at their gate at MYR airport cannot be opened from the inside which would be a hazard during an emergency evacuation.
summary: Crew members reported that jetway doors at Gate XX, MYR, lock from the inside without accessible exit buttons or push bars, trapping occupants. The reporter stated this design prevents escape into the terminal or ramp during an emergency evacuation, creating a safety hazard requiring immediate installation of internal unlock mechanisms.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a taxiway incursion and ground conflict resulted from receiving ATC taxi instructions during a high workload landing roll and not being able to clarify with Ground Control.
summary: During landing rollout, the Captain misheard a Tower instruction to hold short of Taxiway 2 and entered it, causing a conflict with a towed aircraft. The incident resulted from high workload, a blocked Ground transmission, and a breakdown in Crew Resource Management where the First Officer failed to verify the clearance.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported hostility and unprofessional communication when contacting Dispatch and the MOD after a decision to divert for lavatory servicing caused by departure airport ground agents not servicing lavatories before departure.
summary: The pilot diverted due to inoperative lavatories, but Operations Control blamed the decision and failed to arrange repairs, causing sleep loss. This fatigue led the pilot to remove themselves from the subsequent flight for safety reasons.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a fume event during preflight resulting in aircraft swap and flight attendants experiencing physiological symptoms.
summary: During pre-departure boarding at ZZZ, flight attendants reported a "dirty sock" smell from the APU, prompting the crew to execute the Aircraft Odor checklist and deplane passengers. Maintenance was notified, paramedics assessed symptomatic flight attendants and recommended hospital evaluation, and the flight departed three hours later with a new aircraft and crew.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported passenger misconduct related to COVID-19 mask requirements.
summary: Cabin crew managed multiple passengers in seats XX3 and XX4 who repeatedly removed or improperly wore masks during flight and deplaning. After verbal warnings and issuing a formal notice to one passenger, compliance was achieved without further escalation, and the Captain was informed the issue was resolved.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC after descending below cleared altitude on approach to UGN airport.
summary: The pilot, while executing an RNAV 05 approach, descended below the 2,500-foot crossing restriction at FOVOJ and initiated a recovery at 1,300 feet MSL. The pilot attributed the incident to an improper instrument scan.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported that his student pilot input excessive rudder causing him to assume the controls to prevent a runway excursion but was unable to prevent the aircraft from traveling onto the grass, requiring a tow back to the ramp.
summary: An instructor and student veered off Runway XXR during takeoff after the student overcorrected rudder input, causing the instructor to lose control. The pilot aborted the takeoff, exited the runway to protect the propeller and nose gear, and reported a possible light strike requiring a tow.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported reported taking evasive action to avoid an aircraft reported by ADB-B TCAS as 100 feet below altitude and very close.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot executing a touch-and-go in haze lost sight of a preceding Cessna 172. A TCAS alert at 1,400 feet revealed the other aircraft 100 feet below, prompting the pilot to turn right, reduce throttle, and deploy full flaps to increase separation.

synopsis: B737-700 flight cew reported a low altitude alert and initiated a Go Around at an airport that both crew members were flying into for the first time.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring on a ZZZZZ 1 arrival descended below their 7,000-foot clearance limit to 4,000 feet after misinterpreting ATC instructions. This triggered a Low Altitude Alert, requiring a climb before ATC issued an immediate visual clearance and noted a potential pilot deviation.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 flight crew reported an air turn back caused by a malfunctioning central warning computer.
summary: During climb on the ZZZZZ SID at 7,000 feet, the crew experienced simultaneous aural warnings for airspeed, fire, and pressurization with no visual indications. They returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing; post-landing inspections found no fire or system faults, yet the alarms persisted and could not be silenced by maintenance.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported IAH is using an unpublished Tower frequency.
summary: A crew on arrival into IAH experienced high altitude vectors and a frequency confusion involving an unpublished tower frequency, resulting in a potential separation conflict with traffic on runway 8R. The ATC Ops Manager attributed the near-miss to tight spacing and the use of an unlisted frequency, prompting a pilot deviation inquiry.

synopsis: Ground Personnel reported difficulties and communications problems while training new employees to operate the jet bridge safely.
summary: A jetbridge trainee operating Jetbridge XXX nearly contacted an aircraft engine while moving off the gate because she ignored a ramp guide's directions and focused on her screen. A ramp lead intervened via radio to stop the movement and prevent the collision.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported a loss of cabin pressure and inability to control cabin temperature, resulting in an air turn back.
summary: During climb out at 12,000 feet, the crew received a L BLEED DUCT warning, causing cabin temperatures to reach 40°C due to an inoperative engine bleed valve. The aircraft descended below 10,000 feet using ram air for cooling and landed safely at ZZZ for normal deplaning.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported the First Officer's sliding window opened on takeoff roll, causing an air turn back and a precautionary landing.
summary: During takeoff, the First Officer's R2 flight deck window opened at 110 knots, causing extreme noise and communication loss. The Captain took control, continued the takeoff, and returned for a safe landing after determining the window could not be closed in flight.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported No. 1 engine generator drive failure during departure climb. Flight crew requested ATC priority handling for air return followed by a safe landing.
summary: Flight ZZZ-ZZZ1 experienced a Gen 1 failure and IDG disconnect with an INOP APU while climbing from 7,000 ft. The crew coordinated with ATC, Dispatch, and Maintenance to return to ZZZ, where they executed a normal ILS landing and switched aircraft.

synopsis: Captain reported hard braking to avoid collision with a fuel truck being operated outside of the vehicle access roads in the gate area.
summary: A pilot taxiing outbound reported a large fuel truck darting toward the aircraft's wingtip while remaining outside the protected white line, forcing an emergency brake application. No injuries occurred, but the pilot noted insufficient clearance and recommended that full-size aircraft use the centerline to avoid similar ground vehicle conflicts.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported erroneously transported Human Organ (Kidney) on the flight deck in violation of FOM Hazmat policy.
summary: The Captain and a crew member allowed cargo personnel to transport a kidney on the flight deck without an escort, violating FOM 2.1. The crew discovered this error en route to ZZZ2 and attributed the incident to insufficient familiarity with the FOM.

synopsis: Falcon 2000 Captain reported momentary loss of control after encountering wake turbulence on approach to BFI airport.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence while descending on the CHINS4 arrival to BFI between HUMPP and AUBRN at 14,500 ft, causing a temporary loss of control with a bank angle exceeding 30 degrees. The upset occurred behind a Boeing 737-900 despite adequate spacing, but the crew recovered flight and completed a normal approach without aircraft faults.

synopsis: PC-12 First Officer reported an NMAC event during take-off with a landing aircraft that overflew them. Both aircraft executed a successful evasive maneuver.
summary: The crew, cleared for takeoff to 2,000 feet, observed Aircraft Y overhead and received a TCAS 'Traffic' alert. The pilot stopped climbing and turned left while Aircraft Y turned right, resolving the conflict.

synopsis: UAS flight crew operating at an uncontrolled airport had a near miss with a helicopter.
summary: During a military training takeoff of a large unmanned aircraft at ZZZ, a Visual Observer directed an immediate level-off to avoid a helicopter. The helicopter crossed the departure end at approximately 300 feet, narrowly missing the unmanned aircraft by about 100 feet on the upwind leg.

synopsis: Pilot reported they lost the engine on take off and landed on the same runway as used for take off.
summary: The pilot reported losing an engine during takeoff and landing back on the same runway. The aircraft exited and cleared the runway using intersection #1 during the landing roll.

synopsis: Tower Controllers reported a landing aircraft on short final was sent around when the ASDE-X alarm alerted the Local Controller to conflicting traffic landing on an intersecting runway. The Local Controller working both Local positions combined due to a lack of staffing was distracted by a previous arrival stopping on the runway causing the Controller to have to send a subsequent arrival around.
summary: A Local Controller, working alone due to staffing shortages, issued a late go-around to Aircraft Y after ASDE-X alarmed on a conflict with Aircraft Z. The incident was caused by the controller's distraction while managing Aircraft X's delayed exit and a runway inspection vehicle.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Center Controller reported a fractional jet deviated from their assigned heading and flew below the Minimum IFR Altitude after the Controller rescinded a Visual Approach clearance due to confusion of the crew's intentions.
summary: An ATC controller cleared a Citation for a visual approach at ZZZ, but the pilot turned 160 degrees away from the airfield while maintaining 9,000 feet. The controller attributed the near-miss with terrain to slow radar updates and the pilot's failure to keep the field in sight.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a skydiving operation aircraft was operating along the departure path of two air carrier departures. The first air carrier was issued a traffic alert and the second departure turned off course below the Minimum IFR Altitude to avoid jumpers.
summary: A radar controller issued traffic alerts when an IFR air carrier departed into a skydiving zone near ZZZ, causing the carrier to turn at 6,000 feet to avoid jumpers at 12,500 feet. The controller attributed the conflict to the skydive location overlapping active IFR routes and recommended relocating the jump zone.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a dip/bump in the runway at MMUN airport.
summary: A pilot reported a worsening runway dip at MMUN Runway 12R during rotation on two separate takeoffs, caused by settling asphalt where old and new pavement surfaces meet. The jarring impact strained the aircraft's tires and landing gear, with the condition deteriorating between the first and second occurrences.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an advisory from ATC to stop taxi and then observed a tractor pulling three cargo dollies cross the taxi way between aircraft on the vehicle service road, causing them to stop abruptly.
summary: Flight XXXX taxiing to Gate XX nearly collided with a cargo tractor and three dollies that failed to yield and entered the non-movement area. The controller ordered the aircraft to stop, and the cargo runner diverted its path to avoid contact with the nose gear.

synopsis: Global 5000 Captain reported an over reliance on automation caused them to go below altitude on approach, requiring a climb and subsequently continuing the approach.
summary: During a VFR final approach to Runway XXL, the crew executed an S-turn in autopilot to create spacing, resulting in a low altitude alert at 860 ft AGL due to excessive descent. The Pilot Flying manually recovered the aircraft to 1,100 ft, and the reporter attributed the event to over-reliance on automation rather than hand-flying the maneuver.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported that during arrival with an inoperative APU, the fueler hooked up and began his upload prior to the engine being shut down or gate power applied, causing the Captain to secure the engine and order the fueler to discontinue fueling. He further stated that COVID had impacted the currency of training and compliance with procedures.
summary: The flight crew experienced two hot refueling incidents at ZZZ while one engine was running due to an inoperative APU, resulting in approximately 1,100 lbs of unintended fuel. The reporter attributed the errors to ramp personnel rushing and a lack of clear communication regarding the prohibition of refueling with engines running.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported the loss of the green hydraulic system resulted in a precautionary landing and a tow to the gate.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a green hydraulic system low pressure failure during descent on the ZZZZZ1 Arrival. The crew held to complete checklists, landed with degraded brakes and steering, and was subsequently towed to the gate.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilots reported two similar sounding waypoints on this SID which caused a heading deviation and TCAS traffic warning.
summary: During the ORKA5 departure, the flight crew and controller misheard the clearance for fix ARCUS as ORCKA due to similar phonetics, causing the aircraft to fly off course. Although no conflict occurred, the crew passed another aircraft at FL200 while the controller directed a stop climb at FL190.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GA instructor reported smoke in the cockpit after takeoff and elected to do an Air Turn Back and a precautionary landing.
summary: Pilots observed smoke in the cockpit at 2,800 MSL during departure from Runway XXL, prompting an immediate return and engine shutdown on the ramp. The cause remains unknown, as preflight inspections were satisfactory and no smoke or flames were seen after the brief event.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GA instructor pilot reported alternator failure and elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot and student experienced an intermittent then continuous ALTR FAIL warning during an ILS approach to ZZZ, prompting a go-around and load shedding. The pilot suspects an alternator voltage between 30.5 and 32 volts triggered the warning, though the alternator remained functional and the flight completed safely.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GA nstructor reported loss of control during landing and takeoff and discovered that this issue was not addressed by maintenance before flight.
summary: The pilot reported that an aircraft with a recent directional control discrepancy was redispatched without maintenance, leading to suspected tire issues during training landings at ZZZ. Although the tire was later found intact, the pilot attributed the near-miss to a software failure that allowed the unfit aircraft to be assigned to a student pilot.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GA flight instructor on training flight reported NMAC with another aircraft landing on nearby runway at GFK airport.
summary: During a student touch-and-go on Runway 27L, the instructor and student nearly collided with an air carrier on short final for Runway 35L at 200–300 feet AGL. The incident occurred because Tower failed to provide traffic location or runway information, forcing the pilot to execute a 45-degree bank to avoid the jet.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported runway incursion and ground conflict with landing aircraft at TVL non-towered airport.
summary: Two pilots on a VFR departure from Runway 36 held short at intersection Bravo while two other aircraft landed on the same runway. The departing crew stopped past the hold short line after the landing pilots acknowledged their position but made no maneuvers to increase spacing, allowing the departure to proceed after the landings.

synopsis: Visual Observer witnessed a near miss between a UAS and a helicopter.
summary: Aircraft X, conducting flight tests in a right traffic pattern, nearly collided with Helicopter Y while descending near the runway departure end. The reporter attributes the 20-50 foot separation to Helicopter Y failing to read local UAV NOTAMs and flying too low without seeing Aircraft X.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported NMAC with another aircraft not on ADS-B while in climb.
summary: During a Part 91 repositioning flight leveling at 3,000 feet near Charlotte, the Pilot Flying visually detected a high-wing aircraft 25 feet below that was not displayed on ADS-B or by Approach. The crew overtook the unseen aircraft without taking evasive action as they had already passed it.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an IFR pop up aircraft was given an IFR altitude resulting in an airborne conflict with an IFR departure.
summary: A trainee controller in Sector X issued an incorrect IFR clearance to Aircraft X, causing a climb into another sector and a subsequent RA with Aircraft Y. The supervisor corrected the clearance, but Aircraft X filed a near midair collision report due to the trainee's error and lack of coordination.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: HLN Tower Controller reported a NMAC between two opposite direction aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X IFR at FL120 reported a near-miss with VFR Aircraft Y, which climbed to pass 400 feet above in a non-radar sector. The conflict occurred because the non-radar controller lacked surveillance data to issue traffic advisories since Aircraft Y had not self-identified.

synopsis: LAX Ground Controller reported ongoing issues relating to poor signage at the airport.
summary: An ATC trainee and two pilots were involved when Aircraft X and Y deviated from taxi clearances at LAWA. The reporter attributes the errors to conflicting instructions from City Ramp personnel and pilot expectation bias regarding the new Northroute, resulting in unsafe proximity events.

synopsis: LAX Tower Local Controller and the Local Assist Controller reported an aircraft which had been instructed to hold short of the runway taxied on to the runway at the same time a departure was beginning their takeoff roll.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Aircraft Y failed to respond to hold short instructions at Runway 25R. Aircraft Y entered the runway, forcing the controller to cancel Aircraft X's clearance just before an ASDE-X alarm triggered, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported the electric trim for the stabilizer ceased functioning, causing a diversion and overweight landing.
summary: The crew experienced a 'Stab Out of Trim' light at cruise, requiring manual trim and a diversion to ZZZ. They elected to perform an overweight landing rather than hold for fuel burn, resulting in an uneventful approach, landing, and brake cooling.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported transporting Hazmat cargo with incomplete required documents.
summary: The pilot failed to add HAZMAT remarks to the dispatch release for oxygen cylinders and batteries during flight preparation at ZZZ. This omission occurred because the pilot was distracted by servicing requests, weather planning, and rushing, causing them to forget the required action.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported the aircraft was removed from service after a passenger provided photographs of a wing slat delamination issue.
summary: A passenger reported possible damage to the left forward wing, prompting the flight crew to inspect the area after deplaning. Maintenance confirmed delamination and honeycomb tearing on the outboard left wing slat, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported NMAC with another aircraft during climbout from ONT airport.
summary: During departure from Ontario, CA on the RAJEE3 SID, the crew received a TCAS RA while maintaining 7,000 feet due to a small aircraft passing 300 feet below. The pilot attributed the conflict to ATC failing to vector the aircraft off the SID to avoid the converging traffic.

synopsis: Flight crew reported descending below minimum altitude on approach and initiated a climb back up to correct altitude and continued the approach.
summary: During a non-standard vector to Runway XXL, the Pilot Flying descended below 2,600 feet to 2,420 feet due to fatigue, distraction, and complex descent planning. The crew corrected the deviation manually while ATC issued a climb advisory, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a go-around due to an early descent and low speed condition on approach.
summary: The Pilot Flying missed a glide slope out-of-service NOTAM and incorrectly set a low altitude during a visual approach to Runway 15 at CHS, causing an unstable descent. The crew executed a go-around due to low speed and altitude, subsequently landing safely via an RNAV (GPS) approach.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported CIDS failed on takeoff, sounding simultaneous alarms causing an Air Turn Back and precautionary landing with assistance of two jump seaters.
summary: During takeoff of an A321, a continuous EVAC signal and EMER CALL buzzers sounded with no ECAM warnings, caused by a CIDS computer failure. The crew returned for an overweight landing after jumpseaters identified the fault and assisted with cabin communication while the cabin interphone remained inoperative.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a low-altitude warning during base leg of a visual approach to AFW airport.
summary: The flight crew received a low altitude alert from AFW Tower during a night visual approach to Runway 16L after turning base early for traffic and descending to 1,000 feet AGL inside the FAF. The crew intercepted the glide path from below and landed uneventfully, attributing the alert to being lower than normal due to the early turn.

synopsis: CE-560 Captain reported executing a go-around at touchdown on Runway 29 at EWR when jet blast from air carrier aircraft on Runway 22 had a destabilizing effect on their aircraft.
summary: During a landing approach to EWR Runway 29, the crew encountered severe jet blast from departing aircraft on Runway 22R, causing a go-around. The pilot noted that delayed left engine acceleration and the unexpected ground-level jet blast nearly resulted in an accident.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported NMAC during departure climb from SBA airport. Flight Crew took evasive action following TCAS RA guidance.
summary: During initial climb from SBA, the crew encountered a TCAS conflict with another aircraft at 8,000 feet that descended into their path despite ATC instructions. The pilot executed opposing TCAS RAs to avoid collision, attributing the incident to incorrect ATC heading assignments and the other aircraft's failure to follow clearances.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that a component was inadvertently switched off after the other pilot left the cockpit for a lavatory break and a multitude of warnings and ECAM messages went off as a result.
summary: During an initial Captain upgrade flight on a B777, the trainee Captain inadvertently switched off the IR1 mode selector while leaving the cockpit, deactivating the associated ADIRU. This caused multiple ECAM warnings and autopilot disengagement, requiring the check airman to hand-fly while the trainee completed procedures to restore systems.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported NMAC on departure climb.
summary: During departure at 8,000 feet on ATC vectors, the crew received TCAS RA commands to descend and climb to avoid a high-wing single-engine aircraft. The crew manually followed TCAS guidance, the other aircraft maneuvered away, and the incident was reported as a Near Mid Air Collision.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported making an abrupt stop during taxi into the gate at LGA due to a conflict with a vehicle.
summary: During the taxi to the gate at LGA, a maintenance pickup failed to yield, forcing the aircraft to stop abruptly to avoid a collision. The vehicle driver was cited by airport authority personnel, and Company Operations was notified.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported flying low and slow during transition from the STAR to the approach procedure due to missing the ATIS report of the glideslope out of service.
summary: The crew missed that the glideslope was out of service during a night visual approach, causing them to descend too low and trigger a low energy warning. The Captain initiated a go-around due to expectation bias and the new Captain's lack of aircraft experience, returning for an RNAV approach.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an overweight landing at destination airport caused by failure to monitor fuel burn during flight. Captain cited rusty pilot skills caused by COVID inactivity as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew operated a night ETOPS flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 and landed approximately 700 pounds overweight. The overweight landing message appeared only after engine shutdown, prompting the crew to send the appropriate code and notify local maintenance.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a ground conflict with a service truck during taxi out from gate.
summary: During taxi out, a water or service truck passed in front of the aircraft, forcing the crew to apply brakes. The reporter stated the truck driver was looking at his phone and failed to see the aircraft.

synopsis: B737 MAX flight crew reported an altitude deviation caused by the aircraft reverting to MCP SPD that has no altitude protection.
summary: During a descent into ZZZ in a MAX aircraft, the crew inadvertently entered Level Change mode, causing an unmonitored descent below the 11,000-foot restriction at ZZZZZ to 9,500 feet. The Captain manually recovered the altitude, and the First Officer notified ATC, though the cause of the mode change remained undetermined.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported GPS interference caused a course deviation.
summary: The flight crew experienced intermittent GPS and navigation failures at 35,000 feet in Cairo airspace, causing the aircraft to drift off airway Y415 without EICAS alerts. After manually steering and cycling systems, GPS function restored, allowing the crew to return to course with ATC assistance.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a pressurization problem during climbout. The appropriate QRH checklist was completed and the aircraft returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude increase during climb due to an open avionics compartment access door caused by a failed seal. They donned oxygen masks, descended to 9,000 feet, and landed safely after maintenance confirmed the door opened in flight.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported concerns over an A321 interior modification that now has seats blocking the L2 door and could cause egress problems during evacuation.
summary: A flight attendant reported to the Captain on an A321S that exit 2L was partially blocked by a row of seats, preventing a protective position. A maintenance technician confirmed the obstruction was improper and stated the adjacent row must be removed for safety.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp Personnel reported being notified of loading a Hazmat labeled parcel without required documentation.
summary: The reporter, acting alone, was advised they loaded an unidentified Hazmat parcel on Aircraft X without a NOTOC. Investigation confirmed no NOTOC was planned for that flight, prompting the reporter to file a report and suggest double-checking DG labels.

synopsis: Search and rescue helicopter had a near miss with a UAS.
summary: Helicopter crew conducting a search and rescue mission experienced a near midair collision with a small unmanned aerial vehicle. The crew queried other agencies regarding UAV use and increased altitude, with no further sightings reported for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: C172 pilot flying reported a Near Mid Air Collision while on approach to landing due to the other aircraft attempting to also shoot an approach at the same time on the same runway despite not making the required radio call and not being cleared to land.
summary: A Cessna 172N on short final for Runway XXL at 900 MSL experienced an NMAC with a Bombardier CL-600 due to the latter failing to report position or receive landing clearance. The CL-600 veered hard right to avoid a collision after appearing 50 feet behind the Cessna.

synopsis: Air carrier passenger reported noticing a wake turbulence encounter departing DCA airport.
summary: A passenger reported that during departure from DCA, the aircraft's right wing dipped 25 degrees due to wake turbulence as the gear retracted. The pilot's rapid correction prevented a mishap, though the passenger was unaware of the preceding aircraft, wind conditions, or ATC clearances.

synopsis: UAS had a lost link occur during flight. Pilot regained link with UAS and used manual control to recover the UAS.
summary: The RPIC flew a Skydio 2 under a bridge in manual mode when a lost link triggered a failed Return-to-Home, causing the drone to hover statically. The RPIC regained control by moving to the bridge's side, safely recovered the aircraft, and discontinued operations.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported flight release missing required HazMat amendment during cruise.
summary: The crew departed with two aircraft batteries loaded in proper containers but realized a required dispatch amendment was missing after becoming airborne. The Captain notified Dispatch to obtain the amendment, and the flight continued to the destination without further issues.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the in-flight loss of one hydraulic system. The pilot crew followed the QRH procedures and landed at their destination.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew managed a #2 engine-driven B hydraulic system failure that worsened during descent into ZZZ. After landing, Crash Fire Rescue detected hydraulic fluid leaking from the #2 engine and high brake temperatures, causing a ground delay to prevent fluid aerosolization.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew was on an initial ILS approach when they noticed a UAS. Flight crew notified ATC.
summary: The First Officer spotted a stationary drone at 3,000 ft MSL south of BUDDE while on final approach to Runway 08 at BUR. The crew immediately notified ATC and provided further details to the Ground Controller after landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported one of the assigned aircraft reported a NMAC and the pilot crew would submit the necessary reports.
summary: The flight crew experienced a TCAS resolution advisory at 8,000 feet after sighting general aviation traffic, requiring them to descend and then climb. The crew noted that passengers and flight attendants were unaware of the event and stated they were filing the necessary reports.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ramp Personnel reported a smart bag improperly configured for cargo compartment transport at destination airport.
summary: A passenger checked a bag containing a battery at ZZZ without removing it, citing lack of space at the plane side. Staff intercepted the bag and reminded the customer of the hazards.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported confusion during a Bump Thrust takeoff which resulted in the aircraft entering Alpha Floor, requiring the Captain to assume control and descend 300 additional feet to recover airspeed.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an A321 at ZZZ airport took off with a thrust bump to avoid passenger offload but failed to request SID altitude relief early. The Captain's premature flap retraction caused an airspeed drop below VLS and an alpha floor activation, requiring manual recovery to avoid terrain.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported an airspeed and altimeter cross-side mismatch and elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: Pilots experienced intermittent airspeed and altitude cross-side miss-comparisons and Flight Control Panel failures during climb after takeoff. Unable to resolve the issue or safely continue to ZZZ1 due to weather and RVSM constraints, they returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a fume event during cruise causing physiological symptoms. Captain submitted an aircraft maintenance report at destination.
summary: Flight Attendants 1 and 3 on Aircraft X experienced a five-minute fume event during flight, characterized by a severe acrid odor causing eye watering, throat irritation, and headaches. The Captain filed a mechanical report, and the affected crew members are requesting medical evaluation to determine fitness for duty.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported taking evasive action during an NMAC event.
summary: A helicopter pilot reported a near miss with Aircraft Y, which flew overhead from 5 to 10 o'clock at 3500 ft while not communicating on CTAF. The pilot contacted ZZZ1 and ZZZ2 but was advised to file an FAA report for resolution, noting the event caused significant concern.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action on the take-off roll when they encountered a motorcycle on the runway.
summary: The pilot of a 450hp taildragger at 1K1 airport encountered a motorcycle entering the runway during takeoff roll. The pilot maintained full power, veered right to avoid the vehicle, and continued the climb out along the runway's west edge.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported observing his student have a runway excursion during a touch and go, damaging the airplane and having to be told to shut down the engine.
summary: A student pilot with 2.8 solo hours veered off the left side of Runway XX into grass during a touch-and-go attempt after applying power. The student reported the aircraft veered left upon power application, resulting in left fairing impact damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of aircraft brakes on landing roll out caused the aircraft to over run the runway.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft at ZZZ and discovered a total brake failure halfway down the runway. The airplane overran the runway end and came to a stop.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot Examiner reported a runway incursion at OMN airport and cited worn hold short lines as a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot reported that faded hold short markings at the approach end of Runway 27 caused uncertainty about the line's location, potentially resulting in a wing crossing the boundary. The pilot turned the aircraft around without controller intervention and recommended cleaning or repainting the markings to prevent confusion.

aircraft: Small UAS (At or above 0.55 lbs and less than 55 lbs)
synopsis: UAS pilot flew in Class D airspace without authorization.
summary: A pilot flew a drone over a dwelling for roof inspection without checking airspace or obtaining authorization from AZO. Management discovered the airspace incursion during monthly flight reviews, prompting the pilot to commit to checking airspace before every future flight.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported experiencing a lost GPS signal in the same area on different days.
summary: A pilot flying 1,500 feet MSL southeastbound in the Los Angeles basin lost GPS signals on Garmin 650/750 units and an iPad for three minutes near the SLI VOR. The signals returned before the pilot could contact SNA tower, with no cause identified for the isolated incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Student pilot reported loss of control after landing resulting in the aircraft departing the runway. The Student stated that distractions, while on final approach, were a primary cause for the loss of control.
summary: A solo pilot on final approach to Runway XXR experienced violent nose wheel shaking and directional oscillations upon landing, causing the aircraft to veer off into a drainage ditch. The pilot attributed the incident to task overload from ATC communications and a lack of focus on the landing roll.

synopsis: Captain reported that non urgent communications from Company Operations caused distractions during taxi in, requiring hard braking to avoid a B737 being pushed back from an adjoining gate.
summary: During taxi-in at MDW, the flight crew avoided a collision with a pushing 737 after Ground Ops distracted them with a Crew Scheduling call. The pilot attributed the near-miss and subsequent distraction to a violation of sterile cockpit rules caused by non-safety related duties during a critical phase of flight.

synopsis: Air Carrier Personnel reported a Hazmat labeled parcel was 'found on a gate jetbridge'.
summary: A ground handler found a flammable, Hazmat-labeled ice release item on the jetbridge at Gate X. The report does not specify the aircraft, phase of flight, or the outcome of the discovery.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a Stabilizer Out of Trim problem during climb out. They completed the appropriate QRH checklist and performed an air turn back.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a stabilizer trim failure during climb at 17,000 feet, causing inoperative electric trim and requiring manual hand-cranking. They diverted to ZZZ for a safe, slightly overweight landing on Runway XXL after coordinating with ATC and ARFF.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported similar sounding waypoints FASOP and FASON contributed to an altitude and heading deviation while on the VANZE TWO arrival to MEM airport.
summary: The pilot flying a Vanze 2 Arrival into MEM entered a crossing restriction at FASON instead of FASOP in the FMS after a runway change, causing the aircraft to appear high. The error resulted from similar intersection names and was only corrected after ATC issued a direct routing, leaving the crew low and requiring a reduced descent rate.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported departure with incomplete Hazmat documentation on final flight release.
summary: The flight crew failed to verify time and dispatcher initials on an ACARS message regarding Dry Ice Supplementary Procedures during preflight and enroute phases. The reporter attributed the oversight of the amended release to their own inattention to detail.

synopsis: Flight crew reported experiencing a malfunction with one of the aircraft's power levers resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: During takeoff from Runway XXR at ZZZ, the left throttle was difficult to set, causing the left engine APR to fire and become non-responsive to throttle movement. The crew returned to ZZZ for a precautionary landing after resolving the issue by selecting the left engine fire push switch, attributing the event to a defective thrust lever.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported taking evasive action due to a Near Mid Air Collision.
summary: A commercial pilot and student practicing steep spirals in a ZZZ terminal area aircraft detected a C172 on a collision course via ADS-B. The pilot executed an emergency climb to avoid the conflict, while the C172 passed directly underneath without altering course.

synopsis: Captain reported left engine temperatures were fluctuating mostly in the red arc and elected to perform an In Flight Shut Down and continue to destination airport to perform a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot reported a loud bang, intense vibration, and elevated left engine TGT shortly after initiating descent from FL450. The pilot shut down the left engine, which stopped the symptoms, allowing for an uneventful landing at ZZZZ, though the specific cause remains unknown.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported that during taxi-out, the morning sun interfered with being able to see and they inadvertently taxied onto a runway at MYF airport.
summary: The pilot taxied at MYF and accidentally entered Runway 28L instead of following the clearance for Taxiway H to Runway 28R due to sun glare obscuring the narrow runway. The controller notified the pilot, who immediately exited the runway with no traffic impact.

synopsis: Pilot reported distractions lead to a collision on a taxiway with another aircraft during preparations for formation operations.
summary: The #2 pilot in a six-aircraft formation taxi collided with the lead aircraft's rudder after a momentary distraction from frequency congestion caused a delayed stop. The incident resulted in damage to both aircraft's propellers and control surfaces due to the unbriefed stop and closing speed.

synopsis: Flight Instructor and Student reported a Near Mid Air Collision and observed the other aircraft pitched up aggressively to avoid collision.
summary: A pilot and instructor in a right downwind for Runway XX at ZZZ experienced a near miss with a T-38 that executed a go-around for Runway XY. The T-38 leveled co-altitude and headed toward the aircraft before aggressively pitching up to pass 500 feet above and behind, despite conflicting ATC clearances.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action to avoid a mid-air air collision with an aircraft.
summary: A VFR pilot flying northbound at 5,500 feet MSL initially turned left into a Cessna 152 conflict after AWOS audio on Comm 2 blocked the first ATC "turn right" instruction. The pilot corrected to a right turn upon hearing the second warning and visually acquiring the aircraft at approximately 5,300 feet MSL.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a flight crew descended below the minimum IFR altitude after he missed the crews incorrect read back of the assigned altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to cross ZZZ at or above 14,000 ft, but the pilot read back 11,000 ft, which the controller missed. The aircraft subsequently descended below the Minimum IFR Altitude before reaching ZZZ, triggering a low altitude alert.

synopsis: Flight crew reported encountering severe updrafts and downdrafts resulting in deviations from their assigned altitude. The flight crew recovered from the upset condition and continued the flight without issue.
summary: While cruising at FL370 south of SAV, the crew encountered clear air turbulence with no radar echoes, causing a rapid climb to 37,300 ft and descent to 36,500 ft. The First Officer applied upset recovery controls to stabilize the aircraft, and the flight continued normally after reporting the event to Jacksonville Center.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a fume event of 'dirty socks odor' during descent to destination.
summary: A pilot reported a dirty sock odor while descending into ZZZ. The reporter suggested the cause was filtered bleed air.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported GPS jamming.
summary: The crew experienced GPS jamming that caused ADS-B OUT L and R alerts and a loss of GPS position. The incident was attributed to GPS jamming.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported GPS jamming while in Russian airspace.
summary: The pilot reported GPS jamming while flying at 36,000 feet from LOGMU to ROKUB in Russian airspace. The reporter attributed the loss of GPS signal to Russian jamming.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported encountering jet blast while landing as a result of ATC clearance to heavy aircraft while in close proximity to active runway.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing at ORD, a heavy aircraft turning onto Runway 28R generated jet blast that caused a sudden crosswind and stick-shaker activation just before touchdown. The pilot attributed the event to ATC instructing the heavy aircraft to turn while the reporting aircraft was on final approach.

synopsis: E175 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival into SEA in trail of a B737.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B737 while descending to 5,000 ft on the Hawks 7 Arrival into Seattle. The pilot attributed the event to tailwinds delaying vortex dissipation and close spacing, resulting in 15-20 degree roll rates without course deviation.

synopsis: SA-227 Captain reported experiencing an elevator trim malfunction during initial climb. The flight crew opted to continue the flight after troubleshooting the issue and landed uneventfully at their destination.
summary: During a training climb after departure from ZZZ1, the crew experienced a complete nose-down trim failure that reduced to a slow rate before stopping entirely. They executed the Trim Failure checklist, reverted to two-crew operations, and landed safely at ZZZ1, noting the issue had been previously reported but not resolved.

synopsis: 767-300 Inspector reported not ensuring completion of required paperwork to correctly identify Basic Operating Weight changes on two aircraft involved in a crew rest module swap.
summary: A Quality Control inspector incorrectly stamped maintenance paperwork for two aircraft after misreading an email confirming a Basic Operating Weight change for only one. Although the weight data was updated before departure, the error could have resulted in an improper weight and balance computation due to the inspector's oversight.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported that his number two aircraft broke off the wrong way and was directed by ATC to correct his heading to avoid a collision with another aircraft.
summary: The pilot leading two warbirds landing on Runway XX right reported that a trailing aircraft received a non-standard "break left" clearance, causing a brief deviation before correction. A Cessna 172 pilot later claimed a near miss, though the warbird pilot believes this is impossible given the Cessna's downwind position.

synopsis: Pilot reported encountering engine issues during initial climb and immediately returned to the airport where it was discovered the aircraft had been mistakenly fueled with Jet-A.
summary: The pilot reported that after departing ZZZ with 50 gallons of fuel, both engine CHTs spiked to red line during climb. The pilot executed a 180-degree turn to land, discovering the aircraft had been misfueled with Jet A.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported that his student pilot was soloing in the traffic pattern they became confused and failed to follow multiple instructions from ATC, resulting in a NMAC and causing a Learjet to perform a go around.
summary: A student pilot soloing in ZZZ Delta Airspace became disoriented after complex ATC instructions, misheard a clearance, and turned left base toward a Learjet on final for Runway XX. The Learjet executed a go-around to avoid a collision, while the student was vectored for a full stop landing.

synopsis: PA-24 Pilot reported being out of radio contact with ATC while on an IFR flight plan due to distractions.
summary: The pilot flew 200 feet below the 7,200-foot minimum vectoring altitude while transitioning from Victor airway to direct VOR due to a missed hand-off and communication failure. The pilot climbed to 8,000 feet after Center advised the deviation, noting visual contact with terrain in VMC conditions.

synopsis: Flight Instructor and Student Pilot reported that wind shear on landing during a solo flight caused the aircraft to become airborne and then veer to the side upon landing again, striking a light before the aircraft came to a stop.
summary: A student pilot soloing at ZZZ experienced a wind shear event during landing that caused the aircraft to bounce and drift left. The pilot veered off the runway to avoid a parked Cessna 172, striking a taxi light and denting the wing, resulting in minor damage with no injuries.

synopsis: Captain noticed that pitot/static covers were not installed per policy documents and requested maintenance perform a visual inspection of the pitot tubes and static ports for wasps.
summary: The flight crew discovered pitot covers were missing overnight at ZZZ due to a shortage, causing a 29-minute delay for maintenance inspection. The reporter noted that without this inquiry, undetected wasp nests could have caused unreliable airspeed alerts during takeoff, potentially requiring a rejected takeoff or overweight landing.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported an APU fire warning after takeoff and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced an APU fire warning at 3,000 feet during climb-out and returned for an overweight landing. Maintenance later determined the cause was a faulty APU fire control panel, as no actual fire or heat was found.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a fume/smoke event in cockpit during departure taxi when windshield heat was activated.
summary: During taxi to runway XX, the crew detected smoke and odor in the cockpit after activating the cabin heat for defrost. The aircraft returned to the gate, passengers deplaned, and the incident was attributed to a malfunctioning heater.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported performance deficiencies on A321 aircraft when operating in high gross weight configurations and high ambient temperatures.
summary: The A321 crew and ATC faced departure issues due to high weight, heat, and a missing SID, resulting in poor climb performance and incorrect routing. The pilot attributed the event to unsafe operating conditions, uncooperative controllers, manual errors, and distractions, noting that CRM prevented a worse outcome.

synopsis: Pilot reported an air turn back caused by high engine oil temperature.
summary: A solo pilot flying to ZZZ1 experienced low oil pressure and high oil temperature while climbing to 4,000 ft. The pilot returned to ZZZ, landed safely on Runway XXR after requesting immediate landing due to suspected engine failure, triggering a Level 1 alert.

synopsis: Flight Crew while landing is hit by jet blast from departing heavy aircraft .
summary: Pilots landing on Runway 29 at EWR encountered jet blast from a departing heavy aircraft on intersecting Runway 22R during the flare at 10-20 feet. The aircraft weather vaned right of centerline with moderate turbulence, but the crew maintained control and landed safely.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew had a near miss with UAS while on vectors to an approach. Flight crew reported to ATC.
summary: During a visual approach to PDX runway 28R at 4,300 feet, a First Officer spotted a drone passing 50 to 100 feet off the left wing at the same altitude. No avoidance maneuvers were made due to the brief encounter, and the flight continued without incident after reporting to Portland Approach.

synopsis: Flight Instructor on a training flight with a student reported a runway excursion during takeoff roll.
summary: During a student pilot's initial solo training takeoff, improper control inputs caused the aircraft to veer off the runway into grass despite the instructor's immediate corrective actions. The instructor safely taxied the aircraft back onto the runway with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: Flight Instructor on training flight with student reported NMAC on approach.
summary: An instructor and student practicing an ILS approach to Runway 03 at OGD broke off when a departing aircraft turned in front of them instead of passing behind as cleared. The instructor took control to avoid a closer occurrence after the departing pilot failed to maintain the requested separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported misconfiguring his radio which resulted in unheard traffic calls and a ground conflict with a departing aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway incursion risk at Lakefield Airport while taxiing for Runway 26 due to an inaudible Com 1 radio caused by a volume reset after an avionics bus configuration change. The pilot held short of the runway as another aircraft departed Runway 08, attributing the near miss to the radio error and the airport's tight taxiway design.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported receiving a minimum safe altitude warning from ATC during a visual approach for landing.
summary: During a visual approach to runway 19 at MKC, the pilot received a Minimum Safe Altitude Warning (MSAW) from Tower while on a wide right base. The pilot leveled and climbed; the warning was likely caused by a high descent rate, as the aircraft's TAWS did not trigger and the landing was completed without incident.

aircraft: Small UAS (At or above 0.55 lbs and less than 55 lbs)
synopsis: UAS pilot was flying at night and had an airborne conflict with a helicopter.
summary: A recreational drone operator flying a UAS at night in Class E airspace near Whiteman Airport encountered a helicopter that hovered nearby and threatened the operator after landing. The reporter states the helicopter pilot acted recklessly and unprofessionally, forcing the drone into a hover over property and issuing verbal threats to confiscate the aircraft.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported a departing Cessna deviated from the departure procedure and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a Cessna departing SMO that turned right toward a VOR at 1,200 feet based on a pilot's claim of a tower clearance. Investigation confirmed no such clearance was issued, the pilot was instructed to climb above Minimum Vectoring Altitude, and the controller recommended revisiting departure procedures due to frequent errors by inexperienced pilots.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Jacksonville Center Traffic Management Coordinator reported asking the Command Center for help and was denied. This resulted in the East Area getting overwhelmed and sectors becoming so inundated with aircraft that they were almost out of control.
summary: A Traffic Management Coordinator reported that ATCSCC denied requests for an Airspace Flow Program despite severe weather closing East Coast routings and activating military airspace. This refusal led to overwhelmed sectors, excessive controller workload, and aircraft being forced through severe turbulence, resulting in facility Corrective Action Plans.

synopsis: A SAT TRACON Controller reported two instances of jet aircraft on final approach to SAT conflicting with gliders maneuvering into and out of a non-towered airport (5C1) located underneath the final approach course.
summary: An air traffic controller in the final sector issued traffic to a LJ60 arrival at 4,000 feet to avoid a glider squawking 1202 near 5C1, which merged with the jet's track. The controller reported the glider's intermittent transponder and unpredictable maneuvers created a safety risk, recommending airspace changes to protect SAT finals.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZDV Center Controller reported the Monitor Alert Parameter numbers for two sectors became over-saturated and unsafe.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sectors 9 and 16 reported unsafe oversaturation during Denver east arrivals due to high volume, weather deviations, and conflicting arrival route changes. The lack of early rerouting plans caused hand-off refusals, sequence breakdowns, and increased workload for adjacent sectors.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Aspen Tower Controller reported problems associated with aircraft in relationship to the high terrain and high MVA's surrounding the airport.
summary: A VFR Aircraft X flew through the departure and final approach areas at 13,000 feet without ATC communication, forcing Aircraft Y to be vectored off approach and Aircraft Z to remain high. The reporter attributes the conflict to uncontrolled VFR traffic in Aspen's mountainous terrain and recommends controlled airspace requiring two-way communication.

synopsis: Aspen Tower Controller reported a problem with a helicopter and traffic departing Aspen.
summary: A VFR helicopter flew through Aspen's arrival and departure areas at 11,500 feet without contacting ATC, creating a conflict with Aircraft Y on the LINDZ9 departure. The controller expedited a climb to avoid the conflict, delaying Aircraft Z, while the reporter cited the lack of mandatory two-way radio communication as the cause.

synopsis: FLL Tower Controller reported a runway incursion caused by a vehicle entering the runway while an air carrier was flaring to land.
summary: During landing on Runway 10L, the pilot observed an unauthorized vehicle on the runway and executed a go-around just feet above the surface. The incident was caused by a driver on their first day operating near an active taxiway, highlighting a need for better vehicle operator training.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a pack valve failure caused the cabin to not pressurize and resulted in descent and precautionary landing.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a recurring PACK 1 valve closure and rising cabin altitude during climb, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. They returned to ZZZ for a safe landing after following QRH procedures for the pressurization failure.

synopsis: An air carrier pilot conducting an approach at night to SKBO reported they were cleared for a 'RNP Visual Flight Proc.' approach but charts and the Flight Manual were not clear if they were authorized to fly this procedure.
summary: The flight crew encountered confusion over night visual approach rules and a last-minute runway closure at Bogota while descending in mountainous terrain. Tower closed Runway 31L after the Final Approach Fix, forcing a manual transition to Runway 31R, which the crew stabilized and landed successfully.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a GPWS alert while flying a visual approach into the RNO airport.
summary: Pilots flying into Reno received a visual approach clearance to 16L after their RNAV RNP request was denied. The aircraft triggered a ground proximity warning due to rolling terrain during the descent, prompting a climb before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a fume event upon arrival at the aircraft. Aircraft logbook had an open discrepancy by previous flight crew who had rejected the aircraft due to a fume event.
summary: The Captain and First Officer refused an aircraft due to a persistent musty odor in the cabin and flight deck, noting a prior safety refusal in the logbook. Maintenance proposed disinfecting rather than removing the aircraft from service to locate the source, but the crew departed without flying.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reported a near upset shortly after takeoff from DFW when his aircraft was affected by jet blast from a taxiing wide body aircraft.
summary: Aircraft X experienced an upset during takeoff on Runway 17R due to jet blast from a wide-body aircraft taxiing ahead. The crew recovered the aircraft, but the incident highlighted the need for Ground Control to manage taxiing aircraft to protect departing flights.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
