synopsis: Pilot reported a near mid air collision and maintained separation to avoid additional conflict.
summary: During a military close air support orbit at 9,000 ft MSL, the pilot observed a C-172 passing directly above and executed a hard left bank and rapid descent to avoid collision. ADS-B showed the C-172 was 300 ft above, but the other pilot never reacted or appeared to see the military aircraft.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C25B pilot reported encountering wake turbulence climbing out of SJC in trail of a B737.
summary: The pilot experienced an uncommanded 400-foot descent at 5,000 feet while following a 737 on the TECKY3 SID. The reporter attributes the event to wake turbulence despite wake separation, requiring autopilot disconnection to resume the climb.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported they had issued instructions to a VFR aircraft in the pattern which resulted in flight below the minimum safe altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller maneuvering a VFR aircraft for arrival briefly placed it below the Minimum Safe Altitude and then clipped a higher MSA in bravo airspace. The controller attributed the error to being distracted by changing departure plans and failing to recognize the altitude restriction.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported they vectored an aircraft below the Minimum IFR Altitude while trying to assist them in avoiding weather.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X into a 14,700-foot Minimum IFR Altitude while the pilot was at 14,100 feet during a weather-affected departure from ZZZ. The controller issued a low altitude alert after realizing the error, and the pilot confirmed climbing through the required altitude.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after inflight shutdown following loss of left engine oil quantity.
summary: The flight crew diverted an aircraft at FL370 due to left engine oil loss caused by sheared Air Turbine Starter bolts. After burning fuel to reach Maximum Landing Gear Weight, they secured the engine and landed safely with fire trucks standing by.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported the left generator failed during cruise which resulted in an air turn back.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the left generator failed twice despite a QRH reset. With the APU deferred, the crew diverted to the nearest airport, ZZZ, and executed a normal landing operating on a single generator.

synopsis: B737 NG FO reported his aircraft was 'significantly upset' just before touchdown at EWR by jet blast from a taxiing B777.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 29 at EWR, the crew experienced a significant upset caused by jet blast from a B777 taking off from Runway 22R. The aircraft yawed and ballooned, but the pilots recovered control and executed a safe landing without damage.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported DTW taxiway paint is well worn, which resulted in a taxiway incursion.
summary: The flight crew at DTW inadvertently taxied onto a deicing pad instead of holding short of taxiway K due to faded pavement markings at the E2-F intersection. The Captain realized the error after turning south on line 1, notified Ground Control, and received further instructions.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew and Dispatcher reported being notified of unmanifested Hazmat cargo after departure.
summary: Ramp personnel failed to document 79.6 kg of dry ice in position 1, providing incorrect paperwork stating "NO DG ON BOARD" before departure. Dispatch notified the flight crew via ACARS 30 minutes after takeoff that the hazardous material was on board due to this ramp error.

aircraft: Fairchild Swearingen Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reported an airborne fume event in which he experienced persistent physiological symptoms.
summary: The captain of a Metro Liner experienced symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning during cruise at FL80, likely caused by a bleed leak heating the left gasper valve. After turning off the left bleed and descending to 10,000 feet, the flight landed safely, though the captain required medical evaluation for suspected poisoning.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported flight control computer issues during approach resulted in loss of all autoflight capability. Pilot also reported the aircraft had been previously refused due to flight control computer malfunctions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a dual FMS failure and flight control issues during descent to ZZZZ, forcing a manual approach with ATC vectors. Despite initial confusion between a taxiway and runway, the crew landed safely after deciding to bypass extended checklists due to the aircraft's recent flight control computer history.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported encountering severe wake turbulence on arrival into CLT in trail of an A320.
summary: A crew flying into Charlotte at 6,000 feet encountered severe wake turbulence from an A320 five miles ahead. The pilots executed an escape maneuver, climbed to 9,000 feet, and confirmed no injuries before logging the event for maintenance.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported cross winds on landing and failed to take proper action, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot bounced during the landing flare at ZZZ due to a gust and excessive slowness, causing the aircraft to swerve right into the grass. The pilot regained control, stopped, and returned to the runway with no damage, attributing the incident to incorrect speed perception.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported loss of avionics power and was forced to use a cell phone to text a friend at destination airport. The friend relayed pilot's intentions to ATC and was able to land at destination.
summary: During cruise at 8,000 feet in IMC, the pilot's avionics master switch failed, disabling all navigation and communication systems. The pilot hand-flew the aircraft using an iPhone for navigation and texted for priority handling, successfully landing after receiving a green light from the tower.

synopsis: Pilot reported a near mid air collision while in the traffic pattern with other aircraft which passed underneath by 75 feet.
summary: The pilot entering the 45-degree left downwind at ZZZ pulled up when Aircraft Y passed 75 feet below. Despite the pilot broadcasting intentions, Aircraft Y provided no radio response.

synopsis: Citation V First Officer reported that during a Fire Warning event in flight, the Captain declined to follow checklists and established procedures and elected to continue the flight to destination.
summary: During departure, a pilot flying reported a right engine fire light and high oil temperature caused by improper engine installation after a recent change. The PIC incorrectly decided to continue the flight instead of landing as required, while the pilot flying failed to insist on an immediate landing despite the emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Center Controller and pilot reported that while attempting to land at a non towered airport at night the runway lights would not activate so the pilot diverted to a nearby airport. The pilot executed a missed approach to divert but did not comply with ATC instructions and flew below the Minimum IFR Altitudes.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X requested priority handling due to fuel concerns while attempting a night approach to ZZZ with inoperative lights. Despite ATC warnings about terrain and Minimum IFR Altitudes, the pilot descended below safe levels before diverting to ZZZ2, where activated lights allowed a safe landing.

synopsis: TRACON controllers reported communication problems resulting in incorrect altitudes assigned to a UAS.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a UAS clearance for ATCAAs X and Y at or above FL400, but the crew had originally requested FL430. The 3,000-foot discrepancy occurred because the controller assumed the altitude matched the initial coordination without verifying it with the Controller in Charge.

synopsis: B767 Flight Crew reported pressurization problem inflight.
summary: Pilots on Aircraft X experienced a cabin altitude warning at Flight Level 340 while descending with a deferred right pack, likely due to departure from a high-altitude airport. They donned oxygen masks, descended to Flight Level 280, and landed normally after maintenance repaired the pack in ZZZ.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into LAX in trail of a B767.
summary: During an IRNMN arrival into LAX, the flight crew encountered moderate wake turbulence from a preceding B767 at 10,000 feet, causing a 25-degree left bank and autopilot disengagement. The pilot manually stabilized the aircraft, requested a turn away from the B767, and was vectored north to complete the approach with no injuries reported.

synopsis: Captain reported a crossing restriction was not met due to an occasional software glitch which reportedly causes the descent to shallow out temporarily.
summary: The crew inbound to ZZZ on the ZZZZZ arrival at FL330 experienced a VNAV glitch during the FMC transition from Cruise to Descent page, causing pitch stagnation and airspeed bleed. This resulted in crossing the FL320 restriction 240 feet high due to insufficient distance to correct the path deviation.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 First Officer reported finding unusual wear on a main tire which maintenance deferred for a later replacement. First Officer was informed that it was a known problem.
summary: The pilot reported unusual wear on the #3 main tire during preflight, but maintenance deferred replacement citing a known MAX design issue. The pilot contends the tire was unserviceable per AOM guidance due to unclear ply definitions, yet the aircraft departed with the defect.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff and returning to the gate when the aircraft initiated a hard left turn early in the takeoff roll.
summary: During initial takeoff roll below 30 kts, the aircraft executed an uncommanded hard left turn due to suspected nose wheel steering malfunction. The crew rejected the takeoff, but binding tiller limited steering to 10 degrees, resulting in a full stop blocking the taxiway and requiring a tow back.

synopsis: PC-12 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing an engine fire warning.
summary: The crew encountered an Engine Fire CAS and autopilot failure during descent in IMC, prompting a diversion to a nearby alternate for expedited handling. They hand-flew an ILS approach, landed safely, and evacuated the aircraft, though post-landing inspection revealed no visible fire or smoke.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew had an airborne conflict with a UAS while on final approach.
summary: The flight crew observed a large yellow drone pass the left side of the aircraft during the visual approach to runway 12L at MSP at 2,800 feet. The drone was operating in unauthorized airspace, but a post-flight inspection confirmed no impact occurred.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported GPWS warning on approach and flight crew complied with advisory.
summary: The Captain and First Officer received an obstacle caution at 2,700 ft during a visual approach to Runway 33 at SYR. The alert occurred because the Captain misread the approach plate, prompting a climbing right turn to regain the 3,700 ft MSA.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported a loss of aircraft control in severe turbulence.
summary: Pilots vectored by ATC into unseen weather lost 1,200 feet due to severe downdraft and wind shear, causing autopilot disengagement and a 4,000 fpm descent to 1,800 feet MSL. The crew regained control after slowing to maneuvering speed and receiving deviation instructions once contact was re-established.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported TCAS RA on descent. Flight crew took evasive action.
summary: During descent near Sweet intersection, ATC notified the crew of an opposing climbing aircraft and issued a left turn to 070 degrees. A TCAS RA followed immediately, requiring compliance as the other aircraft passed within 500 feet.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported TCAS RA in cruise flight and flight crew took evasive action.
summary: Pilots flying a jet at FL370 near Atlanta received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb after ATC cleared them to FL380 too late, causing a near-miss with an opposing aircraft. The controller admitted a lapse of attention regarding two nose-to-nose aircraft at the same altitude, but TCAS prevented a collision.

synopsis: Pilot reported evasive action to avoid another aircraft identified by the aircraft TCAS system.
summary: The pilot reported a near miss during a visual approach at 3,000 feet when Aircraft Y climbed to within 100 feet vertically, triggering conflicting TCAS RAs. The reporter attributed the event to Aircraft Y's questionable judgment while transitioning near Class B airspace, noting no rules were technically broken.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported taking evasive action to avoid an aircraft that was obscured by weather.
summary: A pilot flying east in wildfire smoke executed a right turn to avoid parallel traffic but encountered a converging white Mooney obscured by haze. Despite ATC reporting the traffic 500 feet above, the pilot performed a rapid descent to avoid conflict after delayed advisories from a busy controller.

synopsis: Small Turboprop pilot reported encountering wake turbulence departing PHX in trail of an A320 NEO.
summary: The pilot of a departing aircraft took off behind an Airbus A320 NEO and was vectored left into its wake turbulence by the controller. This caused passenger injuries, cabin door damage, and baggage displacement, leading the pilot to conclude that more separation was needed.

synopsis: Flight crew reported a hydraulic pump failure in flight and requested priority handling to make a precautionary landing at destination airport.
summary: The crew experienced hydraulic system 1 failures and unreliable landing gear indications during approach to ZZZ1, requiring a missed approach and gravity gear deployment. They declared an emergency, returned to ZZZ, and landed safely with loss of nose wheel steering.

synopsis: Pilot reported transmitting on the wrong frequency contributed to a near mid air collision.
summary: A pilot entering the traffic pattern at ZZZ airport landed on runway XX without hearing other traffic because they were transmitting on 123.7 MHz instead of the correct CTAF frequency 123.0 MHz. Consequently, the pilot failed to detect Aircraft Y, which overflew the runway shortly after the landing.

synopsis: Pilot reported a near mid air collision with an aircraft using the opposing runway without communicating their intentions correctly.
summary: A pilot conducting touch-and-goes on Runway XX observed a Cessna 182 depart the active runway while announcing Runway YY. The Cessna subsequently crossed the pilot's downwind leg at 100 feet above and 200 feet horizontally due to the other pilot's confusion regarding the active runway.

synopsis: Captain reported cargo door departed the aircraft in flight and continued to destination airport.
summary: During initial climb from ZZZZ to ZZZ1 at 700 feet AGL, a cargo door opened and detached after the co-pilot failed to secure it due to a missing interior handle. The door fell into the ocean, but the aircraft maintained normal flight characteristics and completed a visual approach to ZZZZ1 without further issues.

synopsis: Pilot of a single engine aircraft reported losing engine power on departure, returned to the airport, and landed safely. The reporter stated after landing they discovered the fuel gauge was inoperative.
summary: A pilot flying a PA32 experienced sudden engine power loss at 500 feet due to an empty right main tank despite the gauge indicating 11 gallons. Power was restored after switching to the right tip tank, allowing a safe landing on Runway XYR.

synopsis: An instructor pilot departing a non-towered airport reported a NMAC with opposite direction landing traffic which had not been communicating on the CTAF.
summary: Pilots departing Runway XX at ZZZ encountered a descending aircraft on an iPad alert and executed a right turn to avoid a head-on collision. The maneuver inadvertently took them 100 feet into Class Bravo airspace, requiring an immediate descent to exit, while the other aircraft made no radio calls.

synopsis: A pilot on a visual approach to a non-towered airport reported a NMAC with a glider. The reporter did not close out their IFR flight plan in a timely manner causing a delay for another aircraft awaiting departure approval.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach for Runway XY encountered a glider on an intersecting Runway XX at the same altitude, passing 100 feet laterally. The near midair occurred because the glider lacked a transponder and was not seen on ADS-B or TCAS, while the pilot's delayed IFR closure caused a departure delay.

synopsis: Pilot reported landing at a non-towered airport and having a ground conflict with an aircraft landing on an intersecting runway. Reporter indicated this event contributed to his inattention to airspace boundaries and an airspace violation later in the day.
summary: The pilot inadvertently entered ZZZ Class D airspace during descent due to distraction from smokey conditions and a prior near-collision at ZZZ2. While avoiding a landing C180 on a cross runway, the pilot scraped a wingtip on a runway light, which contributed to the subsequent airspace incursion.

synopsis: UAS pilot learned they were flying near a bird sanctuary and landed as a precaution.
summary: A drone operator conducting test flights over Lake Chickamauga in Soddy, TN, discovered the area was a bird sanctuary via Google Maps. The operator immediately shut down the drone and switched to handheld recording to avoid potential airspace violations.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An IFR single engine light aircraft pilot experienced engine surging and diverted to a nearby airport and landed safely. The pilot lost contact with Approach descended on their own and switched to the tower frequency.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR flight experienced worsening engine surging and diverted to ZZZ2 but failed to declare an emergency or squawk 7700 initially. After losing contact with Approach, the pilot descended without clearance and switched to Tower, landing safely with emergency services present.

synopsis: Pilot reported a ground conflict on takeoff with an aircraft that crossed the runway in front of the pilot's aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft experienced radio static and heat haze while taking off from runway XX at ZZZ, obscuring a crossing aircraft. The pilot continued the takeoff to minimize runway usage, lifting off 3,000 feet from the traffic, attributing the near miss to environmental conditions preventing communication.

synopsis: Lead Technician reported a spar bumper fell out of the main wheel well while the aircraft was in the hangar.
summary: A spar bumper in the left main wheel well of Aircraft X fell off while in the hangar due to incorrect factory installation. Textron classified this as a grounding discrepancy because the landing gear could strike the main spar during a gear-up landing.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controller reported issues with weather were further complicated by the TMU's reluctance to help with reroutes or flow.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 38 managed westbound traffic deviating north into Area 5 due to weather, causing Sector 30 overload and requiring holds and descents. The controller attributed the unsafe and inefficient situation to delayed routing plans, lack of TMU support, and insufficient daily training for high-traffic scenarios.

synopsis: JAN Tower Controller reported the fire alarm goes off periodically for no reason. This is a known reoccurring issue. Reporter stated not knowing if it is a real fire or a false alarm every time it goes off is an issue which causes distraction.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a recurring false fire alarm near radar scopes during a busy period with multiple inbound and outbound aircraft. The controller executed a contingency plan after contacting management, citing the alarm as a dangerous distraction that prevents safe monitoring of ten airplanes.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a fumes event during cruise resulting in health issues for some flight attendants and an eventual diversion.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew diverted to ZZZ1 after two flight attendants reported a strong cleaning spray odor and respiratory symptoms in the aft galley. Dispatch confirmed the aircraft had been sprayed the previous night, prompting the crew to execute fume checklists and land uneventfully with the affected crew using portable oxygen.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported filing reroute to avoid weather, but TMU issued a reroute resulting in an unsafe flight into weather.
summary: The flight crew filed a weather-avoidance route approved by Dispatch, but ATC issued a reroute into weather during climbout citing TMU requirements. Despite the crew's safety refusal, ATC provided a borderline legal clearance, which the pilot reported as a safety concern caused by TMU overreach.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported the pilot crew did not accomplish a complete approach briefing. ATC approach clearance and speed reduction were late and the Captain was confused regarding the 'cleared for the approach' from ATC. All these contributed to the Low Altitude Warning.
summary: The crew executed an ILS approach with a circling maneuver to Runway XY in a 10-knot tailwind. ATC issued a low altitude warning due to delayed speed reduction and descent caused by clearance confusion and briefing gaps, though the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an upset at FL340 descending into LAX in trail of a B787.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B787 while descending to FL340, causing a rapid roll to 40 degrees right. They manually recovered with minimal altitude loss, and no injuries were reported among passengers or crew.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported new shipping procedures of Lithium Ion battery powered PED's are not being followed.
summary: A baggage service agent reported that Customer Service Representatives are failing to follow new packing procedures for lithium battery devices due to a lack of official directives and missing Hazardous Material labels. The reporter noted that despite completing training, staff ignored the requirements, and raising the issue with co-workers yielded no results.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a critical ground conflict with a ramp pickup truck. The Captain was able to stop and waited until the truck was removed before entering the gate. The Captain reported there have been previous safety reports filed regarding ramp safety at this location.
summary: A pilot taxiing to gate X stopped to avoid a fast-moving pickup truck that failed to yield on the ramp at ZZZ airport. The driver eventually backed up after ground personnel intervened, preventing a probable wing impact, though the pilot cited a systemic lack of vehicle compliance and safety enforcement at the airport.

synopsis: Captain reported a broken shear pin on the tow bar during push back and was incorrectly advised that a log book entry was not required by maintenance.
summary: During pushback of a Boeing 737 MAX, the tug driver reported a broken tow bar shear pin. Line maintenance incorrectly advised no inspection or logbook entry was needed, though the FOM requires these actions for the MAX, unlike the 737-NG.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported LGB charts did not show the taxiways they were assigned.
summary: A Part 121 pilot departing LGB found active taxiways E2 and E missing from current Jeppesen and FAA charts despite visible signage. The pilot reported that the new taxiways, commissioned two weeks prior, were not reflected in charts or NOTAMs, creating a discrepancy between ground reality and available documentation.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported loss of situational awareness led to a near mid air collision when another aircraft that had announced their intentions and was encountered.
summary: During a training flight at ZZZ, the crew lost situational awareness while configuring for landing and nearly collided with an aircraft on final approach. The pilot attributed the incident to complacency and the lack of ADS-B In traffic display, prompting an immediate pattern exit and re-entry to maintain separation.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported braking hard to avoid a collision with another aircraft during taxi.
summary: A training flight taxiing toward Runway XXR nearly collided with Aircraft Y, operated by a single-pilot student, which entered the taxiway from a run-up area without ground clearance or a right-side check. The training crew avoided impact by braking abruptly after the other pilot failed to follow local taxi procedures.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action on take off when another aircraft departed on the opposing runway.
summary: A pilot at ZZZ airport observed a high-wing aircraft taking off on runway XY while intending to depart on runway XX due to wind conditions. Both aircraft became airborne and avoided collision by breaking right, prompting the pilot to recommend installing cameras at runway ends to improve visibility.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft experienced a complete electrical failure/communication loss and descended through the altitude of another aircraft while reversing course to return to their departure airport.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X, which suffered a total electrical failure and lost comms while returning VFR, and Aircraft Y on an RNAV30 approach. The controller held Aircraft Y at 3,000 feet to avoid conflict with Aircraft X, which passed two miles laterally at an unknown altitude.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported aircraft departure with flight release missing required 'Hazmat cargo' amendment note.
summary: The pilot received a Notice to Crew regarding aircraft batteries in compartment D just prior to pushback but failed to note the release on the document. The oversight was not realized until the cruise phase of flight.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported Hazmat cargo [Class 7] loading error missed prior to departure.
summary: Ramp agents incorrectly loaded radioactive material in position 2L instead of the required position 3 and aft. The flight crew failed to detect the error, prompting the captain to suggest software preventing flight document printing for incorrect hazardous goods loading.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported two ground gate returns due to a recurring fume event during departure taxi.
summary: Crew and passengers experienced toxic fumes causing illness during pushback from ZZZ, prompting two returns to the gate. Although a 21-point inspection found no mechanical issues at idle, the odor persisted under power, forcing a second deplaning.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported engine roughness on approach to landing. They were able to continue to a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot reported engine roughness and a 300-400 RPM power loss during initial descent from 3,500 feet MSL into ZZZ. After applying carburetor heat and squawking 7700, the aircraft landed safely with partial power.

synopsis: Flight crew reported descending 1000 feet below minimum altitude on approach as cleared by ATC.
summary: The flight crew descended to 5,000 feet on ATC clearance while deviating from the ZZZZZ arrival due to thunderstorms, despite the published minimum vectoring altitude being 6,000 feet. The controller later questioned the altitude, but no traffic conflicts occurred.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported a fume event during preflight at the gate due to an APU oil leak.
summary: The flight crew detected a neurotoxic odor from the APU bleed system at the gate, prompting passenger deplaning and an engine run-up that confirmed the smell persisted with engine bleeds. Maintenance confirmed a significant APU oil leak, causing the aircraft to be taken out of service.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported an air turn back after the cabin pressurization failed twice.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated cabin altitude alerts during climbout and at FL320 due to a pressurization system malfunction. They performed emergency descents to 10,000 feet, completed checklists, and diverted back to ZZZ for a safe landing.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported the aircraft unexpectedly rolled forward at the gate while attempting to reposition the aircraft to align better with the jet bridge due to the ground crew not connecting the tug.
summary: Flight crew, fatigued after a long duty day, inadvertently rolled the aircraft two feet forward at the gate due to miscommunication with inexperienced ground crew and a gate agent. The movement occurred while passengers were standing and the bridge was close, but no injuries or damage resulted after the parking brake was set.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew reported a fume event of smoke and strong odor in the cabin occurred in cruise following a number 2 engine bleed leak EICAS message.
summary: The flight crew experienced a No. 2 engine bleed leak and subsequent smoke and odor at FL250, likely caused by a left air conditioning pack failure. After donning oxygen masks and requesting priority handling, they descended to 10,000 feet, where the smoke dissipated, allowing for an uneventful landing at ZZZ1.

synopsis: A pilot departing a non towered airport reported a NMAC with climbing traffic not communication on the CTAF.
summary: A pilot departing runway XX at ZZZ experienced a close call with a twin-engine aircraft climbing through their altitude while executing a noise abatement climb. The intruder was not on the CTAF frequency, causing a near collision that was detected via ADSB-in software before the pilot resumed the pattern.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA Pilot reported SQL ATIS as consistently unreadable and unreliable.
summary: Pilots reported that the [SQL] ATIS recording is frequently unintelligible due to audio cutting in and out, preventing clear reception of critical data like altimeter settings and wind. Despite reports to tower controllers, the issue persists, forcing pilots to request weather information directly and defeating the purpose of the ATIS.

synopsis: A Cirrus pilot reported a conflict with skydivers while flying through a designated parachute jump area. The reporter stated incorrectly configured settings in their Foreflight app to hide parachute jump areas contributed to the incident.
summary: A pilot flying VFR in haze overflew a non-towered airport at 3,500 feet MSL and encountered two parachutists above the aircraft. The incident resulted from the pilot's over-reliance on Foreflight, which failed to display Parachute Jump Area rings due to an unselected airspace setting, causing the pilot to miss the parachute symbol on the sectional chart.

synopsis: A pilot departing a non towered airport reported engine failure and landing in a field.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure just after lift-off. After attempting to feather the inoperative engine and experiencing partial power recovery, the aircraft was unable to climb and landed in a field.

synopsis: A fractional company pilot reported right engine failure. The pilot descended, restarted the engine, and continued to their destination instead of landing at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced moderate turbulence at 43,000 feet, causing a right engine flame out. They immediately requested priority handling at ZZZ.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of all Pitot/Static air systems in IMC, requested immediate assistance and diverted to a precautionary landing.
summary: A pilot in a Mooney Ovation experienced an engine power loss and unusual attitude in IMC during cruise, likely due to a blocked pitot tube causing erroneous airspeed indications. After recovering control and landing at ZZZ for inspection, the mechanic found no faults, and the pilot resumed flight the next day.

synopsis: Technician reported not reinstalling the Captain's Air Data Module after troubleshooting and installing the radar transceiver, causing an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: A mechanic removed the Captain's pitot line to the Air Data Module while replacing a radar transceiver but failed to reinstall it. The cause was the mechanic's failure to attach a red streamer to the line as a reminder to reconnect it after the work.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft instructed to intercept the localizer flew through the localizer twice, once resulting in flight below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for an ILS approach at ZZZ1, but the pilot flew through the localizer twice and descended below the 6,000-foot MVA. The controller attributed the incident to high workload from wildfire smoke, multiple coordination calls, and a sudden traffic surge that impaired situational awareness.

synopsis: A Tower Local Controller reported issuing a go around instruction to a landing aircraft after noticing another aircraft crossing the runway hold short lines.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a go-around to Aircraft X after Aircraft Y failed to hold short of runway XYR due to crew confusion over hold short lights. The controller used ASDE-X alerts to intervene, climbing Aircraft X to 3,000 feet and rerouting it for a safe landing ten minutes later.

synopsis: Tower Local Controller reported a departing aircraft was in conflict with arriving traffic under TRACON control. The reporter advised the departing aircraft who then took evasive action while below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: A ZZZ controller managed a conflict between an arriving Aircraft X and departing Aircraft Y below Minimum Vectoring Altitude, issuing a traffic alert that prompted Aircraft Y to turn and avoid. The controller attributed the incident to limited radar situational awareness and recommended software updates to improve visual aids for approach clearances.

synopsis: Flight crew reported descending below minimum altitude on approach and climbed back to correct altitude. ATC advised flight crew that there had previously been problems with the glide slope.
summary: During an ILS approach at night, the crew received an ATC low altitude warning at 8,100 feet and climbed to 8,600 feet after disconnecting the autopilot. The deviation was attributed to either a faulty glide slope signal or an autopilot overshoot during simultaneous localizer and glide slope capture.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain Line Check Airman reported the aircraft database for the MMMX ILS 05R Z does not match the approach chart.
summary: Pilots reported that the FMGC incorrectly loaded fix CI051 instead of MX901 for the ILS 05R approach at MMMX, a discrepancy not noted on NOTAMs. Failure to manually correct this could cause non-compliance with clearances or jam the aircraft on the approach.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported initiating pushback without DG Final documents onboard. Documents were requested and delivered during pushback.
summary: The flight crew hung a Dry Ice message on the Mode Control Panel as a reminder during pushback but realized the final Dangerous Goods message was missing. They requested and received the required message before disconnecting from the pushback tug.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a fumes event of varying intensity from preflight to arrival at destination where maintenance removed the aircraft from service.
summary: The flight crew encountered a strong odor resembling burning oil or carpet cleaner during the ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight, which caused passenger discomfort but no system malfunctions. Maintenance identified the smell upon arrival, removed the aircraft from service for troubleshooting, and the crew completed the trip on a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the PAPI lights at PTKK are inoperative.
summary: A pilot reported that the PAPIs at PTKK were inoperative, leaving no electronic or visual glidepath for night operations. The reporter requested a company response to address this lack of visual aids.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported refusing the aircraft due to a deferred thrust reverser and high brake temperatures that maintenance could not explain.
summary: The pilot refused the aircraft at the gate due to unexplained high wheel brake temperatures and an inoperative #2 thrust reverser. Maintenance could not verify brake function or explain the heat, leading the pilot to deem the aircraft unsafe for flight.

synopsis: A300 First Officer reported a ground gate return due to a fume event during departure taxi.
summary: The flight crew experienced cockpit smoke and chemical exposure after restarting engines following Blue Hydraulic system servicing. They taxied back to the gate, shut down, and sought medical attention for symptoms attributed to the recent maintenance and potential part failure.

synopsis: An Air Carrier flight crew reported a runway incursion when they were instructed to hold short of a runway on a taxiway in between parallel runways that was not long enough to accommodate their B777.
summary: A B777 crew at ZZZ encroached on Runway XYR while attempting to comply with an impossible clearance to cross Runway XYL and hold short of XYR on Taxiway 1. This caused a PC-12 on final to execute a go-around, which the crew attributed to accepting an unfeasible instruction without declaring "unable."

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported that an APU fire began during taxi and was extinguished after the crew ran the applicable procedure.
summary: The flight crew received an APU fire warning and smoke report from Ground Control while taxiing after landing. They stopped the aircraft, executed the APU fire checklist, discharged one bottle to extinguish the fire, and taxied to the parking spot with fire department support.

synopsis: First Officer reported the aircraft weather radar failed in heavy weather and the flight crew elected to divert to a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence and hail while deviating for thunderstorms at FL350 due to an undetected weather radar failure. They diverted to ZZZ after significant altitude deviations, suspecting possible negative G limits and aircraft damage.

synopsis: C208 pilot reported autopilot malfunctions in IMC conditions and elected to perform an air turn back and a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X experienced an uncommanded autopilot engagement and steep descent at 200 feet after takeoff in IMC. After failing to disconnect the system manually, the pilot turned off the avionics, returned to the airport, and landed safely while the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported a cabin fume event to the Captain during taxi which resulted in an uneventful ground gate return.
summary: Cabin crew and a jumpseater detected a sulfur odor in the back galley shortly after pushback, which intensified during taxi. The flight returned to the gate after the smell reappeared and was traced to the area around row R.

synopsis: Technician reported a misapplied NEF item for a damaged cockpit door peephole was discovered to be not authorized and was changed to a repair order with the aircraft taken out of service.
summary: The flight crew reported a concern regarding a deferred flight deck door peep hole. Maintenance determined the item could not be deferred per MEL or NEF and issued a work order to repair the door.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported a foreign air carrier does not include crew rest time during flights as flight time and is not complying with FAR's regarding crew rest after long overseas flights.
summary: A crew member reported that the company incorrectly calculates flight time for 14-hour U.S. flights by excluding bunk time, causing crews to fly over 130 hours monthly while logging under 100. This practice, approved by the Foreign Civil Aviation Authority and involving less than 24-hour rest, is described as a significant safety threat.

synopsis: Flight crew reported TCAS RA during climbout and took evasive action.
summary: The crew of a departing aircraft received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb after merging with unseen traffic at 10,000 feet. The Captain executed a full-power climb, but the First Officer reported never seeing the traffic and criticized the decision to climb rather than remaining below the other aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported encountering wake turbulence from a military transport in the vicinity of SUU airport.
summary: The pilot flying a light aircraft in cruise at 5,500 feet encountered severe wake turbulence from a descending C-17 despite a caution from Travis RAPCON. The pilot misjudged the wake's location, resulting in rough turbulence that caused head injury and unsecured cockpit items to become airborne.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot flying on approach to land reports traffic warning due to a military helicopter over airport who was not making radio calls.
summary: During approach to ZZZ, a pilot received a TIS traffic warning at 500 ft from a military helicopter in clouds, which the pilot initially dismissed as a transponder echo. The helicopter crew reportedly activated their transponder to alert the pilot, highlighting the value of military transponder use during training near civilian airports.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: MSN Controller reported issued relating to the Oshkosh fly in and departure.
summary: A TRACON Data controller failed to notice a supervisor dropping the tag for Aircraft X, causing a loss of radar identification during a point-out coordination. The incident was attributed to high traffic volume and flight plan errors during the EAA Air Adventure, which created frequency congestion and separation risks.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they vectored two aircraft off the final approach course to avoid an unidentified VFR aircraft which departed an airport underneath the final approach course. The reporter states this conflict occurs frequently and recommends extending controlled airspace to prevent further occurrences.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X and diverted Aircraft Y to avoid an unidentified VFR aircraft departing ZZZ1 that climbed into the ZZZ arrival corridor. The controller attributed the safe outcome to anticipating the VFR pilot's turns and recommended extending controlled airspace over ZZZ1 to prevent future incursions.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported another carrier flight crew commented about flames exiting engine tailpipe during takeoff roll. Flight crew returned to departure airport.
summary: A pilot reported a six-foot flame from engine 2 on takeoff, noted by a regional aircraft as afterburner use. The crew returned to ZZZ, where fire trucks inspected the aircraft; the pilot noted the regional's unclear call prevented an early abort.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported Flight Attendants were experiencing physiological symptoms from 'very strong ' cabin fumes. After consultation with Dispatch it was determined to divert for maintenance action.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZ1 due to a strong antimicrobial spray odor in the aft galley that caused two flight attendants breathing difficulties. Dispatch confirmed the aircraft was sprayed the night before, prompting the diversion and medical standby, though the crew landed uneventfully after following fume checklists.

synopsis: Flight crew reported an airport operations vehicle failed to yield to their taxiing aircraft, requiring the Captain to brake suddenly to avoid a collision.
summary: During taxi after pushback, a First Officer warned the Captain of a high-speed grey airport operations vehicle approaching on a service road. The Captain applied brakes to avoid a collision, but the hard stop caused a Flight Attendant to fall and injure herself in the galley.

synopsis: Captain reported assuming control after First Officer's seat slid back and prevented him from reaching the flight controls.
summary: During takeoff roll, the First Officer's seat unlatched horizontally, causing the pilot to slide aft and requiring the pilot monitoring to assume control. The reporter attributed the incident to a seat not properly locked and suggested maintenance inspection of the latching mechanism.

synopsis: Flight crew reported horizontal trim became inoperative with binding when attempting to use manual trim wheels. Flight crew elected to perform an air turn back.
summary: Pilots experienced an inoperative electric horizontal trim shortly after takeoff, requiring difficult manual trim operation likely caused by motor clutching. The crew followed QRH procedures, returned to ZZZ for a safe landing, and attributed the failure to an unknown maintenance issue.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported a distraction from wake turbulence contributed to climbing through an altitude restriction departing DEN in trail of a B777.
summary: The crew climbing from DEN on the EEONS 8 departure encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 777 and received a traffic call near SHOBO. This distraction caused an unintentional climb to 12,300 feet, exceeding the 12,000-foot restriction, which the pilots corrected without ATC notification.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported a ground gate return to remove Hazmat cargo due to an MEL restriction prohibiting the transport of Dry Ice with an active MEL.
summary: Aircraft X experienced a right pack failure after block out. The crew returned to the gate to remove over 500kg of dry ice because the applicable MEL prohibited carrying it with the inoperative pack.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion after the left hand main tire and wheel assembly failed.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft on Runway XX when the left main gear tire separated, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway, strike grass, and spin 180 degrees. No injuries occurred, but the gear rim and components were scattered on the runway, requiring the aircraft to be towed to a hangar for repairs.

synopsis: Pilot reported that the seat lap belt attaching hardware came off during flight.
summary: A pilot reported that during cruise on an A321, the left lap belt detached from the seat pan due to a failed lock nut fastener. The pilot manually reattached the assembly, logged the discrepancy, and recommended fleet inspections for similar belt security issues.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported GPS jamming.
summary: The crew experienced a loss of ADS-B OUT L and GPS position due to GPS jamming.

synopsis: Captain reported a stabilizer main trim runaway on take off and were able to disconnect and use alternate trim to control the aircraft. Captain elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The crew experienced an uncommanded nose-up trim event shortly after departure from ZZZ. They engaged the trim interrupt, followed the QRH to disable the main motor, and used alternate trim to return for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: First Officer reported a Master Warning light with CAB ALT light and elected to make a rapid descent and air turn back to a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew reported a Master Warning and CAB ALT annunciation illuminating while the aircraft was below 14,000 feet. The narrative does not specify the cause or outcome of this event.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported that after landing, while taxiing on the runway for a 180, the aircraft developed an engine problem causing evacuation of the aircraft on the runway.
summary: The pilot inadvertently moved the condition lever from cut-off to low idle during the landing roll at ZZZ, causing an engine overheat and black smoke. Passengers were evacuated, the aircraft was towed to the ramp, and maintenance determined the engine required replacement.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported a fume event during boarding resulting in deplaning passengers.
summary: Cabin crew and the Captain detected an oil/chemical smell during boarding. The crew deplaned passengers and evacuated the aircraft.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: FDK Tower Controller reported the runway extension which was previously charted was removed from the latest charts and will not be published until March of 2022. The reporter states this will potentially cause runway excursions, incursions and confusion for pilots.
summary: A reporter reported that FAA Approach Office personnel unilaterally reverted FDK Runway 5/23 charts to a shortened length in Cycle 2108 despite a physical extension to 5,819 feet. This discrepancy between charts and actual markings creates risks of runway excursions and incursions due to pilot confusion regarding the relocated threshold.

synopsis: Pilot reported that after writing a discrepancy for an engine oil leak, the technician signed the log book entry as acceptable for service without inspecting, cleaning or operating the engine to determine the airworthiness of the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported an oil leak on a rotorcraft's number 1 engine after landing, but the mechanic allegedly falsified the logbook by signing off a required run-up and visual inspection without performing them. Management refused to act on the pilot's report of the falsified maintenance record.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of aircraft electrical systems and diverted to landing at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a total loss of cockpit electrical power while on an IFR flight plan with ZZZ Center. The pilot diverted to the nearest airport, ZZZ, and canceled the flight plan upon landing with no injuries or property damage.

synopsis: A new Instructor pilot on a flight observing another instructor pilot with an introductory student reported the flying pilot performed unsafe maneuvers, intentionally entered IMC conditions, and flew knowing the aircraft had a faulty alternator.
summary: A new CFI observed a Piper PA-28-161 flight where the instructor operated with an unlatched door, no traffic awareness, and a known alternator failure while performing unsafe maneuvers like cloud penetration and dropping objects. The reporter terminated the flight due to escalating safety risks, including low-altitude ocean flying and a near-miss go-around, citing the instructor's disregard for regulations and equipment status.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported after landing they discovered the right engine cowling had come off in flight and struck the horizontal stabilizer. During their descent they felt a bump which they thought was clear air turbulence.
summary: Pilots reported that during descent through 27,000 feet on a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1, sudden turbulence occurred. Post-flight inspection revealed the right engine cowling was missing and had likely struck the horizontal stabilizer, causing the turbulence.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine power loss on takeoff and elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing. Pilot also reported after post flight inspection revealed damage to the propeller with dents in the wings and wing fairing seals.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness and power loss shortly after takeoff, followed by a loud bang and vibration while attempting to return to the airport. Post-flight inspection revealed propeller and wing damage caused by suspected impact with a tree top, though the engine ran normally after repairs.

synopsis: A Glider pilot reported near midair encounters with skydivers.
summary: A pilot flying eastbound at 6,500 feet encountered multiple skydivers falling from 12,000 feet through clouds, potentially passing within 500 feet. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the inability to see jumpers or the drop aircraft through clouds and criticized ZZZ TRACON for failing to alert traffic in uncontrolled airspace.

synopsis: Cessna 172 Pilot reported taking evasive action to avoid an aircraft that disregarded the Tower's instructions.
summary: The pilot at 1,000 ft. TPA on downwind for Runway XXL descended to 700 ft. after Aircraft X ignored left-turn instructions and climbed straight toward them. The conflict, caused by Aircraft X's non-compliance with departure clearance, triggered a TCAS alert and required immediate evasive action.

synopsis: Pilot reported the left main gear collapsed on landing causing a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that the left landing gear collapsed upon landing due to a part failure that allowed the gear to retract, despite indicators showing it down and locked. The aircraft veered off the runway to the left after touchdown, and the pilot immediately communicated the situation while indicators remained unchanged.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported a right trailing edge flap drive rod failure caused asymmetrical flap deployment and controllability issues. The Instructor made an immediate turn back to the runway and made a precautionary landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a left roll after takeoff due to a right flap rod failure caused by metal fatigue. The pilot maintained control with rudder input and executed a safe landing with no damage, suspecting excessive flap usage above the white arc contributed to the failure.

synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft reported an uneventful landing off airport due to running out of fuel. The reporter stated the aircraft had 'engine blow by' and the fuel consumption rate in the manual is not correct.
summary: The pilot of a 1979 Aircraft X experienced engine sputtering and failure at 15 miles from destination due to excessive fuel consumption and inaccurate POH data. The pilot executed an uneventful off-airport landing on a highway with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light Transport Corporate Pilot reported encountering wake turbulence departing OAK in trail of an A321.
summary: A Part 91 pilot departing OAK on Runway 30 encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding A321 shortly after takeoff in IMC conditions. The pilot experienced violent uncommanded rolls and control difficulties at low altitude but recovered by maintaining wings level and following ATC vectors, resulting in a reported pilot deviation.

synopsis: E145 First Officer reported a wake turbulence encounter in trail of a heavy aircraft resulted in altitude loss of 500 to 700 feet on arrival into IAD.
summary: The pilot reported that wake turbulence from a heavy aircraft landing at IAD caused an abrupt 500-700 foot altitude loss while cleared to FL180. Control was maintained, NY Center was advised of the cause, and the remainder of the flight was normal.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported an NMAC with another light aircraft in the pattern at 7S5 airport.
summary: A pilot on left downwind for Runway 34 at 7S5 at 1,200 feet MSL encountered a light aircraft climbing below pattern altitude directly underneath. The pilot executed a left evasive turn to avoid a collision and subsequently exited the pattern to return to home base.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot observed another aircraft passing 500 feet overhead and did not take any evasive action.
summary: A pilot and student on 6-mile final to ZZZ reported Aircraft Y passing behind them at less than 500 feet separation while descending from the right. The reporter noted Aircraft Y was on a different frequency but believed safety was not compromised, though the separation was borderline for regulations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported engine power loss in cruise and elected to land in grass near the destination airport.
summary: A flight of two STOL aircraft experienced partial engine power loss and smoke during cruise from ZZZ to ZZZ1. The lead pilot requested priority handling, allowing the distressed aircraft to make a safe precautionary landing in an open field with no damage or injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported nose landing gear collapse on landing with no injuries. Pilot reported damage was limited to the nose landing gear and propeller.
summary: The pilot reported a nose gear collapse shortly after touchdown during a normal landing at ZZZ. The propeller contacted the runway, causing the aircraft to slide to a stop with damage confined to the prop and engine, but no injuries or fluid leaks occurred.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported after takeoff noticing a vehicle on the runway and avoiding it by overflying it.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion while taking off from runway YY, where a utility van and a person were found on the active surface. The pilot sidestepped to avoid the vehicle, noting that the tower failed to provide information about the obstruction or the incident.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported loss of engine power and requested priority handling to expedite arrival at destination airport.
summary: During cruise at 7,500 feet, the pilot reported sudden engine power loss attributed to suspected carb-icing in 45-degree temperatures. The aircraft landed safely with no damage or injury after the engine was temporarily restored by pumping the throttle, and a mechanic found no fuel system faults.

synopsis: First Officer reported setting the aircraft parking brake but not charging the brake accumulator with battery power prior to removing the wheel chocks. First officer reported that the aircraft began to roll, moving 20 feet before hitting a parked vehicle.
summary: During pre-flight on an unpowered aircraft, the pilot removed chocks after setting the parking brake, assuming the accumulator was charged. The aircraft rolled and struck a vehicle 20 feet away because the hydraulic pump had not been activated to charge the brake system.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the text on the new SID regarding the assigned altitude by ATC is confusing after receiving the CPDLC which contain a hard altitude.
summary: The pilot reported confusion during departure on a new RNAV SID due to conflicting altitude constraints and a poorly worded ATC clearance to "climb via except maintain 10,000 feet." The reporter stated this wording created a setup for miscommunication and recommended clearer phrasing.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported Final Flight Release was missing required Hazmat notification. Flight Release was amended prior to departure.
summary: The Pilot and Operations Agent failed to add a HAZMAT NOTAC for a Fire Extinguisher to the Release before taxiing for departure. Dispatch contacted the crew via ACARS, and the Captain corrected the paperwork prior to takeoff after fatigue and delays caused the initial oversight.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported a fume event of unidentifiable source after gate pushback resulting in a gate return and deplaning of passengers.
summary: The Captain and crew of a Boeing 777 experienced smoke and electrical odors during engine start on the ground, prompting an immediate shutdown of both engines and the APU. A visual inspection revealed a scorched panel in the electronics compartment, leading to a decision to tow the aircraft back to the gate for orderly deplaning rather than evacuate on the busy tarmac.

synopsis: Flight crew reported difficulty in raising the trailing edge flaps and elected to divert instead of risking a grounded aircraft at an outstation.
summary: The crew experienced significant difficulty retracting the flap lever from detents during climb after a Flaps 3 takeoff, requiring two hands to operate. They diverted to ZZZ1 for safety, landed normally with flaps extending correctly, and found the lever locked at position 1 upon taxi-in.

synopsis: Captain reported receiving altimeter and airspeed malfunction messages during climb and elected to do a precautionary diversion.
summary: The crew experienced ALT and IAS DISAGREE EICAS messages while climbing through FL220 in night IMC, with altimeters differing by hundreds of feet and airspeeds by up to 15 knots. After leveling at FL310 and consulting dispatch, they diverted and landed uneventfully at ZZZ1 without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Ramp Agent reported observing a cargo loader cut in front of a taxiing Dreamliner as it was being marshalled into the gate. The Observer further stated that it was impossible to stop the Dreamliner and the cargo loader was able to get out of the way.
summary: A ramp employee driving a cargo loader cut in front of a 787 marshaling at gate XX at XA20. Although the right wing walker displayed a stop signal, the aircraft could not stop, but the loader cleared the right side without incident.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a near midair collision while executing a go-around and took evasive action at a foreign airport.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X experienced a near midair collision while holding at 6,000 feet after receiving an erroneous 090 vector intended for another aircraft. The conflict was resolved by executing a TCAS resolution advisory, likely caused by controller call sign confusion and English language barriers.

synopsis: A321 pilot reported the ACARS generated Eng Out Acceleration Altitude (EOAA) was not the same as the pilot company data recommended EOAA for this aircraft configuration and runway in use.
summary: During pre-flight MCDU programming, the pilot discovered the ACARS-downloaded Engine Out Acceleration Altitude was 520 feet too low for the specific runway and flap setting. The reporter noted this significant discrepancy could lead to a near mishap if crews fail to verify the value against company performance data.

synopsis: First Officer reported a gate return due to an engine 1 FADEC ECAM message that was a repeat discrepancy.
summary: The flight crew received an ENG 1 FADEC A fault ECAM while holding short of Runway XXR at ZZZ. After a failed circuit breaker reset, maintenance declared it a no-go, forcing a return to the gate for this repeat mechanical failure previously signed off.

synopsis: Captain reported diverting due to #4 hydraulic system losing quantity.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZZ1 due to a suspected slow leak in the #4 hydraulic system, which showed a decreasing quantity trend despite depressurizing the pumps. The crew recommends more frequent ground maintenance to address recurring hydraulic issues documented in the aircraft's logbook.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported a fume event during cruise of a burning odor that smelled electrical resulting in a maintenance diversion.
summary: Flight attendants detected an electrical burning smell from a warm vent near the aft galley during cruise. The Captain diverted to ZZZ, where the vent cooled and the odor ceased before landing.

synopsis: PA-28 Flight Instructor reported taking evasive action to avoid an uncommunicative aircraft as well as a potential midair collision while entering the pattern.
summary: A pilot and student conducting pattern work observed Aircraft Y pass 50 feet below without radio calls or a proper 45-degree entry. The pilot diverted over a lake to avoid conflict, attributing the potential midair collision to Aircraft Y's failure to communicate despite having radio capability.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported engine power loss on climb-out and elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot experienced rough engine operation and high cylinder temperatures shortly after departing ZZZ on Runway XX. Suspecting water-contaminated fuel, the pilot returned and landed safely on Runway XY after resolving a clearance discrepancy with Tower.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Twin Engine Instructor Pilot reported an engine failure in flight due to fuel starvation. One main wing tank ran dry after not being serviced at the FBO.
summary: Two pilots conducting a training flight in an AMEL experienced a right engine failure due to an empty right main tank caused by FBO fueling error and inadequate visual verification. The PIC executed emergency procedures to divert and land safely with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Pilot flying TBM 940 aircraft reported cabin pressurization problem in cruise. Descent was initiated to lower altitude and cabin pressure stabilized.
summary: The pilot experienced a cabin pressure loss at 31,000 ft caused by ice breaking a door seal, triggering an emergency descent to 15,000 ft. After stabilizing the cabin and landing safely, the crew cleaned the seals and added a preflight wipe-down step to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a C208 rapidly descended below its assigned altitude, was not responding to ATC calls, and flew below the Minimum IFR Altitude, later the pilot established communications, climbed to a safe altitude and returned to its point of departure.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a C208 pilot experience a rapid, unexplained descent from 10,000 to 2,400 feet, triggering minimum safe altitude warnings. The pilot, shaken and suspecting a software issue, eventually climbed back to 7,000 feet and requested a return to ZZZ1.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ATC Controller reported during a position change with another controller, two aircraft entered into an airborne conflict situation. The conflict was not immediately noticed because the ATC personnel were social distancing.
summary: An air traffic controller relieving a colleague observed two aircraft flashing on the scope before taking the position. The controller issued turn instructions to separate the traffic and recommended sitting closer to the display to improve situational awareness despite social distancing measures.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported experiencing stress and anxiety resulting from working while being unvaccinated and the company requiring employees to be vaccinated.
summary: A pilot flying a scheduled trip on a new aircraft type reported experiencing anxiety and distraction due to an impending job termination caused by not receiving the COVID vaccine. The pilot attributed this mental conflict to the company's vaccine mandate, noting it degraded concentration and landing performance while creating a potentially dangerous work environment.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported unclear ATIS information and a lack of markings resulted in a taxiway incursion at SJU.
summary: The flight crew at SJU inadvertently crossed the closed S1 intersection while taxiing to Runway 8 due to ambiguous ATIS information and lack of markings. Tower directed them to follow a vehicle through the intersection to return to S1 for takeoff.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported noting radar altimeter readings as low as 900 feet AGL on a night visual approach to SAT.
summary: During a night visual approach at an unfamiliar airport, the crew experienced radar altimeter fluctuations caused by hilly terrain while complying with ATC speed and visual acceptance requests. The pilots identified the terrain as the cause, leveled briefly to verify position, and continued safely to landing.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer reported hydraulic system 1 failure due to a faulty auto brake controller.
summary: The crew experienced a total HYD 1 failure after takeoff due to a faulty auto brake controller causing fluid loss. They landed safely at ZZZZ, stopped on the runway, and were towed to the gate with assistance from maintenance and ground personnel.

synopsis: Captain reported a failed integrated drive generator on final approach and selected the wrong IDG to off, resulting in a loss of electrical power. The Captain reported asking for priority handling and continued to landing.
summary: During final approach vectoring, high workload and radio chatter caused the flight crew to turn off the wrong IDG while executing the QRH, resulting in a momentary AC loss and RAT deployment. The crew requested priority handling and landed uneventfully, attributing the error to rushing the checklist in a busy environment.

synopsis: PA-28 student pilot reported expedited taxi to exit runway when another aircraft landed on the opposing runway without clearly stating intentions.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion at ZZZ while landing on Runway XX, where Aircraft Y landed on the opposite Runway XY without yielding right of way. The investigation concluded the other pilot violated right-of-way rules and landed under reduced safety standards.

synopsis: UAS Crew was conducting a test flight when a motor failed after two separate flights. Software was found to be out of date and after update UAS flew without issues.
summary: During a UAS acceptance flight hover at 15 feet, the vehicle entered a graveyard spiral due to a motor failure caused by mismatched flight controller and controller software. A field software update resolved the issue, allowing successful subsequent testing and mission capability verification.

synopsis: EMB-145 Flight Attendant reported an air turn back due to an inflight cabin depressurization event.
summary: The crew diverted back to ZZZ after the Captain reported a cabin decompression at 10,000 ft. The flight landed safely, and the First Officer inspected the cargo and vent doors immediately after deplaning.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported a fumes event described as a musty odor during initial climbout. Reporter stated face masks hindered the crew communication and ability to smell.
summary: During climbout, a pilot detected a musty odor and expressed concern that their mask impaired their ability to smell and communicate with a coworker. The report does not identify the specific cause or outcome of the odor.

synopsis: Technician reported a fuel spill during an ETOPS Pre Departure Check when the aircraft fueler began fueling while technicians were cross feeding fuel to correct a fuel imbalance.
summary: During preflight ETOPS checks on Aircraft X, a fuel auto transfer fault cleared while moving fuel from the center tank, but a fueler unaware of the transfer overfilled the right wing tank, causing a spill. The crew stopped the transfer and cleaned the spill after the fueler failed to notice the transfer approaching maximum wing capacity.

synopsis: Pilot reported performing an in-flight engine shut down due to a suspected fuel issue and conducted a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a left engine surge and failure during cruise due to a fuel leak at the left main tank filler cap, which emptied the tank. After troubleshooting failed, the pilot caged the engine and executed a successful single-engine landing at ZZZ2.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Captain reported a runway excursion when the winds pushed the aircraft off the runway into soft mud.
summary: During rollout after landing a Part 135 charter flight on Runway XX, the aircraft veered right and exited into soft mud due to a strong, shifting crosswind that reduced rudder effectiveness. Despite maximum braking and rudder inputs by both pilots, directional control was lost, resulting in an off-runway stop with no injuries to the two crew members or passengers.

synopsis: Citation I Captain reported a fumes event during descent.
summary: Two pilots experienced smoke in the right flight deck while descending from 28,000 to 18,000 feet during a demonstration flight. They donned oxygen masks, executed the emergency checklist, requested priority handling, and landed safely at ZZZ Airport without incident.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion due to over correction of steering on landing rollout.
summary: During landing, the pilot overcorrected steering to the left, causing the aircraft to exit the runway. The right-hand stabilator tip subsequently struck a runway light.

aircraft: Small UAS (At or above 0.55 lbs and less than 55 lbs)
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot learned after a flight they flew in controlled airspace without authorization.
summary: The pilot conducted a flight in Class D airspace at PDK without prior authorization after incorrectly referencing a Class G location in Tucker via Airmap. Management identified the error post-flight, leading to a discussion on the necessity of verifying physical addresses before flight.

synopsis: B737 NG Captain reported loss of navigation systems and instruments on lift off. Captain elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain reported that immediately after takeoff, the aircraft experienced simultaneous failures of navigation, heading, PWS, TCAS, and flight director systems. After troubleshooting failed, the crew returned to ZZZ for a priority ILS landing on Runway XXR.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported cabin altitude was uncontrollable and the flight crew elected to request an immediate descent. The flight continued to destination airport at a reduced altitude.
summary: During cruise at 16,000 feet, the crew observed abnormal cabin pressurization with rising cabin altitude and descended to 10,000 feet following QRH procedures. The aircraft landed safely at ZZZ after the crew coordinated with dispatch and maintenance regarding the pressurization system failure.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported diverting due to unreliable airspeed and altitude indications.
summary: The Captain experienced an Air Data Computer failure at FL340, causing airspeed and altitude indications to fail and disconnecting the autopilot and autothrottles. The crew diverted to ZZZ, where Approach provided groundspeed calls to verify airspeed, resulting in an uneventful landing and subsequent water intrusion inspection.

synopsis: Captain reported diverting due to HSDI FAIL message caused by inflight icing.
summary: The flight crew experienced recurring HSDI FAIL and HSDI FAIL ON CAS messages during icing conditions on flights from ZZZ to ZZZ1 and ZZZ1 to ZZZ2. The crew diverted to ZZZ3 after the faults reappeared in icing, though the system functioned normally on the ground.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported engine failure during training and performed an off airport landing.
summary: The pilot and student experienced an engine failure in Aircraft X at 4,000 feet MSL over the ZZZ practice area. After unsuccessful restart attempts, they executed a forced landing on an island, contacting a dirt berm to stop safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Flight Instructor and student reported that during cruise the landing gear began cycling from extend to retract with the control handle in the retract position. They diverted and performed a precautionary landing.
summary: During an IFR training cruise, the aircraft's landing gear cycled automatically due to a malfunctioning electric power pack. The crew diverted, verified gear extension via a low approach, and landed safely after maintenance confirmed the fault.

synopsis: Pilot reported 3J1 airport is in disrepair and deteriorating further under the new owners.
summary: Pilots at airport 3J1 reported that poor management since 2007 caused overgrown vegetation, attracting wildlife and resulting in two bird strikes. Additionally, deteriorating infrastructure, blocked ramps, and inaccessible gates have degraded airport operations and safety.

synopsis: Instructor Captain reported the newly purchased aircraft is possibly missing required avionics manuals.
summary: A pilot and instructor grounded a new Piper PA28 after discovering missing hard copies of required Garmin G3X, G5, and GNX 375 pilot guides listed in the POH limitations. The manufacturer failed to provide these physical manuals upon delivery, prompting an investigation into regulatory compliance before flight operations resume.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported that a miscalculation of fuel requirements resulted in fuel exhaustion and an off-airport landing.
summary: A pilot and student flying a commercial cross-country flight ran out of fuel due to a mathematical error in fuel planning while approaching ZZZ. They executed an uneventful off-airport landing on a highway with no injuries or damage after the engine sputtered on base leg.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported Dispatch notification during cruise stating Hazmat cargo weight not included in the aircraft Weight & Balance data. Weight & Balance data corrected and flight continued.
summary: The flight crew received an ACARS alert during cruise that hazardous materials were excluded from the Zero Fuel Weight calculation. They updated the FMC with corrected takeoff and landing data, and the flight continued normally.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported a fume event during engine start after push back. Both engines were shut down due to a persistent faint fume, abnormal noise, and simultaneous APU failure. A safe ground return was completed.
summary: The flight crew experienced an electrical short in the amp bay causing smoke and engine shutdowns while parked at the ramp. The aircraft was towed back to the gate for inspection after the APU failed and communication systems were compromised, with no fire or injuries reported.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew had a near miss with a UAS while on a visual approach.
summary: The Pilot Flying and co-pilot encountered a drone while descending on a visual approach to Newark Runway 29 between 1000 feet and the runway. The drone passed under the right wing with less than 100 feet separation, prompting the crew to alert Tower and Ground Control to warn succeeding aircraft.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a B767-300 aircraft had electrical issues during departure climb and diverted.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical issues during climbout from ZZZ. The aircraft was diverted to ZZZ1, and ATC was advised.

synopsis: Flight Attendant on a B737 MAX 8 reported the flight crew performed a rejected take off after hearing a loud pop from the number 1 engine.
summary: Cabin crew on a new Boeing 737 MAX reported a loud pop from engine #1 and left yaw shortly after takeoff roll, causing an aborted departure. The aircraft stopped quickly with no injuries, and the crew returned to the gate for inspection due to an unspecified engine malfunction.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported fatigue and being unable to perform duties due to multiple return to gate incidents and plane swaps.
summary: A flight crew member reported being unable to continue duties after two consecutive aircraft maintenance issues caused delays and deplaning in extreme heat. The crew member attributed their physical and mental condition to the stress, heat exposure, and lingering long-haul COVID symptoms.

synopsis: B737-900 Flight Attendant reported a passenger using a breathing device during cruise without prior airline approval.
summary: Flight attendants discovered a passenger using an unapproved oxygen concentrator mid-flight on a [model name] aircraft because no special notes existed and no approved unit list was found in manuals.
