synopsis: Flight Crew reported they were advised after the flight that they almost collided with a deicing truck when they taxied from deicing while the truck was still inspecting the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X at ZZZ-ZZZ1 taxied after deicing, unaware a ramp crew member was re-inspecting the tail without communication. This miscommunication caused the aircraft to move within striking distance of the deice truck, though no collision occurred.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Captain reported that an engine malfunction in flight resulted in a partial loss of power in one of the engines. The flight continued to planned destination and made a safe landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a suspected turbocharger waste gate failure on the left engine shortly after departure, causing manifold pressure to drop before stabilizing at 20 inches. The crew elected to continue to ZZZ1 with priority handling, landing safely and taxiing under partial power without notifying passengers.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported undocumented Hazmat transported by passenger carrying a portable oxygen generator. Gate Agent did not notify flight or cabin crew before gate departure. Flight crew was not provided NOTOC prior to pushback.
summary: The pilot reported that 30 minutes after takeoff, a flight attendant discovered a passenger's portable oxygen generator, which was approved and had sufficient batteries. The pilot noted this was a recurring issue and suggested gate agents be reminded to notify crews about such devices.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Check Pilot reported failure to follow SOP resulted in crossing the final approach fix at MGGT one dot low. No terrain alert was received, and the aircraft landed safely.
summary: A VFR flight into GUA armed the autopilot approach mode too early, causing the aircraft to capture a false glide slope and descend abruptly. The captain disengaged the autopilot to climb back to altitude, resulting in a stabilized approach and landing 600 feet down the runway.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain taxiing for departure from PHL reported confusing taxiway signage.
summary: A pilot reported that S2 and S1 labeling signs located short of Runway 27L create a perception that S2 is S1. The reporter recommends moving the sign to a better location to resolve this confusion.

synopsis: Pilot reported ground loop occurred after landing in windy conditions, resulting in a runway excursion and damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a lightly loaded 1955 C-180 ground looped during a crosswind landing at a remote strip after aggressively lowering the tail wheel. This action induced a right turn and left wing lift, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and sustain left wingtip damage due to a loss of directional control.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC with another aircraft entering the pattern.
summary: A flight instructor and student on upwind at 300 feet during touch-and-goes at ZZZ nearly collided with a pilot on final who switched runways without seeing them. The instructor executed a climbing left turn to avoid the fast-approaching aircraft, which passed within 50 to 100 feet before the other pilot admitted he did not see them.

synopsis: Pilots reported losing 500 feet of altitude on final approach due to moderate turbulence and wind shear.
summary: During approach to Runway XX at ZZZZ, the crew descended 500 ft below the assigned 3,000 ft due to wind shear and turbulence. The controller advised of the deviation, but the crew intercepted the glideslope at the lower altitude and landed safely with the runway in sight.

synopsis: G-IV Captain reported flap control malfunction during departure climb resulted in a return to departure airport and normal configuration landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced auto-throttle disengagement and a "Flap input invalid" message during departure from ZZZ when flaps failed to retract from 10 degrees. After troubleshooting and holding to reduce weight, they landed safely at ZZZ with flaps extended to full.

synopsis: Reporter stated a UAS had the battery changed and software rebooted after flight issues. Upon launching again the Crew was unable to maintain control of the UAS and it crashed.
summary: During a public safety operation, a drone crashed into a nearby wall immediately after relaunch, failing to respond to pilot inputs despite flight logs showing continuous downward commands. A disguised cell tower within 50 feet was found, but it remains unknown if interference or an IMU failure caused the loss of control.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ORD Tower Controller and a flight crew reported the crew departed from a recently constructed runway, turned the wrong direction and contacted the wrong Departure Controller. The reporter states this is a recurring issue.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X mistakenly turned left instead of right after takeoff from Runway 10L due to the crew switching to departure frequency prematurely. The controller corrected the heading, but the incident highlighted a recurring issue with crews mishearing instructions and changing frequencies before receiving clearance.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported descending an IFR aircraft 1,000 feet below the MIA to get the aircraft to VFR conditions and below icing.
summary: An air traffic controller assisted a pilot experiencing moderate rime icing who could not maintain altitude in mountainous terrain. The controller descended the aircraft 1,000 feet below the Minimum IFR Altitude to clear the icing, allowing the pilot to establish VFR conditions and cancel IFR.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the pilot taxiing had to make a sudden stop to avoid a vehicle on the road that began to enter the ramp. Reportedly, flight attendants were injured as a result of the abrupt stop.
summary: During taxi out on the Bravo line, a fuel truck failed to yield, causing the Student Captain to stop the aircraft abruptly. Two flight attendants in the aft galley were possibly injured but elected to continue the flight, which landed uneventfully with EMTs meeting the aircraft at the gate.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to LAX in trail of a B787.
summary: The pilot reported a significant wake turbulence encounter from a preceding B787-9 at the CRCUS waypoint during the ILS 24R approach, causing a rapid 25-degree right bank and dutch-roll. The crew initiated upset recovery, momentarily deviating from the flight path, but landed normally without reporting the event due to frequency congestion.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported GPS jamming.
summary: The crew experienced ATC and GPS advisory EICAS messages during cruise near ABQ due to external GPS jamming testing. Navigation degraded to IRU DME/DME for the remainder of the flight, but no safety was compromised.

synopsis: Air Carrier ramp personnel reported an inability to close out cargo release due to baggage configuration error message.
summary: A ramp lead reported confusion after being unable to close a Hazmat load card on an international flight despite surrounding the cargo with 600 lbs of freight. The reporter questioned why this weight was rejected while previous flights accepted fewer bags supplemented by AOGs, quick packs, or CAP items to meet the 450 lb requirement.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported being notified of a Hazmat violation regarding a cargo pallet shipment that was incorrectly labeled.
summary: A ground handler at ZZZ moved unmarked, shrink-wrapped pallets containing hazardous materials to ZZZ1. The incident occurred because the hazardous cargo was not properly identified or labeled prior to transport.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot flying in foreign country airspace reported GPS jamming.
summary: Aircraft X experienced GPS loss due to suspected jamming or interference while en route from LOGMU to UBONA between XA43z and XB29z. The pilot reported the functionality failure along this specific route segment.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dash 8 flight crew reported smoke and fumes in the cockpit and elected to evacuate the aircraft.
summary: During pre-flight de-icing at the gate, smoke appeared behind the Captain's seat and circuit breaker panel, prompting the flight crew to initiate an evacuation. The crew shut down the APU and evacuated all passengers and crew without fire warnings, though the pilot noted they should have specified exit doors for a faster deplaning.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier Technician reported an APU pressure duct seal clamp not installed and took the aircraft out of service for maintenance.
summary: Aircraft X arrived at the gate with the APU duct pressure seal clamp missing, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service. The repair requires approximately four hours, and the reporter noted several other aircraft have experienced this same issue.

synopsis: PRM1 pilot reported failure of AHRS system after takeoff. The pilot returned to departure airport and landed uneventfully.
summary: The pilot, new to the aircraft, experienced AHRS 1 and 2 failures shortly after takeoff following an unannounced AHRS 1 replacement by maintenance. Relying on the standby gyro and wet compass, the pilot executed an ILS approach and landed safely, recommending improved maintenance communication and risk assessment.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported loss of situational awareness, allowing aircraft to descend below approach altitude in IFR, resulted in GPWS and ATC low altitude alerts.
summary: During an IFR LDA 35 approach to SLC in snow, the crew inadvertently descended below the 4900 MSL minimum at the WEEL waypoint due to the PIC's visual contact with the ground. The aircraft triggered a terrain warning and received a low altitude call from Tower, but the crew corrected the descent and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported stabilizer trim became inoperative and elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
summary: The First Officer landed a Boeing 737-800 at ZZZ with inoperative stabilizer trim after the Captain transferred control shortly after takeoff. The crew performed a safe 15-flap landing following checklist procedures, though maintenance personnel were confrontational regarding the aircraft's switch configuration at the gate.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported EFB content crashed while doing checklists for an engine fire. Reporter recommends retaining the paper copies of the QRH on the aircraft to mitigate this situation.
summary: During takeoff with an engine fire/failure, the pilot's EFB content locker crashed, causing a delay in accessing the QRC checklist. The pilot reported that removing paper QRHs from this fleet would be a mistake, noting this is a recurring EFB issue.

synopsis: Ground employee reported the careless operation by a fuel truck driver resulting in a belt load driver having to take evasive action.
summary: A company fuel truck cut off a belt loader approaching the AFT cargo pit, causing the loader driver to slam on the brakes to avoid a collision.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported leveling at proper altitude and receiving a low altitude alert from ATC.
summary: The pilot received a Low Altitude Alert while leveling at 1,600 feet MSL during a visual approach into ZZZ. The crew attributed the alert to a selected descent rate of 1,200 feet per minute placing the aircraft below the glide slope, though they continued and landed safely.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported nearly being hit by a speeding vehicle while walking under the aircraft's wing during the pre-flight walk around.
summary: During a pre-flight walk-around at Gate Z-XX after sunset, a pilot was nearly struck by a white van driving at high speed under the left wingtip. The reporter attributes the incident to poorly trained drivers who ignore flight line speed limits and supervisors who failed to teach proper lookout techniques.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported a Terrain Warning issued by the Tower Controller while preparing for a visual approach. The FO stated the cause was poor descent planning and not following SOP's for the type of approach.
summary: The flight crew received a low altitude alert during a visual approach base turn after extending the runway by 3 NM. The pilot attributed the event to poor descent planning, noting that a longer downwind leg would have prevented the situation.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported a taxi deviation due to poor marking and signage on this taxiway in LAS airport.
summary: The flight crew departed the gate and mistakenly entered Taxiway Q instead of Taxiway C while taxiing to Runway 26R due to missing signage for Q. ATC queried the error and issued a new clearance to join Taxiway C, prompting a recommendation to improve Taxiway Q sign visibility.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported entering a non-movement area while taxiing at HTS airport, citing poor airport lighting and markings as contributing factors to the incident.
summary: The First Officer and Captain crossed a movement area without taxi clearance while repositioning to a de-ice pad at night. Poor lighting, unclear markings, and reduced situational awareness during aircraft configuration caused the potential pilot deviation at this unfamiliar airport.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into DEN in trail of an A320.
summary: The Captain, acting as Pilot Flying with a student, experienced two wake turbulence events from an A320 while descending to Denver at FL260. The aircraft rolled hard with "Roll Authority" cautions, requiring manual recovery and a speed reduction to 250 knots before a normal landing.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a pressurization malfunction during cruise. The flight diverted and landed uneventfully.
summary: The flight crew received an excessive cabin altitude warning at FL250, donned oxygen masks, and descended to 10,000 feet. Although passenger masks did not deploy, the crew diverted to ZZZ and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: First Officer reported executing an ATC-directed go-around at ORD when wake spacing was lost.
summary: The flight crew on an ILS PRM approach to Runway 10C queried ATC multiple times for clearance due to perceived controller saturation. After intercepting the glide slope at 3,000 feet, they were instructed to go around for wake turbulence and subsequently vectored to Runway 9L.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a gate return after finding it took abnormally high thrust to move the airplane. Maintenance replaced a main tire and wheel assembly due to a frozen wheel bearing.
summary: The flight crew attempted a single-engine taxi but found excessive drag requiring high power, leading to a gate return. Maintenance discovered a frozen internal wheel bearing on the outboard main landing gear axle, which caused the drag on the first flight of the day.

synopsis: First Officer reported almost getting hit by a baggage cart vehicle while doing a walk around inspection of the aircraft.
summary: A baggage cart driver departed the service road at high speed and drove under the tail of an aircraft, nearly striking a mechanic conducting an exterior inspection at DFW. The reporter attributed the incident to driver inattention regarding operating procedures and vehicle speed.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a momentary loss of directional control during takeoff due to non standard procedures. The Captain reported handing control of the aircraft to the First Officer while the throttles were not evenly matched. When the auto throttles were engaged with unmatched N1's, the aircraft began to veer into the lower powered engine. The Captain re-synced the N1's and the takeoff continued.
summary: During a wet departure of flight XA15 from ZZZ, the Captain intervened when the First Officer pressed TOGA with asymmetric engine thrust, causing the aircraft to veer left. The Captain attributed the incident to rushing operations, a language barrier, and imprecise communication regarding the spooled engine.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain is questioning the logic behind the decision to descend to FL290 during the emergency decompression or emergency drift-down maneuver. The Captain believes the correct altitude should be FL250.
summary: A pilot questioned an escape procedure for a future trip to ZZZZ requiring an initial altitude of 29,000 feet in high terrain. The reporter cited training from the late 1980s stating descent to 25,000 feet is imperative to prevent hypoxia and sought justification for the current procedure.

synopsis: B777-200 First Officer reported diverting and making an overweight landing due to unreliable fuel quantity indications.
summary: The flight crew encountered fuel imbalance and disagree alerts during cruise, leading to a diversion for an overweight landing after 9,000 pounds of fuel could not be accounted for. Post-flight analysis suggests a fuel quantity sensor failure caused the discrepancy, though no emergency was declared.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported receiving a terrain warning on final approach.
summary: Pilots of ZZZ1 received a visual approach clearance at 5,000 feet over mountains, but the First Officer descended to 3,500 feet with only flaps 9, triggering a terrain warning at 1,500 feet. The reporter attributed the incident to pilot distraction and Air Traffic Control managing multiple frequencies at low altitude.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a pressurization system malfunction in climb. Returned to departure airport and landed uneventfully.
summary: During climb through FL200, the crew experienced a pressurization malfunction with rapid cabin altitude rise and no ECAM warning. They leveled at FL220, descended, and returned to ZZZ, attributing the cause to a simple mechanical failure potentially involving the left Pack on MEL.

synopsis: A320 pilot reported severe turbulence while attempting to land at original destination. Flight was diverted to a local airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence on arrival into ZZZ1, causing an altitude deviation that required disconnecting the autopilot and diverting to ZZZ2. The event, attributed to a large weather system with inadequate PIREPs, resulted in no injuries but prompted a post-flight inspection and a recommendation to upgrade older weather radar systems.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Flight Attendant reported an odor onboard the aircraft.
summary: Crew detected an odor onboard the aircraft. The narrative does not specify the aircraft type, flight phase, cause, or outcome of the incident.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported a 'strange musty odor' during taxi. Flight returned to gate and did not take aircraft to destination.
summary: A crew of five boarded Aircraft X, which had been cancelled the previous day for fumes, and taxied out. The First Officer and flight attendants detected a musty odor, returned to the gate, and aborted the flight, questioning the decision that the aircraft was safe despite the fumes.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported being notified by pilots of a 'slight odor' due to an aircraft issue. Reporter stated the odor was very noticeable when flight deck door was opened during deplaning at destination.
summary: Cabin crew reported a slight odor and suspected air system malfunction that was noticeable when the flight deck door was open and during deplaning. The reporter stated the flight should not have departed with this known problem.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Service personnel reported a lavatory waste ramp spill caused by a ground equipment malfunction. The waste spill drained into storm drain due to the lack of Spill Kit availability.
summary: A lavatory truck driver servicing an aircraft at Gate XX noticed a cracked hose spilling waste into a nearby storm drain. The driver stopped servicing but could not contain the 6 to 8 gallons of hazardous waste because no spill kits were available at the gate.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Mechanic reported a truck almost hitting an aircraft that was taxiing out of the ramp.
summary: A mechanic driving a truck failed to yield to an aircraft taxiing from the ramp, entering the pilot's blind spot despite the aircraft's active lights and the pilot's horn warnings. The pilot stopped just in time to avoid a collision, which the reporter attributed to the mechanic's lack of situational awareness.

synopsis: PA-34 Pilot reported an engine failure in flight and elected to make an immediate air turn back and precautionary landing at the departure airport.
summary: The Pilot-in-Command of a Piper Seneca II experienced a right engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to an uncommanded fuel flow increase causing excessive temperatures. The pilot safely landed single-engine at the departure airport, attributing the incident to a potential maintenance oversight following a recent overhaul.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA instructor pilot reported an NMAC while on final approach. The Instructor states being aware of another aircraft in the airport traffic pattern. When on final the instructor's ADS-B showed zero vertical feet separation with the other aircraft. It was then the Tower Controller instructed the second aircraft to make a 360 degree turn.
summary: During evening traffic pattern practice, a pilot on left downwind for Runway XX observed another aircraft at zero vertical separation on ADS-B while both were cleared to land. The pilot noticed the trailing aircraft only after Tower instructed it to perform a 360-degree turn, at which point it pulled away to the left at the same altitude.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC in the traffic pattern while preparing to land. The pilot reported the other aircraft did not follow instructions from the Tower. The intruding aircraft caused the reporter to take evasive action.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a high-wing single-engine aircraft on downwind had to maneuver and descend to 600 ft to avoid a same-model aircraft that failed to respond to instructions and followed too closely. The reporter described the event as a close call caused by the other pilot's lack of communication and proximity.

synopsis: C152 pilot reported an NMAC and a wake turbulence encounter departing VNC.
summary: A pilot on downwind for Runway 23 at VNC reported a C182 departed behind and passed 20–30 feet below without radio contact. The pilot felt the C182's wake, feared aircraft damage, and immediately decided to land.

synopsis: A light sport aircraft pilot reported loss of GPS signal.
summary: A pilot flying from ZZZ1 to ZZZ2 inadvertently entered ELP's Class C airspace after an EFIS GPS failure eliminated position data on the moving map. The incursion occurred while the pilot visually searched for landmarks in desert terrain to determine position after troubleshooting failed.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a NMAC while in the traffic pattern and preparing to land.
summary: A pilot conducting a night visual approach to Runway XXL with an inoperative landing light reported a close encounter with a small GA aircraft passing within 150 feet below. The pilot attributed the incident to a lack of traffic advisories from Tower Control while maneuvering in the pattern.

synopsis: Corporate flight crew reported NOTAMs and METAR indicated favorable weather, yet snow and ice were present, resulting in loss of aircraft control and excursion from runway.
summary: The flight crew landed on a runway reported as having medium braking action but found compacted snow on the edges, causing the aircraft to veer left and exit the runway. The crew attributed the incident to inaccurate NOTAMs and METARs that failed to reflect the actual nil surface conditions.

synopsis: Do 328 flight crew reported a runway excursion during landing rollout and cited a strong crosswind and patchy ice on the runway as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing on Runway XX, a stronger-than-reported left crosswind and suspected patchy ice pushed the aircraft off the right side of the runway. Control was reestablished, and the aircraft taxied to the FBO.

synopsis: Solo private pilot and an instructor of another aircraft reported an NMAC and Class C airspace penetration while maneuvering in the CCB airport traffic pattern.
summary: The pilot extended the downwind leg at Cable Airport to maintain spacing behind another aircraft, inadvertently clipping Ontario Airspace. The pilot attributed the incursion to insufficient room to turn north for a new approach while managing traffic separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported practicing in an area during a perceived non-active TFR. Upon landing the pilot noticed UAS operations on the airport which appeared to not coincide with the airport NOTAM times.
summary: A pilot conducting a simulated engine-out emergency landing at an uncontrolled field observed drone operations near Point Mugu Naval Base despite no active TFR or ground contact. The reporter attributed the confusion to unclear NOTAM times and the absence of a standard TFR boundary, noting that Zulu times technically permitted the operation.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a runway excursion during landing rollout.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X departed ZZZ1 in gusty crosswinds and landed at ZZZ on Runway XX. A strong gust during rollout caused the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike a light, which the pilot attributed to inadequate crosswind correction or flap selection.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported while inbound to OSU, ATC instructed a turn to the west, which resulted in a NMAC with an aircraft in pattern.
summary: A pilot inbound to OSU was instructed by Bethel Tower to turn west while approaching, placing the aircraft in a head-on conflict with Aircraft Y on downwind. The pilot avoided a collision by increasing bank to 40 degrees after the other aircraft closed closer than expected.

synopsis: C-150 Student pilot reported electrical failure during taxi for takeoff.
summary: A student pilot experienced repeated transponder transmitter failures and lost radio communication with Tower during taxi at ZZZ. The pilot received light gun signals to exit the runway and taxied back to the hangar after the avionics completely shut down.

synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot was flying in an area of a natural disaster. Prior to the flight the UAS pilot checked for NOTAMs/TFRs and saw none. Reporter learned during post flight that they flew in a TFR that had been created after takeoff.
summary: A UAS pilot operating news coverage in City, State, unknowingly flew into a TFR effective at XB:30 because Foreflight failed to display the restriction due to poor cell coverage. The pilot concluded that contacting FSS is necessary when internet-based mapping reliability is in doubt.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported ATC Altitude Alert on approach to land.
summary: The pilot descended to 1500 ft. MSL during the base turn while arcing at four miles instead of staying at 2000 ft. outside five miles. This deviation triggered a low altitude warning from Tower.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 flight crew reported inflight vibration caused by external power receptacle door left open by ground operations personnel.
summary: Pilots experienced constant vibration during climb and cruise caused by the pushback crew leaving the external power receptacle door open on a 737 Max. The crew continued to the destination where maintenance confirmed the door was open at 90 degrees, attributing the error to confusing ground equipment locations.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported retracting gear before flaps during a go-around procedure.
summary: During an ILS PRM approach in IMC with tailwinds, the crew executed a go-around after losing flight directors and drifting off course. The First Officer inadvertently selected landing gear up before retracting flaps due to distraction, though the aircraft remained within flap speed limits and completed a subsequent uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737 MAX Captain reported RAAS annunciations are extremely loud resulting in blocked or interrupted communications.
summary: Pilots of a 737-MAX could not hear ATC instructions to line up and wait or clear for takeoff because the RAAS announcements occurred simultaneously and loudly. The noise-canceling headsets failed to filter the RAAS volume, forcing ATC to repeat clearances.

synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Captain reported landing safely following loss of IRS 1 that manifested as multiple system failures, including autopilot 1 and Captain's attitude information. Autopilot 2 was engaged but allowed an out-of-trim condition to develop, resulting in control difficulties.
summary: During descent on a MAX aircraft, an IRS fault caused autopilot disconnect and attitude loss, followed by a stabilizer out-of-trim condition upon autopilot disengagement. The crew abandoned the approach, hand-flew the aircraft to stabilize trim, and executed a normal landing on a different approach.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported an engine in flight shut down and air turn back after the #2 engine experienced a re-occurrence of a compressor stall.
summary: The crew experienced a #2 engine stall with EGT exceedance while climbing through 11,000 feet. They secured the engine, returned to ZZZ, and completed a visual overweight landing with no damage found during fire department inspection.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported an engine in flight shut down and diversion caused by incorrect fuel quantity indications.
summary: During climb at FL190, the Captain detected a significant fuel imbalance and suspected a leak, initiating a QRH procedure that resulted in shutting down Engine 1 and diverting to ZZZ. The aircraft landed safely, and the fire chief reported no visual evidence of a leak.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer reported a #1 Engine spool down at cruise. The engine was shut down and the aircraft diverted to make a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine fuel pressure loss at FL320 due to a sheared pump drive shaft, causing power loss and a descent to FL260. After unsuccessful restart attempts, they secured the engine and performed a smooth single-engine landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence departing ATL in trail of an A321.
summary: The crew departed behind an A321 from ATL Runway 8R on the CUTTN2 RNAV departure without a wake turbulence advisory. They encountered severe wake turbulence twice between 1,000 feet and 3,000 feet, requiring autopilot disconnection and full aileron input to maintain control, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported an odor that smelled like dirty socks mid cabin. Plane returned to gate and passengers were deplaned.
summary: The First Officer and flight attendants detected a "dirty socks" odor mid-cabin while taxiing out. The crew returned to the gate, deplaned two passengers, and deferred the flight due to a suspected fume event linked to a previous night's issue.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported mistakenly joined up with the wrong aircraft for a formation flight resulting in an NMAC.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ mistakenly identified a similar-looking aircraft as a friend's and attempted a formation join. After breaking off due to lack of radio contact, the pilot landed and discovered the aircraft was not his friend's, causing a confusion incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew and a Technician reported that the aircraft tipped back onto its tail after cargo was loaded.
summary: Ground personnel loaded the airplane too far aft of the center of gravity, causing it to tip onto its tail. The reporter attributed the incident to incorrect loading, lack of communication, and rushing during freight operations.

synopsis: Flight Instructor flying PA-28 aircraft reported NMAC during departure climb.
summary: A pilot and student conducting pattern work at ZZZ experienced a near-midair conflict with another GA aircraft shortly after takeoff. The pilot descended to 550 ft AGL to create separation after Tower issued a traffic alert, resulting in the other aircraft passing overhead by 400–500 ft.

synopsis: C177RG flight instructor reported a malfunction in the brake system during taxi for takeoff.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 177RG experienced a right brake failure during taxi, causing the aircraft to overrun and strike a taxiway edge light. The incident resulted in propeller damage and hydraulic fluid leakage, though both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: Hobby UAS pilot was using manual flight mode during cruise flight when UAS made a non commanded right hand turn into a nearby tree. The UAS suffered minor damage and was recovered.
summary: A recreational drone pilot crashed the aircraft into trees during cruise flight after it made an uncommanded hard right turn despite left stick input. The pilot attributes the loss of control to suspected local interference from nearby microwave transmitters or a jamming device, resulting in propeller damage with no injuries.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft had a heater problem, aircraft was icing up, and could not hold altitude.
summary: An ATC team assisted a small aircraft experiencing icing and altitude loss below MIA by coordinating weather avoidance and obstruction tracking. The pilot safely landed after losing radar contact, though the incident was complicated by incorrect flight plan data and a lack of depicted obstructions on video maps.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a SOURCE OFF light illuminated during cruise. When running the checklists, the flight crew attempted a start of the APU, subsequently lost many systems and indications, and elected to make a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right generator failure before top of descent, leading to multiple system losses including autopilot, flight directors, and cabin temperature control after attempting APU integration. Despite these failures and new cabin crew, the crew managed manual flight and landed safely with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported receiving an GPWS Terrain Warning while on approach.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway XX, direct sunlight impaired the crew's vision while turning inbound, triggering "terrain, terrain" warnings despite clear terrain. The crew executed a go-around and subsequently landed uneventfully after being vectored for a second approach.

synopsis: GA Flight Instructor reported a NMAC occurred while climbing out after takeoff.
summary: Flight crew and Aircraft Y experienced a near mid-air conflict during the approach phase at ZZZ after Tower cleared both for intersecting turns. The pilot executed an aggressive climb and turn to avoid a head-on collision, attributing the event to conflicting ATC clearances, strong winds, and pilot complacency.

synopsis: Flight Attendant crew reported a Self Balancing (Hover Board) device in the overhead during boarding. The device is not permitted per company policy and the passenger chose to deplane with the device.
summary: During boarding of Aircraft X, a Flight Attendant discovered a prohibited hoverboard after a Gate Agent incorrectly permitted it onboard. The passenger deplaned with the device, causing a delay, while the reporter cited conflicting policies and a lack of specific guidance in the Flight Operations Manual as the cause.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported a fumes event during preflight while using ground AC. Passengers and flight crew deplaned.
summary: Crew members at ZZZZ reported sulfur-like haze and fumes while using ground AC, causing throat irritation and headaches. The reporter attributed the issue to potentially dirty ground units and emphasized the safety need for a working APU in hot locations.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported the B767 aircraft returned to departure airport following Main Landing Gear Disagree and Door Disagree amber lights illuminated after takeoff.
summary: Aircraft X experienced Gear and Door Disagree lights during departure from ZZZ, prompting an air return. Post-landing inspection revealed the #2 Main Landing Gear brake rod was detached, requiring replacement at ZZZ1.

synopsis: Lead Technician reported disagreement and concerns while preparing a damaged aircraft for a maintenance ferry flight that was ultimately cancelled, then rescheduled after additional work.
summary: A maintenance crew chief and mechanics at ZZZ refused a manager's order to run a damaged engine on Aircraft X, but the chief performed the test anyway, revealing high vibrations and abnormal noises. The flight crew subsequently rejected the aircraft for a ferry flight, leading to the maintenance team's removal and alleged retaliation by management.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Crew Chief reported finding an unknown liquid puddle during unloading cargo compartment. Ramp Manager arrived and cleaned up the liquid without following environmental cleanup protocol.
summary: The Crew Chief and ground staff discovered an unknown liquid spill in the F2 cargo compartment of aircraft X after unloading at Gate ZZZ. Maintenance identified the substance as likely wood varnish, while a Ramp CSM improperly attempted to clean it without protective equipment or testing tools, delaying the aircraft's departure.

synopsis: Lead Technician reported required maintenance logbook and electronic entries were not completed prior to the aircraft operating in revenue service.
summary: Maintenance Control contacted the ZZZ Supervisor regarding missing documentation for an APU fuel line deferral authorized by Engineering Authorization 332551. The supervisor assured that the required monitor would be generated once manpower became available, as no work or deferral records currently exist in the system.

synopsis: BE-36 pilot reported fuel system anomaly in flight. They discovered that the fuel selector was not fully in the detent and after repositioning it, the engine ran normally.
summary: During cruise at 6,000 feet MSL, the pilot experienced erratic engine operation and fluctuating fuel flow, suspecting a failing fuel control. The issue resolved after the pilot moved the fuel selector firmly into the detent, allowing for a normal landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported an NMAC while maneuvering in the traffic pattern of a non-towered airport.
summary: During a training climb after takeoff, the pilot and student lost visual contact with a teardrop entry aircraft due to sun glare and cockpit workload. The intruder was discovered 200 feet below via iPad and radio, prompting them to break right and avoid a collision.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported taking evasive action to miss a medium sized helium balloon while on visual approach.
summary: During a manual visual approach at 1,200 ft, the Captain and First Officer avoided a 15-ft helium balloon by banking left. The balloon passed 65 ft from the cockpit and 20 ft under the right wing, with no collision damage observed after landing.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported engine roughness while IFR with malfunctioning transponder, resulted in a divert to a VFR airport.
summary: A pilot with a student experienced engine roughness and a transponder altitude error while being vectored in IMC during an ILS approach to ZZZ. The crew diverted to ZZZ2 and landed with 30 minutes of fuel after the originally offered alternate was no longer VFR.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported a fumes event during initial descent. Flight Attendant experienced multiple physiological symptoms which progressively intensified, resulting in incapacitation. Upon gate arrival paramedics provided treatment and transported Flight Attendant to a local hospital.
summary: A Lead Flight Attendant experienced severe symptoms during cabin service on a flight due to a toxic fume event, resulting in loss of motor control and Supraventricular Tachycardia. The aircraft landed with the crew member on the floor, where paramedics treated her for elevated carbon monoxide levels and acute hyperventilation syndrome before hospital release.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a #2 Engine spool down and subsequent failure at cruise. A fuel imbalance followed and the flight crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a #2 engine failure at 37,000 feet during climb, indicated by throttle split and command sector activation. After unsuccessful restart attempts, they diverted to ZZZ and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported ground crew's failure to properly communicate, resulted in the aircraft moving after tug disconnect.
summary: During pushback, the tug driver failed to instruct the flight crew to set brakes after disconnecting the aircraft. The Captain noticed movement, immediately applied brakes, and prevented an incident; no injuries occurred and the flight proceeded normally.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported gate pushback without the required Final Dangerous Goods Summary. Final DG Summary was received shortly thereafter.
summary: The flight crew pushed back without the Final Dangerous Goods summary, mistakenly believing it was not required for international departures. The error was discovered six minutes after pushback when the message arrived, prompting the First Officer to correct the Captain's misunderstanding.

synopsis: C-208B Captain reported engine surges resulted in diversion to VFR airport.
summary: The pilot experienced uncontrolled engine power surges during cruise while en route to ZZZ1, causing torque to fluctuate between 900 and 1800 foot-pounds. Unable to manage the power, the pilot diverted to ZZZ2 in VFR conditions and landed safely at 120 kts with 10 degrees of flaps, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported poor radar equipment failed to indicate the severity of weather resulted in wind shear encounter and temporary loss of vertical control.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X encountered a fast-moving rain front and upward wind shear during a visual approach go-around at ZZZ, causing a rapid climb and flap overspeed. The crew regained control, returned to the missed approach altitude, and landed safely after ATC vectored them for an ILS approach.

synopsis: Captain reported a fumes event during pushback resulting in the aircraft being pulled back to the gate for Maintenance investigation.
summary: During pushback, the crew received a Main Cargo Fire warning with no cockpit smell, prompting a return to the gate where maintenance found odorless fog in the cargo deck. Crash Fire Rescue investigated, and the crew speculated de-ice fluid entered the cargo area, though the exact cause remains unknown.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported pilot flying being behind the aircraft, failed to communicate this to pilot monitoring resulted in altitude overshoot with low altitude alert.
summary: The crew experienced task saturation and descended below the 4,600-foot restriction at ZZZZZ1 while using FPA to intercept the ILS XX glidepath after confusing ATC holding instructions. The First Officer disconnected the autopilot to recover the profile, resulting in a stabilized approach and landing despite the terrain alert.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported executing a go-around after encountering wake turbulence on approach to EWR in trail of a B737.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence at 3,000 ft behind a B737 on approach to EWR, causing violent banking and autopilot disengagement. The Pilot in Command broke off the approach due to persistent turbulence, later noting the supervisor suggested declaring an emergency despite the immediate focus on aviating.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported there was a slight perceived bleed through using the PAPI of white on the red light and red on the white lights, meaning the colors washed together.
summary: A pilot conducting a night ILS Z approach to Runway 6 at ILM reported that the PAPI displayed high while on the glide slope due to a suspected angle error and light bleed-through. The reporter warned this discrepancy could cause aircraft to descend below the glide slope near the threshold and requested FAA intervention to fix or disable the PAPI.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Twin Turboprop Cargo Pilot reported a Critical Ground Conflict after landing.
summary: Aircraft X and a following Airbus experienced a runway incursion risk at ZZZ during night landing due to ATC's poor spacing and rapidly changing exit instructions. Aircraft X missed exits in low light, forcing a late go-around instruction that the Airbus pilot declined as unsafe, resulting in a delayed runway clearance.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported a fume event, illness, and having to return to the gate.
summary: During taxi at ZZZ airport, Flight Attendant 2 and other crew members experienced a loud noise and strong odor causing incapacitation symptoms. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of specific procedures for fume events during taxi, which delayed medical assistance and forced the crew to improvise safety measures.

synopsis: Technician reported concerns with maintenance personnel not recording their work on Low Weather Minimums Program (LMP) components and experience level for tasks at their station.
summary: Maintenance personnel at ZZZ reset LMP essential components on Aircraft X and Y without recording Maintenance Item Control numbers or starting the required 15-day window. The reporter attributes this to unclear GPM guidance, lack of technician awareness, and insufficient avionics staffing.

synopsis: Technicians reported communications difficulties and failure to adhere to AMM procedures caused aircraft damage during down jacking after hangar maintenance.
summary: The Crew Chief reported that while Aircraft X was being lowered from jacks in the hangar, the tail stand descended slower than the main jacks, causing the aft stabilizer to contact the stand. This resulted in wavy skin damage, which the crew attributed to the tail stand being improperly positioned under the aircraft during the lowering operation.

synopsis: Check Airman reported miscommunication with MIA TRACON issuing clearances as incomplete, unclear, and non standard which resulted in an NMAC.
summary: During a Part 135 IFR flight check at FXE, a PIC and examiner misinterpreted Miami Approach's "turn left to 270" instruction as a minor heading change rather than a 360-degree orbit. This communication breakdown caused a near collision with a descending jet, which the reporter attributes to the controller's failure to use standard phraseology.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported taking evasive action from traffic ATC failed to report which resulted in NMAC at DWH airport.
summary: A pilot and student in a training aircraft experienced a near miss at DWH while on the downwind leg for Runway 17R. The pilot executed an aggressive avoidance maneuver after another aircraft approached within 200 feet, leading to the flight's termination due to student stress.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported engine roughness during departure. The pilot decided to troubleshot and continue to the original destination. The issue got progressively worse, but the pilot was able to safely land at destination.
summary: The pilot of a Laser experienced rough running and a cool cylinder #4 shortly after climbout from ZZZ to ZZZ1, suspecting a partial combustion issue. After receiving priority landing from ZZZ2 Approach and ZZZ1 Tower, post-flight inspection revealed a speck in injector #6, leading to the assumption that a partially clogged #4 injector caused the anomaly.

synopsis: Piper 22 pilot reported a runway excursion that resulted in aircraft damage after he let his feet off the rudder pedals and the instructor pilot could not correct the aircraft's path.
summary: A pilot and CFI conducting tailwheel training on a dirt runway at ZZZ experienced a ground loop due to bumpy conditions and ineffective rudder control. The aircraft swung 180 degrees and tipped on its left wing, damaging the wingtip, elevator, and tail wheel, with no injuries reported.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot reported that during a touch and go training evolution, when flaps up was verbalized, the student raised the landing gear selector lever and the aircraft settled on the runway.
summary: During a touch-and-go landing in a complex multi-engine aircraft, a student pilot prematurely raised the landing gear lever, causing the nose gear to collapse on the runway. The incident resulted from the student's lack of experience and confusion regarding control responsibilities, though all occupants evacuated safely with no injuries.

synopsis: BE-35 pilot reported an engine failure resulting in a glide landing at intended airport.
summary: A pilot operating a single-engine aircraft VFR at 9,500 feet experienced an engine roughness and power loss due to stuck exhaust valves caused by varnish buildup. The pilot glided to a safe landing at the destination airport after the engine quit, with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: A ZAB Center Controller reported aircraft could not navigate safely and one violated Restricted Area airspace due to GPS Jamming. The reporter requested the Controller in Charge initiate a procedure to stop the jamming but they refused.
summary: A pilot reported that Aircraft X could not safely navigate an RNAV arrival into ZZZ due to GPS jamming at Whitesands, but the Controller in Charge refused to stop the jamming. The pilot also noted another controller allowed Aircraft Y to deviate into restricted airspace, attributing these safety issues to peer pressure and a lack of priority on stopping the jamming.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the ramp area at JAN airport is poorly lighted and it's difficult to find the taxi line without using the aircraft's bright taxi light. The Captain is concerned using the aircraft's light is not safe for the ramp personnel.
summary: The flight crew reported poor ramp lighting at Jackson after landing on Runway 34L and exiting via Taxiway A2. Inability to locate the taxi line without using taxi lights, which hindered ground crew, was identified as a safety concern requiring proper illumination.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported fuel imbalance due to possible fuel leak resulting in a diversion.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew detected a fuel imbalance and suspected leak, prompting a diversion to ZZZ1 after consulting Dispatch. Although emergency vehicles found no leakage upon landing, the aircraft taxied to the gate with vehicles following.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the PAPI was showing all white lights while flying the RNAV approach to PKMJ airport. Only at minimums did the PAPI show 2 white and 2 red. The Captain states the PAPI may not be correct.
summary: Pilots flying an RNAV approach to PKMJ reported the PAPI was incorrect, showing four white lights until 510 feet and only switching to two red/two white at 50 feet AGL. The reporter attributes this to an inaccurate PAPI indication during the approach to minimums.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported pushback from the gate without the required Final DG Summary. Final DG Summary was requested and received shortly thereafter.
summary: The pilot failed to verify the Final DG Summary before taxiing, a mistake corrected by the First Officer after an ACARS backlog caused by a jet bridge power failure. The crew requested and received the correct Final DG Summary prior to takeoff, resulting in no further issues.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the illegal transport of passenger's personal Oxygen bottle. Captain stated the cause of the Hazmat violation was due to an inconsistent Hazmat policy agreement with Regional airline partners.
summary: The Captain reported that Flight Attendants and ground agents allowed passengers to board Aircraft X with prohibited compressed oxygen cylinders due to conflicting airline policies and inadequate training. This discrepancy created a significant safety hazard, prompting the Captain to recommend unifying Hazmat procedures and investigating regulatory compliance.

synopsis: Flight crew reported a runway excursion due to incorrect weather reporting and FICON, field conditions, failed to indicate rapidly changing conditions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer landed an aircraft on Runway XX in gusty crosswinds and rain, but the aircraft slid off the left side due to suspected unreported ice contamination. Despite maximum braking and rudder inputs, the crew lost directional control, stopped partially off the runway, and subsequently taxied back onto the surface without damage.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported a rejected takeoff due to a stall fail caution message and popped APU CB resulting in a return to gate.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff at 10 knots due to a stall fail caution message. Maintenance grounded the aircraft after discovering a popped APU battery circuit breaker and yaw damp status message, resulting in a canceled flight.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ First Officer reported receiving and responding to EGPWS alert of noted obstacles risks resulted in distraction on visual approach.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway XX at 3,300 ft, the flight crew received an EGPWS terrain warning and executed a climb to 3,200 ft despite seeing no terrain on their displays. The pilots completed the landing and reported the engine cycle to Dispatch and Maintenance.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported incorrect O2 bottles installed on aircraft and also reported that it is a continuing problem.
summary: A flight attendant discovered four incorrect 66N oxygen bottles during preflight checks, which provided only low-flow oxygen instead of the required high-flow capability. Technicians replaced the equipment before departure, though the aircraft had previously operated multiple cycles with this non-compliant emergency gear.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a fume event which resulted in the reporter becoming ill.
summary: Flight attendants on a short ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight reported a harsh chemical smell resembling APU exhaust during departure and again at 8,000 feet. The crew moved to the rear cabin, but symptoms persisted, leading to an ER visit while the pilots reportedly turned off the APU.

synopsis: Aircraft Mechanic reported upon inspection, a widespread problem of AMM non-compliance to tape joints for fire suppression on several aircraft cargo compartments.
summary: A mechanic performing a transit check on Aircraft X found missing sealing tape on cargo compartment joints, violating the AMM fire suppression requirements. The reporter suspects this widespread compliance issue stems from incomplete work following heavier maintenance checks.

synopsis: GA pilot reported being on short final and an aircraft took off in front of the reporter's aircraft resulting in the landing pilot having to switch runways at F45 Airport.
summary: A pilot on final for a touch-and-go on Runway 14 executed a go-around after another aircraft departed from the holding point with minimal separation. The departing pilot ignored the final approach call and disregarded right-of-way rules, creating a runway incursion risk.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight instructor reported taking evasive action because of ATC's failure to separate BKV pattern traffic which resulted in NMAC.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around with a left side step on final approach to Runway 09 after discovering an aircraft on a low approach approximately 200 feet below. This action was taken despite Tower clearing the landing without traffic warnings and responding lackadaisically when queried about the conflict.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported an airborne conflict and a possible BEC airspace incursion during descent to AAO airport.
summary: The crew received a Resolution Advisory during descent into AAO due to unannounced traffic, forcing a climbing right turn that delayed their briefing. This near miss left the pilots unsettled, causing them to fly closer to complex airspace boundaries than preferred while avoiding a violation.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate pilot reported that while on approach to a Class C airport, they observed a UAS pass over the right wing of the aircraft. The aircraft landed safely.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 32R at OMA, a drone flew over the right wingtip while the crew was turning left base. The pilot reported the drone passed just above the aircraft after the copilot spotted it.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Approach Controller reported aircraft read back clearance correctly, yet turned to wrong heading resulting in entering a higher MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller directed Aircraft X at FL040 to a 350 heading for Runway XX, but the pilot turned to 035 and entered a 050 MVA despite three correction attempts. The pilot eventually exited the MVA after turning west and was deviated following landing.

synopsis: ZBW Controller reported frequency charting error on a third party chart, and also confusion with the Jeppesen charts for BTV airport.
summary: An air traffic controller handling Aircraft X near BTV observed the pilot contacting the wrong frequency (120.35 instead of 121.1) due to ambiguous third-party charts. The controller reported that chart clarification and explicit frequency instructions from clearance delivery and tower are needed to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported fuel issues and diverted to a close airport.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew suspected a fuel leak due to rapid fuel loss and an imbalance light, prompting a diversion to ZZZ1. After balancing fuel by shutting right pumps, the imbalance light reappeared on the left tank on final approach, leading the crew to conclude the aircraft had a fuel system issue.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported violations of two systems limitations when a Wing/Body Overheat Light illuminated in flight.
summary: The flight crew received a request from ZZZ Maintenance to assist with troubleshooting a left wing overheat issue, which would have violated system limitations regarding bleed air sources and APU usage. The reporter attributes this unsafe request to a lack of prudence among newly ordained 737 Captains.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a fume event during initial descent. Flight landed safely and crew provided a logbook entry resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a cockpit fume event during initial descent into ZZZ1 after a reroute to Flight Level 280. Following the odor recognition procedure, the smell dissipated, allowing a safe landing, but the aircraft was subsequently taken out of service.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported complete failure of MCP, flight directors, auto-throttles and auto-pilots requiring ATC vectors for RNAV approach.
summary: During descent on a radar vector to ZZZ, the crew experienced a complete MCP failure that disabled flight directors, autopilots, and auto throttles. After executing QRH procedures and requesting priority handling, they followed ATC vectors for an RNAV approach and landed without incident, though the fire department was dispatched.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported inadvertently failed to comply with the Dry Ice handling requirements while transporting Dry Ice. Flight continued to destination safely.
summary: The B767 crew operating with an MEL for an inoperative left pack auto mode may have misinterpreted the Dry Ice Supplemental QRH procedure, which required the selector in AUTO. The flight remained uneventful, but the next crew noted the potential conflict between the MEL and the QRH requirements.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While inspecting a VOR for data the PNF reported a loss of GPS signal. The pilot reported the aircraft was operating VFR but was relying on the GPS signals to avoid restricted airspace. ATC advised the pilot crew of the close penetration and the aircraft avoided the TFR.
summary: During a VOR MON data collection flight along the US/Mexican border, the crew lost GPS and ground reference due to high workload. ATC warned of an impending Boca Chica TFR penetration, prompting the crew to take immediate evasive action before resuming their inspection path.

synopsis: Flight Attendants reported smoke in the cabin after take off. Smoke dissipated. Captain reported that the ground crew did not disconnect the air start cart supply hose correctly.
summary: Flight attendants on Aircraft X reported smoke and a burn smell during the climb to cruise altitude. The Captain later attributed the haze to the APU and rampers disconnecting a hose on the ground.

synopsis: BE-35 pilot reported fuel problems, being VFR in IMC and ultimately diverting to the nearest airport.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine aircraft en route at 7,500 feet experienced an engine failure after switching to the right main tank due to a loose fuel cap that allowed fuel to vent. The pilot declared a mayday, received vectoring from ZZZ Approach, and executed a safe landing after the engine stopped completely upon rollout.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Gyro-copter pilot reported the nose of the aircraft began to move side to side becoming unsafe to fly resulting in an off-airport landing.
summary: A pilot flying a gyroplane at 800 feet MSL experienced increasing left-right nose oscillations that worsened despite reducing engine RPM. Unable to stabilize the aircraft for a safe return, the pilot executed a precautionary landing on the shoreline.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported an alternator failure and landed the aircraft in IMC weather.
summary: A pilot conducting a VFR pipeline patrol experienced a second alternator failure in two days and elected to continue the mission. Upon approaching the destination with low battery and 800-foot ceilings, the pilot made a no-flap landing after visually acquiring the airport.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported engine failure on takeoff resulted in a return to the airport and a runway excursion during landing.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure during initial climb at 500 AGL after takeoff from Runway XX, prompting a straight-ahead landing on Runway XY. The aircraft exited the runway into grass, but the engine restarted, allowing a safe taxi back with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an NMAC due communication issues with the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X landed at a non-towered airport while another aircraft was simultaneously on the runway, nearly causing a collision. The incident occurred because the pilot's ADS-B signal dropped and two-way communications failed after switching frequencies, preventing other pilots from hearing position reports.

synopsis: Small transport aircraft pilot with a trainee reported disorientation and confusion during taxi at SMO. The reporter stated the lighting and taxiway markings are poor in this area of the airport and they taxied onto an unmarked ramp at night.
summary: The pilot departed Santa Monica at night and inadvertently taxied off the unlit, narrow taxiway into an empty asphalt area while instructing a new right-seater. Ground control directed an immediate left turn to rejoin the taxiway; the pilot attributed the error to fatigue, unfamiliarity with the dark environment, and divided attention, noting no runway incursion occurred.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported ATC failure to separate traffic in pattern resulted in an NMAC on downwind entry to CMA.
summary: The pilot reported that while inbound for landing at CMA on Runway 26, Aircraft Y cut them off at the same altitude during right traffic entry. Tower issued a traffic call but failed to provide sequencing or respond to the pilot's clarification request until after the conflict resolved.

synopsis: PA-28 reported inadvertently flying into ORD Class B airspace due to newly installed autopilot.
summary: The pilot, while practicing takeoff and testing a new autopilot, inadvertently climbed to 4,100 feet MSL, penetrating ORD Bravo airspace starting at 4,000 feet. The pilot attributed the incursion to assuming the autopilot held the set altitude without verification and corrected by descending to 3,300 feet.

synopsis: UAS flight crew member reported GPS interference errors with several UAS during the flight and chose to land all of the UAS.
summary: The Remote Pilot in Command and Safety Pilot canceled a second flight of small unmanned aircraft due to GPS multipathing near a large building, which caused erratic positioning and increased collision risk during the first flight. Subsequent testing confirmed the building's reflections degraded GPS accuracy, prompting the operator to add GPS quality checks to future site surveys.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported distraction caused failure to monitor pilot flying starting early descent which resulted in ATC issuing low altitude alert.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring received a Tower low altitude alert while descending to 1,500 ft. AGL for a visual approach to Runway 10 at BWI. The Pilot Flying climbed to 2,000 ft. to intercept the glideslope, resulting in an uneventful landing despite the advisory.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported gate departure without required Dangerous Good Form. Captain notified Dispatch en route and received document airborne.
summary: The crew failed to notify Dispatch of the Dangerous Goods Form before pushback. They notified Dispatch and added the form to the Release after becoming airborne en route.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported there is no taxiway A depicted on airport diagram from Runway 12L at MMUN airport.
summary: Pilots reported that after exiting Runway 12L at A3 and turning right to join Taxiway Alpha, they found the taxiway missing from the MMUN 10-9 chart. The discrepancy occurred because the chart does not depict Taxiway Alpha south and parallel to Runway 12L.

synopsis: First Officer reported a loss of thrust on the right engine. The Flight Crew elected to perform an in flight shut down of the affected engine and diverted to make a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X experienced a right engine thrust loss during the enroute phase while maintaining 300 knots. Unable to find an applicable QRH procedure with no EICAS messages, they diverted to ZZZ2, performed an inflight engine shutdown, and landed safely using single-engine procedures.

synopsis: First Officer reported problems communicating with ground crew during a pushback.
summary: During pushback with a non-tow-bar tug, the aircraft rolled forward unexpectedly due to poor headset communication and misalignment with the taxi line. The First Officer spotted the tug backing away and alerted the Captain, who applied brakes to stop the aircraft before the steering bypass pin was removed.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported while in position and holding, the Left Engine failed and they returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The pilot reported a left engine failure and fuel valve EICAS while holding at the gate with the park brake set and idle power. The crew executed the checklist and returned to the gate, noting an existing MEL item but unsure if it caused the event.

synopsis: While taxiing for takeoff, Captain reported that another aircraft crew observed an engine fire on their aircraft. The crew of the taxiing aircraft shut down the engine, and after inspection, taxied back to the gate.
summary: During taxi, the crew secured the right engine after a fire report caused by oil pooling in the tailpipe igniting, known as "candle wicking." Although all engine indications were normal and ARFF found no visible damage, maintenance confirmed an oil seal issue, and the aircraft taxied to the gate with an escort.

synopsis: Captain reported a malfunctioning Remote Cabin Sensor already on MEL failed and caused erroneous cabin altitude readings. This caused the passenger O2 masks to deploy and required an immediate descent. The Crew continued to a destination airport.
summary: The crew experienced a momentary false cabin altitude warning and automatic oxygen mask deployment during cruise, likely caused by a deferred Remote Cabin Sensor. They descended to FL100 and continued to the destination with all passengers safe, recommending maintenance fix deferred MELs before ETOPS flights.

synopsis: Pilot reported poor to nil braking action after landing at an airport in mountainous terrain.
summary: A Captain and First Officer landed a heavy jet at a high-altitude airport with a contaminated runway, stopping with less than 200 feet remaining after experiencing poor braking action. The near-excursion was attributed to unreliable field condition reports, a long touchdown, variable winds, and the aircraft's weight on a short runway.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an autopilot problem and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew encountered an autopilot engagement failure and a "no autoland" alert while climbing out from ZZZ1, forcing a return to ZZZ. After dumping 70,000 pounds of fuel at FL280 to meet landing weight limits, they executed a non-eventful landing without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported Flight Crew reported smoke and fumes in cockpit after take off. Flight Crew performed an air turn back.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZZ due to smoke and fumes in the cockpit. The reporter attributed the incident to a maintenance problem.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported draining a small amount of fuel from the tank, to check for contamination, only to find the sump valve was stuck open. Maintenance was contacted but the leak could not be stopped and the flight was canceled. The Captain stated this is a common occurrence with this Pilatus aircraft.
summary: During pre-flight fuel sumping on a Pilatus, the left wing outer sump valve leaked after being opened, despite attempts to reseat it. A mechanic confirmed the valve required replacement and tank draining, causing flight delays, fuel loss, and concerns that the recurring issue discourages mandatory contamination checks.

synopsis: Pilot reported a terrain warning occurred during descent and stated complacency could have contributed to the event.
summary: The Captain received a terrain warning between ZZZ and ZZZ1 during descent due to an aggressive 270+ knot closure rate caused by delayed field elevation entry and reduced automation monitoring. The pilot disengaged the autopilot to hand-fly a visual approach, attributing the event to complacency from good weather.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a fuel imbalance developed while at cruise. After the imbalance worsened, the flight crew performed an in flight engine shut down and continued to the destination airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a fuel imbalance enroute at FL380 due to a failed cross-feed valve lacking power, which they misinterpreted as an engine leak. They secured the right engine and landed safely on one engine, noting that the checklist should explicitly require checking the circuit breaker to identify such valve failures.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew reported what they thought was a cracked window. They returned to the departure airport and had aircraft checked by maintenance to reveal it was a scratch within tolerance.
summary: The First Officer reported a suspected windscreen crack during climb after departing ZZZ, prompting a return to the airport. Maintenance later determined the mark was a pre-existing scratch within limits, obscured by rain and clouds, causing an unnecessary diversion.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight attendant reported battery powered vaping device caught fire during boarding. Flight Attendant extinguished fire with Halon extinguisher, passengers deplaned.
summary: A passenger's vaping device battery caught fire, prompting Flight Attendant #2 to extinguish it with a Halon extinguisher. The Captain was notified, and all passengers were deplaned to the boarding area.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported a low altitude alert on final, a wind shear, and then a second low altitude alert and safely landed the aircraft.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected wind shear twice during an ILS 19C approach at IAD, triggering two low altitude alerts. After correcting to the glide slope and breaking out of IMC, the pilot landed but noted that executing a missed approach initially would have been safer.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Single Engine Pilot reported a NMAC and airspace violation while entering the pilot's intended destination airport traffic pattern.
summary: A pilot arriving at ZZZ via ZZZZZ Transition encountered traffic 300 feet below while squawking VFR in ZZZ2 Bravo airspace. The pilot climbed to 3200 feet to gain separation, eventually sighted the traffic, and landed uneventfully, though the transponder remained on VFR until after touchdown.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Single Engine Pilot reported the engine cowling was torn off the aircraft while in descent.
summary: During descent through 3000 ft MSL at 140 KIAS, an engine cowling tore off, damaging the temperature probe and windshield. The pilot executed a priority landing at Runway XX, ZZZ, with no injuries reported as the cowling fell into a reservoir.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Single Engine low wing pilot reported a NMAC while in the traffic pattern at a non-tower airport.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X reported a near mid-air collision with Aircraft Z during the traffic pattern at S43 while landing on Runway 33R. Aircraft Z turned base without visual contact, passing within 300 feet vertically before executing a 360-degree evasive maneuver.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Student Pilot reported a runway excursion at LNK airport upon landing due to winds.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft at LNK Runway 35 in gusty crosswinds. A sudden wind gust caused the right wing to dip, resulting in an off-runway touchdown in the grass before the aircraft stopped on Runway 32 with no damage.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported having an aircraft below the MVA while on vectors to landing airport.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X to 3,000 feet during the approach to ZZZ airport, mistakenly believing it had passed the 3,200-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude (MVA). After a Data Controller alerted the error, the aircraft was immediately climbed to 3,200 feet because the controller failed to verify the updated MVA map.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a 30 degree bank angle while turning final to PHX airport and also received a GPWS alarm.
summary: The pilot reported that while intercepting Runway 08 final at PHX, a steep turn to correct an overshoot triggered a Bank Angle GPWS warning and caused a 150–200 ft altitude loss. The approach was subsequently corrected without traffic conflict or TCAS alerts.

synopsis: Air Carrier Maintenance Stores personnel reported receiving undeclared ground shipment. The shipment was in violation of company Hazmat recovery procedures.
summary: The AOG desk arranged for undeclared HAZMAT aircraft parts to be driven from ZZZ1 and ZZZ2 to ZZZ stores in two separate incidents. The Hazmat Recovery team was required to retrieve these items and re-ship them with proper documentation.

synopsis: Ground Personal reported the aircraft parked in this ramp location are parked too close together. The agent states there is no stop mark on the ground for the larger sized aircraft.
summary: A ramp supervisor reported that parking Aircraft X at EWR gate CXXX lacks specific stop marks, creating a safety concern because its 9-foot wider wingspan may exceed the painted clearance zone designed for Aircraft Y. Although several Aircraft X flights parked without incident, the supervisor noted the issue is widely known but uncorrected.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported the nose steering locked up during taxi out resulting in having to be towed back to the gate for maintenance action.
summary: The pilot reported a STEER INOP message and nose wheel misalignment while taxiing Aircraft X for departure, causing a runway shutdown and requiring a tow. No physical abnormalities were found during inspection, though a similar transient event occurred previously in the same aircraft at 5 degrees Celsius.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a Ramp check upon arrival at destination which recovered a Hazmat documentation error. A discrepancy report was submitted by the Inspection Team.
summary: Civil Aviation Authority inspectors conducted a ramp inspection on Aircraft X at ZZZZ1, discovering a discrepancy between cargo lithium battery paperwork and the manifest stating "NO DG ON BOARD." The inspectors documented the dangerous goods paperwork error and departed the aircraft at 08:54.

synopsis: MD11 Captain reported APU fire alert warning resulted in a divert.
summary: The flight crew experienced a false APU fire warning at FL350, prompting an expedited descent and evacuation preparation at ZZZ1. Post-flight inspection revealed the APU door was fully open, confirming an equipment malfunction in the fire detection system.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported ground proximity obstacle alert due to ATC improper clearance phraseology resulted in evasive action to avoid a radio tower near CGI airport.
summary: During descent, a task-saturated controller issued non-standard instructions and cleared the crew to 3,000 feet, triggering an obstacle warning near a 2,487-foot tower. The crew diverted to a GPS approach and landed safely, attributing the incident to improper ATC communication, crew distraction from a last-minute runway change, and inadequate obstacle briefing.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported receiving a GPWS during approach descent.
