summary: The pilot reported that after holding at 3,000 ft and receiving clearance for approach, the aircraft descended to 2,100 ft to intercept the glide slope. The Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) activated immediately upon initiating this descent.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported an unstabilized approach and an obstacle alarm on the go-around.
summary: The Captain and First Officer flew Aircraft X on an LDA-Z approach to Runway XX in low ceilings. The Captain took control and executed a go-around after the First Officer failed to stabilize the approach, triggering a ground proximity warning.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported a flight attendant bumped her head during a wake turbulence encounter from the preceding A319.
summary: The flight crew encountered unexpected wake turbulence while following an A319 in trail without prior ATC notification. A flight attendant struck her head against the fuselage but was cleared to continue duties, prompting a recommendation for increased spacing.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Technicians reported disagreement with a Supervisor over damage limits on an aircraft drain mast and felt pressure to sign it off as airworthy instead of replacing it.
summary: A ramp supervisor pressured the reporter and a coworker to defer a damaged drain mast on Aircraft X, despite Maintenance Control stating the aircraft was out of service due to no available deferral limits. The supervisor insisted on signing off the damage, contradicting company procedures and maintenance authority.

synopsis: PA-28 flight instructor reported a stuck throttle due to a carburetor failure resulted in an immediate landing.
summary: A pilot and student experienced a stuck throttle during a training flight in a CFI applicant aircraft due to a carburetor failure where a dislodged fuel needle blocked the butterfly valve. The crew landed safely at ZZZ by pulling the mixture over the runway after receiving radar vectors from Approach.

synopsis: Cessna 340 pilot reported the landing gear collapsed on landing.
summary: A pilot reported that during the rollout after a smooth landing, the right main gear collapsed despite three green lights and Tower confirmation indicating the gear was down and locked. No airport property damage or fluid spills occurred.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported that during on takeoff another aircraft landed on crossing runway resulted in a ground conflict. Instructor determined their radio had failed.
summary: A pilot conducting commercial training at a non-towered field observed a landing aircraft while airborne at 500 ft AGL but heard no transmissions. The pilot discovered their primary radio was inoperative after switching to a second radio to hear the other aircraft's calls.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported an NMAC during takeoff requiring evasive action.
summary: The pilot departed a Class Delta airport with radar out of service, following a twin Piper cleared on the same runway heading. After the Piper deviated and turned toward the pilot at the same altitude, the pilot descended and turned away to avoid a conflict, triggering multiple collision avoidance warnings.

synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported they descended below assigned altitude resulting in ATC issuing a low altitude alert. Captain stated distraction was a contributing factor.
summary: During an RNAV approach to Runway 16, the Pilot Flying descended rapidly through the assigned 2100 feet while the Pilot Monitoring was head down for the final checklist. The crew corrected the descent at 1280 feet after ATC alerted them of the low altitude and continued the approach manually.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported they thought another pilot or the FBO had filled the aircraft with fuel. Engine quit due to fuel starvation.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced an engine failure at 3,500 feet during a missed approach in Aircraft X due to empty fuel tanks. The instructor, who failed to verify fuel quantity despite resetting the totalizer, executed a priority landing at ZZZ after the engine could not be restarted.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported a wake turbulence encounter descending into IAH resulted in a slight track deviation.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence while descending on the DRLLR 5 arrival into IAH, causing an unexpected 20-degree right roll and a one-mile deviation. The pilot attributed the event to poorly timed turbulence rather than severity, reported no injuries, and clarified that no preceding aircraft was observed.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported encountering jet blast during takeoff roll which resulted in momentary loss of yaw control.
summary: During takeoff roll on Runway XXL at ZZZ, an IOE First Officer encountered strong jet blast from a B777 on adjacent Runway XYR, causing a left yaw just above 100 knots. The pilot applied full right rudder to correct the deviation before V1, and the remainder of the takeoff and climb was uneventful.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported that during departure they observed higher obstacle indications requiring expeditious climb counter to NADP2 procedure.
summary: The pilot reported a non-tower IFR departure from Runway 11 where Seattle Center delayed clearance due to frequency congestion. At 1,000 feet AGL, terrain warnings prompted a hold at 200 knots until clearing 6,000 feet MSL, after which the climb resumed normally.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported inaccurate FICON resulted in poor to nil braking action during landing roll.
summary: The crew landed at JAC on a contaminated runway with variable crosswinds, experiencing a slight balloon that resulted in a late touchdown. Despite maximum braking, poor deceleration occurred due to an icy surface, causing the aircraft to stop with minimal runway remaining and prompting a PIREP of poor braking action.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported both Engine Driven Hydraulic Pumps failed on takeoff, and elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced two green system hydraulic pump failures during takeoff from ZZZ Runway XX, resulting in a complete loss of green system pressure before gear retraction. They recovered pressure using electric pumps, followed QRH procedures, and returned to land at ZZZ without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a new Flight Crew reported smoke in the cockpit on initial climb. Flight crew performed an air turn back to make a precautionary landing. This was a repeat discrepancy.
summary: The crew experienced smoke in the cockpit at 3,000 ft. on a flight previously delayed for the same issue. They requested priority handling to return to ZZZZ, and the aircraft landed safely without fuel dumping.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported tug failed to yield while taxiing, resulted in hard braking to avoid collision at ORD airport.
summary: While taxiing outbound on Taxiway A, the pilot braked hard to avoid a tug that failed to yield at a stop sign. The aircraft stopped 10 feet from the crossing, and the pilot attributed the incident to reckless vehicle operation and recommended camera enforcement.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported an air turn back after anti-ice systems failed after takeoff. After trouble shooting restored system operation, Captain reported Dispatch pressured him into continuing to destination airport with additional maintenance work.
summary: The Captain of a ZZZZ-ZZZZ flight experienced a wing anti-ice failure during takeoff in icing conditions, prompting an immediate return to ZZZZ. Although the Quick Reference Handbook procedure restored system function, Dispatch and Maintenance later pressured the Captain to continue the flight despite the critical nature of the failure.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported after maintenance action, parking brake failed after gate pushback, resulted in collision with tug.
summary: The flight crew experienced a parking brake failure during pushback at ZZZ, causing the aircraft to roll forward and strike the tug despite the brake being set. The reporter attributes the incident to insufficient accumulator pressure following maintenance lubrication, which left no cockpit indication of the low pressure.

synopsis: Technicians reported being dispatched on a road trip to replace the HMU and other components on a B737-800, they discovered a popped circuit breaker and reset the fire handle, correcting the malfunction.
summary: Aircraft X experienced a #2 engine inflight shutdown at ZZZ1, prompting maintenance to replace the HMU and fuel pump. Pre-flight checks revealed the engine would not light off due to a popped Spar Valve circuit breaker, which the flight crew omitted from their write-up despite cycling the fire handle.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported overlooking the position of the carburetor heat control, allowing the engine to fail on approach to landing due to fuel starvation.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced an engine stoppage during the ground roll of a VFR landing in a C172 due to suspected carburetor icing. The reporter attributes the failure to forgetting to apply carburetor heat during the approach in cold, moist conditions, though the engine was restarted on a parallel runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA student pilot reported observing a twin piston aircraft converging resulted in taking evasive action.
summary: A pilot descending from 7,500 feet en route to SRB took evasive action when a twin-piston aircraft suddenly turned left to intercept their course. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the other pilot's failure to check ADS-B or conduct a visual scan, suspecting the maneuver may have been intentional.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported the aircraft continued to turn off center line while taxiing to the active runway.
summary: The PIC of Aircraft X with two souls on board experienced a left steering failure while turning onto Taxiway 1A for Runway XX. The pilot stopped the engine, manually steered the aircraft, and requested a mechanic to tow it back to the flight center with no damage reported.

synopsis: C172 student pilot reported a low voltage annunciation while performing engine run-up with an acrid odor present and along with the flight instructor. They elected to shut down the aircraft and evacuate to investigate further.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced a low voltage warning and acrid smoke during a pre-flight run-up on the ramp. They executed an electrical fire checklist, evacuated, and manually towed the aircraft to maintenance for investigation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft that was in icing conditions and having to descend the aircraft below the MIA.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X through severe icing and turbulence near ZZZ1 airport when the pilot could not maintain altitude or heading. The controller descended the aircraft below the Minimum IFR Altitude to 110 to clear the icing, regaining control, but was subsequently reprimanded for the deviation despite the emergency outcome.

synopsis: Developmental Center Controller reported an aircraft came to them at the wrong altitude head on with another aircraft.
summary: A southbound flight coordinated at FL350 crossed the boundary at FL360 and encountered head-on traffic. The report describes this altitude discrepancy and conflict but does not specify the cause or outcome.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported an altitude shown on the JAC airport ALPIN3 SID chart, at the way-point KICNE, does not correspond to that given by the local ATC Tower.
summary: The pilot reported an incorrect ALPIN3 chart restriction at KICNE requiring a 15,000-foot crossing, which the JAC ATC Tower clarified should be at or above 15,000 feet. The FMC database contained no such restriction, and the controller noted they had already filed reports on this chart error.

synopsis: A330 flight crew reported a loss of thrust on the number two engine and elected to return to the departure airport and make an overweight landing.
summary: The crew experienced a Number 2 engine thrust rollback during takeoff of a 501,000 lb aircraft, leading to a pilot deviation on the SID. They continued to ZZZ, followed QRH procedures for an engine failure, and executed a precautionary overweight landing without incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported there are two possible boundary lines for the pad area at ORD airport and the chart does not specify which one to use.
summary: Pilots holding in PAD A after landing were confused by unclear boundary lines in the manual, leading them to stop too close to the taxiway. This resulted in an uncomfortably close wingtip clearance when another aircraft taxied past, highlighting the need for clearer hold pad markings.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported landing safely after experiencing landing gear status light anomalies.
summary: The crew executed two go-arounds due to an unstable approach and a failed nose gear down light indication caused by burnt bulbs. With fuel becoming critical, they performed a low pass for visual confirmation, received priority handling, and landed safely on the third attempt before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported hearing non-aviation information on a ZMA 126.52 frequency interfering with regular communications.
summary: A pilot reported severe radio interference on 126.52 MHz with Miami Center shortly after check-in, caused by a broadcast regarding COVID-19 vaccines. The signal peaked 30 NM east of TPA on Q118, hindering communications until the aircraft transferred to JAX Center.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported Engine 1 Oil Filter Bypass light illuminated after takeoff and elected to perform an inflight shutdown of the affected engine as well as an air turnback and precautionary landing at departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced an Engine 1 Oil Filter Bypass light immediately after takeoff. Following QRH procedures, they shut down the left engine, requested priority handling, and returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing with no further issues.

synopsis: Pilots reported losing control of the aircraft while trying to park the aircraft. Aircraft slid into gate resulting in no damage.
summary: During automatic parking into gate X on an icy, uphill ramp, the aircraft veered left after adding power to engine #2 and struck a B757 stair stand. The pilot attributed the incident to the steep gradient and ice, resulting in no damage after the aircraft was towed to the gate.

synopsis: C500 flight crew reported an engine roll-back at cruise. The flight crew restarted the engine, left it at idle due to oil pressure indicating high and performed an air turnback to landing.
summary: The crew experienced an Engine #2 shutdown at FL410, successfully restarted it, but aborted thrust due to excessive oil pressure and temperature. They diverted to ZZZ, landed single-engine with Engine #2 at idle, and found residual oil on the cowling post-landing.

synopsis: Pilot reported receiving a terrain warning inbound to SFO. Other pilots reported the same issue to reporter.
summary: The First Officer flying an RNAV GPS 10L approach at SFO received a Terrain warning near the FAF at 1,800 ft due to rapid terrain change and high closure rate on the VNAV profile. The crew did not execute a go-around as the warning ceased before they could react, though they noted standard ATC speeds may have prevented the alert.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 First Officer reported a Baggage Smoke annunciation on taxi for takeoff and the Captain elected to stop aircraft operations to have both the passengers and crew safely evacuate the aircraft.
summary: The pilot in command and first officer evacuated two passengers on Taxiway XX at ZZZ after a baggage smoke warning illuminated during taxi. They shut down the aircraft, informed Ground Control, and completed an organized evacuation without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a GPWS while inbound to AVP airport.
summary: The flight crew descended below 3,000 feet during a visual approach to Runway 22 at AVP, triggering a GPWS warning due to premature descent following a forward lavatory smoke incident. Task saturation from the smoke event caused the crew to descend too early, necessitating an escape maneuver and a subsequent ILS approach.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ground crew failed to maintain a safe zone in poorly marked, dimly lit gate, resulted in stopping aircraft.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft while parking at a poorly lit hard stand after two vehicles failed to yield and crossed the safety zone despite wing walkers signaling it was safe. The reporter attributed the incident to non-compliant vehicle traffic, ramp crew failing to establish a safe zone, and inadequate ground markings in wet conditions.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported descent below published safe altitudes, resulting in terrain conflict alert.
summary: The crew flew too low on final approach due to misinterpreting charted altitudes and distance, triggering a terrain warning. They corrected by leveling off at the preselected altitude, noting that visual clearance was maintained throughout the VMC conditions.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported FO steep approach angle initiated a terrain alert due to older technology limitations.
summary: During a visual descent into TYS, the First Officer's excessive descent rate caused the aircraft to briefly trigger a "Terrain, Terrain" caution while leveling off. The pilot attributed the event to the aircraft's outdated technology and the steep descent profile.

synopsis: Maintenance technicians reported fuel sprayed into technicians' eyes from a partially installed fuel quantity switch. Investigation revealed a third technician previously reinstalled the switch without replacing a faulty O ring that was not in stock and did not record the maintenance action correctly.
summary: Technicians Name and Name1 suffered fuel spray to their eyes while replacing an E2 fuel low pressure switch on Aircraft X due to a previously undocumented temporary reinstallation by Mechanic Name3 without pulling circuit breakers or securing the system.

synopsis: Technicians reported that during troubleshooting an aircraft for erroneous fire warning indications, the supervisor on duty directed them to not document the swapping of components used so as to not have to comply with a landing gear operational check that was required and would require an RII action.
summary: Mechanics troubleshooting a landing gear overheat caution on Aircraft X swapped a control panel with Aircraft Y per supervisor instruction but failed to document the work or perform required operational checks. The error was caught by Quality Control before flight, prompting the team to correct the paperwork and complete the necessary inspections.

synopsis: DA-40 Flight Instructor reported NMAC with helicopter descending in conflict resulted in taking evasive action.
summary: A pilot and student performing ground reference maneuvers near ZZZ airport encountered a descending helicopter that cut their approach path, forcing an abrupt climb. The helicopter subsequently cut off another aircraft on final for Runway X, which the reporter attributes to the helicopter pilot's failure to scan for traffic or monitor radio calls.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Single engine small aircraft pilot reported a trim and auto pilot malfunction.
summary: The pilot departed ZZZ in an aircraft with no manual trim wheel and found the nose pitched down due to low nose-down trim settings. After failing to reset the trim via switches or breakers, the pilot hand-flew the aircraft to a safe landing at ZZZ1 while experiencing near-exhaustion from constant sidestick pressure.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported a flap failure on approach to an airport with a contaminated runway caused them to divert to another airport with more favorable runway conditions.
summary: The crew encountered a flap failure during an approach to ZZZ in deteriorating weather, prompting a missed approach and diversion to ZZZ1. They landed using slats only on a visual approach, and subsequent maintenance checks confirmed the flap system remained inoperative despite reset attempts.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported seeing a UAS close by at 2,500 feet. The pilot climbed to avoid the UAS and flew into Class B airspace without clearance.
summary: A pilot flying a general aviation aircraft westbound at 2,500 ft MSL near Houston Class B airspace inadvertently entered the airspace up to 3,300 ft MSL. The incursion occurred because the pilot was distracted by a potential drone or bird, causing them to climb early and fail to monitor their position.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported they flew off course while departing on a SID and received a Low Altitude warning and expedited climb instruction from ATC.
summary: The pilot departed ZZZ on an IFR flight and deviated east of the ZZZ 114 radial while climbing after an expedited climb instruction. The pilot attributed the deviation to distraction from the unusual clearance and a failure to monitor the navigation receiver, resulting in a low altitude alert.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a baggage cart drove under the nose of the aircraft while being marshaled in, resulted in immediate braking.
summary: During gate arrival, a baggage truck and cart drove within 10 feet of the aircraft nose, requiring the First Officer to stop the pilot to avoid a collision. The reporter attributed the incident to blatant unsafe ground equipment operation and criticized Airport OPS for failing to identify the driver.

synopsis: B737-800 pilot reported undetected windshear encounter, resulted in an ATC altitude alert and GPWS terrain caution alert.
summary: The crew experienced an altitude alert and GPWS terrain caution near the FAF during a VNAV approach, likely caused by undetected windshear. The pilot disconnected the autopilot to recover the glidepath, attributing the event to performance monitoring breakdowns driven by LNAV/VNAV design distractions.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported distraction prevented noticing Pilot Flying descended below path, resulted in ATC low altitude alert and GPWS terrain alert.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring on an RNAV RNP approach to BZN RWY 30 became distracted running a checklist, causing the aircraft to descend below the VPATH and trigger terrain warnings. The Captain disconnected the autopilot to climb, and the crew attributed the deviation to fatigue, turbulence, and unfamiliarity with the terrain.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported low oil pressure indications on the left engine during cruise. The flight crew elected to perform an inflight shut down of the affected engine and continue the descent and approach to original destination airport.
summary: During cruise at 23,000 feet, the crew experienced fluctuating left engine oil pressure warnings, leading to an inflight shutdown during descent into ZZZ due to abnormal low oil temperature. The crew executed a single-engine landing but admitted to forgetting the landing checklist due to task saturation, though gear and flaps were correctly set.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported landing in turbulent conditions resulting in a wing tip strike.
summary: The First Officer and Captain landed an aircraft at ZZZ at night in gusty crosswinds when the right wing dropped abruptly during the flare, causing a wingtip strike. The crew attributed the sudden roll to possible wind shear or mechanical turbulence, noting no stall or wind shear warnings were received.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported during an inflight shut down of an engine for low oil pressure indication, checklists were not followed, resulting in the thrust reversers not being armed for landing.
summary: Pilots experienced intermittent low oil pressure on the left engine during descent, leading to an engine shutdown per QRH. Task saturation from managing the emergency caused them to miss the landing checklist and forget to arm the thrust reversers, though the landing was completed safely.

synopsis: Challenger 300 First Officer reported a right engine driven hydraulic pump fail CAS message during climbout. The flight crew elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing at departure airport.
summary: During climb through 12,000 feet, the crew observed hydraulic pump failure and spoiler fault CAS messages. They leveled at 14,000 feet, ran checklists, burned fuel for 30 minutes, and returned to ZZZ for a landing on Runway XX.

synopsis: BE99 pilot reported electrical burning smell was determined after landing to be engine inlet electric boot had burnt.
summary: A pilot descending in IMC toward ZZZ reported an electrical burning smell that worsened after turning off window heat. Post-flight inspection revealed a burnt engine inlet electric boot on the right side, which the pilot believes vented fumes through the bleed air system into the cabin.

synopsis: Technician reported that the Kruger Flap Fairing and deflector were not installed on the thrust reverser translating sleeve and the blank off plugs were in place.
summary: Aircraft X arrived at ZZZ with the #2 engine inboard T-R sleeve missing both the Kruger flap fairing and deflector. The reporter states these parts were never installed and the plugs remained in place.

synopsis: Technician reported a clamp missing on the APU pneumatic duct pressure seal on a B737-900. The aircraft was removed from service due to the length of time required to install a new clamp.
summary: Aircraft X was taken out of service due to a missing APU keel duct pressure seal found upon arrival. This maintenance omission, which can cause pressurization leaks, has also affected several other aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: BD4 pilot reported on test flight aircraft engine failed to produce full power resulted in fly below published pattern altitude.
summary: The pilot conducted the first flight of an aircraft in Phase I testing, experiencing poor acceleration and low altitude due to the engine generating only 65-70% power at full throttle. The pilot safely landed after failing to abort early, attributing the issue to insufficient performance data awareness and an EFIS system lacking situational alarms.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported H25B failed to respond to radio communication while descending and flying erratic course, resulted in entering a higher MVA.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that Aircraft X descended to 600 ft below the 1,800 ft MVA during departure from ZZZ despite multiple climb instructions. The pilot failed to maintain altitude or course for 10 miles, likely due to communication difficulties caused by the pilot's accent, before eventually climbing to 2,000 ft.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported a loud noise while at the gate and during taxi, the noise continued along with an odor throughout the cabin. The crew returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew experienced an overwhelming noise and strong smell after switching packs to engine bleeds, forcing a return to the gate. The issue, caused by a maintenance fault, ceased only when avionics master switches were turned off, allowing the flight to resume after repairs.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an unknown noise and lack of power while starting the number two engine.
summary: During pushback, the flight deck crew and tug driver observed an unusual noise, N2 RPM decay, and sparks from engine #2 at 23% N2. The start was aborted before fuel introduction, and the aircraft was returned to the gate and taken out of service.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported ground personnel reported flames emanating from their number two engine during taxi out. After maintenance inspected the engine and fire personnel reported no fire the flight crew continued their taxi and flight.
summary: During taxi out, ZZZ Maintenance reported flames from Engine 2, suspected to be caused by pooled fuel from extended ramp time. The crew executed the tailpipe fire checklist, and after fire crews confirmed no active fire, the aircraft departed safely with normal engine indications.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported abnormally high engine oil temperature in number one engine. Flight immediately diverted prior to having to shut down the engine.
summary: The crew encountered a high engine oil temperature on Engine #1 at 35,000 ft, peaking at 176C despite reducing power to flight idle. They diverted to ZZZ and landed safely without shutting down the engine, following QRH procedures.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported gate departure without required Hazmat document folder. Flight crew did have a signed copy of the DG manifest but not the required company folder.
summary: A B757 crew departed ZZZ for ZZZ1 without the required DG paperwork due to a pilot oversight caused by rapidly changing weather. Additionally, the Captain misread takeoff minimums for the two-engine aircraft, potentially departing below limits, though the crew confirmed adequate visual references were present.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported communications failure with a company aircraft experiencing a bleed air system failure, resulting in the aircraft diverting.
summary: Maintenance Operations and the flight crew of XA42z managed an 'air sys 3 off' alert with Pack #2 already on MEL, leaving only one pack. Due to the loss of wing anti-ice and probable icing conditions, the crew returned to ZZZZ1 with alternate ZZZZ after failing to restore the system.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported flight crew had an engine oil temperature high indication and the flight crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
summary: The crew of a flight 35 miles southwest of ZZZ diverted after a high oil temperature warning on engine 1. They throttled back the engine without shutting it down, landed uneventfully, and maintenance will evaluate the issue.

synopsis: Beech 1900 Captain reported the smell of electrical smoke during the flight. After landing the smell returned and the Captain turned the aircraft over to maintenance.
summary: The pilot reported a distinct burned rubber smell during cruise and after landing, which intensified when the vent blower was on. Suspecting an electrical fault in the wiring, the pilot turned off the master switch, parked the aircraft, and advised the mechanic, who confirmed the odor.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported the aft cabin flight attendants noticed an oil smell during climb, cruise, and descent. The flight deck and forward flight attendants did not smell anything.
summary: During climb and descent, aft cabin flight attendants reported an oil smell that dissipated before landing, while flight crew and forward attendants detected nothing. The crew documented the event in the logbook and odor report form for the operating crew.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported, while at the gate, turning on the APU bleed valve. The aircraft began to fill with the dirty sock odor. Maintenance action was required.
summary: The pilot activated the APU bleed valve before boarding, triggering a widespread "dirty sock" odor reported by flight attendants. Following odor recognition procedures, the pilot deselected the APU bleed, and maintenance took the aircraft out of service after the odor persisted during troubleshooting.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported a loud noise while at the gate and was believed to be ground equipment. During taxi, the noise continued along with an odor throughout the cabin. An EICAS message appeared on the MFD, Vent Blower Fault" and the crew returned to the gate for maintenance."
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a loud buzzing noise and unusual odor during taxi after pushback, caused by a VENT BLOWER FAULT. The aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance, where the blower was MEL'd after the odor cleared.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC. Reporter thought the aircraft was further away from their aircraft but misunderstood.
summary: A pilot in the traffic pattern misheard another aircraft's distance report, believing it was six miles out when it was actually much closer. The pilot executed a low approach to avoid a conflict with the aircraft, which was 100 feet below and close behind on final.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an aircraft descended below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a 5,000 ft descent clearance to Aircraft X, which subsequently descended below that altitude toward a 5,000 ft MVA. The controller issued a low altitude alert and climb instruction after hearing an aural alarm, which the pilot complied with during unusual runway configurations.

synopsis: Captain reported an in flight shut down of the #1 Engine as a result of an oil filter bypass light illuminating. The flight Crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a #1 engine hydraulic pump failure followed by an oil filter bypass light on Aircraft X, necessitating an engine shutdown and diversion to ZZZ2. Post-landing inspection revealed significant hydraulic fluid leakage in the engine cowling, though the crew attributed the shutdown to the oil filter alert.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported airborne notification of undeclared Hazmat. Hazmat cargo loaded on aircraft without providing flight crew the required Hazmat documentation or flight crew notification.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X en route from ZZZ to ZZZ1 received an ACARS notification at cruise that a battery classified as HAZMAT was onboard. The crew reported they were unaware of the cargo and had not received any paperwork prior to departure.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported taxi instructions to exit at a specific intersection that is not depicted on the Jeppesen charts for MMUN airport.
summary: The flight crew landed at MMUN on Runway 12L and exited via A3, but turned left onto Taxiway Delta instead of the uncharted parallel Taxiway A as instructed by Ground. The crew attributed the deviation to the taxiway's omission on Jeppesen charts and confusing signage, requiring a revised taxi plan from ATC.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a compressor stall on departure and returned to departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported multiple compressor stalls in the #2 engine during initial climb, causing right yaw and popping noises. The crew followed checklists, maintained 5,000 ft MSL, and returned to ZZZ1 for a safe landing, recommending simulator training for this event.

synopsis: Captain reported that the while on descent to the destination airport, the aircraft rolled 30 degrees violently in less than one second. The First Officer disengaged the auto pilot and recovered from the upset attitude. The Flight Crew could discover no other issues and continued the approach to landing.
summary: During descent into ZZZ1 at FL240, the aircraft experienced an uncommanded violent roll to the right caused by an illuminated SPOILERS annunciation. The First Officer disengaged the autopilot to recover, and the crew completed a normal Flaps 30 landing after consulting the QRH and confirming normal control forces.

synopsis: First Officer reported concerns over Engine Fan Blades with wear and discoloration on the aft faces.
summary: A pilot inspecting a MAX aircraft noted surface cracking and hazing on #2 engine blades, which differed from the #1 engine. ZZZ Maintenance confirmed the condition was normal wear, though the pilot warned it could cause unnecessary delays if misidentified by others.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a passenger cell phone fire and smoke. Flight attendants cooled the phone in a toilet with coffee, they then transferred phone to thermal bag.
summary: The First Officer investigated an EICAS lavatory smoke alert after flight attendants failed to answer the cockpit phone. He found smoke caused by a flight attendant cooling a cell phone in coffee, which was later placed in a thermal bag.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported receiving improper & incorrect documents at departure. Flight crew provided a hard copy Hazmat document in place of company required 'colored slip' in violation the FOM procedures. Additionally, ACARS message to flight crew indicated no Hazmat on board.
summary: The flight crew departed for ZZZ after accepting a hard copy from Ramp as valid documentation for a battery-powered wheelchair, despite ACARS showing no dangerous goods. The Captain later realized the pink slip was the only acceptable document per the FOM.

synopsis: B737 Flight Crew reported a UAS passed near the aircraft while on final approach into SFO.
summary: Pilots on a descent through 1,400 feet AGL to SFO Runway 28R sighted a large, unlit black drone near the right wing. The crew reported the man-made object to Tower and completed the landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Ground personnel reported two aircraft simultaneously under tow on the same ramp were not in accordance to safety procedures and resulted in the tug operator taking action to avoid wing tip.
summary: During pushback of Aircraft X, a near-miss occurred with Aircraft Y being towed to an adjacent gate. The pushback operator had to reverse because the wing walker remained inside the tug cab, leaving insufficient clearance between the moving aircraft.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported the lavatory trash receptacles in two lavs were missing the self closing flapper doors and had not been repaired when previously written up. There is no MEL relief for these missing doors, except locking out the lavatory.
summary: A flight attendant on Aircraft X reported that two of four waste receptacles lacked required flame-containment covers during beverage service. The crew filed an inflight report, noting this was a repeat issue previously documented on the same aircraft.

synopsis: Technicians reported that rig pins were left installed after a flight control cable tension check. This was discovered during taxi for takeoff by the flight crew.
summary: Two inexperienced mechanics and an inspector performed a tension check on Aircraft X, leaving a rig pin installed due to rushed work, poor communication, and a missed operational check. The aircraft was pushed out with the pin in a locking position, causing the event to be discovered just before taxi.

synopsis: PA-32 pilot reported a defective alternator resulted in them flying with ADS-B not transmitting.
summary: The pilot diverted an IFR flight after the ammeter dropped to zero, suspecting a new alternator failure. A mechanic later confirmed the alternator was defective and replaced it, though the pilot questioned if low voltage prevented ADS-B Out transmission despite the transponder remaining operable.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot departing JZI non-towered airport reported a NMAC.
summary: The pilot reported a close proximity event shortly after takeoff from JZI at 1,600 ft on the 220 radial. The crew executed an evasive maneuver down and left to avoid an aircraft entering a downwind for Runway 27, resulting in a closest point of approach of 200 ft.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew reported ATC instructed them to cancel takeoff clearance but they did not comply due to their high speed and the critical phase of flight. A landing aircraft initiated a go around during their takeoff roll.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X continued a takeoff on wet Runway XXL after Tower canceled clearance at 115 knots due to an arriving aircraft's go-around. The Captain elected to proceed past V1 (124 knots) to avoid the high risk of rejecting on a wet runway, resulting in an uneventful departure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported issues at KOA gate where parking is unsafe due to poorly lit taxiways and ramp area.
summary: A pilot reported unsafe parking conditions at KOA Gate X due to unlit taxiways and ramp areas that obscured equipment. The pilot successfully parked using a Jeppesen AMM chart but noted that without it, they likely would have requested a tow due to the darkness.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported that during climbout in turbulent conditions, the left engine L ENG VAL EICAS Light, and the ENG VAL Light above the fuel cutout switch illuminated. The Flight Crew elected to perform an air turn back and overweight landing.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a left engine fuel valve light illumination after moderate turbulence shortly after takeoff. They returned to ZZZ, requested priority handling, and performed a safe overweight landing with ARFF standby.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported diverting after encountering engine vibrations severe enough to cause multiple systems failures. Flight Crew reported ice build up was most likely the cause of the vibrations.
summary: Pilots experienced engine vibrations and multiple system failures, including PFD loss, at 15,000 ft in IMC icing conditions shortly after departure. The crew attributed the cascade of failures to ice accumulation, diverted to ZZZ3 using standby instruments, and landed safely after becoming VMC.

synopsis: Pilot reported airline policy about Flight Attendants that were asked to work while sick.
summary: A sick Flight Attendant flew during the holiday period to earn extra pay, exposing the First Officer to illness. The First Officer subsequently tested positive for Covid-19, which the reporter attributes to management's policy of incentivizing crew to fly while sick.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported ramp congestion and charting issues at MSN airport.
summary: The crew attempted a non-standard taxi route at night during snow removal but found the path blocked by parked aircraft and fuel trucks. They required a maintenance pushback to the ramp to select an alternate route due to the obstruction and misleading airport diagram.

synopsis: Captain reported an electrical failure of the cockpit window heat caused a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: Flight X crew experienced sparks and smoke from the forward captain side window heating element during cruise. They shut off power, requested priority handling, and landed safely after refusing ATC vectors to fly a direct visual approach.

synopsis: Captain reported failure of the #1 Rudder Travel Throw Limiter System in flight with the #2 system already deferred causing the Captain to question the airworthiness of the aircraft.
summary: The crew encountered RUD TRV LIM 1 and Trim SYS ECAM faults en route while operating with a deferred RUD TRV LIM 2. The reporter questioned the aircraft's release because the new faults contradicted the deferral's requirement for normal system operation, despite multiple MRMs being signed off.

synopsis: B737-400 flight crew reported the landing gear failed to indicate down and locked.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear indication failure during approach to Runway XX at ZZZ, triggering a go-around and QRH manual extension procedures. Despite no "down and locked" indication, the aircraft landed safely due to fuel constraints and was subsequently towed to the gate.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported the alternator failed on departure and they returned to the airport.
summary: The crew experienced a right alternator failure on takeoff after gear retraction, indicated by the RH Alternator and Alt Out lights. Following an unsuccessful QRH check, ATC granted priority handling, and the aircraft returned to ZZZ for landing.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported they refused ATC clearance for takeoff because they observed another aircraft at the opposite end of the runway facing them.
summary: The flight crew rejected a takeoff clearance on Runway XX due to an opposing aircraft with lights off remaining on the runway. The pilot attributed the near-miss to ATC task saturation and high traffic volume at the airport, though the flight eventually departed safely after the runway was cleared.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence climbing through FL250 15 miles in trail of a B787.
summary: During climb through FL250, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a B787 15 miles ahead, causing two jolts. The pilots slowed from M.79 to M.73 and offset 5 miles right per ATC advice, resulting in no injuries and a subsequent maintenance inspection.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported the #1 engine Oil Filter Bypass light illuminated in flight, causing an in flight shut down of the engine and a diversion to make an overweight landing.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the crew encountered an amber 'Oil Filter Bypass' light on engine #1, leading to an engine shutdown and single-engine diversion to ZZZ2. The event was caused by an oil filter bypass blockage, resulting in a safe landing approximately 500 lbs overweight with 9 quarts of oil lost.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported an air turn back was complicated by turbulence that affected airspeed and the ability to hold altitude. The landing gear systems including weight on wheels sensing caused other systems failures.
summary: During initial climb, the crew encountered nose gear warnings and a subsequent airspeed decay with a brief stick shaker while managing QRH procedures, ATC communications, and turbulence. The Captain attributed the event to crew saturation from simultaneous tasks, gear drag, and power reductions, though they recovered safely and returned to the field.

synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported descending below glide slope intercept altitude due to loss of situational awareness.
summary: The flight crew descended 500 feet below the 2500-foot FAF altitude while conducting an ILS approach to Runway XXR at ZZZ. The pilot recovered to the correct altitude after ATC alert, attributing the event to a brief loss of situational awareness during the Before Landing Checklist.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported concerns with the deferral of lost lithium battery powered electronic devices in the cabin.
summary: A pilot questioned the safety of a 757 deferral allowing flights to continue when a passenger's lithium battery device falls into the cargo pit and cannot be located. The reporter expressed concern that the device could be crushed by cargo loading systems, causing a fire that cannot be fought, and noted a lack of specific risk analysis for this procedure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a momentary terrain warning while passing over a hill on a visual approach.
summary: The flight crew accepted a visual approach to Runway 24 at ROA at night and received a momentary terrain warning while descending outside HIBAN. The pilot attributed the event to a lapse in recognizing the need to start the approach farther out to ensure a full straight-in path.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported out dated airport charts for CLE.
summary: A pilot reported that CLE Jeppesen Page 10-6 contains outdated standardized taxi routes with incorrect taxiway names and non-existent intersections. The reporter attributed potential confusion to chart inaccuracies caused by recent taxiway reconfigurations and requested an update or removal of the page.

synopsis: C99 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence and while trying to descend, the trim control section of the Captain's control yoke broke off and resulted in a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot encountered severe turbulence from embedded thunderstorms during descent, causing the Captain's yoke trim to break and exposing wires. Although the pilot used standby trim to land safely, the incident was attributed to poor ATC vectors and inadequate onboard weather radar.

synopsis: Pilot reported on takeoff the elevator was marginally controllable which resulted in rejected take off. Reporter stated the aircraft had sat for two weeks in freezing conditions.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff from an icy runway in IFR conditions after discovering frozen flight controls preventing rotation. The pilot attributed the malfunction to moisture and freezing temperatures while the aircraft sat exposed on the ramp for over two weeks.

synopsis: Captain reported cabin pressure controllability issues caused an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: The crew experienced rapid cabin pressurization during climb, triggering EICAS alerts and oxygen mask deployment. After leveling at 10,100 ft MSL and requesting priority handling, the aircraft was vectored for an ILS return with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported burning odor 'similar to burning Lithium Ion battery' during climb. FA investigated the area and determined the 'possible' cause was spare Lithium batteries in passenger carry on bag. Flight executed a safe air return.
summary: A flight attendant detected a lithium-ion battery odor and smoke near the exit row shortly after takeoff. Upon finding a passenger's bag emitting smoke, the crew prepared for a precautionary return to the airport, though the smell dissipated within minutes.

synopsis: Commercial Captain reported conducting a go around on short final due to departing traffic still on the runway which resulted from ATC's inadequate traffic separation.
summary: The pilot of Company Y initiated a go-around at 350 ft AGL during a visual approach to Runway XXL to avoid a conflict with Company X, which had just begun its takeoff roll. The pilot attributed the incident to the Tower Controller attempting to squeeze a departure between arrivals, creating an unacceptable closure rate.

synopsis: Helicopter Pilot reported an NMAC during pre-takeoff hover checks on runway.
summary: A helicopter crew conducting hover checks on Runway XX landed immediately after a fixed-wing MEDEVAC aircraft took off toward them without a clear CTAF call. The MEDEVAC plane passed overhead at 150–200 feet, an incident the reporter attributes to the other pilot's failure to identify the helicopter or communicate their emergency status.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported unmarked power lines near 3KY4 airport.
summary: A pilot reported five unmarked high-voltage power lines, including two nearly invisible thin wires, crossing the approach end of Runway 33 and departure end of Runway 15 at 3KY4. The lack of markings or identification balls creates a wire strike hazard, particularly during high-density altitude departures on Runway 15.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A small jet pilot reported ramp personnel did not remove the towing adapter when preparing for departure which resulted in the nose gear stuck in a partially retracted position during gear retraction. The reporter was able to land safely with almost no damage.
summary: The pilot departed with a towing adapter left on the nose strut because they remained inside the aircraft during towing instead of verifying readiness. The adapter locked the nose gear partially retracted, forcing an emergency landing where the nose tire contacted the runway at 35 knots with minimal damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor and Student reported that while they were departing the traffic pattern, the engine malfunctioned followed by excessive vibration and partial loss of power. They returned to the airport and experienced complete engine failure upon landing.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced a catastrophic in-flight engine failure shortly after takeoff when a piston head exploded, severing the cylinder and causing total power loss. Despite violent shaking, oil leakage, and instrument malfunctions, they executed a precautionary landing at ZZZ with no injuries, attributing the cause to a loose cylinder rod or undetected wear.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported while on upwind there was excessive engine vibration and a 'loud popping' noise so they returned to the airport.
summary: During the upwind leg at 200 ft, both pilots heard a loud pop and vibration, though engine instruments remained normal. The instructor pilot declared a Pan-Pan, received clearance to return, and safely landed on Runway XXR after declining tower assistance for other runways.

synopsis: An observer reported seeing an object with a flashing beacon flying between 3,000 and 4,000 feet.
summary: A ground observer reported an unidentified object with a flashing white beacon south of the shore at 3,000–4,000 ft MSL. The object exhibited an erratic flight pattern beyond traditional aircraft capabilities, disappearing and reappearing twice without red or green position lights.

synopsis: UAS pilot reported that while the UAS was in cruise flight being flown by the autopilot the flight crew made changes to the flight profile, resulting in an undesirable aircraft state. The pilot saw the error and made a manual correction before there was a loss of aircraft control.
summary: The pilot reported that while flying a UAS at FL 220, uploading a new mission caused an unexpected pitch-up instead of a descent. Engineering is reviewing the discrepancy, and the pilot plans to verify autopilot modes and upload mission changes sequentially in the future.

synopsis: UAS pilot reported flying into an active TFR due to misunderstanding of LAANC authorization.
summary: A drone pilot obtained LAANC authorization via the Aloft app to fly a DJI Mavic 3 near a fire TFR but was later informed by a colleague that the app's approval did not constitute a valid TFR waiver. The incident highlighted confusion over the restriction wording and the inadequacy of the app's authorization for that specific airspace.

synopsis: UAS pilot reported they unknowingly flew their UAS into a TFR. Reporter stated there were no TFRs prior to launch and the TFR became active during the flight.
summary: The pilot operated a drone flight that unknowingly violated a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) which became effective while the flight was in progress. Despite checking two official apps and the DJI geofence, the pilot self-reported the violation after realizing the airspace restriction had been active.

synopsis: Pilot reported wind gusts during landing forced the balloon into a building, damaging some roof tiles.
summary: A hot air balloon pilot encountered a downdraft at rooftop height during landing, lightly striking a roof and damaging three to four tiles despite heating the envelope. The balloon landed safely in the designated field, and the pilot arranged and paid for repairs after speaking with the understanding homeowner.

synopsis: MIA Center Controller reported a loss of separation between to IFR aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to stop Aircraft X from descending on the SHRVY1 arrival due to sector volume and fatigue, causing a conflict alert with Aircraft Y at FL180. The controller instructed Aircraft X to expedite descent and maintain visual separation, resolving the situation without loss of separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft that entered a MVA at a lower altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller observed an MSAW alert for Aircraft X holding at CAPNA at FL030 during a missed approach. The controller climbed the aircraft to FL040 after suspecting it had entered a higher Minimum Vectoring Altitude area, noting that TAV maps should be used instead of approach plate altitudes.

synopsis: First Officer reported loss of power on the #1 engine during approach but landed safely.
summary: The First Officer reported that Aircraft X experienced severe vibrations, EGT spikes, and compressor stalls in engine 1 below 2000 feet during an ILS approach, leading to a power loss. The crew landed safely, executed fire checklists with no fire confirmed, and taxied to the gate while noting excessive communication from operations and maintenance personnel.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported loss of left hydraulic system during climb. The crew continued to destination airport and made a safe landing.
summary: The crew experienced a left hydraulic quantity EICAS warning and lost the left autopilot at 17,000 ft. They requested priority handling, climbed to FL 230 for VMC, completed the checklist, and landed uneventfully at ZZZ.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported Hazmat documents provided to the flight crew contained numerous weight and description errors. After making multiple attempts to correct the issue without resolution, the flight crew refused the Hazmat shipment and the flight departed safely.
summary: The Captain and First Officer removed all dangerous goods from the aircraft due to discrepancies in the shipping documents and a lack of accurate information from operations. This decision, supported by the Chief Pilot, resulted in a 12,500-pound weight reduction and a 2.5-hour departure delay.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a loss of aircraft control during taxi in to the gate due to the parking brake getting stuck and not releasing.
summary: Flight crew taxied an aircraft with one engine shut down on an icy ramp at ZZZ. After releasing the parking brake, the aircraft unexpectedly pivoted 150 degrees right due to asymmetric thrust caused by a stuck brake indicating 3,000 psi, which resolved after cycling the brake.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported confusion and communications issues while working a flight that diverted due to the loss of the APU generator, which when combined with an engine IDG already on MEL required the Flight Crew to divert and land at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: A flight crew diverted to ZZZ due to an APU generator failure leaving only one AC power source. The Dispatcher failed to notify the Maintenance Director as required by manual, delaying the issuance of company processes for priority handling.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported while taxiing on an icy ramp at night, they began to slide and shut down an engine shut down to stop aircraft.
summary: The flight crew landed at ITH and encountered an unreported ice patch on the ramp, causing a loss of braking and steering control. The pilots stopped the aircraft by shutting down both engines, resulting in no damage or injuries, and passengers were deplaned on foot while maintenance later towed the aircraft to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the APU on their 737 MAX continued to shut down while in service at the gate while in a heavy wet snow storm.
summary: Crews on two Boeing 737-MAX aircraft at Gate XX experienced APU trips and zero duct pressure during heavy wet snow with direct right crosswinds. Maintenance resolved the issue by shutting down the APU to close the inlet door, preventing snow ingestion and restoring normal operation.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a possible runway incursion at ORD airport. While taxiing on a snow covered taxiway and no lights indicating a hold short position, the incursion may have taken place. The pilots reported the Jeppesen airport chart does not show an accurate location for hold short lines.
summary: Pilots taxiing from the Central Deice Facility in snow missed the obscured Taxiway Golf intersection and stopped after ATC queried their position. The incident was caused by unplowed taxiways, poor visibility, and inaccurate Jeppesen charts, though no runway incursion occurred.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported seeing a lighted UAS off the right side of the aircraft during final approach into a Class B airport during night VMC conditions. The flight reported the UAS to the control tower and landed safely.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered a drone at 300 ft AGL during an ILS 16R approach to SEA at night. The drone, located in Class B airspace with only a downward white light, was deemed a near miss, but the aircraft landed safely with no damage.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported on visual approach receiving a confusing ATC low altitude alert.
summary: The pilot, conducting a visual approach to Runway 32 at FRG, received a low altitude advisory from Tower at 600 feet and 1.8 miles from the airport. The pilot regained altitude and continued the approach, noting they were following the approach plate altitudes despite the advisory.

synopsis: Captain reported an in flight shut down and diversion caused by a reverser unlocked light illuminating. The Flight Crew elected to divert and make a precautionary landing.
summary: The captain and first officer experienced a right thrust reverser unlock indication at FL360, prompting a descent to FL240 and eventual shutdown of the right engine at 18,000 feet. They landed safely at ZZZ2 with emergency services standing by, though the reverser never deployed.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported departing the gate without signing the Hazmat declaration due to a maintenance distraction in addition to other time critical departure issues.
summary: The Captain reported that while preparing for departure, a conference call regarding a deferred light switch delay caused a missed HAZMAT declaration signature. Dispatch later notified the crew via ACARS that the required radioactive pharmaceuticals declaration remained unsigned.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a go-around caused by turbulence resulting in airspeed fluctuations. On approach to the reciprocal runways, both PFDs failed with The Captain able to see the runway and continue to land.
summary: The crew experienced a momentary stick shaker and Flight Director loss during two ILS approaches in heavy rain and wind shear, causing a go-around and a subsequent visual landing. The pilot attributed the stall warning to wind shear and anti-ice sensitivity, while noting fatigue and startle factors contributed to an improper upset recovery.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported they improperly deviated left of course in oceanic airspace to avoid wake turbulence.
summary: The Captain offset two miles left of track during cruise to avoid wake turbulence, violating FOM restrictions on left SLOP. After Gander Oceanic queried the deviation, the Relief Pilot and First Officer corrected the error and returned the aircraft to the center of the track.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported an engine fire and engine cowling burn-through while troubleshooting an engine reverser fault on the ground with Maintenance Control.
summary: The crew experienced an Engine 2 reverser fault and a subsequent fire alarm with smoke and sparks during ground engine start at ZZZ. A popped circuit breaker for the oil quantity sensor was reset, leading to a cowling burn-through, after which the aircraft was safely shut down and passengers deplaned.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported while on a go-around, ATC issued an immediate turn off the missed approach procedure and towards rapidly rising terrain. Pilot stated concern with language barrier and procedure could result in confusion and a terrain event.
summary: Pilots at MMMX executed a manual go-around from 500 AGL on Runway 5R after a preceding aircraft missed a turn-off. The crew noted that the Tower's immediate 30-degree right turn clearance directed the aircraft toward rising terrain and off the missed approach course, creating potential confusion despite the event concluding safely.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported aft Flight Attendants notified flight deck crew of 'strong chemical smell' shortly after landing. Flight Attendants reported experiencing physiological symptoms. Flight crew requested expedited taxi clearance and airport support personnel.
summary: Flight attendants reported a strong chemical smell and eye irritation in the aft cabin after landing, prompting the crew to divert to a gate and don oxygen masks. Fire services detected volatile organic compounds in the cabin air, which the reporter attributed to a potential maintenance issue or a spill in the passenger or cargo compartments.

synopsis: Air Carrier Check pilot reported the APU on their 737 MAX continued to shut down while in service at the gate while in a heavy wet snow storm. The pilot also stated that another MAX aircraft at an adjacent gate was experiencing the same scenario.
summary: During pre-flight on a 737 MAX in heavy snow, the APU generator dropped offline twice and bleed pressure dipped, likely due to snow entering the inlet. The flight was cancelled, but the pilot reported a potential safety risk of being stranded without power during pushback if this known issue is not addressed in manuals.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reported diverting after a flap malfunction while on approach and while handling the situation, may have also potentially went over the airspeed restrictions for the stuck flap configuration.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a flap power caution and stuck flaps during approach to ZZZ1, causing a missed approach and diversion to ZZZ2 for a flaps-zero landing. The incident involved an accidental power lever overtravel and an airspeed exceedance while managing the emergency, with the crew citing Dispatch pressure as an added stressor.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported Aft Flight Attendant notified flight deck of 'dirty socks' odor during approach. Two aft cabin FA's who experienced physiological symptoms received medical assistance upon gate arrival.
summary: During the approach phase, two aft inflight crew members reported a "dirty socks" odor and burning eyes, while the flight deck and passengers remained unaffected. Medical personnel assisted the crew at the gate, and the flight crew completed required logbook and cabin odor documentation.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a 'musty/moldy/melted crayon' fume event during flight. Flight crew deselected number 1 pack which weakened the odor.
summary: The crew detected a musty odor in the flight deck and cabin during climb and descent, which weakened after deselecting pack 1. The pilot attributed the smell to the environmental system and reported it as a persistent level 1 occurrence.

synopsis: BE99 Captain reported a trim runaway problem on takeoff and performed an air turnback and precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a trim runaway during takeoff on Runway XXL, where the indicator shifted to full nose down despite being centered during the run-up. Heavy controls and unresponsive trim systems forced an immediate return and landing on Runway XYL for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: UAS pilot reported the UAS flew outside of the authorized operations area. Pilot continued flight after receiving ATC clearance into additional airspace.
summary: The pilot slightly flew outside the cleared section of X, immediately turned around, and requested the desired sectors. ATC subsequently cleared the aircraft for those sectors with no issues.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported keeping an aircraft below the MVA due to icing conditions.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X from Runway 27 at ANE to maintain 3000 ft on heading 090, assuming it would avoid a 3400 ft obstruction. The aircraft turned wider than expected and entered the minimum vectoring altitude, prompting the controller to issue a climb to 4000 ft.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a growing fuel imbalance during cruise and the subsequent decision for an in-flight engine shut down and diversion to another airport.
summary: During cruise at FL 340, the crew observed a growing fuel imbalance reaching 700 lbs with no visible leak. They executed the QRH checklist, shut down the left engine, and diverted to ZZZ for an uneventful single-engine landing.

synopsis: Flight crew reported taking evasive action after receiving a TCAS RA while on departure.
summary: During departure from Miami International in IMC, Departure Control vectored the flight into a near miss with another aircraft at 7,000 ft, triggering a TCAS 'DESCEND' Resolution Advisory. The First Officer executed the RA to avoid the conflict, which the reporter attributes to ATC error and high traffic congestion.

synopsis: C402 pilot reported a loss of engine power and engine roughness resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced significant vibration and right engine manifold pressure fluctuations during cruise, prompting a return to ZZZ. After a safe landing, inspection revealed the right engine nacelle was covered in oil, though no specific cause was identified in flight.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported the failure of ELAC2 in flight and discovered that it was only re-settable on the ground. The Captain elected to continue to destination airport and entered the discrepancy in the aircraft log book.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the crew experienced an uncommanded climb caused by an ELAC 2 fault while the autopilot was engaged. The pilot disconnected the autopilot, the First Officer performed the ECAM procedure without resetting the system, and the flight continued safely to ZZZ.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported an AVIONICS SMOKE alert that lasted 2 minutes during cruise. The Captain requested priority handling to their destination airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a persistent Avionics Smoke indication during cruise at FL320, prompting an emergency descent and landing at ZZZ. Maintenance later attributed the false alarm to a short circuit in the avionics bay caused by water intrusion from days earlier.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported the APU auto shut down on push back. After restart, the push back crew reported an APU fire. The flight crew extinguished the APU fire and was tugged back into the gate.
summary: During pushback, the APU auto-shutdown and a ground crew reported a fire despite no cockpit indications. The crew discharged the #1 fire bottle, extinguishing the fire, and the aircraft was subsequently tugged back to the gate.

synopsis: Flight crew reported observing an unauthorized vehicle on the runway prior to night departure that had gone unnoticed by ATC.
summary: The flight crew spotted an unauthorized van on Runway 8L at Ontario while holding a takeoff clearance, prompting an immediate stop. The controller canceled the clearance, used a helicopter to alert the driver, and cleared the runway after a ground inspection before the flight departed.

synopsis: B767 flight crew and Dispatcher reported a taxiway excursion due to freezing rain and worsening weather conditions.
summary: The flight crew lost braking control on Taxiway XY due to freezing rain and inadequate treatment, causing the aircraft to slide off into the grass. They regained control using reverse thrust, but the left wing leading edge slat was damaged, requiring a tow back for inspection.

synopsis: CRJ 700 First Officer reported his side window shattered at 36,000 feet, requiring an immediate descent and diversion to a precautionary landing.
summary: During a CRJ 700 flight at FL360, the right forward window shattered, causing rapid cabin depressurization and preventing the crew from maintaining required pressure differential. The pilots followed QRH procedures, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely at 8,000 feet with no injuries reported.

synopsis: CL-605 flight crew reported the Cabin Light Controller failed and began to emit sparks and smoke. The flight crew descended and diverted to make a precautionary landing.
summary: During cruise, the crew observed sparks and smoke from the cabin lighting controller screen when moved. They requested priority handling, descended, and landed safely at ZZZ without incident, as emergency personnel determined no further action was needed.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported while operating a super tug at night on movement area, miscommunication and blinding flood lights resulted in near collision with a regional jet.
summary: A pilot and a safety observer towing Aircraft X with a Supertug stopped on Taxiway BRAVO after a regional jet crossed Taxiway MIKE. The reporter attributed the near-miss to floodlights impairing visibility and Ramp Control's lack of situational awareness regarding aircraft positions.

synopsis: First Officer reported Captain flew an unstable approach resulting in GPWS alert and late go around to a landing.
summary: The First Officer reported that during an ILS 16 approach to HPN in IMC, the Captain failed to capture the glide slope, resulting in a full deflection and a GPWS warning at 750 feet. The crew executed a go-around, corrected the approach, and landed safely after the second attempt.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported the need to take evasive action on downwind to avoid a traffic conflict.
summary: An instructor and student in a training aircraft on downwind for Runway 36 at ZZZ avoided a potential collision by banking right and climbing to 2,500 MSL after spotting an unidentified aircraft descending ahead. The other pilot did not respond to radio calls, and subsequent investigation failed to identify the aircraft's owner or pilot.

synopsis: PA32 Pilot reported engine roughness resulted in successful return to departure airport. Pilot suspected fuel contamination.
summary: During a local IFR practice approach, a two-person crew experienced increasing engine roughness and lost #2 EGT readings at 700 feet, leading to an emergency landing. The engine quit on the taxiway, which the pilot attributed to water-ice in the fuel due to extreme cold temperatures.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported executing a go around while on final approach after an aircraft taxied onto the runway.
summary: A pilot on an ILS 26 approach at RIL executed a low right circle to avoid Aircraft X, which entered the runway at less than 200 feet without seeing the approaching aircraft. The near-miss occurred due to Aircraft X's premature departure and lack of visual contact, though both aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: Center Controller reported issues with another ATC facility, COVID cleaning, ATC Zero, and the contingency plan.
summary: An Area X controller reported that the ZOB contingency plan for assuming ZZZ approach airspace lacks sufficient training for ILS vectoring and risks sector overload. The reporter recommends mandatory classroom and lab training for unqualified controllers and separating approach airspace into a dedicated sector.

synopsis: Center Controllers reported issues relating to COVID cleaning.
summary: Controllers at ZAU assumed ZZZ approach airspace during a busy rush after ZZZ went ATC-0 for a COVID cleaning with only a few hours' notice. The reporter cites inadequate training on the unfamiliar airspace, poor coordination, and an outdated ATIS broadcast as dangerous factors that could lead to controller error.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a rejected take off after the T/O Configuration Warning Light and T/O Warning Horn sounded at 80 knots.
summary: The crew experienced a false takeoff warning during the Before Takeoff Checklist that resolved after cycling flaps, but the horn and light reactivated at 125 knots during the takeoff roll. The Captain performed a Rejected Takeoff, and the aircraft returned to the gate for a 50-minute brake cooling period.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported a Pitch Trim Failure during climbout. The crew performed the procedures in the QRH, contacted ATC for assistance, contacted Company and the flight attendant. With approval from the Dispatcher the flight continued on to the destination because of available runway length and available maintenance.
summary: The crew experienced a pitch trim system failure and autopilot disengagement while climbing through 16,000 feet. They diverted to ZZZ2, executed a flaps 22 landing with significant control forces, and landed safely due to effective crew coordination.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a fume event that was also reported by cabin crew during approach and landing. APU was deferred by maintenance at arrival gate.
summary: The Captain and flight attendant reported a strong volatile odor in the aft cabin during approach and landing, which fire and rescue confirmed with equipment. The APU was MEL, and the crew completed checklists and taxied to the gate, suggesting increased preventative maintenance to reduce reliance on MELs.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reported getting an incorrect ACARS fuel weight from Dispatch.
summary: Pilots identified a 100,000 lbs fuel error in the preflight weight and balance data received via ACARS, where total fuel was listed as 111.9 lbs instead of 112,000 lbs. Dispatch confirmed the mistake, which shifted the takeoff center of gravity by 4 units, prompting the crew to recommend process improvements to prevent future occurrences.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported loss of Green Hydraulic System on climb out and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a green hydraulic system leak during climb and cruise, resulting in zero quantity and loss of nose wheel steering. They secured the pumps, extended the landing gear via gravity, and landed uneventfully before being towed to the gate.

synopsis: Captain reported a landing gear unsafe indication on take off resulted in a return to departure airport and precautionary landing.
summary: The crew executed a missed approach and single-engine landing due to a false right main gear unsafe indication caused by inadvertently pulled T-handles. After confirming gear position visually and following checklists, they landed safely, towed the aircraft to the gate, and resolved the issue by resetting the handles.

synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving a Ground Proximity Warning while on final approach due to conducting the approach below the authorized minimum air temperature.
summary: A fatigued crew flying a night visual approach backed by RNAV XX received a GPWS terrain warning due to flying low from unapplied cold temperature compensation at -13°C. The pilots corrected the descent and landed safely, attributing the error to missed briefing notes caused by complacency.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reported loss of hydraulic fluid during climb out. The crew continued to the destination airport and landed safely.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X, operating under a ferry permit with flaps at 5 degrees, experienced a rapid loss of #1 hydraulic fluid en route to ZZZ. Despite receiving no technical guidance from Maintenance regarding diversion options, the crew continued to ZZZ, landing safely with normal brakes and no in-flight cautions.
