summary: Crew noticed an acetone/fume smell descending into ZZZ at 1,200 feet AGL. The odor dissipated after Pack 1 was selected off.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a fume event during descent which was characterized as a 'sweet magic marker type' odor. While the flight crew was proceeding with the appropriate QRH procedure the odor dissipated only to return on short final.
summary: During flight X, the crew and a flight attendant detected a sweet odor at 11,000 ft and again on short final. The aircraft landed safely in ZZZ, and maintenance was notified after a logbook entry was made.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving an RA fault on short final at FLL, citing possible 5G interference as the cause of the event.
summary: The First Officer flying an ILS approach to Runway 28L at FLL with autopilot off experienced a temporary Radio Altimeter 1 fault at 50 ft AGL. The fault cleared after 3-5 seconds, allowing a safe landing, possibly caused by a 5G issue.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a fume event characterized as 'dirty socks' upon gate arrival.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a dirty sock odor and burning sensations on the ground after landing, attributed to the APU. The crew shut down the APU, vented the aircraft, and requested medical assistance for flight attendants suffering from headaches and esophageal burning.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported noting a brief RA error climbing out of BOS, citing 5G interference as the possible cause of the event.
summary: The pilot reported a brief RA error during climb out of BOS, likely caused by 5G interference. Although the event occurred before the 5G NOTAM effective time, the pilot failed to log it, a mistake later corrected through counseling on reporting requirements.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that during departure, the primary display and navigation display lost all data and an ADR fault ECAM was displayed. The flight crew made a return to the departure airport.
summary: During departure from ZZZ at 2000 ft, the Captain's primary and navigation displays lost data with an ADR Fault 1 ECAM. Following checklists and consultations, the crew returned to ZZZ and performed an overweight landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported RA anomalies on taxi in at ROC, citing possible 5G interference as the cause of the event.
summary: The First Officer reported erratic Radio Altimeter indications fluctuating between 0 and 2500 ft while waiting to park at Gate xx. The instrument returned to normal after the aircraft taxied forward to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported glide slope and takeoff configuration warning anomalies on arrival into MCO, citing possible 5G interference as the cause of the issues.
summary: During a visual approach to Orlando Runway 35R, the glide slope failed to capture initially, and a takeoff configuration warning sounded while clearing the runway with low power. Maintenance tests were successful, and they suspect a possible 5G anomaly caused the issue.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported the autopilot descended the aircraft below glide slope causing a Ground Proximity Alert and Low Altitude Warning from the Tower.
summary: During an ILS approach to ZZZ, the aircraft descended prematurely on autopilot before glide slope intercept due to an automation failure. The crew immediately disconnected the autopilot and auto-throttles to climb, triggering a GPWS warning and ATC altitude check, but landed safely.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a fume event during preflight while parked at Gate. After trouble shooting with no change the Captain refused the aircraft, a logbook entry was submitted. A different aircraft was assigned.
summary: The flight crew refused an aircraft scheduled for a ZZZ to ZZ1 flight due to a persistent, unknown musty odor in the cabin and flight deck. After turning off the APU bleed air failed to clear the smell, the Captain removed the crew for safety concerns, resulting in a new aircraft assignment.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing a #1 engine compressor stall.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer experienced a loud bang, yawing, and an Engine Stall alert on Engine #1 while climbing from 12,000 ft. They returned to ZZZ after idling the thrust lever stopped the compressor stalls, attributing the smooth handling to training and CRM.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning on descent into BUR, and recommended ATC use a higher altitude for arrivals over terrain.
summary: The pilot reported a terrain warning during the Janny 5 arrival into BUR while crossing mountain peaks at 5,000 ft on radar vectors. The alert occurred because the aircraft's 1,400 ft radio altitude in a clean configuration triggered the system, prompting a suggestion to raise the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a late instruction from ramp control, a miss communication with the push back crew and a momentary loss of control of the aircraft during push back from the gate. The ground crew was informed by the Captain that brakes were set, ramp tower asked for the aircraft to moved further back and the Captain relayed the instructions to the push back crew. When the brakes were released the aircraft began to roll backwards. The Captain aggressively set the parking brake. The Captain reports the ground crew needs more training in proper procedures and communication.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X experienced an uncontrolled backward movement during pushback at Gate XX due to a confused Ramp Controller and ground crew miscommunication regarding amended clearances. The pilot immediately set the parking brake to stop the aircraft, preventing damage or injury, and attributed the incident to controller confusion, crew inexperience, and on-time performance pressure.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an electrical smell in the cockpit during descent. The Captain reported the stabilizer trim began to make uncommanded trim inputs until flaps were lowered to 5 degrees. The Captain elected to continue the approach to landing.
summary: During descent into ZZZ, the crew smelled hot electricity and experienced intermittent stabilizer trim oscillations that ceased after configuring flaps 5. The aircraft flew normally, landed without event, and the issue was reported to maintenance.

synopsis: Airbus Flight Attendant crew reported a fume event during descent which lasted until gate arrival. Captain was notified and medical assistance requested. After much delay Flight Attendants were transported to local hospital for evaluation.
summary: Three flight attendants on an Airbus experienced severe nausea, throat irritation, and headaches from a strong chemical odor during descent and after landing. The crew evacuated to the terminal, used pilot oxygen, and were transported to a hospital after a delay in obtaining medical clearance.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported an air turn back and precautionary landing after a reported engine fire and in flight shut down of the affected engine.
summary: Cabin crew reported an engine shutdown with fire during climbout from ZZZ, forcing an immediate return. After landing, maintenance determined an aircraft swap was necessary before the crew departed for ZZZ1.

synopsis: Technician reported communications problems and software issues when trying to route engine fuel nozzles to a vendor for repair.
summary: A mechanic performing a fuel nozzle modification on Aircraft X's left engine documented incorrect part numbers, causing a week-long storage delay and unreadable unserviceable tags. The reporter attributes this error to overwhelming administrative paperwork that distracts mechanics from actual maintenance tasks.

synopsis: Beech BE36 pilot reporting diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing issues with the alternate air door, and then engine problems that led to an inflight shutdown after landing was assured.
summary: The crew experienced an alternate air door light and engine overtemp indications during cruise, prompting a precautionary landing with priority routing. They reduced power due to cylinder issues, shut off fuel, and executed an uneventful unpowered landing with no injuries or fire.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate aircraft Captain reported hitting a bird and then having to deviate.
summary: The PIC of a type aircraft struck a flock of five birds at 400 ft AGL shortly after takeoff from ZZZ, causing significant nose cone damage and blood on the left wing and right engine. The crew diverted to ZZZ2, landed safely, and grounded the aircraft for maintenance assessment after confirming no engine blade damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot reported an NMAC at a non-towered airport with an aircraft that was not on CTAF.
summary: An instructor and student in Aircraft X encountered a traffic conflict with non-communicating Aircraft Y while on left downwind for Runway XX at ZZZ. The instructor took evasive action to avoid a collision course and departed the area to return to the home airport.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with another aircraft at a non-towered airport.
summary: An IFR flight conducting a low approach at a non-towered airport encountered a VFR aircraft that turned base to final directly in front of them at the same altitude. The VFR pilot's failure to maintain separation and inability to climb due to traffic ahead forced the IFR crew to offset and execute a missed approach.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a departing aircraft flew directly over them as they taxied off the runway.
summary: A helicopter delaying on Runway XX after a full stop landing was flown over by departing Aircraft Y. The Aircraft Y pilot reported not seeing the helicopter as it exited the runway centerline.

synopsis: Pilot reported another aircraft taxied over their aircraft wing, and reporter attempted to contact other pilot. Other pilot did not appear to care about what had just happened.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X reported that while stationary before taxiing, Aircraft Y taxied between them and a hangar, passing its wing over Aircraft X's wing. The pilot considered the maneuver unsafe and unnecessary, noting that Aircraft Y refused to exchange contact information and agreed to the incident being reported.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported a fume event during approach which he characterized as 'dirty socks'. Fumes persisted until gate arrival.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a chemical odor and tingling sensations while descending through 4,000 ft to land on the ILS for XXL. The reporter attributed the incident to engine oil contaminants in the bleed air system, which caused elevated carbon monoxide levels confirmed by bloodwork, though maintenance could not duplicate the issue.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported slowing too early on approach to ATL in his efforts to avoid wake turbulence in trail of a B767.
summary: The pilot reported that while on approach to Runway 26R behind a Boeing 767, they were assigned 170 knots to AJAAY but had to slow earlier to avoid wake turbulence. The pilot noted they should have informed Tower of the need to slow for spacing and wake avoidance.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported having problems with the aircraft data link resulting in their flight number not matching with Foreign ATC displays.
summary: The crew of an aircraft returning to ZZZZ encountered a data link outage during maintenance, forcing manual route input and a shutdown until systems partially recovered. Later, at cruise altitude, a flight number mismatch with ADS-B occurred due to incorrect manual entry of the aircraft identifier, which was corrected after consulting stored information.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp employee reported a near-collision with a ground vehicle while he was wing walking an aircraft into the gate.
summary: A ground handler preparing to wing walk an aircraft to the gate was nearly struck by a vehicle driven by a young man texting. The driver jerked the vehicle back upon seeing the handler, preventing an accident caused by the driver's unsafe distraction.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported they were cleared to cross 8L at HNL even though another air carrier aircraft was on short final for landing.
summary: The crew entered Runway 08L at HNL while crossing from Runway 04R after receiving clearance from Tower, despite an aircraft on short final. Contributing factors included high workload, control transfer, and speed, leading to a runway incursion that was resolved by accelerating across the runway before the other aircraft landed.

synopsis: B747-400 flight crew reported a malfunction during engine start was not observed by the ground crew during push back. The ground crew disconnected the tug without asking the Captain to set the parking brake. The aircraft rolled into a parked cart and damaged an engine inlet.
summary: During a night engine start in freezing fog, the flight crew released brakes to straighten the nose, believing the aircraft was under tow, but the tug had disconnected. The aircraft rolled forward and struck a ground cart, damaging engine 3's tail cone, caused by unclear towing status and equipment left in the safety area.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported executing a go-around at ORD after experiencing autoflight anomalies possibly related to 5G interference.
summary: The flight crew executing an RNAV (GPS) 27R approach at Chicago experienced full-scale LNAV and VNAV deviations while the First Officer saw no indications. The crew executed a go-around and successfully landed on the ILS 28C, though the cause of the anomaly remained undetermined by both the crew and ATC.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a priority right side stick anomaly during approach and elected to perform a go-around. The Captain disconnected autothrust and autopilot and re-tried the approach and landing after assigning side stick priority to the Captain's side.
summary: During short final with the First Officer flying, an uncommanded "priority right" annunciation and thrust increase occurred. The Captain took control, assigned side stick priority, disconnected auto thrust, and executed a go-around, resulting in a normal landing after maintenance was notified.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a runway incursion occurred at FAI when they were unable to stop the aircraft at the hold short line because of nil braking action.
summary: The flight crew taxiing to Runway 2L in FAI slid past the hold line due to nil braking action on compacted snow and ice. The Tower instructed an aircraft on final to go around before clearing the crew for takeoff after they reported the poor braking conditions.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a safe landing following the failure of the Captain's airspeed indicator.
summary: The crew experienced unreliable airspeed indications on the Captain's side during descent to ZZZ due to a failed indicator. They executed memory items, verified ground speed with ATC, and landed uneventfully with the First Officer flying after switching to an LDA approach.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported executing a go-around after receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on a night visual approach to BHM.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain flying into BHM initiated a go-around during a night Visual 36 approach after the Ground Proximity light illuminated and Tower issued a low altitude alert. They subsequently stabilized and landed safely on Runway 06.

synopsis: Technician reported aircraft arrived at station with the keel Beam APU pressure duct seal clamp not installed. The aircraft was taken out of service for maintenance action.
summary: Aircraft X arrived at the gate with a clamp on the keel beam APU duct pressure seal that had slipped off, initially appearing missing. The aircraft was taken out of service for repairs due to the time required to fix the issue, which could cause pressurization leaks.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported landing safely after experiencing loss of power related to water in the fuel.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss on the crosswind leg of a Cessna 172 departure due to water entering the left fuel tank through a leaky cap seal. Water accumulated in the tank while parked downslope during maintenance and migrated to the carburetor during flight, causing the engine to fail.

synopsis: Air Carrier Safety Analyst reported undeclared Dangerous Goods had been shipped without required Hazmat documentation. Packaged was missing Hazmat label and improperly packaged for air shipment. Package smelled of petrol and package was damp due to spillage.
summary: A pilot reported an undeclared package smelling of petrol and damp from spillage on Airways Bill XXXXX. The company warehouse insulated the package, but no dangerous goods had been declared.

synopsis: GA student pilot reported a runway excursion just prior rotation on takeoff. Pilot regained directional control on adjacent taxiway and was cleared to taxi to hangar where a mechanic noted cosmetic damage to left gear. No determination of why the aircraft suddenly veered left.
summary: A student pilot executing a second solo takeoff in a training aircraft veered left just before rotation, exiting the runway and damaging a runway light. The cause remains undetermined, though mechanical failure, obstruction, or pilot input error are suspected, resulting in minor cosmetic damage to the left gear strut.

synopsis: C550 Captain reported the left engine fan speed began increasing on climb. The Captain elected to perform an in flight shut down and diverted to make a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during cruise at 34,000 ft, the left engine fan speed increased autonomously while other parameters remained nominal. The pilot shut down the engine and landed at ZZZ2; mechanics later found the left engine Fuel Control Unit had failed.

synopsis: Helicopter inspector reported the flight crew had a tail rotor gearbox chip light illuminate in flight. Inspector found incorrect records and procedures for the gearbox that resulted in non-compliance in maintenance tasks and logbook entries.
summary: An ENG flight crew performed a precautionary landing after a tail rotor gearbox chip light illuminated. The cause was an overhauled gearbox installed without required post-installation checks or record updates due to operational pressure and inadequate maintenance oversight.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Corporate jet Flight Crew reported they deviated from an ATC clearance. Flight crew was issued a new clearance and landed safely.
summary: The flight crew and controller experienced a routing misunderstanding during the ILS 30 approach at GYY after the crew flew direct to the outer marker instead of the expected KIKVE intercept. The controller subsequently cleared the crew for a visual approach after realizing there was insufficient room to vector them, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: TRACON Controller and Pilot reported the aircraft went through final approach course heading toward terrain, then switched to tower frequency, resulting in confusion on both sides. The aircraft was then vectored for another approach.
summary: Pilots and controllers at SNA experienced a communication breakdown where the aircraft missed vectors and entered high terrain areas while on the base leg. The crew eventually received a climb to 5,000 feet and vectors away from terrain, landing uneventfully after resolving the frequency confusion.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported a late instruction from ramp control, a miscommunication with the push back crew and a momentary loss of control of the aircraft during push back from the gate.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced uncontrolled aircraft movement during pushback at ZZZ after the tug disconnected while the Captain released the brakes. The incident resulted from confusing, amended Ramp Control instructions that led to ground crew miscommunication regarding their connection status, though the Captain stopped the aircraft safely.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported autoflight anomalies in cruise flight in the vicinity of MEI VORTAC, citing 5G interference as possibly contributing. Reporter noted that two other air carrier flights in the same area were experiencing similar issues.
summary: The pilot flying reported altitude and system fluctuations at FL320 on Q40 near Meridian, suspecting 5G interference from nearby antennas. After descending to FL280, the aircraft stabilized, while two other flights on the same airway experienced similar or more severe issues, including autopilot loss.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported a malfunction with the radio altimeter while on initial approach to PHL.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 09R, the crew received a 'NAV RA 1 FAULT' message 2 nm west of KELEE while both radio altimeters displayed accurate data. The flight continued to a manual landing without incident, and the reporter suggested turning off 5G cell service near airports.

synopsis: A320 Pilot reported a fume event during descent characterized as a 'very strong chemical odor'. Reporter experienced multiple physiological symptoms.
summary: During descent into ZZZZ at 7,000–10,000 feet, a pilot inhaled a strong chemical odor while passing through moisture, causing dizziness and fatigue for 30–45 seconds. Following a medical evaluation, the pilot called out sick for the return leg due to lingering unwellness and anxiety.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air Carrier Maintenance Stock Clerk reported being notified of Hazmat packaging violation a week after violation occurred. Stock clerk requested more clear and concise packaging information.
summary: A ground staff member shipped two Hazmat items to ZZZ using corrugated paper for cushioning, interpreting IATA procedures as allowing any material. A supervisor later identified this as improper packing, prompting the staff member to request written clarification on restricted materials from the procedures department.

synopsis: Cessna 172 student pilot reported loss of directional control on landing roll, resulting in a runway excursion. No damage or injuries reported.
summary: A solo pilot was cleared for a left midfield Runway XXL but was instructed to land straight in on Runway XY, requiring a faster descent and approach. The resulting high-speed landing caused a bounce onto the grass, though the pilot maintained control with no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: Aeronca 65CA pilot reported loss of directional control in gusty wind conditions that resulted in a runway excursion during landing.
summary: During landing, strong crosswinds gusting to 19 knots blew the aircraft off the runway to the right, causing the right main landing gear to scrape the grass. No visible damage was found on the aircraft, though a rut was left in the grass.

synopsis: PA-46 Flight Instructor and student reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on approach to landing when they were having difficulty maintaining altitude in turbulence and wind shear conditions.
summary: A flight instructor and student encountered severe wind shear and turbulence after takeoff, forcing a return to the departure airport. Despite descending below minimum ILS altitude and receiving an altitude alert from TRACON, they maintained visual contact and completed an uneventful landing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light jet Captain reported they received a low altitude alert from ATC departing SJC.
summary: The flight crew departed SJC on Runway 30R with an incorrect FMS SID sequence, causing an early turn and a low altitude warning from ATC. The crew maintained control, expedited the climb to 12,000 ft, and attributed the event to rushing the takeoff clearance without verifying the FMS.

synopsis: BE-33 pilot reported a recently installed Garmin GFC 500 autopilot pushed the aircraft nose over un-commanded. The pilot recovered by continuously pushing the disconnect switch. The pilot believes this should be addressed by the manufacturer.
summary: During a visual landing at ZZZ, the pilot reported that the Garmin GFC 500 autopilot's ESP feature unexpectedly pushed the nose down below 70 knots. The pilot manually disconnected the system to recover and land, identifying the ESP speed setting as a hazard requiring software modification.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot Crew reported while on final approach the autothrottle failed to keep the aircraft on speed. As the aircraft slowed the pilots disconnected the autothrottle and continued in manual mode to landing. The pilots reported they were aware of 5G interference around LGA.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS 04 approach at LGA experienced an uncommanded throttle rollback near Tower frequency, which they mitigated by disengaging automation to maintain stability. Post-landing, they suspected a missed landing clearance due to the landing light remaining off, though ATC provided no indication of an issue.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported the radio altimeters began to malfunction while on initial approach to PHX. The pilots began to receive RA and EFIS COMP MON caution messages.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 26 at 2.5 NM final, both radar altimeters fluctuated, triggering RA and EFIS COMP MON caution messages. The pilot noted these alerts coexisted throughout the remainder of the approach.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported braking did not stop their aircraft while parking at a snow covered gate so they applied reverse thrust to stop the aircraft.
summary: Pilots reported that during taxi in heavy snow and low visibility, the aircraft failed to stop at a line person's signal despite full braking and reverse thrust. The crew attributed the overrun to unexpectedly slick ramp surfaces, though they stopped before hitting ground equipment.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Crew reported false targets displayed on their TCAS. The reporters heard a succeeding flight reporting the same anomaly.
summary: Pilots reported intermittent TCAS lights on the PFD during a visual approach to Runway 6 between 1500 and 200 feet. The brief flashes occurred twice without aural alerts, and the crew did not suspect a system failure or 5G interference.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the Radio Altimeter display on their Heads Up Display blinked and they received an unstable ILS signal while on approach.
summary: The pilot reported Localizer flutter and Radio Altimeter blinking on the HUD during a visual ILS Z 16R approach below 200 ft. The First Officer observed no anomalies on other displays, and the crew continued the safe landing despite the unusual but non-failing signal behavior.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported undocumented Dangerous Goods transported. Discrepancy occurred due to inaccurate DG manifest data and no onboard visual DG verification.
summary: Flight crew on Aircraft X operating ZZZ-ZZZ1 discovered unmanifested Class 3 and 8 Accessible Dangerous Goods in a container after landing. The reporter attributed the error to improperly manifested DG by ground personnel, where the ULD manifest was misplaced in the container pouch rather than the crew envelope.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the First Officer's radio altimeter worked intermittently and the Autoland Status indicator went blank while on approach to JAX.
summary: During the approach to Runway 8 at JAX in VMC, the First Officer's radio altimeter failed intermittently and the Autoland Status indicator went blank. The crew noted a 5G NOTAM but cited an approved Alternate Means of Compliance for the runways.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported receiving multiple alert messages on final approach at DFW and suspected possible 5G interference.
summary: During an autopilot-off approach to DFW at 200 ft AGL, the crew received brief alerts including "use manual spoilers," suspecting 5G interference with radio altimeter-dependent auto spoilers. Systems functioned normally during landing, and Tower was not notified as analysis occurred post-flight.

synopsis: Small aircraft Flight Instructor reported a rough running engine during initial climb and returned to safe landing at departure airport.
summary: The pilot and student experienced repeated engine roughness and power loss shortly after takeoff, forcing an immediate return to land on Runway XX. Despite normal pre-flight checks, the engine ran extremely rough on the ground but did not seize, resulting in no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported on approach the VNAV indicated the aircraft was below the flight path while the FMA indicated on path. Pilot stated this could have been caused by possible 5G interference.
summary: The pilot flying a visual approach with RNAV RNP backup reported possible 5G interference causing VNAV to display "below PATH" while the aircraft was high on the PAPI. The pilot disconnected the autopilot and auto throttles to hand-fly the aircraft using V/S mode and the heads-up display.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported gate departure without the required [dangerous goods form] due to a communication breakdown between flight crew and Dispatcher. The high workload of multiple issues and time pressure at departure time caused the communication issue.
summary: The pilot reported a potential failure to receive or verify a Dangerous Goods Form for HAZMAT cargo during a flight with weight and schedule pressures. The reporter noted uncertainty regarding whether the HAZMAT was removed or if the required documentation was properly delivered to the cockpit and logbook.

synopsis: Flight Crew and Dispatcher reported communications issues after the Flight Crew elected to perform an air turn back caused by trim failure.
summary: A 737 crew experienced electric trim failure after takeoff and diverted to ZZZZ1/ZZZZ following troubleshooting with Dispatch. The report attributes significant delays to Maintenance Control's poor response, including unanswered calls and an initial connection with a non-737 specialist, though the flight landed safely.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported during departure from IAH the mode control panel altitude window indicated incorrectly and the altitude alerter sounded continuously.
summary: The pilot reported 5G interference with flight instruments while climbing through 400 ft after takeoff from Runway 27 at IAH. The altitude window erroneously displayed 50,000 ft and the alerter sounded until the cleared altitude was re-selected, restoring the pitch bar and VNAV.

synopsis: Captain reported receiving engine overheat and fire warning system indications which resulted in return to departure airport.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X ZZZ-ZZZ1 experienced intermittent master caution and engine fire warnings at FL310 while all engine indications remained normal. The crew elected to return to ZZZ for an overweight landing on Runway XXR, where crash fire/rescue confirmed no fire indications before normal deplaning.

synopsis: Flight crew reported possible 5G interference at cruise, 20 NM North of CLT.
summary: While cruising at FL390 near CLT, the crew experienced a radar altimeter anomaly displaying 1,400–1,790 ft AGL, triggering false landing ECAM warnings. The reporter attributed this to possible 5G interference, noting the Atlanta Center controller confirmed the area was a 5G hotspot.

synopsis: Air Carrier Tow personnel reported control was lost of an aircraft under tow which slid into a tug denting the aircraft.
summary: A tug driver towing Aircraft X on an icy ramp lost control while turning into a lead-in line, causing the aircraft to jack-knife and dent the fuselage. The incident resulted from a lack of traction on the frozen surface, which prevented the driver from regaining control despite corrective steering attempts.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a fume event during departure climb. After trouble shooting and conferring with Dispatch, Maintenance and also flight attendants crew executed an air return due to the persistent fumes.
summary: Pilots and flight attendants detected a persistent odor shortly after takeoff while flying the SID with engine anti-ice active due to icing conditions. The crew returned to ZZZ, where the odor ceased upon engine shutdown, attributed to a faulty aircraft system requiring design or maintenance improvements.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported confusion over MEL procedures led to a Cabin Altitude Master Warning. The Flight Crew performed an expedited descent and air turn back to make a precautionary landing.
summary: Pilots and a mechanic incorrectly configured the aircraft by turning off Pack 1 instead of the inoperative Pack 2 during MEL review. This error caused a cabin altitude rise to 10,300 ft, requiring an emergency descent and hand-flying due to repeated autopilot disconnects, though the flight landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported engine vibration and RPM decay resulted in a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew experienced #2 engine vibration and loud banging, with N1 dropping to 45-55%, likely due to a maintenance issue. They diverted to ZZZ, secured the engine after ARFF inspection found no fire or damage, and taxied single-engine to the gate.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported a fume event during climb. The fumes dissipated initially but returned during final landing approach. All flight attendants experienced physiological symptoms.
summary: Flight crew and flight attendants on a ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight reported smelling fumes and experiencing headaches, watery eyes, and a weird taste during climb and landing. The odor dissipated at cruise altitude but returned during taxi and after deplaning, prompting the crew to contact maintenance for medical guidance and reporting procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported seeing traffic to follow, became distracted, then followed the wrong aircraft creating a NMAC.
summary: The pilot, while on downwind and final approach, lost visual contact with the traffic to follow due to cockpit distractions and misidentified another aircraft. The Tower Controller intervened by instructing an immediate right 360-degree turn, preventing a mid-air collision with the aircraft that was actually below.

synopsis: M-20 Pilot reported fuel starvation caused engine failure and resulted in an air turn back and off airport landing.
summary: The pilot returned to ZZZ due to unexpected fuel depletion, attempted three landings on runway XXR, and experienced an engine quit on final approach. The pilot attributed the forced desert landing to fuel starvation caused by inaccurate fuel gauges.

synopsis: Captain reported a cockpit side window shattered, resulting in an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: During climb through 19,000 feet, the PC24 crew heard a pop and discovered a crack in the outer ply of the left cockpit window. With no QRH procedure for this specific damage, they returned to ZZZ for a normal landing where emergency trucks were standing by.

synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with a MEDEVAC helicopter.
summary: A Mooney M20E pilot approaching ZZZ received a MEDEVAC transmission claiming the helicopter flew within 500 feet of the aircraft, though the pilot never saw the helicopter. The pilot suspects the conflict occurred during a 360-degree turn or approach west of ZZZ, potentially due to ground clutter or blind spots obscuring a lower-flying helicopter.

synopsis: ABQ Local Controller reported a departing aircraft was issued a traffic avoidance turn and altitude restriction, which resulted in entering a higher MVA.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller vectored Aircraft X away from Aircraft Y to avoid a potential NMAC after Aircraft X crossed hold lines without acknowledging a Line Up And Wait instruction. The controller issued a late turn and altitude restriction, resulting in a sloppy climb and deviation from the SID, which management later criticized despite the controller's intent to prevent a collision.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: TPA TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict between an aircraft climbing out of SPG and an aircraft on approach to Runway 36 at PIE airport.
summary: SPG Tower cleared Aircraft X for a VFR GPS Runway 7 missed approach without coordination, causing it to turn directly into Aircraft Y at 2,000 feet on base to Runway 36 at PIE. The controller issued a traffic alert and broke Aircraft Y off approach as the aircraft passed 1.25 miles apart at the same altitude in opposite directions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported poor coordination leading to an aircraft flying towards a higher MIA, Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: A Stockton Controller requested a direct routing to MLF at 12,000 feet for Aircraft X, which the reporter approved despite the route approaching terrain with 13,000-foot minimums. The incident highlights a failure to coordinate terrain clearance, prompting a recommendation to verify routes and clarify instructions to avoid similar risks.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Monterey Tower Controller reported a visibility issue with trees blocking the view of certain spots at MRY airport.
summary: Air traffic controllers at Monterey Airport reported that trees obstruct the tower's view of FBO ramps, the southeast ramp, and left base to Runway 28L/R. This blockage prevents controllers from seeing aircraft and vehicles, creating potential conflicts, delaying traffic flow, and hindering the issuance of control instructions.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a momentary Radio Altimeter flag enunciated during approach on the First Officer's Radio Altimeter. Flight continued to a safe landing.
summary: During approach to IAH Runway 26L, a momentary RA flag appeared on the First Officer's side at 5,300 feet for five seconds while the Captain's side showed no failure. The flight continued uneventfully with no disruptions or errors.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Check Pilot reported an erroneous RA from the First Officer's radio altimeter while on approach to IAH. The Captain stated this was the second such event and in a different aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a First Officer-side RA flag lasting five seconds at 8,300 ft near ZAPPO intersection during approach to IAH 26L. The pilot noted this was the second occurrence on this approach in a different aircraft, with no other failures observed.

synopsis: First Officer reported a tripped circuit breaker caused a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ after a pop sound at FL330 tripped the Bat Bus Sect 2 circuit breaker, causing electrical and air conditioning warnings, loss of PA, and zero brake pressure. The Captain descended to FL250 for pressurization concerns and fuel burn, landing uneventfully with a potential reverse thrust issue.

synopsis: Air Carrier baggage ground personnel reported a personal bag arrived with a hand written 'fire arms' note and without required firearms forms attached.
summary: A baggage handler received an untagged bag with a handwritten "fire arms" label ten minutes before departure. Unable to contact on-duty management for guidance, the handler was forced to guess whether it was safe to load the bag.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported an erroneous radio altimeter after takeoff and during climb out from DFW. The First Officer also reported they had reviewed the NOTAMs referring to 5G interference at this location.
summary: During departure from DFW Runway 36R, the pilot reported erratic radar altimeter readings and a red RA between 550 and 1000 feet AGL, suspecting 5G interference. The system functioned normally thereafter, with no issues observed by the Captain or during the subsequent arrival.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported autopilot issues on final approach at DCA, citing 5G interference as possibly contributing.
summary: The pilot reported an uncommanded pitch-down and increased descent rate on final approach to DCA in strong tailwinds while on autopilot. After disconnecting the autopilot to stabilize the aircraft below 500 feet, the pilot attributed the event to potential ground facility or 5G interference.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported executing a go-around from short final at MEM after receiving a tail strike warning just before touchdown.
summary: The pilot received an unexplained tailstrike warning during the flare for Runway 36L at MEM and executed a go-around. The aircraft landed normally on the subsequent attempt, with the pilot suggesting the tailstrike warning system may require recalibration.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported returning to departure airport after experiencing loss of oil in the left engine.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine oil loss shortly after takeoff, causing rising temperatures, cockpit smoke, and an engine shutdown. They returned to the departure airport for a safe landing, where ground inspection confirmed oil on the wing and engine blades.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported operational difficulties at PDX related to restrictions in place due to the proximity of a 5G tower.
summary: The flight crew conducted ILS approaches at PDX in low visibility, missing the first attempt on 10L before landing on 10R after passing the FAF despite marginal RVR. The pilot attributed the inability to use autoland and increased workload to 5G tower interference and unclear ATIS visibility reports.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported during final descent being notified by F/A 4 that F/A 3 had lost consciousness temporarily due to fumes in the aft cabin. Upon gate arrival Captain submitted a fume report to Maintenance and Flight Attendant crew received Medical evaluation.
summary: During the approach to landing, a flight attendant reported a fumes event and a colleague feeling light-headed, though the flight crew smelled nothing. The aircraft landed safely, and post-flight medical advice required three flight attendants to be examined before returning to duty.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a fume event localized to the flight deck during initial climb which dissipated and resumed during descent. After troubleshooting and conferring with Maintenance the flight continued to destination.
summary: The flight crew detected a strong "dirty sock" odor in the cockpit shortly after takeoff and again during descent at FL 230, likely linked to recent APU auto-shutdowns. They used oxygen intermittently and turned off PACK 1, but the odor persisted until dissipating before landing at ZZZ1.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported radio altimeter anomalies climbing out of ILM, citing 5G interference as the possible cause of the event.
summary: The pilot reported unreliable Radio Altimeter readings and a GPWS terrain caution shortly after takeoff from Runway 35 at ILM. The alert resolved above 500 feet, likely due to 5G interference, and the flight continued safely with no further issues.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the Captain experienced loss of flight director and ILS on approach to EWR, resulting in a low altitude alert from ATC.
summary: During an ILS approach to EWR 4R, the Captain lost flight director and ILS data at 900 feet, causing a low and right deviation. The First Officer provided situational awareness while the Captain corrected the flight path, resulting in a stable, uneventful landing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported autoflight anomalies on approach to BOS, citing 5G interference with the radio altimeter as the possible cause.
summary: The flight crew executed a Cat 3 autoland in marginal weather but manually disconnected the autopilot at 80–100 ft after an unexplained red autoland light illuminated. The crew suspects 5G interference caused a radar altimeter discrepancy, though the aircraft landed safely without notifying ATC due to tower workload.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported loss of the green hydraulic system resulted in a diversion and precautionary landing.
summary: During preflight, a Teflon seal discrepancy was found on the #1 engine, and later at FL360, a green hydraulic reservoir low level warning indicated a leak. The crew diverted to ZZZ, performed a gravity gear extension, and landed safely on Runway XXL using emergency brakes after confirming fluid under the #1 engine.

synopsis: CL30 Captain reported that due to fatigue, lack of compliance during ice checks and deicing led to engine start problems as the engine fan was frozen in place.
summary: The fatigued pilot and co-pilot attempted to start engines in freezing, windy conditions but received Amber FADEC CAS messages and N1 dashes. Inspection revealed ice had frozen the N1 fan blades to the nacelle, causing the failure after the crew delayed de-winterizing due to fatigue and schedule pressure.

synopsis: Captain reported aircraft failed to pressurized correctly on climb and elected to perform an air turn back and precautionary landing at departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZ airport during climb due to a high-pitched noise and abnormal pressurization readings caused by an uninstalled potable water service cap. The leak was identified in the lavatory, leading to a safe landing and subsequent aircraft swap.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported being notified by flight attendants during departure climb of a persistent odor. Flight crew determined odor was not dissipating and elected to execute a safe air return.
summary: The pilot and flight attendants detected a strange odor during takeoff that persisted at 7,000 feet, prompting a return to ZZZ. The reporter attributed the incident to poor aircraft design allowing contaminated air into the cabin and cockpit.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported being notified by the flight attendants of a 'chemical/exhaust' odor after departure. The fumes dissipated after a brief period only to resume during descent. Flight Attendants received medical evaluation after the flight.
summary: Flight crew and flight attendants experienced chemical and exhaust odors in the cabin and cockpit during descent and idle thrust after takeoff from ZZZ. The aircraft was taken out of service and cancelled due to crew medical evaluations, with the pilot suspecting latent fluids steamed off by bleed air following 24 hours of rain.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a single terrain warning during initial climb despite being well clear of terrain. Captain cited 5G interference as possibly contributing.
summary: A pilot reported a single terrain warning during a climb to 3,200 ft after being cleared direct WAVEY from JFK runway 4L. The crew took no evasive action as the warning ceased, suspecting a false alarm caused by a 5G event.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported a loss of directional control while attempting to park on an icy ramp area with nil braking action. The aircraft slid uncontrolled during a turn while taxiing, but stopped short of ground equipment.
summary: Pilots lost steering and braking control on an icy, water-covered ramp with strong tailwinds while attempting to park, sliding toward ground equipment. After stopping short of impact, the crew deplaned via the right door, waited for sanding and equipment removal, then successfully repositioned the aircraft with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving an alert for the air/ground switch on final approach to OAK.
summary: The crew received a LG AIR/GND FAIL message on final for Runway 28R, prompting a go-around to land on Runway 30 with gear down and flaps 45. Systems functioned normally after landing, and the pilot attributed the event to a faulty air/ground sensor.

synopsis: Air carrier flight attendants reported a fumes event during pre-flight which dissipated initially and resumed during descent. Flight attendants reported experiencing physiological symptoms to the Captain who requested medical assistance and submitted a fumes report to maintenance at gate arrival.
summary: Flight attendants and pilots experienced a strong musty odor and symptoms like dizziness and headaches during a flight, suspecting fumes from a dirty air conditioning filter. The crew was medically tested for carbon monoxide with negative results, though symptoms persisted, prompting recommendations for immediate maintenance and cabin detectors.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Student Pilot on a solo cross-country flight reported an NMAC with another aircraft seen on ADS-B. The reporter was receiving flight following from ATC but had inadvertently turned down the volume of the radio and missed the traffic advisory for the aircraft.
summary: A student pilot on a solo VFR flight missed ATC traffic advisories due to adjusting the wrong radio volume knob, fast controller speech, and failure to report communication difficulties. The pilot used ADS-B In to visually acquire and climb above converging traffic, avoiding a collision despite the communication breakdown.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action during an NMAC with another aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported flying in close proximity to another aircraft approaching from the opposite direction. An evasive maneuver was executed to avoid contact.

synopsis: First Officer reported a critical ground conflict event during takeoff roll with a landing aircraft on an intersecting runway. Pilot immediately rejected takeoff when tower cancelled takeoff clearance.
summary: Pilots received an immediate takeoff clearance for Runway 23 but were instructed to abort 20-30 seconds into the roll after a light transport jet landed on Runway 14 and crossed their path. The reporter attributed the incident to controller saturation during a runway change from 14 to 23.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Pilot reported smoke in the cockpit during a training flight. Flight Crew turned off all electrical power and the smoke dissipated. The Flight Crew elected to return to the departure airport and make a precautionary landing.
summary: Pilots experienced electrical smoke during a simulated emergency descent over ZZZ and turned off all systems to clear it. They returned to ZZZ1 for an uneventful landing without ADSB-out or transponder due to the electrical shutdown.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZNY Center Controller reported a perceived lack of training for space launch procedures and also stated the hazard areas implemented during these events are insufficient.
summary: ZNY oceanic controllers received a launch package for ALTRV J0001 containing a Transitional Hazard Area (THA) in the non-radar environment, despite THAs being prohibited there due to separation limitations. The reporter cites a lack of specific training, procedures, and clear risk assumption guidance for non-radar space operations as the cause of this unsafe condition.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported witnessing what they determined to be an inappropriate deicing procedure.
summary: A pilot at ZZZ observed a contractor deicing a departing aircraft during a winter storm using a one-person, one-truck operation. The pilot reported concern that the operator applied Type 1 and Type 4 fluids sequentially on each section, potentially contaminating the anti-ice fluid and reducing holdover time.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from tower during visual approach while in the process of correcting to glidepath.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer flew a busy RNAV approach to Runway XXL in overcast conditions with a tailwind. They descended low on the glidepath due to task saturation and using Level Change instead of VNAV, but corrected the descent after a tower altitude check and landed safely.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported while on the MARCS 1 STAR and RNAV (RNP) 22 approach into SAT the GPWS Warning activated just as the pilots noticed a nearby ground object. The pilot stated the object is poorly marked on the approach chart and should be corrected.
summary: The flight crew flying an RNAV (RNP) 22 approach at SAT received a GPWS obstacle call while descending to 1,700 feet near the ZIGDA fix during a visual approach. The crew climbed back to 2,100 feet and landed safely, attributing the warning to a charted obstacle hidden by approach course arrows that was not readily evident on the plan view.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to Runway 24R at LAX, and recommended increased spacing.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence on short final to LAX Runway 24R, triggering EICAS messages and a missed approach discussion. They continued the visual hand-flown landing, after which ADS probe failure messages appeared, likely caused by turbulence-induced sensor disagreement.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC while entering the traffic pattern at a non-towered airport. Pilot maneuvered past the aircraft and landed.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair conflict while approaching Runway 30 at 1,100 feet with a light aircraft that was wide on downwind. A TCAS warning prompted the pilot to maneuver lower and right, passing 100 feet below and 300 feet right of the other aircraft before landing safely.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Small jet flight crew reported loss of directional control during taxi in snowy and icy conditions at BED that resulted in an excursion off the taxiway.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing at BED after landing, the aircraft slid sideways onto snow and grass during a turn from a snow-covered to a swept-but-unsanded taxiway. The slow taxi speed prevented damage, and after ground personnel towed the aircraft and a mechanic verified no damage, it returned to duty the next day.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported landing gear mechanical and electrical issues while in the traffic pattern and made a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot requested priority handling due to a gear mechanical and electrical failure. Despite three green down lights, the gear unsafe light and horn remained active, though the aircraft landed safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor providing instruction reported taking evasive action to avoid collision with another aircraft turning base leg while on final approach.
summary: An instructor and student conducting a practice approach near ZZZ experienced a near-miss when another aircraft descended rapidly on top of them. The intruder turned off course for spacing after the instructor contacted Tower, coming within 20 feet before avoiding a collision.

synopsis: Air Taxi flight crew reported during takeoff the nose wheel was vibrating due to the nose gear pin not secured so they rejected the take off and taxied back to the FBO.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff at 40 knots due to nose-wheel vibration caused by an unsecured gear pin. The crew re-secured the pin, taxied back to the FBO, and maintenance replaced the damaged tire.

synopsis: Pilot of a light single engine aircraft reported a bounced landing at higher than normal speed resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft bounced at a slightly higher than normal speed upon landing. An over-correction caused the aircraft to leave the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor on final approach to a non-towered airport reported initiating a go around due to a departing aircraft on the runway.
summary: An instructor and student in Aircraft X executed a go-around during night arrival at ZZZ due to Aircraft Y initiating takeoff on the same runway without prior communication. The conflict occurred on short final, requiring evasive action to the right, but resulted in no collision and both flights continued safely.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported they allowed an aircraft conducting a go around to fly at an altitude below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: A controller allowed a pilot to maintain 1,500 feet below the 2,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude during a VFR approach attempt after a go-around. The pilot subsequently failed to join the final approach and landed on an opposite runway, prompting the controller to cite improper coordination and altitude clearance as causes.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported on departure from IAH the Captain's side Radio Altimeter failed for about 15 seconds.
summary: The crew observed a temporary amber Radio Altimeter flag on the Captain's PFD 10 to 20 seconds after takeoff, while the First Officer's unit remained normal. The flag cleared after 15 seconds, the flight continued without incident, and the anomaly was reported to maintenance and dispatch.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier First Officer reported their Radio Altimeter malfunctioned while on downwind to MSY.
summary: During the downwind approach to MSY, the First Officer's radar altimeter displayed incorrect readings and triggered a warning horn below 1,000 ft until landing gear deployment. Maintenance found no faults but suggested 5G interference caused the irregular indications.

synopsis: Air Carrier ramp personnel reported refusing supervisor's order to clean up liquid on Class 9 Hazmat package. Ramp agent's refusal was based on company Hazmat cleanup policy which requires specific training to do so.
summary: Ramp service employees refused an Area Manager's aggressive order to clean a Class 9 Hazmat spill in Pit 3 of an arrival aircraft using only paper towels and Clorox wipes. The crew cited lack of proper PPE and training, noting the directive violated safety policies, which caused a departure delay until a Shop Steward intervened.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported receiving Terrain Alerts on downwind on two approaches even though they were at altitudes above terrain and as assigned from ATC. The alerts caused an unstable approach requiring a go around.
summary: The flight crew received false EGPWS terrain alerts during a night visual approach to Runway XXL, likely caused by an IRS revert message or 5G interference. They executed recovery procedures, terminated the unstable approach, and landed safely after ATC confirmed no actual terrain existed.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported they were task saturated and their desk has a heavy workload. Dispatcher expressed concern that 5G-related NOTAMs and additional flights increase the workload.
summary: A dispatcher reported that Desk X on the AM shift was task-saturated due to high flight volume, 5G NOTAMs, weather, and ZZZ Functional Check Flights. The reporter sent a help alert, fearing potential loss of operational control during irregular operations and recommending task reduction to prevent failure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported sliding when parking the aircraft due to water and slush being on the ground surface at PWM airport.
summary: The pilot reported an uncontrolled deceleration while taxiing to a gate at PWM on a slush-covered ramp, requiring thrust reversers to stop. The incident was caused by the airport's failure to treat the icy surface or notify the crew of the hazard, though no damage occurred.

synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert on arrival into DEN after having to override automation in an attempt to comply with ATC instructions that kept them high on approach.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 17R at Denver, the crew overshot the centerline and triggered bank and low altitude warnings due to high speed, altitude, and task saturation. The Captain took control to correct the flight path, and the aircraft was stabilized by 1,000 feet for a safe landing.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival into ATL in trail of a B747.
summary: During the CHPPR arrival into ATL, the crew encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding 747, causing abrupt rolls. After refusing a lower altitude, the crew demanded and received a heading offset from Atlanta Approach to avoid the turbulence, resolving the issue once the 747 passed.

synopsis: Light Transport aircraft First Officer reported receiving a TCAS RA during visual approach to Runway 36 to PIE airport. The TCAS RA was followed and was reportedly triggered by a VFR aircraft transiting below the TPA Class B airspace.
summary: The crew received a TCAS climb resolution advisory while vectored for a visual approach to Runway 36 at PIE. The pilot attributes the conflict to a VFR aircraft 500 feet below that likely initiated a climb, prompting a 300-400 foot climb before ATC cleared a descent to 3,000 feet.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of normal brakes on landing. The flight Crew ran QRH procedures and regained braking control to stop the aircraft and taxi off the active runway using differential braking.
summary: The flight crew experienced limited braking upon landing at ZZZ due to a 'Brakes Released' ECAM warning. They regained braking using yellow hydraulics, stopped on the runway, and were towed after inspection revealed a flat spot on tire #3.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a fume event during final descent which had a serious physiological affect on flight crew's clear thinking and coordination during landing. Captain debriefed with maintenance after a safe arrival and stated the fogginess was temporary.
summary: The flight crew encountered heavy fumes below 10,000 feet, causing cognitive impairment and delayed responses during approach and taxi. Despite switching air conditioning packs, the pilots landed safely but experienced lingering confusion, which the reporter attributed to potential oil over-servicing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being notified by the flight attendants of a fume event during descent. All flight attendants experienced physiological symptoms but no medical assistance was requested.
summary: After landing at ZZZ, the flight crew reported a fume event occurring shortly after passing 10,000 ft. on descent. All four flight attendants experienced symptoms including burning throat, dizziness, and nausea but declined medical assistance.

synopsis: Pilot reported technician failed to follow correct procedure when deactivating the WiFi. The procedure followed deactivated the hydraulic PTU, which was required for flight due to another MEL, resulting in an air turn back and precautionary landing.
summary: During preflight, a technician incorrectly locked the ACMP 2B circuit breaker while deferring an entertainment system issue, causing a HYD 2B INOP caution at 1,000 feet. The crew returned to ZZZ, where maintenance confirmed the error resulted from the technician following a misleading NEF guide hyperlink.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a stuck Press To Talk button hampered communications, requiring a divert and precautionary landing.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the flight crew experienced a total loss of radio communications due to a stuck PTT and pulsing static, forcing a diversion to ZZZ1. The crew maintained contact with ATC and Dispatch via a personal WiFi phone call and landed safely after coordinating with maintenance and cabin crew.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported excessive noise from a main cabin door in flight. The measure decibel level was or 107Db and was causing pain to the Flight Attendant.
summary: Flight attendants on aircraft X reported a loud noise from the left front door hinge area during four flights, caused by a missing metal piece confirmed by maintenance. The noise reached 107 decibels, preventing crew from hearing the 10,000-foot chime and causing hearing issues, with the repair delayed until end of day.

synopsis: Pilot reported losing the alternator on a ferry flight and landing NORDO.
summary: The pilot ferrying Aircraft X experienced an alternator failure and battery loss, resulting in a radio silence entry into ZZZ Class D airspace. After landing without tower contact, the pilot was initially told no flight plan existed, though this was later verified, and the aircraft remained for two days for repairs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported losing control of aircraft after landing when the aircraft hit a snow berm that hadn't been cleared off the runway correctly.
summary: The pilot of a charter flight landed on a snow-covered runway at ZZZ, where the left main wheel struck an off-center berm, causing the aircraft to yaw 270 degrees and stop in the snow. Subsequent taxiing resulted in the right propeller contacting a ramp berm, and the left wing flap became frozen in the retracted position due to trapped snow.

synopsis: Technician reported not complying with MEL procedures for engine anti ice deferral, resulting in a rejected take off and a return to the gate for maintenance actions.
summary: A mechanic servicing Aircraft X's right engine mistakenly disconnected the anti-ice valve cannon plug instead of the TAI pressure switch due to distraction from incoming calls. This error caused an EICAS warning requiring a return to the gate for correction before the flight completed its journey to ZZZ.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude due to an incorrect readback of the controller's clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a climb clearance to 14,000 feet for a departing jet, but misheard the pilot's readback regarding a crossing restriction at 7,000 feet. The controller later reissued the correct altitude after realizing the error, attributing the incident to distraction from VFR traffic and the pilot's failure to query the ambiguous clearance.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported during arrival to MSY the gear position disagreement lights illuminated and aural warning occurred and continued until landing gear was lowered. The First Officer's Radio Altimeter had erratic indications.
summary: During descent on RYTHM4 to MSY, the crew experienced intermittent gear disagreement warnings and erratic First Officer radio altimeter indications below 1,000 feet. These false alerts ceased when landing gear was lowered at 3,000 feet, and subsequent maintenance diagnostics recorded no faults.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier pilot taxiing at night in IAH reported turning at the wrong spot due to lack of painted taxi lanes on the pavement.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X at IAH night taxi reported a potential runway incursion risk while following Ground Control instructions to join Taxiway WB from NC. The incident occurred due to a lack of painted taxi lines and inadequate nose taxi lighting, which obscured the hard surface and created uncertainty about the aircraft's position.

synopsis: Air carrier Lead Ramp personnel reported a communication breakdown between Ramp personnel and Ramp Assistant Manager regarding the clean up of a Hazmat class 9 spill in pit 3. During the resolution of the clean up issue, the excess gate check bags were loaded in pit 3 without knowledge of clean up status.
summary: A ground crew member reported a Class 9 Hazmat spill in Pit 3, where an Assistant Manager ordered the crew to clean it despite supervisor instructions to wait. Consequently, bags were loaded into the contaminated pit after the rear hold filled, while customers boarded unaware of the hazard.

synopsis: A320 pilot reported a short-duration overspeed occurred in cruise flight, and cited wake turbulence as the probable cause.
summary: During cruise, wake turbulence caused the aircraft to exceed speed limits, reaching Mach 0.83 for three seconds. The pilot noted this is a common occurrence that can only be addressed after the event by changing altitude or flight path.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported during approach that erroneous altitude and RA warnings continued until touchdown at MEM, citing possible 5G interference.
summary: The crew received continuous erroneous EGPWS warnings and intermittent RA flags on both PFDs while on vectors for approach 18R at Memphis with autopilots engaged. The reporter suspects 5G interference caused the alerts, which persisted from the river crossing to touchdown.

synopsis: LJ-70 Captain reported a fume event during takeoff accompanied by a Cabin Duct Overheat CAS message. Flight crew executed a safe air return.
summary: The crew experienced a cabin duct overheat warning during takeoff from ZZZ, likely caused by bleed air. They returned to the airport, burned fuel while circling, and noted that landing configuration could have achieved similar fuel burn rates while remaining below 200 knots in Class D airspace.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported that the Flight Attendants were having difficulty closing the main cabin door. After contacting Maintenance Control, Contract Maintenance Technicians discovered the ice breaker cable detached and broken.
summary: The Captain and Flight Attendants on Aircraft X could not close the main cabin door during pre-departure. Maintenance eventually found a snapped Ice Breaker Cable, correcting a recurring safety issue that previous "ops test good" clearances had missed.

synopsis: Pilot reported receiving several MFD error messages during departure from GSO and cited possible 5G interference as contributing.
summary: The pilot reported a 5G interference incident during takeoff from GSO in low IFR conditions, which triggered amber RA, APPR2 NOT AVAIL, and VA DOOM messages. The FAA later noted the event was not recorded in the maintenance logbook, prompting the pilot to submit a report and review company 5G guidance.

synopsis: Flight attendants reported during the flight they heard a noise emanating from the area by the door and notified the Flight Crew. The cause of the noise was not confirmed.
summary: Cabin crew reported a forward service door that initially failed to seal properly on Aircraft X, later producing whistling and loud vibrations during ascent and descent. Although pilots dismissed the noise as a loose rubber piece, maintenance later declared the aircraft unairworthy and grounded it after the crew alerted an operations agent.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported no engine response to throttle movement and returned to land immediately at departure airport.
summary: During student training, an instructor managed an engine that failed to idle, requesting priority handling from ZZZ Approach. The engine was secured on final approach for a safe landing, resulting in no injuries but requiring aircraft grounding and instructor re-evaluation.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being notified by Flight Attendant of a fume event during descent. After gate arrival Captain entered a fume event in the AML, submitted a fume report, and notified appropriate personnel.
summary: During descent through 12,000 ft, the flight crew and a flight attendant detected a sweet, pungent odor in the forward cabin and cockpit. The pilot logged the incident and notified maintenance and dispatch upon arrival, with no passengers reporting effects.

synopsis: An air carrier Flight Attendant reported an inflight fume event during cabin service. Reporter experienced physiological symptoms which caused her to vomit twice during taxi to gate.
summary: A flight attendant experienced dizziness, shortness of breath, and vomiting during final descent and taxi due to a strong cabin odor. Fear of managerial retribution prevented the crew member from reporting the incident immediately, though they intended to file a report later.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC with another aircraft that was flying in the traffic pattern for an intersecting runway when the opposite runway was in use.
summary: The reporter and a pilot of Aircraft Y experienced two near-misses at ZZZ Airport while the latter operated on a crossing runway against the designated flow. The reporter attributes the conflicts to the other pilot's hazardous attitude and admits their own poor judgment for not departing the area sooner.

synopsis: C172 pilot trainee reported a ground conflict during the landing roll out. As the trainee and instructor landed, a single engine turboprop landed while the trainee was still on the runway. The instructor took control of the aircraft and exited quickly out of the turboprop's way. There was no communication after landing with the conflicting turboprop aircraft.
summary: During a training descent into ZZZ, the pilot and instructor observed Aircraft Y extending its downwind and closing rapidly on final due to a 25-knot headwind. After landing, a traffic alert revealed Aircraft Y only 1,000–1,500 feet behind, prompting the instructor to expedite the runway exit to maintain separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported an electrical failure while en route that affected the operation of the landing gear and made communications difficult. The pilot was in contact with ATC and a gear up landing was accomplished.
summary: A pilot experienced a total electrical failure during the cruise and approach phases of a VFR flight, causing the autopilot, transponder, and avionics to shut down. The alternator failure prevented landing gear extension, forcing a gear-up landing at the destination airport after the pilot deemed emergency pumping impractical.

synopsis: Helicopter Pilot reported landing short of the runway in a field. Pilot states the aircraft was in wind gusts and did not have enough altitude to recover.
summary: During approach to airport ZZZ at 250 ft AGL, the helicopter descended too rapidly into a field short of the runway despite raising collective. The pilot attributed the incident to settling with power caused by wind gusts and insufficient altitude to correct.

synopsis: ZLC Center Controller reported an aircraft on the ILS approach to IDA airport entered holding with left turns instead of right turns and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for an ILS approach into IDA and issued a hold at WOTES at 080 without specifying a turn direction. The pilot subsequently made a non-standard left turn, clipped a terrain box, and was issued a climb to 090.

synopsis: Center Controller reported an airspace violation associated with presumed equipment issues.
summary: A radar controller in Sector XX, working without a D-side during high traffic, failed to verify a point-out acceptance for Aircraft Y, causing its data block to flash at the boundary near climbing Aircraft X. The controller attributed the error to excessive workload, inadequate staffing, and fatigue, resulting in an amended altitude clearance and traffic call.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported while vectoring a departing climbing aircraft it flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a climb to 5000 ft to Aircraft X, which subsequently entered a 025 Minimum Vector Altitude at 022, triggering a low altitude safety alert. The violation occurred because the Minimum Vector Altitude south of ZZZ1 was raised by 400 ft, and the aircraft did not perform as expected for its type.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported lack of lighting at JAN airport ramp area.
summary: A pilot reported a complete absence of ramp lighting at JAN, making the parking center line invisible and walkarounds dangerous due to tripping hazards. Ramp personnel stated they have requested lighting improvements since the station reopened, but the issue remains unaddressed.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a Hazmat cargo load configuration error which resulted in the collapse of two adjacent Lithium Ion battery pallets while enroute.
summary: The Captain and Relief Pilot identified stacking issues at pallet position RL, delaying departure until the Load Master fixed them. Post-landing, ground personnel discovered pallet SR collapsed into SL, revealing both positions contained hazardous lithium batteries.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a flight control system malfunction and hydraulics system quantity decreasing made flight control sluggish during cruise. The crew decided to return to the departure airport.
summary: During cruise at FL350, FLT CTRL SYS B failure caused additional system failures and hydraulic fluid loss, prompting a diversion to ZZZ. The crew performed an overweight landing with sluggish controls per QRH procedures and suggested updating the manual to address follow-on failures and priority handling requirements.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported a Flight Attendant was injured during a wake turbulence encounter on descent into SEA in trail of an A380.
summary: The crew descended from FL340 to FL240 on the Chins arrival when they encountered residual wake turbulence from an unseen Airbus 380 at FL360. The turbulence injured a flight attendant, prompting a medical request, which the pilot attributed to a lack of ATC traffic advisories regarding the large aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a predictive wind shear warning passing 100 kts on the takeoff roll at IAD. They continued the takeoff because there were no secondary indications of wind shear.
summary: The flight crew received a predictive wind shear alert at approximately 100 knots during takeoff from Runway 30 in clear weather. They elected to continue the departure after assessing no actual shear or airspeed fluctuations, later agreeing to be more assertive with such alerts in the future.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported during push back operations at BOS airport, a lack of communication and visual with tug resulted in aircraft rolling into tug.
summary: During pushback, the tug disconnected and lost communication while maneuvering, causing it to strike the right engine nacelle after the First Officer applied brakes. A fuel smell was reported but determined to be from the aborted engine start, and the aircraft was towed back to the gate with no injuries.
