The controller lost altitude awareness due to Mode C quadruple Xing but coordinated with Sector 76 to expedite the aircraft above the refueling tract without losing separation.

synopsis: Local Controller in training issued a runway crossing clearance to another Local Controller and then issued a conflicting take off clearance resulting in an aborted take off. Pilot of conflicting takeoff clearance states I called the Tower and told them I was going to stop and wait until further advised.
summary: A solo SR20 pilot executing a takeoff on Runway 19L performed an emergency stop after an SR22 crossed the runway ahead. The incident was caused by a trainee controller's error in clearing the crossing aircraft without specifying it must wait behind the departing SR20.

synopsis: TRACON Controller with the approval of a supervisor, declared an emergency for a VFR aircraft requesting a SVFR clearance into an airport that was IFR, after official sunset.
summary: A non-IFR rated C172 pilot requested Special VFR into an IFR Class D airport after sunset, violating regulations. The Radar Controller coordinated an emergency deviation to allow the pilot to land safely at the Class D airport after the pilot encountered clouds while attempting alternatives.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reports a left engine bleed trip at FL390 that cannot be reset. Flight is able to continue to destination, avoiding icing conditions per the QRH.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the crew managed a number one engine Bleed Trip Off light by turning off the left pack and consulting Dispatch regarding icing risks. They completed the arrival in VMC after controllers reported no icing, though the crew recommended clearer QRH guidance on anti-icing system limitations.

synopsis: B737 Captain describes the discovery during preflight inspection of a cable broken in the slat asymmetry system. The cable was difficult to detect in the darkness.
summary: The Captain and First Officer discovered a broken slat asymmetry cable on the left wing during a night pre-flight walk-around. Maintenance repaired the defect on the ground, preventing an unsafe condition despite the inbound crew receiving no leading edge disagree indication.

synopsis: An A320 Captain discovered that although all of his Company's airbus aircraft have GPS installed, not all of the systems have been connected. The Flight Manual does not reflect this and appropriate MEL actions are not being accomplished.
summary: A Captain reported that eight Airbus aircraft have installed but disconnected GPS units, a discrepancy not documented on flight releases or MELs. Although Maintenance Control confirmed the specific aircraft was fixed prior to the flight, the reporter questioned the legality of dispatching crews on RNAV approaches without knowledge of the inoperative equipment.

synopsis: A pilot describes why Maintenance should have placarded the overhead Hydraulic's Panel for their own safety, while performing a brake change at their terminal gate.
summary: The flight crew was advised by maintenance at the gate that a brake change was in progress and hydraulics should not be used. The pilot recommended placing a placard on the cockpit hydraulic panel to prevent inadvertent pump activation and ensure mechanic safety.

synopsis: A B737 'A' Hydraulic System braided hose failed in cruise causing the loss of all fluid so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The crew diverted and declared an emergency after a braided hose failure caused loss of System A Hydraulics. They performed an overweight landing with inoperative nose wheel steering, requiring a tow to the gate before passengers and crew repositioned to continue the flight.

synopsis: An A320 crew detected an oil odor during preflight which dissipated but at cruise flight the odor again became very strong so that the crew donned oxygen until landing.
summary: Flight crew encountered overwhelming exhaust fumes on an aircraft that had been towed from a remote stand, suspecting an external air cart caused the issue. The smell persisted through takeoff and cruise, forcing pilots to don oxygen masks until landing, while the reporter attributed the recurring hazard to sub-standard contracted maintenance.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain experiences HYD1 LOW QT advisory message on the EICAS after takeoff. The quantity continues to decrease and the crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew received a HYD1 LOW QT advisory after takeoff and returned to land following a continued decrease in hydraulic quantity. Maintenance identified a leak in the number one hydraulic system after the uneventful emergency landing.

synopsis: ERJ170 First Officer reports two rejected takeoffs due to flight director and autothrottle disengagement during takeoff roll at 40 KTS. No aircraft anomalies can be discerned and the problem is thought to be related to the very strong gusting winds, a third attempt was made during without difficulty.
summary: The crew aborted two takeoffs due to flight director and autothrottle disengagement with master caution at 40 KTS in -3°C snow and 45-knot gusts. They attributed the false airspeed indications to wind gusts and successfully departed on the third attempt after waiting for calmer conditions.

synopsis: A Captain reports that one of their CRJ-200 aircraft had six maintenance resets of their Flaps Electronics Control Unit (FECU) for recurring Flaps Fail messages. The practice is allowed under an FAA Airworthiness Directive (AD) using a maintenance carry-over procedure that is similar to a deferral, but not actually deferred under any specific MEL Chapter.
summary: The pilot accepted an aircraft with a history of flap resets and deferred maintenance, but the flaps failed again at zero degrees during the approach. This caused an emergency landing using QRH procedures, leading the pilot to recommend grounding the aircraft until the recurring issue is resolved.

synopsis: A CRJ700 First Officer found that his O2 mask had an adhesive on the flow control knob causing the O2 to flow continuously when O2 compartment doors were open.
summary: During a preflight safety check, the First Officer found an oxygen mask with adhesive on the flow control knob, causing continuous flow and a 100 PSI loss. Mechanics could not repair the jammed knob or reset button, resulting in a flight delay and a report that the mask would have failed in flight.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew experiences high engine oil temperature at FL320 and diverts to the nearest suitable airport. The engine is shut down, an emergency is declared, and an uneventful landing ensues. A broken wire is found to have caused a false indication.
summary: The crew diverted and performed an overweight landing after a left engine oil temperature and pressure increase at FL320 triggered an in-flight shutdown. Mechanics later identified a broken wire as the cause, though no fire or leaks were observed.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Beech A36 closed the fuel tank selector valve in flight causing the engine to shutdown because he had been flying the BE36TC, whose fuel selector is opposite the A36. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed safely at a nearby field.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna A36 at 4,500 feet experienced an engine stoppage during leaning after inadvertently selecting the fuel valve to OFF due to confusion with a previous aircraft's valve layout. The pilot declared an emergency, landed safely at a nearby airport, and identified the incorrect fuel selector position as the cause.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot landed on DWH Runway 35L and did not hold short of the Runway 17L Safety Zone as a departing aircraft flew 75 FT overhead. ATC advised him of his incursion.
summary: The pilot, unfamiliar with the airport, crossed into the Runway 17L safety zone while contacting Ground after landing on Runway 35L, causing a departing aircraft to pass 75 feet overhead. The Tower Supervisor advised the pilot to stop completely before contacting Ground and wait for taxi instructions.

synopsis: A C421 cargo door opened on takeoff so the pilot attempted a straight ahead landing. Upon hearing a scraping sound, the pilot went around. After landing found propeller and fuselage damage from runway contact.
summary: During an IFR takeoff, the forward right cargo door opened, causing a right yaw and deceleration. The pilot elected to land straight ahead, resulting in propeller tip damage and gear door scraping, influenced by a prior anecdote about similar control difficulties.

synopsis: An aircraft on approach to SBA Runway 33R circled to provide distance from an aircraft landing Runway 15L. Then when the trainee Controller cleared them to land 33R they had near miss with another aircraft departing 15L.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision while landing at SBA on Runway 33R after a trainee controller cleared the approach despite a departing aircraft on a collision course. The crew executed evasive maneuvers to avoid the traffic, which passed within 150 feet, caused by the controller's failure to coordinate the landing and departure.

synopsis: A CL604 First Officer reported the NACO airport diagram for PWK has not been revised to reflect substantial changes in the southwestern-most quadrant of the airport.
summary: The flight crew reported that the FAA/NACO airport diagram for PWK is inaccurate regarding T-Hangars and Taxiway L, which now extends south of Runway 6/24. Ground controllers confirmed the chart has been wrong for months, but no NOTAMs were issued to alert operators of the layout differences.

synopsis: A Lead Mechanic and Line Mechanic were informed that a High Pressure Shut-off Valve (HPSOV) controller borrowed from another air carrier was not effective for the PW-4000 engine on their B767-300ER aircraft. The borrowed controller came from a GE CF-6 engine, but was physically interchangeable.
summary: A B767-300 mechanic installed an incorrect PRV controller (XXX-15 instead of XXX-16) while troubleshooting a right engine bleed issue, relying on supervisor approval despite noticing the part number mismatch. The fault persisted until the correct part was installed two days later, and the borrowed part was never deferred in the logbook.

synopsis: ZBW Controller voiced concern regarding the new 'Q' routing system that seems to contradict the HOST PDR/PDAR efforts. The reporter noted that the facility staff has been less than helpful in resolving this issue.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that the HOST system generated three incorrect flight proposals from BDL to IAD by applying conflicting PDR and PDAR routing instead of the new Q structure. Staff refused to create a necessary PDAR incorporating the HYPER3 arrival, leaving controllers to manage the routing errors caused by the system's blue HERT assignments.

synopsis: Tower Controller described the failure of an inbound air carrier to maneuver on a taxiway due to NIL braking action. Additional reporters, controllers, and pilots provided other variations of the incident.
summary: Local Control instructed a CRJ2 to exit Runway XXL onto closed Taxiway Bravo, which was approved for use by Airport Operations. The aircraft became perpendicular on the taxiway due to ice and nil braking action, despite a preceding SW4 exiting without issue.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an engine failure event when traffic at FL370 experienced clear air turbulence and requested an immediate descent to re-start the engine. The report indicated that ATC's follow up PIREP actions was inadequate.
summary: A DC87 pilot encountered extreme mountain wave turbulence at FL370, causing altitude fluctuations and a #1 engine flameout. The pilot descended to FL310 to attempt a restart but remained unable to recover the engine, proceeding to destination without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an airspace incursion event into an adjacent Center sector when departure traffic, without a transponder, went unnoticed by the reporter after initially being RADAR identified as a primary target off the runway.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller forgot to instruct an A320 pilot to activate the transponder during departure, causing the aircraft to remain a primary target. The pilot later verified frequency, turned on the transponder at 15,000 FT beyond the airspace boundary, and was handed off to Center.

synopsis: B737-300 Flight Crew experiences an AUTO Fail with a green STBY light climbing through 5000 feet. The QRH is consulted and the crew continues climbing with normal pressurization indications except for the cabin indicating a descent. At 13000 feet the First Officer believes he is experiencing hypoxia and dons his oxygen mask and noses over. Flight returns to departure airport uneventfully.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a dual pressure control failure during climb, indicated by conflicting gauges and a misleading green STBY light. The First Officer felt hypoxia symptoms at 13,000 feet, prompting an immediate descent to 10,000 feet and an uneventful return to the departure airport.

synopsis: A Captain reports he found the left overwing emergency exit slide panel release pins painted over during a preflight of an A320 aircraft.
summary: During preflight, the Captain and First Officer discovered paint covering two of three left overwing emergency slide release pins, which Maintenance subsequently removed. The crew reported that Maintenance claimed the pins were never painted, prompting a recommendation to improve communication regarding Engineering Order 25-YYY and Alert Bulletin XXX.

synopsis: A CE560 flight crew disagrees on what altitude the autopilot can be engaged at (500 or 1,000 FT) after takeoff on the RUUDY 4 at TEB. When the autopilot will not engage at 1,000 FT a rapid manual level off produces oscillations above and below 1,500 FT. The autopilot engages normally once level at 1,500 FT.
summary: During a CJ3 departure from TEB, the pilot flying attempted to engage the autopilot at 500 feet, believing the 1,000-foot limitation applied only enroute. The autopilot failed to engage, causing a momentary altitude excursion and high workload until it was successfully engaged after flap retraction.

synopsis: A CRJ200 CAS alerted FLAPS FAIL at 0 while on approach, so a go-around was executed and the QRH complied with before landing. The aircraft had a maintenance history of flap faults.
summary: The crew experienced a flap failure at zero flaps during approach, prompting an emergency declaration and a go-around to comply with the QRH. The aircraft landed safely with no further incident, though maintenance history indicates previous flap failure occurrences.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic, after forgetting to set the hand brake, describes a chain of events that contributed to his de-icing truck rolling into the fuselage nose section of a company B737-800 aircraft.
summary: A deicing technician operating a truck at a B737-800 forgot to set the hand brake before exiting the vehicle, causing it to roll forward and strike the aircraft. The incident resulted from a combination of a new four-truck procedure, equipment delays, and the technician's failure to secure the truck during an unplanned hold.

synopsis: Enroute controllers and flight crew describe a conflict event in which an ATC issued crossing restriction was not achieved. The reporters provided multiple perspectives on the circumstances experienced.
summary: A B737 descended to FL340 instead of the cleared FL360 due to a pilot FMS input error and a controller's failure to catch the incorrect readback, creating a conflict with a DC10 at FL340. Vectors were issued to separate the aircraft, which were 2-3 miles apart at the same altitude.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described an opposite direction conflict, reportedly due to the Controller's inability to communicate with either aircraft. Other information indicates the possibility of wrong standby frequency assignments.
summary: Air traffic controllers in the W and S sectors lost communication with a CRJ2 and CRJ7 converging head-on at 6,000 feet due to a frequency error. The aircraft passed within two miles at the same altitude before the W sector issued blind instructions, which were not followed until the conflict resolved.

synopsis: A First Officer reports about a Captain's frustration with a Line Mechanic who was sent out to their gate to determine the cause of a fresh fluid stream on the belly and lower tail surface of their A320 aircraft. Company Mechanic did not have any training or experience on Airbus aircraft.
summary: Flight crew of an Airbus A320 identified a hydraulic leak and an untrained mechanic who incorrectly assessed the fluid and lacked Airbus knowledge. Maintenance Control intervened to guide proper testing, confirming the leak resulted from over-servicing, allowing the aircraft to depart after a delayed release.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew reported a wake turbulence encounter that caused minor injuries to two flight attendants.
summary: During cruise at FL370 west of MLF, a pilot and two flight attendants encountered momentary moderate clear air turbulence suggestive of wake turbulence. The event caused back and elbow injuries to the flight attendants, who were not immediately reported to the cockpit, requiring one to occupy a passenger seat for landing.

synopsis: DC-8 flight crew described encountering a severe mountain wave and flight upset event that resulted in an engine failure and ATC's initiation of an emergency declaration.
summary: The crew encountered severe mountain waves at 37,000 feet, causing a flight upset and a compressor stall that hung Engine #1. After an unsuccessful restart attempt, they continued a 3-engine cruise to 31,000 feet and landed safely, though ATC had declared an emergency on their behalf.

synopsis: A B767-300 leading edge slat sensor malfunctioned after takeoff with the aircraft cleaned up, but because of the LE SLAT Assymetry EICAS warning an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer flew the aircraft, which returned to the departure airport after an LE Slat Asymmetry EICAS message appeared during flap retraction. An emergency was declared for the overweight landing, but the aircraft was deemed safe after inspection and the crew changed planes to proceed to their destination.

synopsis: A Line Technician, Avionics Technician, and a Maintenance Controller report about conflicting information between their Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) and the Airbus Maintenance Manual regarding the correct Cabin Intercommunication DATA System (CIDS) Directors they could use on an A320 aircraft with a CIDS Director ECAM fault and Evacuation Warning that would not silence.
summary: Technicians replaced CIDS Directors on an A320 after the crew reported an unsilenceable evacuation warning and ECAM faults. A conflict was discovered between the Illustrated Parts Catalog and a Maintenance Tip regarding correct part numbers, prompting an Engineering review while the aircraft was dispatched.

synopsis: After re-torquing the Captain's control column nut for an aileron clicking during actuation to the left and right at 3/4 scale deflection, Mechanic determines the item does not require an RII Inspection and the CRJ-200 aircraft is released. Aircraft is grounded several days later for the missed RII Inspection.
summary: A CRJ-200 was released from heavy maintenance with a Captain's aileron clicking discrepancy incorrectly logged as non-RII by the pilot and repair representative. The aircraft was later grounded for two hours after maintenance personnel discovered the missed RII item and inspected the control column.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports about a new and confusing sign-off process in their Procedures Manual (P/M) that does not allow a Mechanic, assigned a Periodic Service (P/S) Check Card, to sign-off multiple sequential tasks with the reference 'Previously Accomplished' (PA), after a previous Mechanic has already performed the same maintenance that is required in the assigned Task Cards.
summary: A mechanic signed off sequential tasks on Aircraft Y and Z as Previously Accomplished with a single signature, violating Procedures Manual XXXX.11.G which excludes this method. The error resulted from confusing manual requirements regarding how to document maintenance performed by a previous shift.

synopsis: C172 student with instructor was turning final for the right runway and experiences a NMAC with a PA28 on the ILS for the left runway. The instructor takes evasive action and the PA28 goes around.
summary: An instructor and student in a training aircraft on final for touch-and-goes executed a rapid right turn and descent to avoid a Piper Cherokee drifting from the left runway. The near mid-air collision occurred because the Cherokee was executing a missed approach on the ILS while the training aircraft was cleared for landing.

synopsis: An airline pilot, recently reintroduced to general aviation and flying a light sport aircraft, wrongly assumed the GPS would warn him before he climbed into Class B airspace.
summary: A general aviation pilot flying VFR climbed to 3,500 feet and inadvertently entered Class B airspace, assuming the floor was at 4,000 feet. The incident occurred because the pilot over-relied on GPS warnings for forward airspace rather than vertical penetration, resulting in no traffic conflicts or harm.

synopsis: A BE58 pilot was given a late runway change vector while flying on autopilot with a GPS. The pilot became distracted after failing to select the new ILS frequency, which resulted in confusion and additional vectors.
summary: The pilot flying an ILS approach in IMC accepted a controller's unsolicited offer to switch runways, inadvertently capturing the wrong localizer due to automation dependency and confusion. This resulted in significant altitude deviations before the aircraft was finally stabilized on the correct approach just inside the final approach fix.

synopsis: A Gulfstream V pilot departed ASE south and the EGPWS terrain warning activated after the aircraft entered IMC around 12,000 FT with mountains top around 14,500 FT and a 15,700 FT MSA.
summary: The pilot departed Aspen in deteriorating weather, signing a waiver to climb VFR southeast over terrain instead of turning left. This decision caused the aircraft to enter clouds below the Minimum Safe Altitude, triggering EGPWS warnings and raising concerns about terrain clearance.

synopsis: SFO Controller described a possible rule infraction. Traffic cleared for take off on Runway 1L, rotated prior to the intersection of Runways 28L and 1L. Immediately after aircraft had departed Runway 28L, the reporter noting the rule covering this operation is somewhat vague.
summary: Local Control cleared a B762 for departure on Runway 28L and another aircraft for takeoff on Runway 01L, anticipating non-intersecting flight paths. The controller attributed the safety concern to the vagueness of projected flight paths and decided to strictly adhere to the two-minute separation rule instead of relying on performance projections.

synopsis: PBI Controller described a conflict event when IFR departure traffic had to be vectored off the SID to avoid descending VFR traffic, the reporter suggesting PBI be given a Class B to preclude future similar type events.
summary: An air traffic controller stopped Aircraft X at 7,000 feet and turned it off its RNAV departure to avoid a descending VFR aircraft, resulting in less than 3 miles separation from Aircraft Y. The controller accepted this loss of separation as the safer option and recommended upgrading PBI to Class Bravo airspace due to uncoordinated VFR traffic.

synopsis: LNK Controller voiced concern regarding a false 'Conflict Alert' apparently caused by a 'split target' and/or 'ghost/duplicate' target anomaly.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared an LR40 for departure from Runway 35 but received a Conflict Alert caused by a duplicate transponder beacon north of the airport. The system incorrectly associated the LR40's data tag with the duplicate beacon, creating a temporary distraction until the tag corrected itself on the actual aircraft.

synopsis: A B737 crew became distracted while discussing the windshear takeoff performance calculations at the same time ATC issued a line up and wait clearance and so took off without clearance.
summary: The flight crew of a departing aircraft took off without a takeoff clearance after misinterpreting a "line up and wait" instruction. The pilot attributed the error to task saturation from managing windshear data and expecting a clearance due to no other traffic.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported that signage on Taxiway C does not identify Taxiway B while taxiing in either direction.
summary: A pilot reported inadequate or missing taxiway signs at Charleston (CHS) Airport while taxiing between Taxiways B and C and the ramp. The reporter noted that turn signs were placed nonstandardly past intersections or were entirely absent, creating potential navigation hazards.

synopsis: The Captain of an international flight crew reported ongoing difficulties encountered when crew attempt to comply with poorly trained and uncertainly understood SOPs which are the result of a recent merger of two large air carriers.
summary: During a seven-hour flight, the Captain, First Officer, and Relief Pilot disagreed on new procedures due to conflicting training and a lack of written updates. The crew experienced confusion over checklist responses and altitude settings during the approach, leading to the Captain halting the debate to maintain safety.

synopsis: An A320 crew executed the escape maneuver after an EGPWS CAUTION, TERRAIN warning at 6,300 FT on a night visual to BOI Runway 28R ten miles from the airport near a 4,180 FT obstacle.
summary: During a night visual approach to 28R, the crew received a 'caution terrain' warning at 6,300 FT and climbed to 7,300 FT, overspeeding flaps by 10 knots. The Tower recleared them for a right downwind to 10L, and the overspeed was reported to Maintenance after landing.

synopsis: A B737 at 7,400 FT, descending, had a near miss on the PHL BOJID arrival and took evasive action in response to a TCAS RA from an aircraft apparently at the PHL 7,000 FT Class B ceiling.
summary: During a descent on the BOJID arrival, a TCAS RA occurred when an uncontrolled target aircraft climbed within 400 feet vertically of the reporting airliner. The First Officer executed a climb to 7,800 feet to resolve the conflict, while the controller noted the target's proximity to two airliners on the published STAR.

synopsis: An B767-300 CAPT INST TRANSFER BUS status message alerted while in cruise so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew received a 'CA INST TXFER BUS' message one hour after takeoff and returned to the departure airport. They declared an emergency for an overweight landing, touching down safely at 332,500 LBS, but were unable to contact Dispatch.

synopsis: A MD83 Captain questioned whether the aircraft should be permitted into RVSM airspace with the autopilot trim MEL'ed because in a turn the aircraft can potentially not hold altitude, and additionally a discrepancy exists between manuals about CAT II/III operations without the trim functioning.
summary: A pilot operating an aircraft with MEL 22-2 Autopilot Pitch Trim experienced altitude loss during a 90-degree turn at FL320 while being vectored. Manual intervention prevented significant deviation, prompting the pilot to recommend MEL changes regarding CAT II/III status and RVSM altitude restrictions.

synopsis: A Maintenance Manager reports he signed off the Maintenance Release for a Hawker-800 aircraft after assuming, and without verifying, that a Starter/Generator unit he had previously removed had been reinstalled on the aircraft's APU.
summary: The Maintenance Manager removed a seized APU starter/generator from a Hawker-800 but failed to verify its reinstallation before releasing the aircraft. The missing part was later found in the workshop, revealing the aircraft was sent to a vendor without the component due to the manager's assumption rather than verification.

synopsis: A Class B Tower Controller set the facility's altimeter at 29.60 with an actual altimeter of 30.60 and as a result issued an aircraft on final a low altitude alert when in fact the aircraft was on profile.
summary: The pilot received a low altitude alert from Tower during the ILS 10R final approach due to a 1-inch altimeter setting discrepancy between the crew (30.60) and controllers (29.60). The crew verified their instruments showed 600 feet AGL, continued to a full stop landing, and later questioned if a missed approach would have been safer.

synopsis: A BE40's thrust reversers and brakes were not available for activation until below 70 KTS, so the emergency brakes were used which caused tire failures. Squat switch malfunctions were suspected.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing on Runway 13, thrust reversers remained locked and normal brakes failed due to suspected flight mode squat switch malfunction. Emergency braking stopped the aircraft at the runway end with blown tires but no injuries, leading to squat switch replacement.

aircraft: Bombardier Learjet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a confused sequence event and potential conflict when a Lear was cleared for a Visual Approach to follow another Lear on final, but cut in front of the straight in traffic.
summary: A Developmental controller cleared a Learjet for a visual approach based on incorrect traffic sequencing, causing the pilot to follow the wrong aircraft. The Tower reported the Lear was turning base early, creating a separation issue that required immediate coordination to resolve.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Two STS controllers report a Runway 14 incursion at Taxiway A because of poor taxiway and runway signage.
summary: An aircraft taxied onto active Runway 14 without clearance due to confusing taxiway markings and signage at Santa Rosa Sonoma County Airport. The pilot deviation was intercepted by the Local Controller, who instructed the aircraft to exit the runway and report the incident.

synopsis: TEB Controller described a potential ground conflict when traffic exiting the runway initiated a 'U' turn toward the landing runway, the reporter directed a subsequent landing aircraft to stop on roll out.
summary: A C560 pilot made an unauthorized U-turn on Taxiway Q toward Runway 01 while a Gulfstream was landing, forcing the controller to order the Gulfstream to stop. Both aircraft exited safely, though the controller attributed the incident to the C560 pilot's confusion and poor decision-making.

synopsis: Enroute Controller experienced a loss of separation during multiple play book re-route procedures, the reports listing weather, non-familiar routing's, Data Block overlap, traffic complexity/volume as causal factors.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sectors 68 and 79 lost separation between Air Carrier X climbing to FL330 and Air Carrier Y descending to FL320 due to conflicting clearances and weather-induced reroutes. The Conflict Alert triggered late, resulting in a minimum separation of 800 feet and 3.8 miles before emergency vectors were issued.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a TCAS RA and filed NMAC involving landing Air Carrier traffic and an EMS helicopter passing behind to land at a near by hospital, the reporter indicated the helicopter had the landing traffic in sight.
summary: An ATC instructor and trainee managed a lifeguard helicopter and a B190 on final approach when the landing aircraft reported a Resolution Advisory. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the helicopter's refusal to follow standard airport procedures despite ATC instructions.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a potential conflict event between traffic cleared to land Runway 25R and traffic cleared off Runway 25L, but in fact was initiating a departure from Runway 25R that resulted in a go around and an aborted takeoff.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a Cessna to land Runway 25R and a Champ for a left crosswind departure from Runway 25L. When the Champ mistakenly departed Runway 25R, the controller sent the Cessna around, stopped the Champ's takeoff, and cleared it for an intersection departure from Runway 25R.

synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding the URET equipment noted that unless the described problem is resolved the value of URET as a safety tool is rendered useless.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a URET processing problem at Atlanta Approach where nearly all arrivals incorrectly displayed a blue route for the ERLIN9 arrival. This error rendered the color-coded safety tool useless for quickly identifying aircraft requiring routing changes to RMG4, creating a risk of controllers assuming incorrect flight paths.

synopsis: A MD11's control columns were mildly vibrating at cruise with no other indications. Both stall warning cannon plugs were found loose and when the left was connected, with the right disconnected, the vibration ceased.
summary: During cruise in a non-radar environment, both pilots experienced yoke vibration caused by loosely secured stick shaker cannon plugs on both yokes. The crew identified the loose connections, which triggered a 'Stall Warn Fail' alert, and left the plugs disconnected for maintenance to resolve the issue.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew expressed bewilderment as why an alpha character was attached to their flight number (call sign).
summary: The pilot queried Dispatch and ATC regarding an extra alpha character in their call sign, XXXC, which ATC confirmed was required to differentiate from similar call signs of other carriers. Although the Duty Manager initially feared FAA sanctions, the event concluded without incident after the Dispatch Manager explained the change was a standard safety measure to prevent clearance confusion.

synopsis: After a B737-700 returned to land because of an abnormal N1 indication on takeoff, maintenance found a T12 inlet temperature probe fault.
summary: The crew returned to the departure airport after N1 abnormal indications caused by a T12 malfunction. An overweight landing of 129,000 LBS was performed with a VSI sink of 50 FPM.

synopsis: A B737 Captain gave his First Officer aircraft control while he made a PA and the First Officer failed to monitor the aircraft's descent. They were 2,000 FT low crossing a KORRY 3 arrival constraint.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended a jet en route to LGA using VERT SPD mode with a strong tailwind. The crew crossed SKIPY 2,000 feet below the FL190 restriction due to divided attention and a breakdown in CRM while the Captain addressed passengers.

synopsis: ERJ170 Captain reports descending to 1900 feet prior to glide slope capture during the ILS Runway 05 at CYYZ after being cleared to 3000 feet until established cleared for the ILS.
summary: The flight crew on a ROKTO 3 arrival into CYYZ descended below the 3000-foot restriction at DULPA due to unclear chart labeling and conflicting approach plate information. ATC subsequently instructed them to level at 2000 feet and advised intercepting the glide slope at 3000 feet in the future.

synopsis: Corporate jet cleared for a Visual Approach in mountainous terrain and maneuvering for final was given what seemed to be contradictory instructions when transferred to the Tower, the reporter posing a number of questions regarding ATC's handling.
summary: The crew of a turbo-jet aircraft received a TCAS Resolution Advisory during a visual approach after Tower instructed them to align with the runway centerline, conflicting with a departing VFR Cessna 210. The crew complied with the advisory and landed safely, but the controller later incorrectly claimed they were not required to follow the advisory if they had the traffic in sight.

synopsis: An A319 departed LIT and encountered hail in heavy precipitation, which cracked the First Officer's window, damaged the radome, an engine pylon and the landing lights. The flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew departed LIT into a thunderstorm, encountering hail that cracked the First Officer's windshield and damaged the nosecone and engine pylon. Consequently, they diverted to an alternate airport for maintenance inspection after determining their altitude was restricted to FL230.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted WHEEL N/W STRG FAULT on approach so a go around was executed to comply with the QRH, an emergency was declared, and a normal landing completed on a snowy runway after which the aircraft was towed to the gate.
summary: The flight crew encountered a nose wheel steering fault during an ILS 35 approach in snow and low visibility. They declared an emergency, landed using differential braking, and were towed to the gate after maintenance confirmed the fault.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted WHEEL N/W STRG FAULT when the landing gear were extended, so a go around was executed to comply with the QRH, an emergency declared and a normal landing completed followed by a steering fault reset which allowed a normal taxi to the gate.
summary: The flight crew received a nose wheel steering fault during landing gear extension, prompting a go-around and emergency declaration. After landing and a system reset, steering returned to normal, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate with fire and rescue present.

synopsis: A CRJ200 CAS alerted FLAPS FAIL at flaps 14 during flap movement from 8 to 20. An emergency was declared, the QRH complied with and a normal landing followed.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced a flap system failure stopping at position 14 during approach to runway 6L, triggering a FLAPS FAIL message. After completing the QRH and declaring an emergency, the crew successfully executed an ILS 6L approach and landed normally with flaps set to 14.

synopsis: A SF340 engine developed high oil temperature during approach so an emergency was declared, a short approach requested while the oil remained below the red arc and a normal landing followed after which the engine was shutdown.
summary: The Captain and First Officer declared an emergency during approach due to rising #1 engine oil temperature nearing the red arc. They landed immediately, shut down the engine after touchdown when the gauge entered the red arc, and taxied to the gate without requiring ground services.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported taking evasive action, including a TCAS RA, during a near miss with an unreported helicopter at 1,300 FT on a four mile final to FLL Runway 9R.
summary: A pilot on an ILS final approach to Runway 09L observed a helicopter turning into their flight path at 300 feet below, triggering a TCAS climb resolution advisory. The crew climbed from 1,000 to 1,300 feet MSL to avoid the unannounced traffic, which passed beneath them before the pilot rejoined the glide path and landed safely.

synopsis: A B757 left engine hydraulic pump low pressure light illuminated so the pump was turned OFF and because the fluid continued decreasing the electric pump was also turned off to conserve fluid for gear and flap extension. An emergency was declared.
summary: The pilot reported a left engine hydraulic pump light and fluid loss during descent, prompting an emergency declaration. Although flaps and gear extended normally using the electric pump, nose steering was lost after landing, requiring a tow to the gate.

synopsis: A B737-400 ailerons became very sluggish and heavy in flight similar to manual reversion. An emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport where an actuator cable was found failed and the aileron feel sense unit was also replaced.
summary: The crew experienced a left turn and heavy, sluggish flight controls at FL260 due to a deployed left flight spoiler, likely caused by a feel/centering unit or electrical issue. They declared an emergency, diverted to a larger airport, and landed safely after following the jammed flight control procedure.

synopsis: When the altitude alert display stuck at 50,000 FT on initial climbout the flight crew of a B737-700 decided to continue the flight using FMS cruise altitude programming to maintain altitude in cruise and utilizing Vertical Speed Mode for the descent. When given a crossing altitude restriction on their descent they miscalculated the required Top of Descent point and crossed the restricted fix 10,000 FT high.
summary: Pilots encountered a stuck altitude selector displaying 50,000 feet during climbout, causing continuous alerts and loss of V-NAV descent tools. Distraction from the alerts and a late ATC crossing restriction led to an incorrect manual descent calculation, resulting in crossing a fix 10,000 feet high before a stable landing.

synopsis: G-V First Officer reports damage to the left wing tip during taxi in after landing on Runway 13 at HBV. Damage was caused by a dead bush along the taxiway.
summary: The crew taxied northwest after landing on Runway 13 and struck an unseen scrub bush near a reflective marker, causing damage to the left wingtip. The incident occurred because the bush was unlisted on airport diagrams or flight releases, prompting a recommendation to remove the obstruction and issue a NOTAM.

synopsis: A B757 potable water pump overheated during preflight filling the Cabin and eventually the Cockpit with noxious fumes causing all crew members to seek medical attention. A Maintenance Supervisor attempted to push the crew to fly the aircraft.
summary: The cockpit and cabin crew encountered strong electrical fumes from an overheating water system compressor pump during pre-flight, causing nausea and breathing difficulties for all crewmembers. After maintenance supervisors initially disputed the source, the crew refused to accept the aircraft, resulting in all personnel receiving medical treatment and the flight being cancelled.

synopsis: MD83 First Officer experiences an IRU fault during cruise which is corrected using QRH procedures. Fifteen minutes later the IRU fails completely. An emergency is declared and the flight continues to destination uneventfully.
summary: During cruise, a #2 IRU fault triggered subsequent failures of the copilot's displays, flight directors, and autopilot. The crew declared an emergency, hand-flew using VOR and standby compass, and executed a visual approach after receiving ATC vectors for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Two Line Mechanics report that a nose gear axle nut washer was not reinstalled on a B767-300 aircraft during a nose tire change at a terminal gate.
summary: A mechanic assisting with a nose tire change left the outer washer off the axle nut while rushing to another aircraft. Although no damage occurred, the mechanic signed off the job and subsequently removed and replaced the entire nose wheel and tire assembly per the Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports an MEL applied to an engine start valve on an MD-82 aircraft was improper. He also notes the known, loose, exposed electrical wiring for the start valve that were not capped or stowed inside the engine compartment prior to issuing the MEL, could have shorted or sparked and caused a fire.
summary: Mechanics performing a manual engine start on an MD-82 found exposed wiring in the engine compartment, though the MEL placard only addressed the start valve. Maintenance Control dismissed the hazard, leaving the wiring exposed and creating a potential fire risk despite the known issue.

synopsis: An Aircraft Inspector reports a maintenance practice has developed in their facility during C-Checks and become a 'NORM' when working on Fuel Systems. After an aircraft is defueled, Maintenance is started right away, without regard to the Fuel General Maintenance Practices and the Fire Safety Precautions listed in the Cessna 560XL Maintenance Manual Chapter 28.
summary: A mechanic reported that Cessna 560XL fuel system maintenance often violates safety manuals by using ungrounded plastic buckets and operating electrical carts near open fuel panels. The reporter attributes these risks to a company culture ignoring General Maintenance Practices and recommends refresher training and proper equipment to ensure compliance.

synopsis: A PA28 alternator switch physically failed on a night flight resulting in a battery drain from lights so after securing all power except radio the pilot could hear ATC but not transmit and was cleared to return to the airport.
summary: The pilot experienced an alternator switch failure during the approach phase, causing radio transmission loss due to battery drain from lights. After turning off lights to maintain communication, the pilot landed on Runway 31R following ATC instructions and parked safely.

synopsis: SR22 pilot discovers after a flight that she may have penetrated a law enforcement TFR earlier in the day. The FAA map did not display the TFR but a NOTAM did exist.
summary: The pilot flew solo from Illinois to an FBO between 2,500 and 2,900 feet, altering course for traffic in hazy conditions. Post-flight review revealed an unmarked TFR for a cadaver search below 3,000 feet, suggesting the pilot may have inadvertently entered the restricted area.

synopsis: King Air pilot reports low fuel indication on the fuel gauges during approach although the flight departed with sufficient fuel. An emergency is declared and a short cut is made on the approach along with an early descent, resulting in a low altitude alert from ATC. A normal landing ensues and post flight reveals faulty fuel gauges.
summary: The pilot flying and instructor pilot experienced rapidly dropping fuel gauges during a GPS approach, prompting an emergency declaration and a shortcut to the field. Post-landing checks confirmed the FMS fuel calculation was correct and the gauges were faulty, though the pilot noted a previous similar incident involved an actual fuel leak.

synopsis: Citabria pilot is cleared to Runway 25R via Taxiway's K and B at LVK. After the run up the pilot is cleared for takeoff on Runway 25R with a left crosswind departure. Upon advancing the throttle another aircraft is seen to be going around and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The pilot requested a left crosswind departure from 25R but received conflicting clearance from LVK Tower, which intended 25L. This misunderstanding caused a near-midair collision with an aircraft going around, forcing the pilot to abort the takeoff and accept an intersection departure from Delta.

synopsis: A SR20 had an incorrect nose landing gear installed which allowed the gear to rotate 180 degrees and during a nose wheel shimmy event the propeller struck the nose wheel pant.
summary: A pilot and student experienced severe nose gear shimmy during short field training landings, which worsened after a bounced landing. Upon returning home, they discovered the gear had turned 120 degrees into the prop arc, causing a strike and damage, potentially due to an incorrect gear design or excessive steering range.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports that the hazard beacons on the new wind turbine farms in the vicinity of Rumford and Berlin, NH are not visible with Night Vision Goggles.
summary: A pilot reported that new wind turbine farms near Rumford and Berlin, NH, are invisible through Night Vision Goggles because their beacons emit an incompatible spectrum. This visibility issue poses a potential hazard for military and HEMS operations, as the turbines are only detectable with the naked eye.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot departing SQL on a special VFR clearance reports inadvertently entering IMC and initially losing control. Control is regained using flight instruments and assistance from ATC is requested. With ATC assistance the reporter returns to VMC and a visual approach and landing is accomplished at SQL.
summary: A VFR pilot departed San Carlos in deteriorating conditions, entered a cloud with zero visibility, and became disoriented while attempting to return. The pilot stabilized the aircraft using instruments and, guided by Tower instructions, eventually regained visual reference and landed safely.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports entering IMC inadvertently at low altitude and requesting an IFR clearance from ATC. With the aid of another pilot ATC is quickly able to vector the reporter to visual conditions allowing the flight to continue to destination.
summary: The pilot and passenger departed HGR in VFR conditions but entered IMC while avoiding terrain warnings from towers near I-81. After requesting and receiving an IFR clearance from Harrisburg Approach, the pilot climbed to 2,000 feet and returned to VFR without incident.

synopsis: Three mechanics report a required spacer was not installed at the aft cap position on the aft side of a Bell 206L-3 helicopter's engine gearbox case during an engine change, outside, at night, in cold temperatures with limited lighting and communication terminology issues.
summary: During an engine replacement on a Bell 206L-3 helicopter, mechanics failed to install a freewheeling unit spacer due to miscommunication and lack of training on the new airframe. The aircraft was removed from service until the missing spacer was ordered and installed following a visual inspection.

synopsis: Enroute D-Side Controller described a confused hand off event when accepting RADAR on a VFR target when in fact the hand off involved an IFR aircraft requesting climb, the event resulting in an airspace incursion.
summary: An air traffic controller coordinated a handoff for a VFR aircraft without a call sign, assuming it was a nearby target. The aircraft lacked a flight plan in the NAS, delaying its climb to FL280 until the controller manually transferred data to the correct sector.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event apparently a result of confused and incomplete coordination between sectors.
summary: Sector X and Y controllers managed an E120 and C172 during descent, resulting in a 2.6-mile, 500-foot proximity. The reporter attributed the conflict to Sector Y's lack of awareness regarding the C172's control transfer and off-route status, citing poor communication.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an unauthorized airspace entry event when thinking one altitude but assigning another.
summary: A Radar Controller in Sector X mistakenly cleared an A319 to FL290 instead of FL260 while simultaneously typing a handoff command to Sector Y. Sector Y accepted the handoff at FL220, recognized the error, and allowed the climb to continue as no traffic conflict existed.

synopsis: TRACON Controller failed to note an incorrect altitude assignment read back resulting in an airspace infraction, the reporter noting heading and altitude assignments were likely confused.
summary: A Departure Radar controller assigned an E135 departing Runway 23 a heading of 140 and altitude of 100, but the pilot read back climbing to 140. The controller attributes the error to pilot confusion and their own complacency in not verifying the altitude readback due to a lack of immediate traffic conflicts.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences an A system hydraulic failure during approach. The approach is continued to landing but post flight review determines that the aircraft was overweight for a flaps 40 landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a System A hydraulic failure during descent in a high-workload terminal area and landed uneventfully after completing checklists. Post-flight review revealed they were slightly overweight for a flaps 40 approach climb, prompting a recommendation to request vectors for a slower, more thorough performance review.

synopsis: A B747-400 intermittent flap position sensor malfunction at cruise caused a partial flap extended signal which positioned the autothrottles to idle because of an overspeed detection. The warning was false and a normal landing ensued.
summary: The crew experienced an autothrottle idle and FLAP DRIVE EICAS message at FL310 caused by an erroneous left outboard flap sensor signal. After coordinating with Dispatch and ATC to maintain clean speeds, the flaps extended normally on arrival, though the crew noted a lack of specific no-flap landing procedures.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports losing control during landing due to a wind gust. Damage results to the aircraft and airport signs during the ensuing go around.
summary: During landing, a pilot was pushed right by a wind gust and aborted the approach. This resulted in damage to the aircraft's wheel pant and ground taxi signs.

synopsis: M20 pilot departing MYF reports a NMAC with a Cirrus entering the pattern. Evasive action is taken and the event reported to the Tower.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a Cirrus during a VFR departure from Runway 28R, occurring approximately 300 feet horizontally and 50 to 100 feet vertically apart. The pilot attributed the incident to the Cirrus entering the pattern from the incorrect side, as no traffic advisories were issued by the Tower.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports a possible Class D airspace incursion while attempting to troubleshoot a rough running engine. The reporter elects to land at the airport in question where contaminated fuel is discovered.
summary: The pilot experienced a possible Class D airspace intrusion and deviated from the flight path while descending due to rough engine operation. The aircraft landed after fuel contamination was discovered, though carburetor heat, lean mixture, and pitch changes temporarily resolved the engine issue.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described an unsafe condition situation when DTW arrivals were subjected to Time Based Metering (TBM) restrictions resulting in potential conflicts and increased workload volume and complexity.
summary: A Ravena Sector controller and D-Side managed Air Carrier X and Y inbound to DTW under Time Based Metering. The controller issued then cancelled a descent clearance for Air Carrier X to avoid a conflict with Air Carrier Y, attributing the incident to ineffective metering times and poor coordination between sectors.

synopsis: An Enroute Controller reported that an IFR aircraft was below MIA and unable to hold altitude in an emergency situation due to icing.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X, which encountered severe icing after departing northbound and descending below the Minimum Icing Altitude. The controller coordinated emergency descents and terrain avoidance, allowing the pilot to eventually sight the departure airport and execute a visual approach.

synopsis: Confused coordination/communications efforts between FLM's and the TMU and inaccurate information provided to the controllers regarding weather required re-routes in the Caribbean caused difficulty for ZMA.
summary: Air traffic controllers in the Caribbean area prematurely combined sectors for a skill-check due to miscommunication and inaccurate ESIS displays regarding weather reroutes. This created a vulnerable situation with unexpected high-volume Fort Lauderdale traffic, though the teams managed the complexity without incident.

synopsis: An Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event listing read back hear back and phraseology non-conformance issues as causal factors.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller descended a C510 to FL170 after mishearing a B737 conflict reference during coordination with Approach. This caused a loss of minimum separation with the climbing B737, requiring immediate corrective climbs and descents to restore safe spacing.

synopsis: A B737-NG crew originally scheduled to fly a non EOW aircraft to MMUN over water were rescheduled over land and exceeded eight hours but were told because the original over water flight was less than eight hours they were legal to fly the rescheduled flight.
summary: The flight crew reported a scheduling dispute regarding a round trip to MMUN where a non-life raft equipped aircraft was assigned for a flight exceeding 162 NM over the Gulf. The crew argued they were not legal to start the flight due to the aircraft's equipment limitations, contradicting Scheduling's claim that the flight remained legal to finish.

synopsis: SF340 Captain experiences a master caution and a flaps light on the CWP at cruise altitude. The flaps indicate up and a no flap landing at destination is planned and successfully executed. Maintenance found that some flaps were out and that a circuit breaker had tripped. Resetting the circuit breaker returned the flaps to normal operation.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a flap caution and executed a QRH procedure for a flaps-zero landing after Dispatch approval. Maintenance later found a tripped circuit breaker causing false indications, reset it, and signed the aircraft off for a return trip.

synopsis: An E-145 Captain refused a reassignment to additional flying following a ten day period that included only a single day off.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported that a 12-hour duty day, new first officers, multiple MELs, and poor sleep caused excessive workload and exhaustion. The pilot felt unfit to operate an aircraft but considered these conditions part of the job.

synopsis: An HS-125 Captain for a fractional operator alleged coercion of some pilots to fly fatiguing schedules and preferential treatment for others to avoid the same, resulting in flight crews being compelled to fly when not fit to do so.
summary: A pilot for an unscheduled fractional operator reported that erratic duty start times and early wake-ups caused excessive fatigue, forcing them to call in unfit. The pilot stated that management's scrutiny of fatigue calls created a stigma and discouraged reporting, while preferential scheduling skewed fatigue statistics.

synopsis: When their localizer receiver provided anomalous guidance the flight crew of a B767-300ER elected to divert to their VFR alternate. While utilizing the ILS at the alternate it functioned normally.
summary: The pilot flying and Captain executed a missed approach at DFW after the localizer drifted left despite autopilot disconnection and aggressive manual correction. ATC confirmed the aircraft was visually left of course, prompting a go-around and a successful ILS test at the alternate to verify receiver operation.

synopsis: A PC12 tire failed during landing when a student used the brakes aggressively after touch down.
summary: During a training flight, a student pilot in the left seat applied excessive brake pressure during the landing roll, causing the left main tire to deflate. The aircraft stopped safely with no injuries or damage, and the tire was subsequently replaced.

synopsis: A G-550 Captain reported excessively deteriorated pavement on Taxiway M at the approach end of Runway 23 in CLT.
summary: A pilot reported that General Aviation aircraft taxiing from Runway 23 to Runway 18L at Charlotte Airport are experiencing increased tire wear due to cracked and separated pavement on Taxiway M. The reporter attributes this significant deterioration to increased traffic volume caused by restrictions on using Taxiway D.

synopsis: An inexperienced Private Pilot failed to note the Tower had cleared him for a straight out departure vice the downwind deparature he had requested. When the pilot turned the crosswind leg he had to perform evasive maneuvers to avoid another aircraft entering the pattern on the downwind leg.
summary: A new private pilot departed runway 29R assuming a right downwind departure despite a tower clearance for a straight-out departure, causing a near collision with an inbound Cessna. The pilot accepted sole responsibility for the error and suggested ATC explicitly state "amended clearance" when instructions differ from requests.

synopsis: ZOA Controller described an apparent false conflict alarm when an Airline Data Block failed to drop off the operational display after the aircraft had landed, the reporter listing Data Link/ATOP anomalies as causal factors.
summary: An air traffic controller in Oceanic Sector 3 accidentally deleted a Data Link aircraft's flight plan while processing another arrival due to distraction. The controller recommends system logic checks to prevent deleting Data Link aircraft before they log off and to require arrival airport entry.

synopsis: Ground Controller described a confused Flight Plan status event when an IFR departure was initially handled as a VFR but changed after the IFR status was verified.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller taxied a C206 to the runway without knowing its flight plan status, later discovering it was IFR. The controller corrected the situation by obtaining an IFR heading from the TRACON and relaying it to Local Control.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a MVA non-compliance event when issuing a direct routing to a departure, failing to note the route went through a higher MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a pilot's discretion descent to 3,000 feet for an IFR BE20, routing it over an antenna with a 3,500-foot MVA. The controller admitted the error resulted from forgetting the recently increased obstacle height, which is the highest in the airspace.

synopsis: A B737-300 flight crew encountered some confusion and distraction when an engine experienced compressor stalls right at rotation at night. Well intentioned but flawed observations from the Tower Controller contributed to the complexity of resolving the issues as they suggested there may have been problems with both engines.
summary: During takeoff on the last leg of a pairing, the left engine compressor stalled repeatedly, causing confusion with ATC reports of right engine flames. The crew executed the stall checklist, returned for a single-engine landing with the engine running, and landed safely with no damage.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew dealt with multiple failures with both their initially assigned MD-83 and the second aircraft provided after their return with the first.
summary: The crew experienced a total loss of flight instruments and electrical power during climb, forcing an emergency return to the departure airport. Subsequently, the replacement aircraft suffered a right engine spool-up failure requiring a maintenance restart, resulting in significant delays attributed to unresolved electrical and engine history issues.

synopsis: A Turbine Shop Mechanic reports several jobcards have disclaimers that he feels relieves the responsibility to maintain accurate jobcards.
summary: A mechanic reported that jobcards contain disclaimers stating listed part numbers may not be current, requiring reference to the Illustrated Parts Catalog. The reporter believes this relieves the Powerplant Engineering Department of its General Manual responsibility to maintain Job Instruction Card accuracy.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic raises concerns about the serviceability of the 3-point vendor-repaired passenger restraint type seat belts used on their Dassault 2000 aircraft. A re-webbed seat belt buckle, tagged as serviceable, had fallen apart due to missing parts.
summary: A mechanic and Lead Mechanic X investigated a failed seat belt buckle on a Dassault Falcon 2000 that had been recently reworked by a vendor. The reporter attributes the failure to the vendor assigning non-standard part numbers and removing original tags, suggesting a need for quality oversight.

synopsis: A PA44 conducting practice pattern maneuvers was instructed by ATC to reduce the spacing between himself and preceding traffic that resulted in a required go around, the reporter questioning ATC's knowledge of aircraft performance characteristics.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 152 reported a safety issue during touch-and-go practice when an air traffic controller instructed a late base turn, causing the pilot to go around due to insufficient separation from a preceding Piper PA28. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller's lack of understanding regarding aircraft aerodynamics and airspeed limitations.

synopsis: Instructor pilot, flying as a safety pilot in a BE55, describes a loss of situational awareness by the pilot flying and an attempt to descend to minimums early. The reporter assumes control and returns to a safe altitude.
summary: During a GPS 24 practice approach, the flying pilot lost situational awareness and descended rapidly, prompting the reporter to take control and climb. The aircraft descended to approximately 500 feet AGL due to cockpit confusion and windshear, an incident the reporter attributed to an insufficient approach briefing.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic was informed the Digital Flight Data Recorder (DFDR) he installed on a B767-400 aircraft was not 'Effective' for that airplane, even though both he and a Maintenance Controller for Aircraft On Ground (AOG) had noted the DFDR he installed was correct per their Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) at that time.
summary: A mechanic replaced a B767-400's DFDR with P/N YY00-042 based on an Illustrated Parts Catalog entry that later disappeared. Although Maintenance Control initially confirmed the part was effective, the aircraft required a scheduled replacement with the original P/N XX43-00 five days later.

synopsis: An HS125-700 compass system malfunctioned after takeoff on the TEB 8 SID. Consequently the pilot failed to turn to the 280 heading until after an ATC alert.
summary: The pilot reported a 20-degree compass discrepancy during the TEB8 departure after leveling at 1,500 feet, prompting a turn to 280 degrees and climb to 2,000 feet. No further issues occurred, but the crew noted they were not instructed to contact ATC or provided a phone number for post-flight reporting.

synopsis: Local Controller described a questionable 'Contact Approach' clearance issued when requested by the pilot and the weather conditions deteriorate to IFR.
summary: A newly certified controller and a C172 pilot experienced a safety incident during IFR snow conditions when the pilot landed without proper coordination. The controller attributed the event to mutual inexperience, miscommunication, and distraction while attempting to contact the N90 sector.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a conflict event between a SNA Air Carrier departure and a VFR overflight, the reporter suggesting some type of improved procedure between the Tower and TRACON.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing the PACR Sector issued a traffic alert to a departing B737 climbing toward a C182 at 3,500 feet due to unclear coordination with SNA Tower. The controller advised the B737 to stop climbing at 3,000 feet, but the pilot eventually spotted the traffic and turned left without reporting a conflict.

synopsis: A B767-300 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence from a preceding B757 that was eight miles ahead.
summary: While level at 7,000 FT behind a B757, the crew encountered wake turbulence causing a 15-degree right roll and momentary stickshaker activation. The pilot disengaged the autopilot and leveled the aircraft with ailerons within 3 seconds, with no altitude loss or parameter exceedances.

synopsis: A Reserve First Officer was awakened after three hours of sleep by Crew Scheduling to be assigned a trip 14 hours in the future. The trip is declined due to fatigue.
summary: A pilot reported fatigue after being assigned a flight 14 hours following a canceled standby duty and only three hours of sleep. The pilot refused the assignment, citing that the scheduling error and insufficient rest made it unsafe to drive and fly to an international destination.

synopsis: A B737-300 suffered a loss of pressurization, declared an emergency, initiated an emergency descent and diverted to a nearby airport as a precaution.
summary: The crew experienced a cabin altitude warning and rapid climb to 10,000 feet during cruise at FL250 with an inoperative left pack. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and diverted due to suspected bad door seals and a misaligned left rear door.

synopsis: An MD-82 flight crew declared and emergency and returned to their departure airport when they experienced compressor stalls from the right engine during their climb out. Inspection after landing revealed the engine's nose bullet had sheared off and had remained in the cowling inlet.
summary: During climb through 13,000 feet, the crew experienced right engine compressor stalls caused by a sheared inlet nose bullet resting against the guide vanes. The crew declared an emergency, secured the engine, and returned to the departure airport for inspection.

synopsis: An MD11 crew took off into icing conditions. All communication was lost when anti-ice was turned on. PFD route data was unavailable. The crew used VOR for navigation and updated the IRS crossing the first VOR.
summary: The Captain entered incorrect coordinates for Runway 28 in the FMS, causing PFD data loss and radio failure after takeoff due to ice. The crew recovered by using VOR navigation and updating the IRS, attributing the incident to a lack of cross-verification and checklist compliance.

synopsis: Pitts pilot reports nosing over after landing due to the right wheel pant coming into contact with the tire and slide to a stop on the runway. The wheel pant bolt had apparently departed the aircraft in flight.
summary: During touch-and-go operations, the right wheel pant contacted the tire, causing the aircraft to nose over and stop on the runway. The pilot attributed the incident to the center bolt holding the pant failing in flight.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event when traffic was issued holding instructions awaiting a 'landing assured report', experienced a fuel issue, and descended below assigned altitude.
summary: Air Traffic Control issued holding instructions to Aircraft X, which reported minimum fuel and descended below 4,000 FT without entering the hold while Aircraft Y landed. After failing to respond to approach clearance, Aircraft X requested vectors, climbed back to 4,000 FT, and subsequently landed safely.

synopsis: PBI Controller described an unauthorized descent below assigned altitudes resulting in a MVA infraction.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a Learjet 40 to a south downwind and cleared it to descend and maintain 2,500 feet. The controller later observed the aircraft had descended to 1,500 feet just south of the localizer.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: TRACON Controller described a climb above authorized altitude during the application of visual separation.
summary: Air traffic controllers and an MD80 pilot were involved during the departure phase when the MD80 climbed above its assigned 11,000 feet to 11,300 feet. The controller instructed a 180-degree turn for traffic separation, but the pilot did not comply, so the controller waited for vertical separation before issuing new instructions.

synopsis: ZDC Controller reported an loss of separation, citing sector reconfiguration as contributory.
summary: An air traffic controller in a newly reconfigured sector with limited certification issued a 30-degree right turn to an MD82 and a heading change to a C510 to resolve crossing traffic. The controller attributed the near-miss to reduced situational awareness caused by the recent sector changes and lack of familiarity with the new airspace configuration.

synopsis: Ground Controller described a taxiway excursion by an Air Carrier taxiing for departure, the reporting noting no taxiway braking action reports were available at the time of the incident.
summary: The pilot taxied an aircraft in snow and low visibility, requested a 270-degree turn, and reported poor braking action before entering the grass. The controller attributed the excursion to unreported taxiway conditions despite recent plowing, noting the pilot could not comply with alternative instructions.

synopsis: Controller providing OJT failed to note that the trainee has permitted an aircraft to enter a restricted area, the reporter indicating that the constant training being conducted has rendered CPC's 'non-proficient' on operational positions.
summary: An air traffic controller and trainee allowed a PA32 to enter a restricted area because the controller was distracted by another problem. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of proficiency caused by constant training of trainees and infrequent solo radar shifts.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller described an airspace incursion event when the data tag on an IFR aircraft failed to remain with the target. The reporter suggested several automated prevention stops that may have prevented the incursion.
summary: An air traffic controller accepted an IFR handoff for Aircraft X without a flight plan, causing the radar tag to drop while manually entering data. The controller subsequently lost radar contact and transferred the aircraft to another sector, recommending system changes to prevent handoffs without active flight plans.

synopsis: IAH Controller described a developing runway incursion event, prevented by Local Control intervention, the reporter listing runway status lighting procedures and delayed ASDE-X alarms as causal factors.
summary: Ground Control reported an E145 taxiing excessively slowly, causing anxiety that led the Local Controller to position it on Runway 33L. The aircraft then made a wrong turn toward Runway 33R during a 737 takeoff roll, requiring the controller to order a hold after a late ASDE-X alarm.

synopsis: ZLA Controller described a confused climb clearance and routing event involving an aircraft being transferred from Nellis ATC, the reporter listing problematic radio/RADAR coverage and incorrect routing issuance as causal factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing a Shorts 330 at 13,000 feet in ZLA16 reported poor radio quality and radar limitations caused the pilot to deviate from the required V135 airway. The pilot mistakenly believed he had a climb clearance to 16,000 feet, prompting the controller to reissue instructions and vector the aircraft to regain radar coverage.

synopsis: EWR Controller described a loss of separation event between a EWR missed approach aircraft and N90 traffic, noting that airspace changes are need to prevent conflicts between EWR arrivals and TEB missed approach aircraft.
summary: A trainee controller managed a Learjet 60 missed approach and a Gulfstream departure on Runway 24, issuing conflicting headings before the Gulfstream switched frequencies. N90 Departure later reported a potential loss of separation between the Learjet and an EWR arrival, prompting a request to modify airspace to prevent future conflicts.

synopsis: ZKX Controller described the loss of RADAR on a military training jet in Class A airspace requiring re-identification of same by an adjacent facility.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller lost radar contact with a T-38 in Class A airspace north of LBL while coordinating a handoff to ZDV. The pilot provided conflicting position reports, leading the controller to conclude that aircraft with non-operating equipment should not be permitted in Class A airspace.

synopsis: HCF Controller expressed concern regarding the competance of the 'Contract ATC Controllers' at KOA Tower, citing a recent example of a clearance issued that was not understood.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued a departure clearance to a B737 that conflicted with an inbound ILS 17 approach, causing the pilot to deviate south and cross the missed approach fix. The reporter attributed the incident to incompetent KOA Tower controllers and recommended FAA takeover and Class C airspace designation.

synopsis: A D21 Controller reported a possible phraseology/clearance error when issuing a 'maintain visual separation' clearance and the pilot not responding with the exact phraseology required.
summary: An air traffic controller instructed a CRJ7 to maintain visual separation from a B737, but the pilot responded with "will do" instead of the full phrase. The controller noted uncertainty about the acceptability of this readback and decided to request the specific phrase in future similar situations.

synopsis: A BE-400XP flight crew returned to their departure airport when they experienced multiple nav system and pitch control anomalies.
summary: The crew experienced a total loss of flight displays and annunciation panels 15 minutes into the flight, causing a return to the airport without declaring an emergency. They performed a no-flap landing with extended gear, evacuated the cabin, and found no aircraft damage post-flight.

synopsis: Upon experiencing a loud thump and a R ENG FIRE EICAS warning during the initial climbout the flight crew of a B767-300ER shut down the engine, extinguished the fire, declared an emergency and returned to their departure aiport. Subsequent inspection of the engine revealed evidence of an actual fire.
summary: The crew of a twin-engine aircraft experienced a right engine fire at 9,000 feet, indicated by a loud thump and illuminated fire light. They executed emergency procedures, diverted to runway 4R, and landed safely with extensive engine damage after a 30-minute total event time.

synopsis: A CRJ200 CAS alerted a HYDRAULIC 3 LOW PRESS caution message five knots below V1 so the takeoff was continued, the QRH complied with and a normal landing completed at the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Hydraulic 3 low pressure caution and subsequent gear disagreement warnings during takeoff. After complying with the QRH to retract the gear, they returned to the departure airport where maintenance attributed the issue to work performed the previous night.

synopsis: A Q400 Captain reported encountering a jolt of severe turbulence from a preceding B747 on departure from SEA. The Captain reported that he banged his head and sustained a concussion from the event.
summary: After departing SEA behind a B747, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence at 5,000 feet, causing autopilot disengagement and injuring the Captain. The flight continued to the destination, where the Captain sought emergency medical care for head and neck injuries.

synopsis: BE400 Captain describes a reoccurring series of failures of the Horizontal Stabilizer (HSTAB) de-ice system of aircraft in his company's fleet.
summary: Pilots flying a Hawker 400XP encountered a Horizontal Stabilizer de-ice system failure at altitude while in icing conditions, forcing a difficult diversion with ATC assistance. The crew attributes these recurring failures across multiple aircraft to a flawed design rather than maintenance, warning that the system's inability to function in flight creates an unrecoverable icing risk.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Fractional Airline crew reported a near miss with a Navajo on the TEB RUUDY 4 SID at 1,500 FT approaching WENTZ Intersection.
summary: During the RUUDY departure from TEB Runway 24, a Navajo aircraft executed a sharp right turn and dive to avoid a midair collision after the pilot reported visual contact.
