The reporter attributes the conflict to saturated airspace and questionable see-and-avoid reliability, noting ATC appeared unaware of the proximity despite issuing traffic advisories.

synopsis: A CRJ200 Captain was descending at 1,300 FPM and below the glideslope in mountainous terrain at night when the Terrain Warning sounded while ATC was calling low altitude alert. A go around was executed and the flight diverted.
summary: During a night approach in icing conditions, the Captain descended at 1,300 FPM without an active glide slope, triggering GPWS and low altitude alerts. The First Officer initiated a go-around at 1,000 feet AGL, and the crew diverted due to the unsafe descent in mountainous terrain.

synopsis: A flight crew who refused an aircraft with a MEL'ed pressurization system because of concerns about passenger safety and comfort in worsening weather were then questioned by the Company about the refusal after ferrying the aircraft to a maintenance station.
summary: The flight crew refused to depart with passengers due to a recurring pressurization system failure and management's initial refusal to authorize maintenance. After escalating concerns through multiple management levels, the aircraft was repositioned to a maintenance base for repairs instead of operating the scheduled revenue flights.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain describes his reservations as to whether company mechanics at one of their island airports are properly inspecting their aircraft prior to ETOPS departures. An overserviced 'A' system hydraulic reservoir quantity and 'nicks' on #1 engine fan blade and spinner dome had not been corrected or addressed.
summary: Pilots discovered an over-serviced hydraulic system and a paper lodged in Engine #1 during preflight checks for an ETOPS flight. The reporter attributed these issues to Maintenance's failure to correct discrepancies before signing off the Pre-Departure Checks.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew on approach to FAI Runway 20 at night in cold weather, got an EGPWS Terrain Warning, aggressively added power, returned to the glideslope and completed a normal landing.
summary: The crew descended into FAI at night on a visual approach to Runway 20R and triggered an EGPWS terrain alert due to an excessive descent rate. The First Officer applied power to climb and stabilize, allowing a normal landing, with the pilot attributing the event to failing to monitor vertical descent relative to terrain.

synopsis: When dispatched with one generator inoperative the flight crew of a B737-800 was forced to divert to their nearest suitable airport when the APU, required to be operative to provide a secondary electrical power source, failed enroute.
summary: The Captain and First Officer operated an aircraft with a deferred #1 Generator, requiring APU backup per MEL. The APU failed 45 minutes from destination, causing single electrical power operation and necessitating an emergency landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: A B767-300 crew shut an engine down for low oil pressure as they began their approach descent and because of high workload missed the autopilot's failure to capture the glideslope which resulted in an unstabilized approach with a low airspeed. The crew rectified the errors and landed safely.
summary: The First Officer and Captain of a Boeing 767 declared an emergency due to zero left engine oil quantity and executed a single-engine approach in IMC. The aircraft experienced speed degradation when the autopilot inadvertently captured the glide slope, but the crew disengaged it, recovered control, and landed safely.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports the APU and #2 engine fire bottles were inadvertently discharged, even with the battery switch 'OFF', when he was transferring a lighted faceplate from a malfunctioning Fire Control Panel (FCP) to a replacement FCP on the P-8 Center Control console of a B737 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic servicing a B737's Fire Control Unit pulled a circuit breaker before paperwork arrived, inadvertently discharging fire bottles while installing a missing light plate. The pilot refused the aircraft due to low crew oxygen, causing a delay, temporary grounding, and mandatory drug and alcohol testing for all involved.

synopsis: Two Contract Maintenance Technicians were informed a B727 aircraft had diverted after they had replaced the #1 and #2 vertical gyros.
summary: A B727 diverted after an avionics technician installed the #1 vertical gyro without washers, causing erratic ADI indications and autopilot porpoising. The technician followed maintenance manual procedures that omitted washer requirements, leading to the gyro moving in its rack.

synopsis: Operating from a non-towered airport, the pilot of a light aircraft had to takeoff prematurely to avoid an aircraft which had previously landed and exited the runway but then turned back and was recrossing the runway despite the reporter's declaration of his takeoff given on UNICOM.
summary: The pilot initiated a takeoff on Runway 24 while a Cessna crossed the runway without UNICOM communication. The pilot continued the takeoff, climbing over the Cessna at more than 250 feet AGL, attributing the incident to the other pilot's failure to look and announce intentions.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain approaching BQK noticed aircraft lights on the opposite runway and executed a go around only find out that the First Officer was broadcasting CTAF position reports on an incorrect frequency.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot on a visual approach to Runway 7 initiated a go-around after spotting an opposing aircraft, realizing they were tuned one digit off on the CTAF frequency. The runway lights had activated coincidentally due to the other aircraft, but the error was corrected, allowing both planes to land uneventfully.

synopsis: J-3 Cub instructor providing training in emergency landings was admonished by the Local Controller for making a remark in jest about having engine problems.
summary: A pilot practicing simulated emergency landings joked to Tower about engine trouble, prompting controllers to ask if the aircraft had an actual emergency. The pilot clarified it was a quip, and controllers warned that all transmissions are recorded, emphasizing the need to avoid non-essential remarks about emergencies.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A single engine aircraft pilot reported a near miss with a VFR military aircraft descending through 9,000 FT and not talking with ATC.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 9,000 feet reported a near-miss with a military jet descending from 9,500 feet to 100 feet below. The pilot attributed the incident to the military crew's reckless VFR flight without ATC communication and questioned the timeliness of the controller's traffic advisory.

synopsis: C170 pilot reports a ground loop during landing, citing complacency as the likely cause.
summary: The pilot ground looped during the landing phase, damaging one runway light but causing no aircraft damage. The reporter attributed the incident to complacency and corrected it by reviewing and re-flying the procedure.

synopsis: A BE36 pilot on an IFR flight plan reported a near miss at 9,000 FT with no advance ATC notification as the unidentified aircraft took evasive action.
summary: A pilot reported a near miss during cruise in VMC when another aircraft climbing from below appeared ahead and left, executing a hard right climbing turn. The pilot stated ATC provided no proximity warning before the event was reported.

synopsis: Two Line Maintenance Technicians report on their involvement with an MD-88 aircraft's Main Landing Gear (MLG) doors hydraulic bypass handle that was initially believed responsible for an air turnback.
summary: Two mechanics on an MD-88 replaced a borrowed flap actuator, but the lead technician failed to follow AMM procedures for bleeding the hydraulic system or pinning the landing gear. The reporter attributes the subsequent air turnback to miscommunication, complacency, and signing off on an unaccomplished hydraulic inspection.

synopsis: A Lead and Avionic's Mechanic had difficulty getting correct parts information when utilizing their Maintenance Control group for support to help reduce aircraft delays. They replaced a Spoiler Control Module (SCM) with an SCM not 'Effective' for a B757-300 aircraft based on information from Maintenance Control.
summary: A B757-300 mechanic installed an incompatible Spoiler Control Module (P/N 285TXXXX-118) after Maintenance Control incorrectly approved it to fix a spoiler fault. The error occurred due to time pressure during a quick turn and failure to verify part effectivity in the Illustrated Parts Catalog.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor was informed that he allowed a B767-400 aircraft to depart with non-operating latches for a cabin overhead luggage bin that contained emergency equipment. Tape had been applied to help keep the bin closed in flight, but was not documented. Concerns about meeting aircraft departure schedules were also noted.
summary: A mechanic canceled a write-up for a broken overhead bin containing emergency equipment to avoid delaying departure, despite knowing repairs were incomplete. The aircraft departed with the bin secured only by tape, requiring maintenance to fix the issue after landing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported that after landing on FAR Runway 36 he was instructed to exit right on Taxiway C but because of ice slid past Charlie and made a tight left turn back to exit on C but did not notify the Tower of the incursion.
summary: A freight pilot landing in IMC at FAR reported fair-to-good braking but slid past Taxiway Charlie due to slicker runway edges. The pilot corrected with differential power and left brakes to avoid going off the runway but failed to inform the Tower.

synopsis: A PA32 compass system became inaccurate on an ILS vector so the clearance was canceled. Then the landing gear indicated unsafe at the same time as the airspeed and altimeter became erratic because of a popped circuit breaker in icing. Finally, an ATC NO GYRO approach go them below the clouds where the became reoriented.
summary: The flight crew encountered rime ice and instrument failures on an ILS 13 approach due to a popped pitot heat breaker and gyro precession. These issues caused gear extension and navigation errors, leading to a descent below 3,200 feet before the crew recovered and landed safely.

synopsis: A LR25 right engine fire warning momentarily alerted at cruise but was found to be inoperative after a fire system test so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a transient right engine fire warning at FL380 and a failed fire test, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. After landing and shutting down the right engine, maintenance identified a broken fire detection loop as the cause.

synopsis: A ZDV Controller described a below MEA event when a pilot failed to respond to a climb clearance because radio difficulties. The reporter noted a loss com clearance would have prevented the event but radio failure is totally unpredictable.
summary: Air traffic controllers lost communication with a PA34 en route from BDG to GUP, causing the pilot to enter the 110 MEA at 100. The controller eventually re-established contact on an adjacent frequency, and the pilot climbed to the required altitude.

synopsis: A Tower Controller described an unsafe event when a B767 was cleared for take off with Citation traffic on a five mile final. The reporter acknowledged questionable spacing judgement on his part.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared a B767 for takeoff from Runway 13R while a Citation X was on five-mile final, relying on visual separation. The B767's delayed departure created a close call, prompting the Citation X to land with standard separation, though the controller noted better timing or cancellation would have been safer.

synopsis: Tower CIC voiced concern regarding the lack of response to his direction to a controller reference runway separation, noting shift supervisor rarely reside in the Tower but spend time in the TRACON and their offices during the shift.
summary: A Tower CIC advised a Local Controller to order an E170 on final for Runway 10 to go around because an MD82 had not cleared the runway. The Local Controller refused the instruction, resulting in a loss of required runway separation and creating an unsafe situation.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event between an IFR arrival and departure complicated by failed internal coordination regarding a release and an intervention vector that did not provide adequate spacing.
summary: Satellite sector controllers lost separation between a departing C421 and an inbound BE30 due to a miscommunication regarding the C421's release. The controller assumed the release was complete, leading to a conflict that required canceling the BE30's approach and turning it westbound.

synopsis: Traffic assigned FL350 continued the climb above the assigned altitude conflicting with other traffic. Several versions of the factors involved are provided in this combined ATC/flight crew report.
summary: An ATC controller and CRJ crew experienced a conflict during climb north of SSO VOR when the pilot misread the altitude preselect as 35,000 instead of 36,000 due to sun glare and fatigue. The aircraft overshot FL350 to FL355, triggering a Conflict Alert and TCAS advisory before the crew manually arrested the climb.

synopsis: A B737-300 number two engine developed a tail pipe fire during start so the Engine Fire Switch was pulled, the fire bottle discharged, the fire extinguished and the aircraft towed to the gate.
summary: Ramp personnel reported a fire on engine 2 during pushback start. The crew pulled the fire switch and discharged the bottle, suppressing the fire; the aircraft was towed back to the gate with no injuries.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 Captain reported discrepancies between the ILS glideslope signal and the VASI for Runway 34 at AVL, advising the ILS glideslope signal commands an excessively steep descent and a threshold crossing well above the charted TCH.
summary: A pilot conducting a visual approach to Runway 34 at AVL reported a significant discrepancy between the ILS glideslope and VASI, noting the glideslope indicated a 150–200 ft touchdown height. The pilot questioned the Tower, which stated the FAA considers the deviation normal, though the pilot believes the ILS requires correction.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported a near miss on BRO Runway 31L short final with another aircraft on a visual approach to Runway 35 after the crew had previously reported that aircraft not in sight and ATC failed update the traffic's position.
summary: The crew on a LOC/BC 31L approach at BRO received a TCAS TA at 200 feet while the Tower queried about unseen traffic. They visually acquired the aircraft directly overhead with 400 feet vertical separation and continued landing, noting insufficient altitude to safely execute a go-around.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain discovers that the Engine Out procedures for PDX, stored in the FMC are different from the printed procedures issued by the company.
summary: The flight crew discovered a discrepancy during preflight where the FMC Engine Out SID for PDX 10L showed a left turn to 290 degrees, contradicting the provided written and pictorial procedures which indicated a right turn. This error could cause confusion and potential terrain clearance issues during an engine failure.

synopsis: A B737-800 was dispatched with an engine generator on MEL and an APU with a history of low oil pressure auto shutdowns. While inflight the APU auto shutdown causing the crew to declare an emergency and divert single generator to a nearby airport with suitable weather.
summary: The pilot flying reported that during cruise, the APU shut down due to low oil pressure while the left generator was already placarded inoperative, leaving the aircraft with one generator. The crew diverted to a VFR airport and landed safely, concluding the emergency was preventable given the APU's prior history.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor reported the need for more Aircraft Systems and Trouble Shooting training for their Air Carrier Maintenance Technicians working Airbus aircraft. The Supervisor noted that he has never seen an airline with such sub-par training.
summary: A maintenance technician reported that airline maintenance personnel lack adequate aircraft systems and troubleshooting training, despite requests to management and Airbus. No event occurred, but the reporter stated that proper training is necessary to prevent future incidents.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor describes Air Carrier Line Maintenance environment that includes low experience mechanics, high mechanic turnovers, a Director of Maintenance (DOM) who pushes mechanics to 'rush' their work, no maintenance hangars for their aircraft resulting in engine changes that are accomplished in the rain.
summary: A new Director of Maintenance pressured technicians to rush work, causing two instances where Thrust Reverser Hydraulic Control Unit lockout pins were left installed on V2500 engines. This management pressure created a fear of termination, leading to errors that prevented thrust reverser deployment during landing.

synopsis: A Line Avionics Technician reports their B737-800 NexGen aircraft External Power Panel (P19) receptacle has redesigned electrical pins that break more frequently, causing External Power drop-offs, increase use of their APUs and fuel burn to supply electrical power for their aircraft at the gates.
summary: A mechanic replaced a broken External Power receptacle pin that failed again days later. The reporter attributes the frequent breakage to the pin's weak threaded mounting design and the shallow housing that fails to support the power cord.

synopsis: A PA23-250 oil dipstick 'popper' cap unseated in flight and permitted an oil leak severe enough that the pilot shut the engine down, declared an emergency and landed at a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot of a Lycoming IO-540 aircraft discovered excessive oil venting from the left engine during cruise, caused by an unseated dipstick cap. After declaring an emergency and shutting down the engine, the pilot executed a safe single-engine landing with ATC and ARFF assistance.

synopsis: A CH2T instructor reported a student lost control of the aircraft after an aborted takeoff, refused to relinquish control, had a runway excursion damaging an airport sign and the aircraft wing.
summary: During a takeoff attempt, a student pilot incorrectly applied power and failed to correct left-turning tendencies, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike a sign and light. The student refused to release the throttle, rendering the CFI's braking ineffective, resulting in minor damage to the starboard wing leading edge.

synopsis: A CE560XL Captain reported the aircraft's FMS missed a crossing restriction because the Company's newly acquired aircraft's Honeywell FMS VNAV did not respond like the Company's original aircraft's Universal FMS.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft with a Honeywell FMZ FMS failed to meet a 11,000-foot crossing restriction after the system did not follow VNAV constraints as expected. The crew attributed the descent error to the non-intuitive FMS interface and inadequate training software, resulting in a controller alert regarding nearby traffic.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: VRB RADAR was taken down for maintenance during a busy traffic period. A ZMA Controller suggests, as a safety issue, this type of elective maintenance should be completed during late night operations.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector three lost radar contact with an aircraft conducting a practice approach at VRB due to a preventative maintenance outage on the VRB RADAR. The controller attributed the resulting safety and efficiency degradation to scheduling maintenance during peak daylight hours instead of midnight shifts.

synopsis: B757 has a nose gear disagree EICAS message during approach and goes around, the QRH is consulted and nose gear is extended using the Alternate Gear Extend Switch. The crew reported some confusion using the QRH procedure.
summary: Pilots experienced a nose gear disagreement at 1,100 feet during landing, prompting a go-around and emergency declaration. After confirming the gear was up via tower observation, they successfully extended it using the alternate system and landed uneventfully, attributing task delays to inadequate QRH training.

synopsis: A B767 TE Flap Disagree occurred during approach when flaps are selected from one to fove. QRH procedures are complied with, an emergency declared and a trailing edge flaps up landing was made.
summary: The pilot flying encountered repeated TE Flaps disagree warnings while selecting Flaps 5 on approach. After running the QRH and declaring an emergency, the crew landed with Flaps 1 because the trailing edge flaps would not extend.

synopsis: An Air Carrier had a taxiway excursion while taxiing for takeoff in snowy conditions with the braking action reported as good.
summary: The flight crew lost directional control while taxiing a snow-covered aircraft after a 270-degree turn, sliding off the pavement into grass due to poor braking action despite reports of good conditions. Airport operations towed the aircraft back to the gate after the crew declined to continue taxiing in the hazardous environment.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A CRJ50 Captain discussed the confusion resulting from not understanding the meaning of the new Canadian descent clearance phraseology, 'Descend when you're ready to XXXXX.' He understood constraints were removed, but in fact they were not.
summary: The pilot descended gradually on the WATERLOO FOUR arrival to CYYZ, misinterpreting "Descend when ready" clearances as voiding crossing restrictions under new Canadian rules. ATC queried the altitude at ROKTO, clarified the misunderstanding, and reassigned 11,000 feet without requiring a climb or causing a conflict.

synopsis: A B737 Flight Attendant discovered an entry slide gauge in the red during preflight and informed the Captain. During the time it took to discuss the situation with Maintenance ambient temperatures and the gauge pressure rose to be on the red/green line allowing the flight to depart.
summary: A flight attendant reported a forward entry slide gauge in the red during preflight, but the Captain departed after the gauge temporarily moved to the red/green line due to temperature changes. The aircraft was dispatched with a potentially inoperative slide to avoid delay, prompting the reporter to call for clearer procedures regarding slide gauge readings.

synopsis: A PA28 possibly entered a TFR east of PHX that he was not aware of. The top of the TFR was into the base of the Class B making a flight to FFZ from the northwest difficult.
summary: A pilot flying a general aviation aircraft near Phoenix, Arizona, inadvertently entered a VIP Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) up to 4,100 feet MSL while descending to avoid Class B airspace. The pilot acknowledged the deviation resulted from inadequate pre-flight planning and failure to contact Flight Service Station for updated restrictions.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported difficulty tracking the hand-flown HOLTZ 9 Departure off LAX because of a wake or weather encounter.
summary: A pilot hand-flew a new aircraft on the HOLTZ 9 RNAV departure and encountered turbulence attributed to a preceding B777's wake within the 0.5-mile tolerance. The pilot concluded that engaging the autopilot would have been safer for monitoring navigation limits during the rough ride near PEVEE Intersection.

synopsis: A CE560XL Power Brakes circuit breaker opened simultaneously annunciating the Anti-Skid Inop and LO Brake Pressure so a go around was executed and the flight diverted to nearby major airport.
summary: During approach, a Power Brakes circuit breaker opened, causing anti-skid and brake pressure warnings and loss of normal braking. The crew diverted, declared minimum fuel, and landed using emergency brakes and thrust reversers before being towed to the ramp.

synopsis: A Lancair Legacy's landing gear collapsed during the takeoff roll damaging the propeller, inner gear doors, brakes, left outer flap hinge, and wing under surfaces.
summary: During the takeoff roll of a VFR flight, the pilot reported a landing gear collapse while the engine was at full power, causing the aircraft to skid and stop on the runway. The incident resulted in damage to the propeller, engine, gear doors, brakes, flap hinge, and left wing before the aircraft was recovered and towed to a hangar.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A light twin aircraft's parking brake was not set after fueling at I39, which has a slightly sloped ramp. The aircraft rolled across the ramp and struck a Cessna, causing only superficial damage.
summary: The pilot parked a 10,000-pound aircraft at I39 fuel pumps, exited, and the plane rolled down a slope to strike another aircraft's tail hook. The pilot attributed the cosmetic damage to failing to block wheels or set the parking brake, citing the pad's slope and loss of pilot-in-command attitude as causes.

synopsis: A80 Controller providing OJT described a loss of separation event when traffic departing on an RNAV SID experienced equipment difficulties straying from the published route and conflicted with parallel runway departure traffic.
summary: An Air Carrier X pilot reported compass issues and deviated south of the NOV RNAV SID, compromising separation with Air Carrier Y on the DAW SID. The controller assigned a 270 heading to Air Carrier X and a 255 heading to Air Carrier Y to restore separation, noting the pilot should have advised Tower before deviating.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event when the R-Side Controller issued an altitude assignment to the wrong aircraft, similar call signs were in play.
summary: The R-Side controller mistakenly issued a climb clearance to NYXX instead of NXXX, causing a conflict with an MD82 at FL310. This error triggered TCAS responses from the MD82, NYXX, and the controller.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a conflict event when an issued crossing restriction was missed, the reporter noting this NAVAID DME dependant restriction is often missed, questioning the DME and/or RADAR display accuracy.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance to a B757 at FL390 to cross 85 miles south of YXU at FL330, but the aircraft missed the restriction and conflicted with another flight. The controller resolved the conflict without loss of separation, suspecting the cause is a map error or DME issue at YXU.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict when a VFR departure was turn back over the airport by Approach Control during a military flight tactical over head approach maneuver.
summary: A Departure Controller turned a C206 left to 030 and held it at 5,500 feet, creating a nose-to-nose conflict with military jets on a tactical overhead approach at the same altitude. The controller instructed the jets to climb to 6,500 feet to avoid a collision, noting that departing traffic should not be turned back into arrivals.

synopsis: A B737 descending on a night visual to TUS 11L received a TOO LOW TERRAIN warning, executed the escape maneuver and were vectored around for another approach.
summary: The flight crew descended from 6,000 to 5,000 feet near CALLS Intersection during a visual approach to Tucson Runway 11L, triggering a "Caution Terrain" warning. The pilot executed a go-around to 7,000 feet, and the crew recommends ATC vector aircraft north of the mountain ridge to prevent future warnings.

synopsis: When the B747-400 flight crew received a RIGHT DUCT LEAK OVHT EICAS message shortly after takeoff from ZBAA they elected to divert for maintenance due to enroute weather over the Pacific and wing anti-ice considerations.
summary: The crew diverted to RJAA after an ECIAS right duct leak warning at 500 feet, caused by a broken clamp and missing duct covering. A subsequent #3 bleed valve failure prevented departure due to a night curfew, though the valve eventually closed after an engine run-up on the taxiway.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 flight returned to their departure airport for an overweight landing and maintenance following failure of the nose gear to retract.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose landing gear retraction failure shortly after departure, triggering disagree warnings. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and executed a successful planned overweight landing after completing the QRH checklist.

synopsis: A CRJ200 Captain's windshield developed hairline cracks over the entire window so the flight diverted to a nearby airport for a precautionary landing.
summary: During cruise at FL300, the left windshield glowed orange, sparked, and shattered into a spider web pattern. The crew completed the QRH procedure, maintained pressurization, and diverted uneventfully to a nearby airport 40 NM away.

synopsis: A B767-300 L1 escape slide fell out of the door at the arrival gate after a ferry flight. The door was closed but the slide not armed prior to departure.
summary: The pilot closed the L1 door without arming the slide before departure. Upon arrival, another pilot opened the door for ground personnel, causing the slide to fall onto the jet bridge without deploying.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Smoke and fumes during a simulated engine failure prompt an emergency return for landing.
summary: During a climb-out with a simulated single-engine failure, smoke and fumes appeared in the cockpit. The pilot turned off the heat and returned to the airfield.

synopsis: The third attempt to start the APU of a CRJ-200 on a cold morning, resulted in insufficient spool up and an EGT at or above redline followed by a report from ground crew advising of sparks from the APU exhaust. CFR was called as a precaution and maintenance was initiated.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced failed APU starts with low rotation and high EGT on the first flight of the day. Smoke and sparks were observed, prompting a fire truck response that confirmed no fire, leading to a maintenance write-up.

synopsis: A pallet shifted during takeoff and landing on a B747, causing cargo damage. It was found that aft pallet locks were not properly set.
summary: A cargo pallet shifted rearward on takeoff because aft locks were not secured, despite a pre-flight inspection by the First Officer and ground crew. The reporter attributed the oversight to distraction by non-normal conditions and noted that the Load Master was unaware of unauthorized personnel entering the aircraft during a maintenance delay.

synopsis: A MD82's fuel transfer system did not properly pump fuel from the center tank to the engines until the wing tank boost pumps were turned OFF. Because of the fuel and CG imbalance an emergency was declared for landing.
summary: During cruise, the crew observed fuel feeding from wing tanks instead of the center tank despite pumps being ON. They executed the QRH procedure, declared an emergency, and landed normally after confirming fuel balance and weight limits with Dispatch.

synopsis: A B737 crew did not comply with the WATERLOO THREE ROKTO 16,000 FT to 14,000 FT crossing constraint after being cleared to 11,000 FT because it was not clear to them that they were flying the WATERLOO Arrival and the clearance phraseology did not make it clear that there were descent constraints in their clearance routing.
summary: The flight crew descended below the ROKTO crossing restriction while on the Waterloo 03 arrival after receiving a direct descent clearance to 11,000 feet. The pilot attributed the error to ambiguous ATC terminology regarding arrival restrictions and noted that ATC accepted the situation without further issue.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: When cleared ['direct to IPPOD, cleared for the LDA DME Runway 19 approach to SGU'] the flight crew of a regional jet inappropriately began a descent from their assigned altitude of 13,000 MSL to the MEA at IPPOD of 10,300 MSL, apparently uncognizant of possible intervening high terrain between their location and IPPOD.
summary: During descent into St. George, the flight crew descended below 13,000 feet after receiving a clearance for the LDA Runway 19 approach, which the controller later claimed did not authorize descent. The crew leveled off but resumed descent after the controller re-cleared them, attributing the incident to a misunderstanding of the initial approach clearance.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 crew, with only minutes to prepare for a possible emergency evacuation due to a failed left engine, calmly accomplished all required preparations and, while prepared for the worst, managed a safe, uneventful and responsibly managed completion of the flight.
summary: Flight attendants on a commercial flight prepared the cabin for an emergency landing after the First Officer announced a left engine failure with eight minutes remaining. The crew secured the aircraft and briefed passengers, resulting in a normal landing and gate arrival without incident.

synopsis: A Helicopter Mechanic has a work environment that included high workload saturation, excessive work hours, fatigue. A Medical Power Inverter access panel was not reinstalled on a BK-117 air ambulance helicopter and the Maintenance Base was in disarray after a tornado struck.
summary: A fatigued mechanic working on a BK-117 helicopter forgot to reinstall an access panel due to excessive workload and rushed maintenance. The aircraft departed with the panel missing, was subsequently grounded by the pilot, and required a 200-mile drive to repair, delaying the mission.

synopsis: Corporate flight crew experienced a TCAS RA descending on a STAR, no traffic information was provided by ATC.
summary: Pilots descending from FL350 to FL240 received a TCAS RA while ATC issued a conflicting left vector. The crew followed the RA, passing 500 feet above and to the left of the other aircraft, then resumed their descent after ATC failed to respond to their status report.

synopsis: A TCAS RA on downwind at 3,000 FT for landing at ADS cause an EMB135 to take evasive action by climbing to 4,000 FT.
summary: A pilot flying to ADS at 3,000 MSL executed a TCAS climb resolution advisory after a VFR Cessna climbed rapidly into their path from below. The crew successfully avoided the conflict, which was hidden by clouds, and landed safely after the controller acknowledged the deviation.

synopsis: A CE560XL turned to an incorrect heading after the automation was engaged on the Runway 6 TEB 8 SID and while the Captain was correcting the track error the aircraft accelerated to 220 KTS.
summary: The flight crew departed TEB on the TEB8 departure and noticed the autopilot turning the aircraft incorrectly while leveling at 2,000 FT MSL. The pilot disengaged NAV to arrest the turn and reduced power to idle to slow from 220 KTS to 200 KTS before resuming the SID.

synopsis: A C90 crew read back a Center vector clearance to 3,500 FT so while descending got a low altitude alert and ATC stated they were cleared to 4,200 FT but had not corrected the pilot's 3,500 FT readback error.
summary: Pilots cruising at 10,000 feet received vectors for an ILS approach but misinterpreted the descent clearance as 3,500 feet instead of 4,200 feet. The controller failed to correct the readback, resulting in a low altitude alert caused by miscommunication.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described an event where they cleared an aircraft to descend below the MVA while distracted by an overtake 'wake' situation on final and then failing to note an incorrect altitude assignment.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and trainee managed a B757 and E135 during an IFR approach where weather caused spacing issues. The trainee missed the E135's altitude clearance due to distraction, leading to a go-around and expedite climb after a readback error between 3,000 and 5,000 feet.

synopsis: ZAN Controller voiced concern regarding a recent facility SOP change that does not conform to national directives with regard to MIA altitude assignments and provided details on a recent example event.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 9 managed a C130 missed approach and a Dash 8 holding at CHINI, issuing a non-compliant direct HINBU clearance due to a dogleg transition. The controller also noted that ADQ Tower failed to report a tall ship prohibiting Runway 25 approaches, creating a safety conflict.

synopsis: ZMA Controller described an airspace incursion noting several internal coordination failures and suggested improvements.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a C750 vectored by ZJX Center entered active military airspace W497B before receiving a point out to HOBEE. The controller attributed the incursion to launch paperwork lacking specific coordinates, which forced sectors to estimate boundaries on the radar scope.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain believes TPA Commercial charts 21-1A (for CAT II) and 21-1B have the same DH for radar (155 FT), but the barometric altitude is different.
summary: A pilot reported a discrepancy in TPA Commercial charts 21-1A and 21-1B, where the radar decision height is 155 FT but barometric altitudes differ. The pilot suspects one chart is incorrect by approximately 50 FT and requires correction.

synopsis: A B757 Captain's windshield began arcing at about 12,000 FT and the outer pane shattered at 16,000 FT, so an emergency was declared while the aircraft returned to land at the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 10,000 feet, the First Officer observed arcing and delamination on the Captain's forward window, which later shattered. The crew returned to the departure airport with ARFF support but failed to declare an emergency as required by the FOM for the deviation.

synopsis: B767 crew experienced a right engine fuel filter EICAS message shortly after takeoff and returns to the departure airport.
summary: The relief pilot and crew received a right engine fuel filter EICAS message during flap retraction on departure. They followed QRH checklists, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An A320 Captain reject the takeoff at 75 KTS after the ECAM alerted SKIN VALVE FAULT.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 75 KTS after a SKIN VALVE FAULT ECAM alert appeared during the takeoff roll.

synopsis: An MD11 flight crew was dispatched with an MEL requiring manual fuel pump operation. Passing FL180 the center engine lost power and eventually flamed out. The First Officer discovered that the fuel pumps are not on.They were turned on, along with ignition. The engine started up and the flight continued to destination.
summary: During climb to FL210, the crew experienced an Engine 2 rollback caused by fuel pumps being left off, likely due to missed manual procedures from operational delays. The First Officer restored engine parameters by activating the pumps and ignition override, allowing the flight to continue to destination without further incident.

synopsis: B757 flight crew was cleared to taxi from their pushed back position to Runway 22L via Taxiway A. As the aircraft began to move the Check Airman on the jump seat sights a fast moving RJ from the left rear and commands a stop.
summary: During taxi out from ORD, a Line Check observer in the jumpseat alerted the Captain to a high-speed RJ in a blind spot, causing an abrupt stop at 2–3 knots. The sudden maneuver caused the Lead Flight Attendant to fall against an open galley door, though she reported no injury and the flight continued.

synopsis: A DHC8-200 Right Main Landing Gear indicated unsafe on approach so an emergency was declared, the checklist completed and after landing on the runway a Mechanic was unable to install the gear pin until all passengers were removed. After the pin was installed the gear indicated down and locked.
summary: The crew executed a go-around and emergency landing after the right main gear failed to indicate "Down and Locked" during a visual approach. Post-landing inspection revealed the gear was not locked, requiring hydraulic pressure from the number two engine to allow a mechanic to pin the gear before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: A B737 Captain taxied onto LAX Taxiway E13 when cleared onto Taxiway R, because the R sign is too near Taxiway E13's throat and makes it appear to be R.
summary: The flight crew mistook Taxiway E13 for Taxiway R while taxiing at LAX due to a poorly positioned sign located between the two taxiways. No further action was taken by Ground Control, and the crew attributed the error to the sign's confusing orientation and small size.

synopsis: A PA31 tire failed on landing which caused the aircraft to be immobile after the pilot successfully guided the aircraft to a safe stop on the runway.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing rollout on Runway 19L, the aircraft rapidly decelerated and pulled right, likely due to a tire failure caused by FOD or a defect. The pilot maintained control using rudder and brake inputs, stopping the aircraft beyond Taxiway U, and attributed the safe outcome to established SOPs.

synopsis: When the left generator drive malfunctioned the flight crew of a B757-200 disconnected the generator, started the APU, brought its generator on-line and proceeded to their destination.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine generator failure due to a Gen Drive Caution EICAS message, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. After restoring power via the APU generator, they canceled the emergency and continued to their destination.

synopsis: MD82 First Officer notices wing fuel beginning to to decrease in cruise with fuel remaining in the center tank. Checklist procedures are complied with, reversing the trend and allowing the flight to continue to destination.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew observed wing fuel quantity decreasing while center tank fuel remained. They executed the checklist to stop the loss, confirmed sufficient fuel and weight limits with Dispatch, and declared an emergency as a precaution for the abnormal situation.

synopsis: A G550 over shot the TEB RUUDY 4 initial level off altitude of 1,500 FT because both elevator and autopilot trim systems momentarily failed and so the aircraft did not level until the pilot manually returned to 1,500 FT.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after departing TEB with a 1,500 FT clearance, the aircraft displayed transient 'ELEVATOR TRIM FAIL' and 'AUTOPILOT TRIM FAIL' messages while hand-flown. The airplane briefly deviated to 1,700 FT before returning to 1,500 FT, causing a distraction but resulting in no separation issues.

synopsis: A B747 flight had a 'Burning Electrical Fumes' event in cruise flight. The incident was successfully resolved in flight partly due to the events recurring nature. The Lav-Galley fan system had been written up four times previously and signed off with circuit breaker resets.
summary: The flight crew managed a burning electrical fumes event in cruise flight, attributing the issue to repeated circuit breaker resets for a faulty lav-galley fan system. The incident caused major inconvenience and revealed a communication disconnect where ground staff were unaware of the required passenger recovery team upon arrival.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A Citation Single pilot experienced a cabin altitude warning during his climb, declared an emergency, descended and returned the aircraft to the service center where it had recently undergone routine maintenance service. After a safe landing the pilot discovered the Air Source Select knob had been placed in the 'OFF' position, possibly during the previous maintenance visit, thus depriving the system of the air required to control cabin altitude. Subsequent flights with the knob in the 'BOTH' [sources] position have proven trouble free.
summary: The pilot experienced a cabin altitude rise to 10,000 feet during climb after recent maintenance, prompting an emergency descent. Post-landing troubleshooting revealed the Air Source Select Knob was left in the 'OFF' position, likely by a technician, causing the loss of pressurization.

synopsis: A C175 departed with more than enough fuel for a 3 and a half hour flight but the engine quit because of fuel starvation while executing a windshear go around so the pilot diverted to a military field with the boost pumps ON.
summary: A pilot flying a 175 tail dragger experienced an engine stoppage at 300 feet during final approach due to suspected fuel exhaustion despite visual checks. The pilot declared an emergency, landed at a closed military base, and later attributed the fuel loss to an unexplained cause rather than temperature expansion.

synopsis: VFR Tower Controller described a potential separation issue when the Approach Controller failed to insure required separation between two IFR arrivals.
summary: A Local Control controller managed a BE33 circling to Runway 3 and a MU2 on a visual approach, but the MU2 pilot failed to see the BE33 despite close proximity. The reporter attributed the issue to SCT Approach controllers lacking training on IFR separation requirements and the tower's inability to provide such separation per LOA.

synopsis: Distracted by attempts to resolve 'bad ride' reports, an Enroute Controller experienced a near separation loss.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance to an E170 at FL350 while distracted by another sector situation, triggering a Conflict Alert with an E145 at FL340. The controller turned the E170 left to increase separation, noting that the close proximity resulted from distraction and the urgency of the pilot's request for smoother air.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a below MVA entry event when failing to note an incorrect altitude assignment during the clearance read back.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a Southwest Airlines flight to descend to 7,000 feet, but the pilot misread the clearance as 6,000 feet and descended below the 7,000-foot MVA by 100 feet. The controller corrected the error after multiple radio attempts, and the pilot climbed back to the assigned altitude with no further incident.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an emergency event experienced by a military aircraft, the event hampered due to lack of both needed land lines to adjacent Approach Control facilities and UHF frequencies.
summary: An F-15 pilot declared an emergency due to an engine fire while descending from FL430 to FL230 during a supersonic run. The controller could not coordinate with Military Approach because the sector lacked access to required UHF frequencies or a direct line.

synopsis: FAY Controller described a conflict event noting the continued 'orbiter' operations near the airport are contributing to these types of instances.
summary: A Tower Controller and trainee managed a CRJ departure that triggered a Resolution Advisory while converging with a PC6 at 2,000 feet. The incident likely resulted from frequency congestion and data block clutter caused by orbiting aircraft, complicating communication with Departure Radar.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a potential conflict event between IFR traffic assigned the SKYES 1 SID from RIV and parachute operations in the departure path, the reporter acknowledging the need to vector aircraft clear of the jump zone if required.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a C17 departing RIV on the SKYES 1 departure while a jump aircraft unexpectedly dropped paratroopers in close proximity. The controller determined the jumpers were down and the jump aircraft had the C17 in sight, prompting a plan to vector departures away from the jump zone if it is not clear.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a conflict event when dealing with bad ride requests. The reporter failed to observe the conflict developing.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector X issued a B737-400 a climb to FL350, causing it to approach a B737-900 at FL340. The controller recognized the conflict before the alert triggered, instructed the B737-400 to expedite, and achieved 4.3 miles separation at FL350.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported that the use of UQ108 in Colombia is inconsistent with the aircraft's emergency descent procedure over high terrain in that there is a mountain peak, El Cucoy, that rises to an altitude some 871 FT higher than the procedure's temporary level off altitude of 17,000 FT.
summary: A B777 pilot reported a terrain risk on airway UQ108 between ILVIR and GEKAR, where a 17,841 FT peak lies within 2 NM of the centerline. The pilot fears crews following emergency descent procedures could descend below terrain and requested Dispatch block this route in favor of safer alternatives.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports the Captain using the restroom facilities while waiting for a gate with one engine shut down and the parking brake set, without summoning a Flight Attendant.
summary: The Captain left his seat to use the restroom after shutting down the right engine, believing the disabled aircraft did not require a Flight Attendant barrier. The crew subsequently taxied to the gate without incident.

synopsis: A B767-300 EICAS alerted LT ENG HPSOV at cruise shortly after takeoff so an emergency was declared. The aircraft returned to the departure airport where repairs were made and flight continued to its scheduled destination.
summary: During climb, the crew received an 'L ENG HPSOV' EICAS message, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport. They extended the landing pattern to reduce weight below the maximum limit before executing a normal approach and landing.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An aircraft landed on YUM Runway 26 and exited earlier than ATC expected, at Taxiway K. While crossing Runway 21L a KC-135 flew directly overhead.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew exited the runway at taxiway K despite Tower instructions to exit at the end, citing safety concerns. A KC-135 subsequently landed on a crossing runway shortly after the crew passed the hold-short point, which the pilot attributed to ATC confusion regarding their location and delayed communication.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports an acrid odor in the cockpit just prior to top of descent. As the smoke and fumes checklist was completed the smell quickly dissipated. An emergency was declared and the flight continued to destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered an acrid smell in the cockpit and cabin during cruise, initiating the Smoke/Fume/Odor QRH and declaring an emergency. After the odor dissipated and a diversion was ruled out due to a closed runway, the crew expedited to their original destination and landed safely.

synopsis: Following receipt of a LE SLAT DISAGREE EICAS message, a B757-200 flight crew declared an emergency, entered a holding pattern to burn fuel, accomplished the appropriate QRH procedures and landed without incident.
summary: The flight crew received a 'LE SLAT DISAGREE' EICAS message during initial climb-out while retracting flaps. They declared an emergency, held at 10,000 FT to burn fuel, and executed an uneventful ILS approach using QRH procedures.

synopsis: At the top of descent with the engines at idle, an entire B737-400 aircraft filled with toxic fumes affecting the entire crew and requiring medical attention after landing. Tricresyl phosphate (TCP) was suspected.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced toxic fumes during descent from TOD, likely caused by Tri-cresyl phosphate (T.C.P.) from engine oil vaporizing into the air conditioning system. All crew members suffered symptoms requiring hospital screening, and the aircraft has a history of similar events.

synopsis: A Q400 experienced wake turbulance from an A320 on approach to YEG.
summary: The pilot reported climbing from 5,200 to 5,800 FT while attempting to capture the glide slope and slow to 170 KTS after encountering wake turbulence from a preceding A320. Approach controllers expressed concern because another aircraft was being vectored above the pilot's position for Runway 20.

synopsis: An E145 flight crew climbing on a heading of 092 degrees to intercept course 079 into RONII per the SUMMT RNAV SID from ATL was advised of a course deviation by the Tower despite the fact their Nav Display showed them to be following the procedure as published.
summary: The crew departed ATL on an RNAV departure but was instructed by Tower to turn left after being told they were south of course, despite the FMS indicating they were on track. The pilot attributed the discrepancy to a difference between the aircraft's RNAV intercept logic and ATC expectations, noting a missed initial instruction due to a wrong callsign.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA during approach to Runway 9L at FLL at 1,300 FT caused by a banner tow aircraft passing under the glide path at 1,000 FT.
summary: The First Officer reported a TCAS RA during an ILS 9L approach at FLL caused by a Banner Tow aircraft flying 400 feet below the glide slope. Although the conflict was resolved and the landing was uneventful, the pilot criticized the Tower for allowing the VFR traffic too close to the active runway.

synopsis: A Captain and Maintenance Technician report about extensive corrosion damage found in the Aft Cargo Compartment, Aft Equipment Bay of a B757-200 aircraft. Pilot also notes immediate inspections and maintenance need to be accomplished on B757/767 aft fuselage sections to prevent a hull lost from similar excessive corrosion.
summary: A pilot assisting a mechanic discovered extensive corrosion and loose wiring in the aft cargo compartment of a Boeing B757 during a ferry flight. The aircraft was diverted to a maintenance base for fuselage repairs, prompting the pilot to call for a system-wide inspection to prevent potential hull loss.

synopsis: An A320 crew rejected their takeoff below 100 KTS when a DMC fault caused the Captain's flight displays and the upper multi-function screen to blank out. After brakes cooled and maintenance deferred the #1 DMC the flight continued to its destination.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff at 95–100 KTS due to a Display Management Computer 1 fault blanking the PFD, ND, and top E/WD screens. After cooling brakes and switching to DMC 3, the crew departed with a deferred fault and replaced DMC 1 upon arrival.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences an autobrake fault in cruise after the fault had been previously written up and diagnosed as an autobrake panel light fault and MELed as such. BSCU 1 was also MELed separately. Flight continues to destination.
summary: The crew discovered an improper dispatch where maintenance incorrectly linked a BSCU 1 fault to an autobrake fault, treating it as a single issue. En route near FL350, the separate autobrake failure recurred, revealing the aircraft was illegally dispatched with two distinct, unaddressed brake system faults.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew rejected their takeoff below 80 KTS due to an ECAM reverser fault warning. After exiting the runway the fault extinguished.
summary: During takeoff at 75 KTS, the crew received an ECAM amber reverser fault warning and executed a rejected takeoff. The fault cleared before the aircraft stopped, leading to a return to the gate for maintenance and a logbook entry.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew returned to their departure airport when they lost control of the pressurization system.
summary: The flight crew experienced left AC pack failure and dual pressurization system inop while climbing to FL340. Manual pressurization control failed, forcing a return to the departure airport where the cabin could only depressurize after shutting down the right pack on the ground.

synopsis: B717 Captain reports receiving a right main gear unsafe indication after gear retraction. Abnormal checklist procedures are complied with and flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a right main gear unsafe light during gear retraction, triggering an abnormal checklist and a return to the gate. The aircraft landed uneventfully below maximum weight, and the event was attributed to an unspecified mechanical issue.

synopsis: A B737-NG's diversion from the short runways at their planned destination to the longer ones at a nearby airport due to a failure of the flaps to extend was complicated by the minimum legal fuel reserves boarded for the flight.
summary: The crew experienced a flap indicator split and failure to extend flaps to 15 degrees during approach, prompting a go-around and emergency diversion. They landed with critically low fuel after a lengthy checklist execution, noting that ATC distractions and fuel concerns impaired their concentration and decision-making.

synopsis: A B737-300 L1 door escape slide girth bar fell off its retainer after the door was disarmed and subsequently the slide fell partially out of its container before the door was fully opened but the slide did not deploy.
summary: A flight attendant reported that while opening the door at arrival, the girt bar fell from the hooks despite being disarmed, partially deploying the slide. The crew deplaned passengers via rear air stairs, and the attendant attributed the incident to weak hooks on the older aircraft.

synopsis: When unable to disarm her assigned passenger exit slide at Door 4L on the B757-200, a Flight Attendant guarded it against its inappropriate operation until Maintenance arrived to relieve her. The reporter expressed dismay that after informing the Captain of the problem he asked her to guard the door and then, apparently, left the aircraft without insuring the problem was resolved.
summary: A flight attendant reported that door 4L would not disarm due to a stuck lever upon arrival. Although the Captain and Purser attempted to fix it, a mechanic eventually opened the adjacent door for catering while the crew guarded the armed door until further assistance arrived.

synopsis: Three Line Mechanics describe a chain of events that led to an inadvertent discharge of an A319 aircraft's forward (#1) Fire Bottle for #2 Engine. Mechanics were attempting to accomplish a Fire Bottle/Squib Firing Circuit Test Maintenance (M) procedure, required by their MEL, to defer a Squib Indication fault. Excessive cold and fatigue were also noted.
summary: A maintenance technician troubleshooting a fire detection issue on a replacement aircraft inadvertently discharged a fire bottle and mistakenly reinstalled an unserviceable squib due to fatigue, cold, and crew pressure. The aircraft was eventually returned to service under an MEL after the error was identified.

synopsis: A Lead Mechanic and another Mechanic report about installing five (6-point type) bolts for the left-hand inboard flap track during a C-Check on a B757-200 aircraft. The Lead Mechanic had misread the parts list on an engineering blueprint.
summary: A maintenance planner misread a blueprint and ordered six identical 6-point bolts instead of one 6-point and five 12-point bolts for a B757-200's flap track during a C-Check. The incorrect hardware was installed but later identified and replaced with the correct parts after the planner recalled the error while working on a similar discrepancy.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reports that a midnight shift Technician found an 8-inch file laying up against the fan exit guide vanes of #1 engine during a service check on a B757-200 aircraft after noticing damage to three fan blades, the fan exit case, and fan exit guide vanes.
summary: A midnight shift mechanic inspecting a B757-200 discovered damage to three fan blades, the fan exit case, and guide vanes in engine #1. An 8-inch file found against the vanes was identified as the cause, leading to blade replacement and repairs or deferrals for other damage.

synopsis: A Mechanic reports how a lack of communication contributed to a damaged flap position transmitter during simultaneous Removal and Replacements (R/R) of the inboard and outboard flap actuators for the right-hand inboard flap on a CRJ-200 aircraft. The aircraft returned to gate with a 'STALL FAIL' EICAS message due to a bent arm on the flap transmitter.
summary: Two mechanics replacing CRJ-200 flap actuators failed to communicate, removing both simultaneously without supporting the flap as required. This caused flap indication damage, leading to a Minimum Equipment List deferral, a subsequent stall failure, and flight cancellation.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he deferred the #2 Hydraulic System Accumulator on a company CRJ-CL65 aircraft under their MEL procedures after the flight crew reported incorrect pressure readings. Downline Maintenance reported #2 Hydraulic Accumulator had been previously removed per an Airworthiness Directive (AD), but their MEL had not been updated.
summary: A flight crew reported a #2 Hydraulic System discrepancy, leading maintenance to discover the #2 Accumulator was missing due to an Airworthiness Directive. The aircraft was taken offline because the crew and MEL were unaware of the removal, prompting an immediate MEL update.

synopsis: Three Avionics Technicians, a Maintenance Specialist, a Maintenance Analyst, and a Maintenance Controller report about their involvement with four COAX cables robbed (cannibalized) from one B747-400 and installed on another B747-400 aircraft for a TCAS unit with a faulted lower antenna. The TCAS cable configurations were not Effective, not interchangeable, between aircraft.
summary: A maintenance mechanic installed a known defective TCAS harness from a B747-400 onto another B747-400 under pressure from a management specialist. The mechanic followed verbal orders to cannibalize a serviceable harness from a ferry-bound aircraft, deferring the repair despite uncertainty that the bad part would fix the issue.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported turning left after a CMA Runway 26 departure, because he misread the CMA commercial chart Obstacle Departure Procedure (ODP) which formats the Runway 8 and Runway 26 procedures without sufficient textual separation.
summary: The pilot departed Camarillo Runway 26 and misread the Obstacle Departure Procedure, executing a left turn instead of the required right turn to intercept the 265 radial. The error was discovered at 2,000 feet when the Magu controller questioned VOR reception, resulting in no traffic conflict due to early departure.

synopsis: B737 First Officer describes a misunderstood clearance from Departure Control that results in a track deviation when the Captain enters and turns toward the fix before the First Officer can verify the route with the next Controller.
summary: During climb from LAX, the crew misheard a clearance for "HECTOR" instead of "EXERT," prompting the hand-flying Captain to initiate an unauthorized turn. The First Officer intervened to stop the deviation, clarified the correct fix and frequency with ATC, and attributed the incident to the Captain bypassing standard FMC entry procedures.

synopsis: An EMB135 Captain began his descent early on a GPS approach because of fatigue or complacency, but his First Officer did not correct his error although the Captain had expected him to.
summary: The pilot initiated a descent early on a GPS approach due to fatigue and relying on visual cues instead of the MFD distance display. After descending to 1,500 feet MSL and incorrectly pressing the altitude button, the pilot recovered by acquiring the VASI and completing a normal visual approach.

aircraft: Sikorsky Helicopter Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Helicopter First Officer experiences difficulties obtaining and IFR clearance from an off shore oil platform via the platform SATCOM and is hung up on by the Supervisor who answers. The Gulf sectors had recently been revised and the call was not going to the correct Sector Controller.
summary: A helicopter pilot on a platform helideck could not obtain an IFR clearance from Houston Center due to unreliable radio, complex dialing procedures, and an unprofessional supervisor who hung up. The crew departed in VMC, cancelled IFR via EFB, and noted the communication issues threatened safe operations.

synopsis: A BE-55 pilot reported a wake vortex encounter while on approach to LOU from an air-taxiing helicopter, resulting in a temporary loss of control.
summary: A pilot on IFR approach to Runway 24 at LOU encountered violent pitch and roll at 200 feet, attributing the upset to wake turbulence from a helicopter crossing the runway. The pilot executed a go-around, while a ground lineman reported seeing the aircraft pitch down toward the FBO.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: CL300 Captain reports misunderstanding an oceanic clearance from PHKO, resulting in a track deviation before the error is detected and corrected.
summary: The PIC at PHKO incorrectly modified the FMS Legs page during taxi, causing the aircraft to deviate from the cleared route via ADOPE to HALLI instead. The error was identified enroute after ATC verification, prompting a successful re-route request to correct the navigation.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain complained that MIA TRACON set his aircraft up for a night visual approach and almost insisted that they accept a visual approach when his preference, after an all night flight, was to fly a published approach.
summary: The pilot reported that Miami Approach Control pressured the crew into an unrequested visual approach to Runway 09 by repeatedly asking if the field was in sight while vectoring for a steep descent. Although the crew stabilized the aircraft at 1,000 feet using speed brakes and gear, the controller's aggressive tactics created a challenging "slam-dunk" scenario.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a conflict event between two IFR aircraft complicated by a photo mission operation nearby and less than adequate briefings provided to the Controller workforce.
summary: A Developmental Controller issued a traffic alert when a CRJ at 5,000 feet flew near a Dash 8 at 4,600 feet during departure. The reporter attributed the conflict to unbriefed reduced separation procedures and picture takers causing the jet to climb unexpectedly.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event when failing to note the conflict aircraft in time to prevent the occurrence. The reporter indicated that the Developmental's RADAR display set-up contributed to the error.
summary: An air traffic controller missed an E145 departure during a busy OJT session, noticing it only after an A320 received a TCAS/RA. The controller attributed the oversight to working from a trainee's scope with different display settings while positioned behind the trainee.

synopsis: B737 flight crew leveling at 8,000 FT experiences a TCAS RA due to VFR traffic at 8,500 FT and descends.
summary: The flight crew on an RMBLR departure from Atlanta received a TCAS "Descend Now" RA while level at 8,000 FT due to another aircraft vectored at 8,500 FT without prior traffic advisories. The crew descended to 7,600 FT, resolved the conflict, and attributed the event to the other aircraft's descent rate and insufficient vertical separation.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain experiences a false windshear warning at 500 FT during a visual approach to Runway 27 at BOS. The approach is continued to landing and no windshear is encuntered.
summary: The flight crew received a windshear warning at 500 feet on approach to Runway 27 at BOS despite clear weather and steady winds. After Tower reported no other windshear activity, the crew continued the approach and landed without incident.

synopsis: A B737-300 crew reported a partial EGPWS TERRAIN warning at 4,400 FT near a charted 2,709 FT hilltop north of the SAN LOC 27 VYDDA intersection while the aircraft was on profile and in a slight descent.
summary: The flight crew received an erroneous EGPWS "Terrain, Terrain" warning while descending in a turn to intercept the LOC 27 approach at SAN. The pilots attributed the false alert to potential GPS error or software issues, as they were well above minimum vectoring altitudes and safely continued the approach.

synopsis: A320 Captain describes a fatiguing training/line check scenario beginning with a long drive for an early check in to deadhead to TNCM. Training/checking occurs on the return leg ending with a low fuel declaration and landing in a down pour.
summary: A fatigued Captain and Check Airman conducted a Class II line check from Saint Maarten to the East Coast after a deadhead flight. Heavy headwinds and ATC vectors caused significant fuel overburn, forcing a Minimum Fuel declaration and a stressful landing in rain with only 3.8 lbs fuel remaining.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain experiences a TE Flap Disagree EICAS message when flaps are moved from 1 to 5 during approach. Delay vectors are requested, an emergency is declared, and QRH procedures are complied with.
summary: The pilot declared a 'pan' emergency while on vectors at 3,000 feet after selecting flaps 5 and receiving a TE Flap disagree EICAS message. The crew delayed vectors to follow QRH procedures, landed safely, and taxied to the gate.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A jet on final to JAN Runway 16 executed a go around because of a conflict with a single engine airplane, which was told to follow the jet to the airport, but instead deviated toward the final approach course from its downwind track.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 16R at Jackson, MS, the crew executed a go-around after spotting a single-engine aircraft drifting onto final from the downwind leg. The near miss occurred due to the other pilot's loss of situational awareness, resulting in a head-on conflict resolved by immediate evasive action before a TCAS resolution advisory issued.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain recounts the difficulties encountered in performing a night visual approach with ILS backup and advises that the reverse, an ILS approach backed up by the visual, is a far better practice.
summary: The Captain and First Officer flew a night visual approach to Runway 2L but mistakenly turned toward Runway 2R while low and slow due to altitude miscalculation. The First Officer identified the error and speed decay, prompting a power increase and correction to the glide slope for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: During preflight on a cold morning, a DHC8-300 cabin filled with smoke after the APU and air conditioning were selected ON, so the passengers were deplaned and Maintenance was called.
summary: The flight crew experienced an APU bleed system failure during pre-flight boarding, causing exhaust odor and smoke to enter the cabin. The APU automatically shut down, prompting the crew to deplane passengers and request a fire truck as a precaution, though no fire was found.

synopsis: Civil Jet landing Runway 6 at TEB was instructed to turn off at Taxiway B and to hold short of Runway 1. During the attempt to clear the landing runway the flight crew crossed the hold lines for Runway 1 causing an aborted takeoff.
summary: The flight crew exiting Runway 6 at TEB crossed the hold short line of Runway 1 due to insufficient separation between the runway exit and hold short lines. This incursion forced the cancellation of a departure clearance for an aircraft on Runway 1.

synopsis: At FL380 a B767-300's Left PACK TEMP HI and PACK OFF lights illuminated followed shortly by the Right PACK OFF light annunciating. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport with the cabin always below 10,000 FT.
summary: The flight crew at FL380 experienced dual pack failures shortly after level off, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. They burned fuel to reduce weight and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing with no injuries.

synopsis: A CRJ200 Captain reported loosing situational awareness after starting his taxi at DEN and taking an incorrect taxiway even though he had been there and followed the route hundreds of times previously.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of Air Carrier 123 taxied incorrectly on Taxiway Z at Denver instead of turning onto G due to the Captain's loss of situational awareness and mental confusion regarding the clearance. Ground Control intercepted the error, reissued a corrected clearance via Taxiway L, and the crew acknowledged the need for stricter adherence to standard operating procedures.

synopsis: Flight attendants aboard a B747-400 notified the flight crew of inoperative cabin PA and interphone handsets at several doors during taxi for takeoff. Only after takeoff and the initial food service were the flight attendants advised that the inoperative handsets were deferable and that notification occurred only because flight attendants took the initiative to call and ask.
summary: Cabin crew reported that the PA system and interphones on doors 2L/R, 3L/R, and 4L/R were inoperative during taxi and takeoff. The Captain confirmed the issue but authorized the 15-hour flight to proceed without repairs or alternative emergency communication methods.

synopsis: SR22 pilot descending into HPN from the east experiences a conflict with a CRJ climbing from behind. ATC assistance had been requested one minute prior over BDR and the reporter was instructed to call a different Controller.
summary: A VFR pilot descending to HPN pattern altitude nearly collided with a regional jet after the controller declined to provide flight following. The pilot avoided a mid-air collision by hearing the controller's traffic advisory and arresting descent, though the jet had already received a TCAS RA.

synopsis: A BE35 lost primary guidance systems (attitude, HSI, airspeed, altimeter, VSI) in flight during unforecast icing conditions on and IFR flight plan. His backup ASPEN PFD did provide partial information.
summary: The pilot encountered unforecast trace ice in IMC, activating pitot heat before losing primary instruments and autopilot. The aircraft descended 600 feet while transitioning to secondary instruments, but the pilot recovered to the assigned 6,000 feet with Center's assistance.

synopsis: MD83 Captain experiences traffic alert immediately followed by a resolution advisory upon descending out of 6,000 FT. Commands for climb and descent were received and the target remained co-located and same altitude. ATC reported no traffic in the area.
summary: During descent from 6,000 feet, the crew followed TCAS resolution advisories despite ATC reporting no traffic, suspecting an equipment malfunction as the alert persisted for five minutes without a clear of conflict. Two flight attendants later reported sore backs, and the discrepancy was logged.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A CL-65 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport for an overweight landing following receipt of a 'GEAR DISAGREE' warning after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew encountered a nose landing gear retraction failure shortly after departure, triggering a gear disagree warning. They followed the QRH checklist, declared an emergency, and executed a successful precautionary overweight landing at the nearest airport.

synopsis: C172 pilot taking off on an ice runway reports loosing directional control when full throttle is applied too early. Control is regained and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during takeoff on an ice runway due to applying throttle too quickly, causing the aircraft to skid and strike a stick with the wing strut. No injuries or damage occurred, though a nearby pickup truck was briefly in the skid path before control was regained.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A CE525 FMS failed while the single pilot was on a GPS approach so after descending 400 FT below the final approach fix altitude he disconnected the autopilot.
summary: During a GPS approach to Runway XXR, the FMS failed, causing the aircraft to descend 400 feet below the final approach fix altitude. The pilot manually corrected the deviation by disengaging the autopilot.

synopsis: ZOA Controller reported a conflict event involving IFR traffic departing from APC with a military aircraft departing SUU. The reporter suggested some airspace adjustments.
summary: An FA90 departed APC and turned to ECA before reaching SGD, climbing to 5,000 feet into head-on traffic with a departing KC35. The controller used visual separation to climb the FA90 through the KC35, attributing the conflict to SGD being a flyby point rather than a flyover.

synopsis: ZNY Controller described an unsafe condition when traffic inbound from the Santa Maria facility was NORDO for some time, developing into a separation problem. The reporter suggests improved procedures between the two subject ATC facilities.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Sector 86 observed an unidentified A340 at FL380 near MARIG, causing a potential conflict with a northbound Boeing. The controller cleared the Boeing to descend to FL360 to maintain separation, attributing the incident to a failure in flight data transfer from Santa Maria to New York Ocean.

synopsis: An FCM Controller described a runway incursion event claiming the lack of tower visibility contributed to the incident.
summary: An aircraft incorrectly taxied onto Runway 28R, forcing Ground Control to divert it and Local Control to cancel a takeoff clearance. The reporter attributes the incident to poor tower visibility of the northwest corner and confusing taxiway geometry that caused the pilot to misjudge the runway location.

synopsis: A B757 made a quick return to departure airport because of an engine failure after takeoff. Am emergency was declared and evacuation preparations made. The Purser's perspective of the incident is included along with that of the flight crew.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a left engine failure and overtemp at 2,000 FT following a loud pop and yaw during climb. They declared an emergency, executed the Severe Engine Damage checklist, and landed safely after returning to the airport.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence just before touchdown at PHL behind a B757 that extended their touchdown point and caused some issues with ATC.
summary: The crew experienced wake turbulence from a preceding B757 during the flare at PHL, extending their touchdown. A hurried exit and simultaneous ATC communication caused confusion over taxi instructions and resulted in the pilot forgetting to retract flaps during the after-landing flow.
