summary: The pilot executed an ILS to Runway 5 with a 9-10 KT tailwind, causing rapid runway consumption. The aircraft overran the end of Runway 5 and collided with two approach lights for Runway 23.

synopsis: A Metroliner pilot was told he needed 10 hours rest but that was changed back to 9 hours so he flew the assigned trip and was told after arrival that 10 hours was legally required. The Company wanted to move the freight at any cost to satisfy the customer.
summary: A pilot reported that Operations instructed him to fly after a 9-hour rest, later admitting a 10-hour rest was required. The pilot attributed the potential duty time violation to company error, customer pressure, and lack of sleep, feeling the carrier disregarded safety regulations.

synopsis: An AT6 pilot entered a CTAF airport on the incorrect frequency on clear day and had a near miss with an aircraft when he did not comply with this airport's established traffic pattern.
summary: The pilot executed a right base turn to Runway 15 and passed under another aircraft while on the wrong CTAF frequency. The near miss resulted from the pilot's complacency, inattention, and failure to follow standard pattern procedures, leading the pilot to self-ground for evaluation.

synopsis: A PA32 Student Pilot changed the fuel tank transfer at 200' on final before his instructor could comment and the engine quit due to fuel starvation so they landed straight ahead just short of the runway causing no damage.
summary: During a training flight in a Cherokee 6, a student pilot switched fuel tanks on short final, causing an engine power loss. The instructor executed a safe off-runway landing on grass, restarted the engine, and taxied back with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew confused PCM for LAL on a night VOR Runway 9 approach and executed a go around simultaneously with an ATC low altitude alert when they realized the airport identification error.
summary: The crew vectored for the VOR 9 approach at Lakeland Linder (LAL) mistakenly descended toward the similarly aligned Plant City Airport due to pilot-controlled lighting. They executed a missed approach after DME discrepancies and a low altitude warning, then completed a normal landing on a subsequent approach.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a wrong sector hand off event when inadvertently initiating a hand off to an incorrect sector, the reporter suggesting automation help to prevent future occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller relieving the R-Side position inadvertently initiated a handoff to the wrong sector for a B737-800 while conducting a briefing. The controller corrected the error by recalling the handoff and issuing a verbal transfer to the correct sector, noting the need for system safeguards against invalid route penetrations.

synopsis: ANC Controller described an overtake event on Runway 7R/L when heavy traffic landing Runway 7R passed a large aircraft on final to Runway 7L, the reporter suggesting more defined ATC procedures to prevent future occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a B747 overtaking a B737 on final approach due to unclear sequencing, language barriers, and the aircraft being on different frequencies. The controller issued visual separation instructions after realizing the B747 was passing the B737 on the right.

synopsis: Enroute Controller experienced a loss of separation event indicating more vigilance should have been exercised during the relief briefing.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller, feeling ill but unable to take sick leave, lost separation between a B717 and an E145 after inheriting a conflicting descent clearance during a sector combination. The controller's delayed corrective instructions failed to prevent the loss of separation, which they attributed to insufficient skepticism during the position relief briefing.

synopsis: Air Carrier departing MCO received a 'line up and wait' clearance from ATC but then noted a landing aircraft on final and questioned the Controller, the Controller revised the clearance to 'hold short' admitting error on his/her part.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Company flight were cleared to line up and wait on Runway 17R at MCO while another aircraft was landing. The crew stopped short after spotting the landing aircraft, prompting the controller to admit a mistake and issue a hold short clearance, preventing a runway incursion.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After landing at MDW and told by ATC to exit at the Taxiway D only, the confused crew stopped prior to Taxiway Y and remained there until ATC gave further clearance along with an admonishment about not clearing the runway.
summary: The flight crew landed at MDW and held short of the forward high-speed exit (D) due to confusion over Tower's instruction to avoid Taxiway Y. This delay occurred because the crew misinterpreted the clearance, though Ground Control later clarified that AIM rules permitted turning onto Y to clear the runway.

synopsis: An MD11 alerted SEL ENG #3 FADEC ALT, followed by ENG #3 RPM LOW and the engine flamed out so the ENG SHUTDOWN Checklist followed by the INFLIGHT START Checklist resulted in a normal engine operation.
summary: The crew received FADEC and RPM low alerts on Engine #3, causing a flameout. After completing shutdown and start checklists, the engine restarted normally, and ATC cleared the flight to continue to its planned destination.

synopsis: A B767-300 had a minor tail strike on takeoff in gusty weather but also the aircraft may have been mis-loaded because after returning to the airport the cargo and bags were shifted followed by a normal takeoff.
summary: The First Officer reported a suspected tail strike during a gusty takeoff from SFO after flight attendants heard a scraping sound, prompting a return and manual depressurization. Mechanics found only minor tailskid damage, while the crew attributed the event to possible gusts, over-rotation, or recent cargo loading system issues.

synopsis: An ERJ190 Captain rejected the takeoff at about 40 KTS after the EICAS alerted STEER OFF and the First Officer had difficulty controlling the aircraft's track which veered right of the runway centerline.
summary: The Captain rejected a takeoff on Runway 4 at under 40 knots after the First Officer struggled to track the centerline due to a "STEER OFF" EICAS message disabling nose wheel steering. The crew aborted, confirmed the aircraft was airworthy, and successfully completed the flight after acknowledging the steering limitation at low speeds.

synopsis: A321 flight crew experiences dual FMGC failures during approach when 'No Star' is used to clear unneeded waypoints during vectors. With CAT III approaches in use, the crew elects to divert to a nearby VMC alternate.
summary: The crew experienced a dual FMGC reset on a Thales FMS system during a CAT III ILS approach while clearing waypoints. This known software fault caused a total loss of flight plans, forcing a diversion to a VFR alternate for a visual landing.

synopsis: A B737-700 crew was notified in flight about a weight and balance error after 960 LBS of luggage from a previous flight was mistakenly left in the aft compartment.
summary: The flight crew and ground operations were involved in a departure where 32 bags were omitted from the forward cargo weight and balance due to miscommunication. Although the aircraft remained within weight limits, the crew departed with incorrect data because Station Operations failed to inform the ramp crew of the bags left from a previous flight.

synopsis: A B737-700's left engine ingested an unsecured jetway conditioned air hose chain after parking at its gate under a Marshaller's guidance.
summary: During ramp operations with the #1 engine running, the jet bridge shook and banged against the aircraft, prompting ground crew to signal an immediate engine shutdown. The pilot reported that the #1 engine ingested a conditioned air hose, which a ramp worker later attributed to unsecured chains allowing the hose to move into the ingestion area.

synopsis: An 'O' ring on a DHC8-300's Number Two Hydraulic system failed in flight causing the loss of all hydraulic fluid and system pressure so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a complete loss of #2 hydraulic system quantity and pressure at FL190 due to a blown o-ring on a hydraulic line. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed uneventfully with ARFF escort.

synopsis: Flight crew report about the inability of tall pilots to safely operate CE-560XL aircraft with the new thicker replacement cushions for pilot seats that reduces vertical seat adjustments, restricts full outside vision, restricts full movement of flight controls and full vision of flight instrument panels. The new cushions no longer meet the Original Equipment Manufacturer's (OEM) standards for 560XL pilot seats.
summary: The PIC of a Cessna CE-560XL refused to accept the aircraft after finding the modified seat cushion prevented safe instrument visibility and control movement. Management dismissed the safety concern, pressuring the crew to fly despite the seat exceeding OEM standards and FAR Part 25 Design Eye Reference Point requirements.

synopsis: A MD83's left generator failed in flight so the crew returned to the departure airport after evaluating enroute and destination weather because they were unable to start the APU.
summary: During cruise at FL320, the crew experienced a left generator failure and could not reset it or start the APU below FL300. After consulting maintenance, they returned to the departure airport and landed using the Single Generator checklist.

synopsis: A CRJ200 Captain descended 300 FT into VNY airspace on a visual approach to BUR Runway 8 because he was unfamiliar with VNY's location and the Runway 8 ILS was OTS.
summary: The pilot flying descended 200–500 feet below the assigned 3,000 feet while on a visual approach to Runway 8 at BUR at night. The deviation occurred because the pilot misidentified Van Nuys Airport as Burbank due to distraction and unfamiliarity, but the First Officer corrected the error before the aircraft reached the runway.

synopsis: A BE55's landing gear failed to retract after takeoff so the crew diverted to a nearby airport where maintenance was available.
summary: The pilot flying called for gear up after departure, triggering a 'LG lever disagree' alert and red gear indications. Following QRH procedures, the gear remained down and locked with green lights, allowing a safe diversion to the base airport for factory repairs.

synopsis: An MD11 Captain turned off an IRU in flight when he intended to open the flight station door because the switches are located very close to each other on the overhead panel.
summary: The Captain inadvertently switched off the number 2 inertial reference unit (IRU) while attempting to disarm the flight deck access system at initial cruise. The crew consulted the Quick Reference Handbook to utilize the auxiliary IRU, allowing the flight to continue safely, though the report cites co-located switches without guards as the cause.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot flying over a dry lake bed near 0L7 (Jean, NV) struck a parasail related cable attached to a wench but the area is not marked on the sectional as supporting recreational aviation activities.
summary: During a low-level training flight, the aircraft's left wing struck a parasailer cable attached to a ground winch, causing wing damage. The cable hung on the pitot tube for 15 seconds, but the aircraft returned to base safely from the unmarked dry lake bed.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An Instructor pilot returned to OMA from training to find it IFR and the ILS OTS so he began the LOC/DME 14 only to discover he was not DME equipped but fortunately became VMC before having to execute a missed approach.
summary: A private pilot and student encountered deteriorating VFR conditions, leading to an unplanned IFR approach at OMA where the pilot inadvertently accepted a LOC/DME approach without required DME equipment. The pilot descended below the minimum altitude before realizing the error, climbed, and safely landed via a contact approach, attributing the incident to poor planning, inadequate briefing, and outdated ATIS information.

synopsis: A pilot reported flying through R-4812 southeast of FLX after he did not see the restriction between R-4810 and R-4804A because of MOA chart clutter even though his GPS gave him advanced warning.
summary: A VFR pilot flying north from LAS inadvertently entered restricted airspace R-4812 between R-4810 and R-4804 due to poor chart reading. Although the GPS issued a warning, the pilot misidentified the alert as R-4804A and only realized the error after being informed by a Sheriff during a fuel stop.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a confused arrival procedure event prompted by a Data Block indicator that was inaccurate, the reporter suggesting the discontinuation of the problematic procedure until briefings and a proper fix can be completed.
summary: An ATC controller observed a B737 at 11,000 feet with a Data Block trailing 'R' indicating the CEEME1 arrival, though the pilot reported flying the FERNANDO5 arrival due to a flawed routing. The controller reported the equipment issue, leading to a directive to discontinue the CEEME1 arrival until proper design and briefing are completed.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a loss of separation event during attempts to vector aircraft below an overcast layer for visual approaches, the reporter acknowledging a failure to intervene in a timely manner.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a Developmental Controller lost separation between a CRJ2 and a B717 during visual approaches to Runways 26R and 27L in low visibility. The incident occurred because the Controller provided instructions instead of issuing immediate control commands to position the CRJ2 behind the B717.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event complicated by a number of other contributing factors, the reporter acknowledging the sector complexity was 'self induced.'
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing Departure Radar One lost situational awareness of a departing BE36 due to distraction from a C130 automation failure, allowing the BE36 to conflict with an inbound B737. The controller issued an immediate turn to resolve the conflict, attributing the event to self-induced sector complexity and failure to use automation tools.

synopsis: BWI Controller described a ASDE-X Alarm indicating an aircraft on Runway 15L, the reporter noting a taxiing aircraft was observed by Tower personnel as clear of the runway so a landing clearance was issued contrary to procedures.
summary: A trainee controller at BWI instructed an SR22 to cross Runway 15L, causing a false ASDE-X alert when a C525 was on final. Although the SR22 was visually confirmed clear, the system triggered an "occupied" warning, and the reporter admitted the C525 should have been instructed to go around per procedure.

synopsis: APA Controller voiced concern regarding some controllers common practice of not advising opposite direction traffic of one another's position during a Runway 17L Departure and Runway 35R Approach operation.
summary: A Ground Control controller reported that Local Control cleared Aircraft X on a runway heading from Runway 17L without advising of a C182 on a VFR practice approach to Runway 35R. The controller described this daily occurrence at APA as dangerous due to the risk of collision if communication fails, noting the FLM observed but did not intervene.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller, working all frequencies temporarily due to headset problems, described a confused takeoff clearance event when an air carrier failed to depart as instructed.
summary: A Local Controller covering Ground frequencies cleared a CRJ for takeoff while a Mooney was on final, but the CRJ pilot did not hear instructions to expedite due to mechanical checklists and confusion over frequency changes. The controller ordered a go-around for the Mooney, and no loss of separation occurred.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: MMU Controller described a take off clearance not accepted by the departing aircraft because of traffic on short final, the Controller noting the Tower visibility from the temporary tower is obstructed by the wind sock location.
summary: A CPC trainee on Local Control cleared Aircraft 1 for takeoff while Aircraft 2 was on short final, requiring an immediate cancellation. The trainee missed Aircraft 2 because a windsock obstructed the view from the mobile tower, prompting a recommendation to relocate the obstruction.

synopsis: A B757 encountered severe mountain wave activity over the Front Range at FL370 which resulted in a 5 second, 5 KT overspeed and later the Captain's PFD, ND and FMC blanked along with an uncommanded 10 degree roll. The Left AC Bus may have had a problem.
summary: While crossing the Front Range eastbound at FL370, the crew encountered severe mountain waves causing a 5-knot overspeed and subsequent left AC bus failure. This resulted in dark PFD, ND, and FMC screens with an uncommanded 10-degree left roll, but the crew consulted Dispatch and Maintenance to continue safely.

synopsis: A B757's left pack air conditioning duct ruptured slightly at takeoff, then completely failed at FL280, causing the loss of cabin pressurization. The crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport.
summary: Pilots reported a dull thud at takeoff followed by uncontrollable cockpit temperature and a cabin altitude warning at FL280. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 FT and performed a successful overweight landing after passenger oxygen masks failed to deploy.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences an ECAM message HYD Pump Low Pressure Green. The pump is turned off and initially the PTU appears to be maintaining Green system pressure. While holding at FL190 a PTU low pressure ECAM is annunciated along with a Yellow system overheat. The PTU is turned of and the crew elects to return to the departure airport after the Yellow system cools.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Green hydraulic pump failure and PTU cavitation during climb, leading to an emergency return with no nose wheel steering. They performed a gravity gear extension and landed safely, requiring a tug to tow the aircraft to the gate.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences a crew oxygen system failure during preflight testing and informs Maintenance. Maintenance attempts to defer the oxygen indication system but the crew refuses to accept the aircraft.
summary: During preflight, a pilot observed an amber OXY ECAM indication and low regulator pressure, which Maintenance initially attributed to a sensor fault. However, testing revealed actual airflow failure when masks were donned, leading to an aircraft swap and likely removal from service due to a suspected fleet-wide issue.

synopsis: Q400 Captain experiences a flap drive failure during approach with the flaps stopping at 30 degrees in icing conditions. After considering a go around the approach is continued to an uneventful landing.
summary: The Captain continued an approach in moderate icing after flaps stuck at 30 degrees instead of 35, triggering a FLAP DRIVE caution. The crew reviewed landing considerations and executed a safe landing, rollout, and taxi-in without incident.

synopsis: B737-400 flight crew experiences several issues including lack of pressurization, after picking up the aircraft after heavy maintenance for a ferry flight. Flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned an aircraft shortly after an 'A' Check due to a cabin altitude warning caused by maintenance personnel leaving bleed air switches OFF. Additional issues included a failed autopilot from a blown AFDS circuit breaker, a hung engine start, and inoperative radios and terrain displays.

synopsis: A CRJ700, six miles behind an A380 on approach to JFK Runway 22L, experienced localizer deviations two dots left and right of center while the A380 was on short final and landing roll.
summary: During a coupled ILS approach to JFK Runway 22L at 1,800 feet, the localizer deviated erratically, likely due to interference from an Airbus A380 six nautical miles ahead. The crew stabilized the aircraft in heading mode, re-engaged the localizer, and completed the approach normally.

synopsis: DHC8-300 Captain reports aircraft was struck by lightening during descent, causing the Left DC Generator to trip off. Flight continues to an uneventful landing at destination airport. Radar did not show any significant weather nearby at the time of the lightening strike.
summary: The crew encountered an unforecast isolated thundercell during descent, resulting in a lightning strike near the right wing that illuminated the Left DC Generator CL light. After resetting the generator and managing UNS errors, the flight landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: G200 First Officer experiences a Cabin Door CAS message shortly after takeoff and the crew elects to return to the departure airport. The problem is diagnosed as a faulty pressurization controller which is deferred requiring the crew to manually control the pressurization.
summary: During a Part 135 flight, the crew received a cabin door warning and pressurization issue shortly after takeoff, requiring a fuel burn to reduce landing weight before returning. Maintenance MEL'd the auto-pressurization system, forcing manual operation that the pilot reported created an unsafe, high-workload environment for the crew.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports that the PAPI for Runway 28 at MTPP are misaligned with the lights on the right indicating high while the left lights indicate low.
summary: The pilot and First Officer encountered conflicting PAPI indications on Runway 28 during a circle-to-land approach, with the right side showing high and the left showing low. This discrepancy caused the pilot flying to become high on short final, requiring a correction.

synopsis: B767 Captain experiences a left engine HI-STAGE light during takeoff and continues. After complying with QRH procedures Maintenance Control is contacted and the Captain is instructed to cycle the bleed switch to attempt to restore the system. The Captain refuses.
summary: During takeoff, the crew observed left engine HI-STAGE and EICAS warnings, closed the ENG BLEED switch, and refused Maintenance Control's instruction to cycle the ENG BLEED and left pack switches to reset the system.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew is informed by passengers in cruise that part of the left wing near the engine was sticking up into the slip stream in an abnormal fashion. After discussion with Maintenance the crew diverts to a suitable airport. Upon being viewed by Maintenance on the ground the aircraft is taken out of service.
summary: During cruise, a passenger noticed a left wing panel sticking up, prompting the flight crew to divert and land overweight at approximately 325,000 to 345,000 lbs due to concerns the panel might detach and strike the tail. The aircraft landed normally with fire department escort, and no emergency was declared.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reports discovering that both fire indicator lights were inoperative on the nose gear during preflight. A Maintenance Supervisor states to the First Officer that finding the discrepancies so close to departure time indicate that the First Officer does not care about on time departures.
summary: During preflight, a pilot reported inoperative nose gear fire lights and suspect rivets, but a Maintenance Supervisor aggressively questioned the write-ups to prioritize on-time departure. The pilot cited recent training on fire panel failures as the reason for reporting these safety-critical items despite the supervisor's intimidation.

synopsis: A319 Flight Crew experiences autopilot and side stick controller anomalies during climb out. The autopilot is unresponsive to MCP heading inputs nor does the First Officer's side stick controller have any effect after the autopilot is disconnected. Control is passed to the Captain and flight returns to departure airport for an uneventful over weight landing.
summary: The First Officer reported that during climbout, the heading knob became unresponsive and the aircraft failed to turn despite disconnecting the autopilot. After the Captain took priority control, the crew returned for a safe, overweight landing.

synopsis: An A319 crew detected a diesel bus exhaust odor as thrust was reduced for a climb constraint so they went on oxygen immediately, declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport where a CFM56 bent compressor section blade was found which caused a slight shaft wobble.
summary: During climb through 8,000 feet, the flight crew and cabin crew detected a strong oily smell resembling diesel exhaust. They donned oxygen masks, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing and passenger deplaning with no injuries.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain reports receiving an aircraft that has been written up by the previous crew for rolling during approach when the flaps are extended from 15 to 30 degrees. Maintenance can find no faults and the aircraft is dispatched, only to have the problem occur again on the next landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer flew an aircraft with a known flap roll issue that maintenance initially cleared. During the approach with flaps 30, the First Officer applied right aileron to maintain wings level, resulting in an uneventful landing and a subsequent logbook write-up for a flap spindle problem.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer describes an engine failure during approach below 800 FT possibly due to a bird strike. After performing memory items for the engine failure the crew elects to continue to a safe landing.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced an uncommanded Engine 2 failure with N1/N2 fluctuations and vibrations at 800 feet on short final, possibly triggered by a bird strike. They declared an emergency, managed the engine rollback to idle, and landed safely on Runway 26R without fire.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports being confused after being issued taxi instructions to taxi via B and M to hold short of Runway 4L and expedite through the 4L approach. A right turn is initiated at M resulting in a possible runway incursion. Poor signage is cited as a factor.
summary: The flight crew experienced a potential runway encroachment while taxiing due to delayed weight reconciliation, changing clearances, and poor signage at the B and M intersection. The pilot mistakenly turned right onto Runway 14 instead of left toward Runway 9, requiring Tower to redirect them to hold short of Runway 4R.

synopsis: A Pilot reports a Flight Attendant notified him halfway through their second flight that Row 10-CD had two speaker panes and Row 9-CD had two Oxygen (O2) panels on their CRJ-700 aircraft. If an emergency had occurred, Oxygen would not have been available to passengers in Row 10-CD.
summary: During Flight YYY, a Flight Attendant discovered that Row 10-CD lacked oxygen panels because maintenance personnel incorrectly installed speaker and oxygen panels in Rows 9 and 10. This error meant passengers in Row 10-CD would have had no oxygen access in an emergency.

synopsis: SF340 flight crew reports departing with 2,800 LBS of fuel on board then discovering during preflight for the next leg that is the gauges indicated 3,400 LBS of fuel on board, although none was added.
summary: The First Officer and Captain discovered a fuel quantity gauge discrepancy showing 3,400 LBS instead of the expected 2,198 LBS after a flight with no refueling. Maintenance Control verified the aircraft did not exceed structural limits, and Contract Maintenance inspected the faulty gauges before the aircraft was signed off for further operations.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer experiences the failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff. The QRH is consulted to no avail and the Dispatcher requests that the crew attempt to make it to destination and divert if it becomes necessary. It becomes necessary.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear retraction failure after takeoff, prompting a diversion to ZZZ due to fuel concerns caused by dispatcher delays. They maintained safe operations at lower altitudes without declaring an emergency and landed safely.

synopsis: Captain reports he noticed a large difference in brake temperatures between the left and right Main Landing Gear (MLG) brakes on an EMB-170 aircraft during preflight. While taxiing out, the left MLG brakes did not respond to pedal pressure. Maintenance re-attached both left MLG brake ratchet type hydraulic connectors and brakes worked normally.
summary: The pilot discovered inoperative left main gear brakes during taxi after noting abnormal temperature differences during preflight. Maintenance attributed the failure to unsecured brake lines backing off their fittings, a known issue lacking safety wire, and restored function by re-attaching the hoses.

synopsis: A B737-800 Flight Attendant was assigned an aircraft the day following a flight in the aircraft which had the dirty socks odor after engine start, on climb and again on descent. Following this event, crew members had headaches, burning throats, metallic mouth taste and skin reactions. The APU was replaced.
summary: Cabin crew reported a strong odor and physical symptoms on an aircraft previously flagged for similar issues, which intensified during engine start and descent. The smell, described as a "dirty gym" odor, caused headaches and rashes in crew and passengers, prompting a report to the Duty Supervisor.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he may have left an 'activator/deactivator' installed at the left Main Landing Gear (MLG) up-and-locked sensor on the uplock assembly of a B757-200 aircraft, after an Operational Test for a landing gear handle replacement.
summary: A mechanic on a B757-200 left a left main landing gear uplock activator installed after an operational test. The oversight was attributed to the sensor's difficult visibility, high winds, and fatigue from repeated ladder use.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports an Engineering Order (EO) with time restrictions was issued on a B737-400 aircraft for temporary repair of a bussing plug requiring accomplishment prior to flight that conflicted with a Maintenance Control Service Item replacement of the same bussing plug that was eventually deferred without time restrictions.
summary: A mechanic deferred a B737-400 bussing plug replacement due to a missing part, unaware an issued Engineering Order required completion before further flight. The aircraft flew nine legs over two days before being removed from service to comply with the order, which was caused by issuing a restrictive EO before parts were available.

synopsis: While taxiing southeast on Taxiway 'A;' a C210 pilot failed to hold short at Taxiway 'B' at KMKL as cleared by Ground Control. A contributing factor was the fact that 'B' intersects 'A' a two points and only the point further from the point the clearance was received is marked.
summary: The pilot missed a hold-short instruction at the first intersection of Taxiway A and B while taxiing because the visible sign was at a second intersection. The reporter attributes the error to the lack of a sign at the first intersection and recommends renaming the taxiway or clarifying which intersection is intended.

synopsis: BE36 pilot notices his door ajar climbing through 3,200 FT and requests a level off at 5,000 FT. The door cannot be closed in flight and a request to divert is made to ATC, but comm 1 has apparently failed. Reporter squawks 7600 and turns toward the nearest airport and is able to communicate on comm 2 with the Tower prior to landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a door opening and radio failure while climbing to 7,000 feet after departure. After canceling IFR and squawking 7600, the pilot returned to the nearest airport, declared an emergency on a working radio, and landed without incident.

synopsis: The pilot of a pusher canard homebuilt suffered a nose gear strut failure on landing.
summary: During landing, the nose wheel strut broke, causing the aircraft to slide to a stop. The pilot reported no further damage or injuries.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot, anticipating a low approach found himself high for a safe landing when smoke in the cockpit made a full stop landing on the short runway a necessity. As he approached the intersection of a longer runway he opted to align with and land on it. He was unable to communicate with the Tower as a result of unpowering the radios in response to the electrical smoke event.
summary: The pilot experienced smoke from the instrument panel while turning final for Runway 2L and diverted to land on Runway 34 to avoid hard braking. After shutting down avionics, the pilot taxied to parking using flight line marshalers, reporting the incident was handled safely without danger.

synopsis: Vertigo combined with either a malfunctioning or improperly operated GPS in IMC had to be overcome by the instrument rated Instructor pilot in command of a BE58 to affect a safe landing. Assistance from ATC, her multiengine rated student and another CFII in the back seat contributed to a safe recovery from the event.
summary: The PIC, instructing a student in IMC, experienced spatial disorientation and GPS navigation failures during an ILS approach, causing altitude and heading deviations. The crew utilized CRM, autopilot, and a backup VOR approach to land safely, attributing the incident to overconfidence, potential sinus issues, and fatigue.

synopsis: BE35 pilot describes difficulties flying up the east coast from Florida due to Class B airspace, TFR's, and restricted areas, suggesting that airborne information could be provided by ADS-B or commercial services (XM or WSI).
summary: An IFR flight northbound on V3 encountered a TFR over Titusville and heavy weather, forcing ATC to issue conflicting vectors through restricted airspace without verifying its status. The pilot reported that frequency saturation and rigid routing left no time to confirm if restricted areas were active, creating a risk of inadvertent entry.

synopsis: As he exited clouds on an IFR flight a C182T pilot experienced an NMAC with a sailplane operating in close proximity to the cloud cover. The reporter believed the sailplane pilot to have been in violation of required VFR separation from the cloud system.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 7,000 MSL narrowly avoided a collision with a glider descending from clouds by executing a hard right turn. The reporter attributed the incident to the glider pilot's failure to maintain VFR cloud separation, noting ATC lacked radar contact and no NOTAMs were filed for the activity.

synopsis: A BE33 pilot momentarily lost control and the aircraft pitched up abruptly during takeoff when the seat moved aft and off of its tracks. Through extraorinary effort he was able to regain control and proceed to a safe landing. The cause was the failure of maintenance personnel to reinstall the seat on both tracks following refurbishment of the upholstery.
summary: The sole pilot of a privately owned aircraft experienced a seat separation during takeoff after refurbishment, causing a pitch-up and loss of control due to improper rail reinstallation. The pilot recovered by manually pulling forward to lower the nose and landed safely at a nearby field.

synopsis: An observant Flight Attendant detected an overheated side wall lighting fixture aboard a B777 halfway across the Atlantic Ocean. The Captain ordered the sidewall lights to be unpowered for the duration of the flight.
summary: A flight attendant detected a burning wire odor and found a blackened sidewall lighting fixture above rows 21AB to 25AB during snack service. The Captain inspected the area and instructed that the sidewall lighting not be used for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event noting some of the coordination relative to this incident was made without utilizing a recorded land line.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a loss of separation between a CRJ2 and an MD90 while climbing near FL320. The incident occurred after the CRJ2 reverted to its original course following a handoff, triggering a Conflict Alert despite corrective turns.

synopsis: ZBW Controller described an airspace incursion event when the route read out provided on the display did not match up with that provided by URET.
summary: A Radar Controller descended an aircraft to 170 and handed it off to Sector 05, but the aircraft turned right into ZNY airspace because it lacked the PAR route. The controller attributed the error to the scope displaying an incorrect route readout that did not match the aircraft's actual flight plan.

synopsis: ZAU Controller described a confused and unsafe event when coordination between Centers was confused and not in the best interest of the user, the reporter noting that procedures should be flexible with coordination during some instances.
summary: An air traffic controller managing an E145 climb to 10,000 feet encountered an abrasive handoff from ZOB Lansing Sector, who demanded a 360-degree turn and correct routing despite no immediate safety conflict. The reporter attributed the unsafe situation to the other controller's unprofessional attitude and rigid adherence to rules over common sense.

synopsis: Air Carrier on final for ONT was issued go around instructions by the Tower only to be questioned by SCT Controllers regarding the assigned heading.
summary: Pilots executing an ILS approach to SCT were instructed by Tower to go around with a climbing left turn heading 180 due to IMC conditions. SCT controllers later criticized this clearance for conflicting with Chico's localizer, though no traffic conflicts occurred, and a supervisor apologized citing ongoing training issues.

synopsis: A B737-300 flight crew rejected their takeoff at V1 when a chronic leading edge slat in transit light illuminated but was, this time, backed up by individual slat indicators showing #5 and #6 had retracted.

synopsis: Following a thorough flight inspection, which discovered an open access panel on the left engine cowling, a CRJ-200 flight crew experienced a loud bang followed by a jammed left throttle at high thrust which required them to perform an inflight shutdown and perform a single engine landing. Following a safe landing, Maintenance found the upper half of the tailcone cowling missing and the lower half still attached, but displaced from its design location.
summary: During climb, a left engine tailcone panel that was previously found popped open at an intermediate stop detached, causing a bang, momentary N1 overspeed, and a thrust lever jam at 81% N1. The crew declared an emergency, shut down the left engine, and landed safely; maintenance later confirmed a latch failure from the previous night's maintenance caused the cowling to separate.
